# Plan: Migrate kix-platform-docs to Docusaurus 3.9.2 with Konecta Branding + MCP Server

## Context

The kix-platform-docs repo currently uses Jekyll with `jekyll-theme-minimal` to serve documentation via GitHub Pages. The content covers architecture, developer guides, security reviews, CI/CD runbooks, strategy, and more across 15 markdown files with 10 PNG diagrams.

This migration replaces Jekyll with Docusaurus 3.9.2, applies strict Konecta branding, restructures content by audience, rewrites docs using the platform specification documents as the source of truth, and adds an MCP server that exposes the full docs as resources/tools for AI agents.

---

## Phase 1: Scaffold Docusaurus Project

### 1.1 Clean up Jekyll artifacts
- Archive `_config.yml` and old `index.md` to `archive/jekyll/`
- Remove Gemfile if present
- Create new `.gitignore` for Node.js/Docusaurus

### 1.2 Initialize Docusaurus
- Create `package.json` pinning `@docusaurus/core` and `@docusaurus/preset-classic` to `3.9.2`
- Install dependencies: `clsx`, `prism-react-renderer`, `react`, `react-dom`, `@easyops-cn/docusaurus-search-local`
- Create `babel.config.js` (standard Docusaurus preset)
- Create `docusaurus.config.js` with:
  - `url: 'https://konecta-ix-platform.github.io'`
  - `baseUrl: '/kix-platform-docs/'`
  - `organizationName: 'konecta-ix-platform'`
  - `onBrokenLinks: 'throw'` (catches migration errors at build time)
  - Blog disabled
  - Local search via `@easyops-cn/docusaurus-search-local`
  - Prism languages: bash, hcl, json, yaml, python, go
  - Navbar: Documentation, Modules, Infrastructure links + GitHub
  - Footer: dark style with doc links, repo links, support links
- Create `sidebars.js` with 8 top-level categories (see 1.4)

| `ARCHITECTURE.md` | `docs/architecture/` (7 files) | Split into infrastructure, gke-cluster, namespaces, network-flows, decision-records. Extract TDRs to ADR files |

| `CICD_RUNBOOK.md` | `docs/infrastructure-ops/cicd-runbook.md` | Migrate with front matter |
| `DNS_MIGRATION.md` | `docs/infrastructure-ops/dns-migration.md` | Migrate with front matter |
| `EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md` | `docs/strategy/executive-summary.md` | Migrate with front matter |
| `PROJECT_PLAN.md` | `docs/strategy/roadmap.md` | Merge into roadmap |
| `UI_DESIGN.md` | `docs/reference/ui-design.md` | Migrate with front matter |

## Phase 3: MCP Server

### 3.1 Structure
```
mcp-server/
  package.json          # Separate from Docusaurus deps
  tsconfig.json         # TypeScript config (ES2022, Node16)
  src/
    index.ts            # Entry: McpServer + StdioServerTransport
    content-loader.ts   # Reads + indexes all docs at startup
    search-index.ts     # MiniSearch wrapper
    resources.ts        # Resource handlers
    tools.ts            # Tool handlers
    prompts.ts          # Prompt templates
```

### 3.2 Dependencies
- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (latest v1.x or v2.x)
- `zod` (schema validation)
- `gray-matter` (front matter parsing)
- `minisearch` (full-text search index)
- `glob` (file discovery)

### 3.3 Resources
- **doc-page** (`docs://kix-platform/{path}`) - Every markdown file as a resource
- **doc-index** (`docs://kix-platform/index`) - JSON listing of all pages with titles/descriptions

### 3.4 Tools
| Tool | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `search_docs` | `query`, `category?`, `limit?` | Array of `{path, title, snippet, score}` |
| `lookup_glossary` | `term` | `{term, definition}` or suggestions |
| `lookup_module` | `module_name` | `{name, type, description, path, repo_url}` |
| `lookup_adr` | `adr_id?`, `keyword?` | ADR content with decision + rationale |

### 3.5 Prompts
- **doc-review** - Template for reviewing a doc page for accuracy, completeness, clarity

### 3.6 Transport
- stdio (works with Claude Code and Claude Desktop)
- All logging via `console.error()` (never `console.log()`)

### 3.7 Configuration
`.mcp.json` at project root:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kix-docs": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["mcp-server/build/index.js"],
      "env": { "DOCS_ROOT": "docs" }
    }
  }
}
```

### 3.8 Verify MCP server
```bash
cd mcp-server && npm install && npm run build
# Test with MCP Inspector:
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node build/index.js
```

```yaml
# Jekyll configuration for KIX Platform Documentation
# GitHub Pages will use this to build the site

title: KIX Platform Documentation
description: Enterprise AI Agent Platform on Google Cloud Platform
baseurl: "" # Leave empty for organization sites
url: "https://konecta-ix-platform.github.io"

# Theme
theme: jekyll-theme-minimal
# Alternative themes: jekyll-theme-cayman, jekyll-theme-slate, jekyll-theme-modernist

# GitHub Pages settings
github:
  repository_url: https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs
  is_project_page: true

# Navigation
navigation:
  - title: Home
    url: /
  - title: Architecture
    url: /docs/ARCHITECTURE
  - title: Onboarding
    url: /docs/ONBOARDING
  - title: Developer Guide
    url: /docs/DEVELOPER_GUIDE
  - title: Strategy
    url: /docs/STRATEGY
  - title: Security
    url: /docs/SECURITY_REVIEW
  - title: CI/CD
    url: /docs/CICD_RUNBOOK

# Markdown processing
markdown: kramdown
kramdown:
  input: GFM
  syntax_highlighter: rouge

# Exclude from processing
exclude:
  - README.md
  - Gemfile
  - Gemfile.lock
  - vendor
  - .git
  - .gitignore

# Include
include:
  - _config.yml

# Plugins
plugins:
  - jekyll-feed
  - jekyll-seo-tag
  - jekyll-sitemap

# Defaults
defaults:
  - scope:
      path: "docs"
    values:
      layout: default
      permalink: /:path/

# Footer
footer:
  text: "Platform Engineering Team"
  links:
    - title: GitHub
      url: https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform
    - title: Modules
      url: https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules
    - title: Infrastructure
      url: https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-infrastructure
```

     2→
     3→Welcome to the **Konecta KIX Platform** infrastructure repository. This guide takes you from zero to deploying infrastructure and contributing to the codebase.
     4→
     5→**Version:** 1.0
     6→**Date:** January 2026
     7→**Classification:** Confidential - Internal Use Only
     8→**Estimated Time:** 60-90 minutes
     9→

    11→

    13→

    28→
    29→## Prerequisites
    30→
    31→### GCP Organization Access
    32→
    33→Before you begin, ensure you have access to the Konecta GCP Organization:
    34→
    35→1. **Request GCP Organization Access** - Contact IT Service Desk with:
    36→   - Your konecta-group.com email address
    37→   - Team: Platform Engineering
    38→   - Required access: Delegated folder admin for KIX Platform
    39→
    40→2. **Required IAM Roles**
    41→
    42→You'll need the following roles on the delegated root folder:
    43→- `roles/resourcemanager.folderAdmin` - Create folders and projects
    44→- `roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator` - Create GCP projects
    45→- `roles/billing.user` - Link projects to billing account
    46→- `roles/compute.networkAdmin` - Create VPCs and networking
    47→- `roles/container.admin` - Create GKE clusters
    48→
    49→### Required Tools
    50→
    51→| Tool | Version | Installation |
    52→|------|---------|--------------|
    53→| Terraform | >= 1.5.0 | [terraform.io/downloads](https://www.terraform.io/downloads) |
    54→| gcloud CLI | Latest | [cloud.google.com/sdk/install](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/install) |
    55→| Go | >= 1.21 | [go.dev/doc/install](https://go.dev/doc/install) |
    56→| kubectl | >= 1.28 | [kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/) |
    57→| git | >= 2.0 | Installed on most systems |
    58→
    59→**Verify installations:**
    60→
    61→```bash
    62→terraform version  # Should show v1.5.0 or higher
    63→gcloud version     # Should show latest SDK
    64→go version         # Should show go1.21 or higher
    65→kubectl version --client  # Should show v1.28 or higher
    66→```
    67→
    68→---
    69→
    70→## Repository Setup
    71→
    72→### 1. Clone the Repository
    73→
    74→```bash
    75→# Currently hosted on Bitbucket (migrating to GitHub soon)
    76→git clone https://bitbucket.org/konecta-group/kon-gcp-platform.git
    77→cd kon-gcp-platform
    78→
    79→git branch
    80→# Expected output: * develop
    81→```
    82→
    83→**Note:** The repository is currently on Bitbucket but will migrate to GitHub. The CI/CD pipelines already use GitHub Actions.
    84→
    85→**Branching Strategy:**
    86→- `main` - Production-ready code, pushed at sprint end or new environment delivery
    87→- `develop` - Main development branch during sprint, integration point for features
    88→- Feature branches - Work in progress, merge to `develop` via PR
    89→
    90→### 2. Key Files to Read First
    91→
    92→| File | Time | Description |
    93→|------|------|-------------|
    94→| `CLAUDE.md` | 10 min | Project overview, security requirements, naming conventions |
    95→| `docs/ONBOARDING.md` | 15 min | This file |
    96→| `docs/STRATEGY.md` | 20 min | Platform vision and architecture |
    97→| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | 20 min | Technical infrastructure details |
    98→
    99→### 3. Directory Structure
   100→
   101→```
   102→kon-gcp-platform/
   103→+-- CLAUDE.md                       # Project standards (READ THIS FIRST)
   104→+-- terraform/
   105→|   +-- bootstrap/                  # Org-level state buckets (run first)
   106→|   +-- modules/
   107→|   |   +-- gcp/                    # GCP-specific modules
   108→|   |   |   +-- base-environment/   # GCP projects and folder structure
   109→|   |   |   +-- landing-zone/       # VPC, networking, security baseline
   110→|   |   |   +-- gke-cluster/        # GKE cluster creation
   111→|   |   |   +-- data-services/      # Cloud SQL, Redis, GCS, Pub/Sub
   112→|   |   +-- kubernetes/             # Kubernetes-specific modules
   113→|   |       +-- gke-config/         # Namespace, RBAC, network policies
   114→|   |       +-- kong-gateway/       # Kong API Gateway
   115→|   |       +-- litellm/            # LiteLLM proxy
   116→|   |       +-- argocd/             # ArgoCD GitOps (shared cluster)
   117→|   +-- environments/               # Environment-specific configurations
   118→|   |   +-- shared/                 # Shared services (ArgoCD, DNS)
   119→|   |   +-- lab/                    # Playground for new technology
   120→|   |   +-- dev/                    # Development
   121→|   |   +-- qa/                     # QA (mirrors prod)
   122→|   |   +-- prod/                   # Production
   123→|   +-- test/                       # Terratest integration tests
   124→+-- docs/                           # Documentation

   129→## Authentication Setup
   130→
   131→### 1. Authenticate with GCP
   132→
   133→```bash
   134→# Login with your konecta-group.com account
   135→gcloud auth login
   136→
   137→# Set up application default credentials for Terraform
   138→gcloud auth application-default login
   139→
   140→# Verify authentication
   141→gcloud auth list
   142→```
   143→
   144→### 2. Configure gcloud Defaults
   145→
   146→```bash
   147→# Set default region (MUST be EU per org policy)
   148→gcloud config set compute/region europe-west1
   149→gcloud config set compute/zone europe-west1-b
   150→
   151→# Verify configuration
   152→gcloud config list
   153→```
   154→
   155→### 3. Environment Variables
   156→
   157→Add to your `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`:
   158→
   159→```bash
   160→# GCP Configuration
   161→export GOOGLE_REGION="europe-west1"
   162→export TF_VAR_default_region="europe-west1"
   163→export TF_VAR_billing_account="XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX"  # Get from platform team
   164→export TF_VAR_root_folder_id="folders/XXXXXXXXXXXX"   # Get from platform team
   165→
   166→# Terratest Configuration
   167→export SKIP_TEARDOWN=false
   168→export TEST_TIMEOUT=60m
   169→```
   170→
   171→---
   172→
   173→## Understanding the Repository Structure
   174→
   175→### Module Organization
   176→
   177→Modules are organized by provider type:
   178→
   179→**GCP Modules** (`modules/gcp/`):
   180→- `base-environment` - GCP folders and projects
   181→- `landing-zone` - VPC, networking, security baseline
   182→- `gke-cluster` - GKE cluster creation
   183→- `data-services/*` - Cloud SQL, Redis, GCS, Pub/Sub
   184→
   185→**Kubernetes Modules** (`modules/kubernetes/`):
   186→- `gke-config` - Namespaces, RBAC, network policies
   187→- `kong-gateway` - Kong API Gateway
   188→- `litellm` - LiteLLM proxy
   189→- `argocd` - ArgoCD GitOps continuous delivery (shared cluster)
   190→
   191→### Service Dependency Chain
   192→
   193→Services must be deployed in order:
   194→
   195→```
   196→+---------------------+
   197→|     bootstrap       |  Creates state buckets (run once)
   198→+---------+-----------+
   199→          |
   200→          v
   201→+---------------------+
   202→|    gcp/network      |  VPC, subnets, NAT, firewall
   203→+---------+-----------+
   204→          |
   205→          +----------------+
   206→          v                v
   207→+---------------+  +---------------+
   208→|   gcp/gke     |  |   gcp/data    |  (can run in parallel)
   209→+-------+-------+  +---------------+
   210→        |
   211→        v
   212→+---------------------+
   213→| kubernetes/platform |  gke-config, kong, litellm
   214→+---------------------+
   215→```
   216→
   217→### State Management
   218→
   219→Each service has its own state file:
   220→
   221→```
   222→gs://kd-tfstate-{env}/
   223→+-- gcp/network/
   224→+-- gcp/gke/
   225→+-- gcp/data/
   226→+-- kubernetes/platform/
   227→```
   228→
   229→---
   230→
   231→## Environment Configuration
   232→
   233→### config.json (Per Environment)
   234→
   235→Each environment has a `config.json` that drives all deployments:
   236→
   237→```json
   238→{
   239→  "global": {
   240→    "environment": "dev",
   241→    "region": "europe-west1",
   242→    "gke_project_id": "kd-ix-eur-dev-gke",
   243→    "data_project_id": "kd-ix-eur-dev-data"
   244→  },
   245→  "landing_zone": { ... },
   246→  "gke_cluster": { ... },
   247→  "gke_config": { ... },
   248→  "kong_gateway": { ... }
   249→}
   250→```
   251→
   252→**Usage in Terraform:**
   253→
   254→```hcl
   255→locals {
   256→  config = jsondecode(file("${path.module}/../config.json"))
   257→}
   258→
   259→module "landing_zone" {
   260→  source   = "../../../../modules/gcp/landing-zone"
   261→  vpc_name = local.config.landing_zone.vpc_name
   262→}
   263→```
   264→
   265→### Environment Differences
   266→
   267→| Setting | Dev | QA | Prod |
   268→|---------|-----|-----|------|
   269→| Flow logs | 50% sampling | 50% sampling | 100% sampling |
   270→| Node pool min nodes | 1 | 1 | 2 |
   271→| Deletion protection | false | false | true |
   272→| Kong replicas | 2 | 2 | 3 |
   273→| VPC Service Controls | false | false | true |
   274→
   275→---
   276→
   277→## Your First Deployment
   278→
   279→### Step 0: Bootstrap (One-time)
   280→
   281→```bash
   282→cd terraform/environments/bootstrap
   283→cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars
   284→# Edit terraform.tfvars with your organization values
   285→
   286→terraform init
   287→terraform apply
   288→```
   289→
   290→### Step 1: Deploy Network
   291→
   292→```bash
   293→cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   294→
   295→terraform init
   296→terraform plan
   297→terraform apply
   298→# Takes 3-5 minutes
   299→```
   300→
   301→**Verify:**
   302→```bash
   303→gcloud compute networks describe kix-dev-vpc \
   304→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-network
   305→```
   306→
   307→### Step 2: Deploy GKE
   308→
   309→```bash
   310→cd ../gke
   311→
   312→terraform init
   313→terraform plan
   314→terraform apply
   315→# Takes 15-20 minutes
   316→```
   317→
   318→**Verify:**
   319→```bash
   320→gcloud container clusters get-credentials kix-dev-cluster \
   321→  --region=europe-west1 \
   322→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke
   323→
   324→kubectl cluster-info
   325→kubectl get nodes
   326→```
   327→
   328→### Step 3: Deploy Kubernetes Platform
   329→
   330→```bash
   331→cd ../../kubernetes/platform
   332→
   333→terraform init
   334→terraform plan
   335→terraform apply
   336→```
   337→
   338→**Verify:**
   339→```bash
   340→kubectl get namespaces
   341→kubectl get pods -n kong
   342→```
   343→
   344→### Cleanup (Optional)
   345→
   346→Destroy in reverse order:
   347→```bash
   348→cd terraform/environments/dev/kubernetes/platform && terraform destroy
   349→cd ../../gcp/gke && terraform destroy
   350→cd ../network && terraform destroy
   351→```
   352→
   353→---
   354→
   355→## Terraform Development Standards
   356→
   357→### Module Structure
   358→
   359→Every module MUST include:
   360→
   361→```
   362→module-name/
   363→+-- main.tf           # Resource definitions
   364→+-- variables.tf      # Input variables with descriptions
   365→+-- outputs.tf        # Output values with descriptions
   366→+-- versions.tf       # Provider version constraints
   367→+-- README.md         # Documentation
   368→+-- examples/         # Working examples
   369→```
   370→
   371→### Variable Naming Conventions
   372→
   373→| Pattern | Use Case | Example |
   374→|---------|----------|---------|
   375→| `enable_*` | Feature flags | `enable_versioning`, `enable_auth` |
   376→| `create_*` | Resource creation | `create_service_account` |
   377→| `*_config` | Configuration objects | `maintenance_config`, `logging_config` |
   378→| `*_policy` | Policy definitions | `retention_policy` |
   379→
   380→**Correct:**
   381→```hcl
   382→variable "enable_versioning" {
   383→  type        = bool
   384→  default     = true
   385→  description = "Enable object versioning for the bucket"
   386→}
   387→
   388→variable "maintenance_config" {
   389→  type = object({
   390→    day  = string
   391→    hour = number
   392→  })
   393→  description = "Maintenance window configuration"
   394→}
   395→```
   396→
   397→**Incorrect:**
   398→```hcl
   399→variable "auth_enabled" { ... }      # Use enable_* prefix
   400→variable "maintenance_policy" { ... } # Use *_config suffix
   401→```
   402→
   403→### Required Variables (All Modules)
   404→
   405→| Variable | Type | Description |
   406→|----------|------|-------------|
   407→| `project_id` | string | GCP project ID |
   408→| `environment` | string | Environment name (dev, qa, prod, lab) |
   409→| `cost_center` | string | Cost center for billing |
   410→
   411→### Variable Validation
   412→
   413→```hcl
   414→variable "environment" {
   415→  type        = string
   416→  description = "Environment name"
   417→
   418→  validation {
   419→    condition     = contains(["dev", "qa", "prod", "lab", "shared"], var.environment)
   420→    error_message = "Environment must be one of: dev, qa, prod, lab, shared"
   421→  }
   422→}
   423→```
   424→
   425→### README Standards
   426→
   427→All module READMEs MUST include:
   428→- Overview and architecture
   429→- Usage examples (basic and production)
   430→- **Security Requirements section** (mandatory)
   431→- Inputs/Outputs tables
   432→- Document metadata footer
   433→
   434→### Common Patterns
   435→
   436→**Use for_each:**
   437→```hcl
   438→resource "google_storage_bucket" "buckets" {
   439→  for_each = toset(["documents", "artifacts", "logs"])
   440→  name     = "${var.usecase_name}-${each.value}-${var.environment}"
   441→}
   442→```
   443→
   444→**Use locals for computed values:**
   445→```hcl
   446→locals {
   447→  project_id = "kix-${var.environment}-${var.function}"
   448→  common_labels = {
   449→    environment = var.environment
   450→    managed_by  = "terraform"
   451→  }
   452→}
   453→```
   454→
   455→### Pre-Commit Checklist
   456→
   457→```bash
   458→terraform fmt -recursive
   459→terraform validate
   460→terraform plan -out=tfplan
   461→terraform-docs markdown . > README.md
   462→```
   463→
   464→---
   465→
   466→## Running Tests
   467→
   468→### Run Individual Tests
   469→
   470→```bash
   471→cd terraform/test
   472→
   473→go test -v -timeout 30m -run TestBaseEnvironment
   474→go test -v -timeout 30m -run TestLandingZone
   475→go test -v -timeout 60m -run TestGKECluster
   476→go test -v -timeout 30m -run TestArgoCD
   477→```
   478→
   479→### Run All Tests
   480→
   481→```bash
   482→go test -v -timeout 120m ./...
   483→```
   484→
   485→### Debug Mode
   486→
   487→```bash
   488→export SKIP_TEARDOWN=true
   489→go test -v -timeout 30m -run TestGKECluster
   490→# Manually inspect, then destroy
   491→```
   492→
   493→---
   494→
   495→## Deploying Infrastructure Changes
   496→
   497→Changes to infrastructure follow a **controlled deployment process** with manual approvals for production.
   498→
   499→### Overview
   500→
   501→```
   502→Feature Branch → PR Validation → Merge to Main → Manual Deploy
   503→    (fast)         (~10 min)      (validates)     (controlled)
   504→```
   505→
   506→### 1. Make Changes in Feature Branch
   507→
   508→```bash
   509→# Create feature branch
   510→git checkout -b feature/add-redis-instance
   511→
   512→# Make Terraform changes
   513→cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/data
   514→# Edit *.tf files
   515→
   516→# Validate locally
   517→terraform fmt -recursive
   518→terraform validate
   519→terraform plan
   520→```
   521→
   522→### 2. Open Pull Request
   523→
   524→Submit PR to `main` branch. PR validation runs automatically (~10 minutes):
   525→
   526→**What happens:**
   527→- ✅ Terraform format check
   528→- ✅ Security scan (tfsec)
   529→- ✅ Terraform validate
   530→- ✅ Generate plans for changed directories
   531→- ✅ Run fast smoke tests (if modules changed)
   532→- 💬 Plan summary posted as PR comment
   533→
   534→**Review the plan output:**
   535→```
   536→Plan: 2 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy
   537→
   538→+ google_redis_instance.cache
   539→+ google_compute_firewall.redis_ingress
   540→~ google_service_account.redis (labels)
   541→```
   542→
   543→### 3. Merge to Main
   544→
   545→After PR approval, merge to `main`. **No automatic deployment occurs.**
   546→
   547→**What happens:**
   548→- ✅ Main validation runs (validates all changes)
   549→- ✅ Plans regenerated to prove deployability
   550→- 🏷️ Release tagged with semantic version (e.g., v1.2.3)
   551→- ℹ️ No infrastructure changes applied
   552→
   553→### 4. Deploy During Change Window
   554→
   555→Navigate to **Actions → Deploy Infrastructure** workflow and click **Run workflow**.
   556→
   557→**Configure deployment:**
   558→
   559→| Input | Description | Example |
   560→|-------|-------------|---------|
   561→| **environment** | Target environment | `dev`, `qa`, `prod`, `shared` |
   562→| **scope** | What to deploy | `network`, `gke`, `data`, `kong`, `all` |
   563→| **dry_run** | Plan only, no apply | `false` (deploy) or `true` (plan only) |
   564→| **auto_approve** | Skip approval (dev only) | `true` (dev) or `false` (qa/prod) |
   565→
   566→**Example: Deploy Redis to Dev**
   567→```yaml
   568→environment: dev
   569→scope: data
   570→dry_run: false
   571→auto_approve: true  # Dev allows auto-approve
   572→```
   573→
   574→**Example: Deploy GKE to Production**
   575→```yaml
   576→environment: prod
   577→scope: gke
   578→dry_run: false
   579→auto_approve: false  # Prod requires approval
   580→```
   581→
   582→**Deployment flow:**
   583→1. **Pre-flight checks** - Validates change window, permissions
   584→2. **Validate** - Format, security scan
   585→3. **Plan** - Generates fresh plan (catches drift)
   586→4. **Approval** - Manual review and approval (QA/Prod)
   587→5. **Apply** - Executes Terraform apply
   588→6. **Verify** - Runs smoke tests
   589→7. **Summary** - Posts deployment report
   590→
   591→### 5. Monitor Deployment
   592→
   593→Watch the workflow run:
   594→- Green checkmarks indicate success
   595→- Review plan output before approval
   596→- Monitor apply progress
   597→- Verify outputs after completion
   598→
   599→### Change Windows
   600→
   601→Infrastructure deployments are restricted by environment:
   602→
   603→| Environment | Change Window | Approval | Notes |
   604→|-------------|---------------|----------|-------|
   605→| **dev** | Anytime | Optional (auto-approve allowed) | Rapid iteration |
   606→| **qa** | Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC) | Required | Avoid during testing |
   607→| **prod** | **Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC only** | Required + change ticket | Restricted window |
   608→| **shared** | Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC) | Required | Impacts all environments |
   609→
   610→**Production restrictions:**
   611→- Deployments outside the window are **automatically blocked**
   612→- Emergency hotfixes require manual approval bypass (see CICD_RUNBOOK.md)
   613→- Change tickets must be referenced in deployment approval
   614→
   615→### Scope Mapping
   616→
   617→The `scope` input maps to Terraform directories:
   618→
   619→| Scope | Description | Directories |
   620→|-------|-------------|-------------|
   621→| `network` | VPC, subnets, firewall | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/network` |
   622→| `security` | Security baseline | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/security` |
   623→| `gke` | GKE cluster | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/gke` |
   624→| `platform` | Namespaces, RBAC | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/platform` |
   625→| `data` | Cloud SQL, Redis, GCS | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/data` |
   626→| `kong` | Kong API Gateway | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/kong` |
   627→| `gateway` | GKE Gateway | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/gateway` |
   628→| `litellm` | LiteLLM proxy | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/litellm` |
   629→| `argocd` | ArgoCD (shared only) | `terraform/environments/shared/kubernetes/argocd` |
   630→| `all` | All of the above | Sequential deployment (network → security → gke → platform → data) |
   631→
   632→### Deployment Best Practices
   633→
   634→**Before deploying:**
   635→- ✅ Verify plan output matches intent
   636→- ✅ Check for unexpected resource destruction
   637→- ✅ Ensure change window compliance (production)
   638→- ✅ Notify team in #kix-platform-engineering
   639→
   640→**During deployment:**
   641→- ✅ Monitor workflow progress
   642→- ✅ Watch for errors in real-time
   643→- ❌ Don't close browser until complete
   644→
   645→**After deployment:**
   646→- ✅ Verify services are healthy
   647→- ✅ Review Terraform outputs
   648→- ✅ Monitor metrics for anomalies
   649→- ✅ Update deployment log
   650→
   651→### Rollback Procedure
   652→
   653→If deployment causes issues:
   654→
   655→```bash
   656→# Option 1: Revert code and redeploy
   657→git revert <commit-hash>
   658→git push origin main
   659→# Then run deploy workflow with reverted code
   660→
   661→# Option 2: Manual Terraform rollback (emergency only)
   662→cd terraform/environments/{env}/{scope}
   663→terraform init
   664→terraform state pull > backup.tfstate
   665→# Manually fix state or apply reverted config
   666→```
   667→
   668→### Advanced: Drift Detection
   669→
   670→Nightly workflow checks for infrastructure drift:
   671→- Runs daily at 02:00 UTC
   672→- Checks all environments and scopes
   673→- Creates GitHub issues if drift detected
   674→
   675→**Manually trigger drift detection:**
   676→```
   677→Actions → Nightly Quality Checks → Run workflow
   678→```
   679→
   680→### Troubleshooting Deployments
   681→
   682→See [CICD_RUNBOOK.md](./CICD_RUNBOOK.md) for detailed troubleshooting:
   683→- Plan shows unexpected changes
   684→- Apply fails with "resource already exists"
   685→- Workflow stuck on approval
   686→- Change window blocked production deployment
   687→
   688→---

   690→## Contributing
   691→
   692→### Before Contributing
   693→
   694→1. Read `CLAUDE.md` section "Approval Requirements"
   695→2. Create feature branch: `git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name`
   696→3. Follow pre-commit checklist
   697→4. Submit PR for review
   698→
   699→### Good First Contributions
   700→
   701→- Fix documentation typos
   702→- Add examples to module READMEs
   703→- Improve variable descriptions
   704→- Add validation rules
   705→
   706→### Approval Requirements
   707→
   708→| Environment | Approvers |
   709→|-------------|-----------|
   710→| Dev | Infrastructure Lead |
   711→| QA | Infrastructure Lead + DevSecOps Lead |
   712→| Prod | Chief Engineer + Infrastructure Lead + CISO |
   713→

   715→
   716→## Troubleshooting
   717→
   718→### Error: "The caller does not have permission"
   719→
   720→```bash
   721→gcloud auth list
   722→gcloud config get-value account
   723→# If wrong account:
   724→gcloud auth login your.email@konecta-group.com
   725→gcloud auth application-default login
   726→```
   727→
   728→### Error: "Failed to save state: AccessDenied"
   729→
   730→```bash
   731→gsutil ls gs://kd-tfstate-dev
   732→terraform init -reconfigure
   733→```
   734→
   735→### Error: "Quota exceeded"
   736→
   737→```bash
   738→gcloud compute project-info describe \
   739→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke \
   740→  --format="table(quotas.metric,quotas.limit,quotas.usage)"
   741→# Request quota increase in GCP Console
   742→```
   743→
   744→### Error: "Timeout waiting for cluster"
   745→
   746→GKE clusters take 15-20 minutes. Check status:
   747→```bash
   748→gcloud container clusters describe kix-dev-cluster \
   749→  --region=europe-west1 \
   750→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke
   751→```
   752→
   753→### State Lock Error
   754→
   755→```bash
   756→# Only if certain no other process is running:
   757→terraform force-unlock LOCK_ID
   758→```
   759→
   760→### Debug Logging
   761→
   762→```bash
   763→export TF_LOG=DEBUG
   764→export TF_LOG_PATH=./terraform-debug.log
   765→terraform plan
   766→# Review logs
   767→cat terraform-debug.log
   768→unset TF_LOG TF_LOG_PATH
   769→```
   770→
   771→### Getting Help
   772→
   773→**Include when asking for help:**
   774→1. Full error message
   775→2. Terraform version: `terraform version`
   776→3. Module/environment
   777→4. Steps to reproduce
   778→
   779→**Support Channels:**
   780→- Slack: #kix-platform-engineering
   781→- Urgent: #kix-platform-oncall
   782→- Security: security@konecta-group.com

     1→# KIX Platform Developer Guide
     2→
     3→**Version:** 1.0
     4→**Date:** January 2026
     5→**Classification:** Confidential - Internal Use Only
     6→**Audience:** Use case developers building on KIX
     7→
     8→---
     9→
    10→## Overview
    11→
    12→This guide explains how to build services on the KIX Platform. It covers what the platform provides, how to build use cases, service patterns, and technology specifications for each component.
    13→
    14→**Related Documents:**
    15→- `STRATEGY.md` — Platform vision and business goals
    16→- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — Technical infrastructure details
    17→- `ONBOARDING.md` — Getting started with the repository
    18→
    19→---
    20→
    21→## Table of Contents
    22→
    23→1. [Platform Overview](#platform-overview)
    24→2. [What the Platform Provides](#what-the-platform-provides)
    25→3. [What Developers Build](#what-developers-build)
    26→4. [BAOE Readiness Framework](#baoe-readiness-framework)
    27→5. [Autonomy Tiers](#autonomy-tiers)
    28→6. [Technology Specifications](#technology-specifications)
    29→7. [Service Patterns](#service-patterns)
    30→8. [Use Case Examples](#use-case-examples)
    31→9. [Governance Requirements](#governance-requirements)
    32→
    33→---
    34→
    35→## Platform Overview
    36→
    37→### Architecture Layers
    38→
    39→| Layer | Purpose | Components |
    40→|-------|---------|------------|
    41→| **Northbound** | Service exposure to consumers | Kong API Gateway, LiteLLM MCP Gateway, Admin UI |
    42→| **Capability** | Business logic and orchestration | Control Plane, Agents, Voice, Messaging, Knowledge |
    43→| **Southbound** | Infrastructure (abstracted) | GCP services, databases, storage, events |
    44→
    45→### Service Consumption Model
    46→
    47→Consumers access platform capabilities through three methods:
    48→
    49→| Method | Consumer Type | Authentication |
    50→|--------|---------------|----------------|
    51→| REST API (Kong) | External systems, applications | API Key or JWT |
    52→| MCP Tools (LiteLLM) | AI agents | Service account |
    53→| Admin UI | Internal users | OIDC |
    54→
    55→All requests are authenticated, routed through the appropriate gateway, and executed by the capability layer. Infrastructure is never exposed directly to consumers.
    56→
    57→---
    58→
    59→## What the Platform Provides
    60→
    61→When a use case is onboarded, the platform automatically provisions:
    62→
    63→| Resource | Description |
    64→|----------|-------------|
    65→| **Kubernetes Namespace** | Isolated environment for workloads |
    66→| **PostgreSQL Database** | Dedicated database with credentials |
    67→| **Redis Key Prefix** | Shared cache with isolated keyspace |
    68→| **GCS Bucket** | Object storage for documents and artifacts |
    69→| **Pub/Sub Topic** | Event bus for async messaging |
    70→| **Kong Routes** | API endpoints at `/api/v1/{use-case}/*` |
    71→| **Secrets Folder** | Secret Manager path for credentials |
    72→| **Service Account** | GCP identity with least-privilege permissions |
    73→| **Observability** | Pre-configured dashboard, logs, and traces |
    74→| **Identity** | Identity services abstracting credential handling |
    75→| **Security** | Security monitoring, WAF, and firewall services |
    76→| **Service Catalogue** | Backstage portal for discovering available services |
    77→
    78→### Service Discovery via Backstage
    79→
    80→Use case developers discover available platform services through **Backstage**, the internal service catalogue:
    81→
    82→| What You Can Discover | Examples |
    83→|----------------------|----------|
    84→| **Platform Services** | LiteLLM endpoints, Kong routes, MCP tools |
    85→| **Data Services** | Available databases, Redis instances, GCS buckets |
    86→| **CrewAI Agents** | Existing agents you can call or integrate with |
    87→| **Pub/Sub Topics** | Event bus topics for async messaging |
    88→| **API Schemas** | OpenAPI specs for all platform APIs |
    89→| **Documentation** | Tech docs aggregated from all services |
    90→
    91→Access Backstage at: `https://backstage.kix.konecta.com` (internal only)
    92→
    93→### What Developers CAN Access
    94→
    95→- Kubernetes namespace (isolated)
    96→- Database connection (their database only)
    97→- Cache client (their key prefix only)
    98→- Storage bucket (their bucket only)
    99→- Pub/Sub topic (their topic only)
   100→
   101→### What Developers CANNOT Access
   102→
   103→- GCP console directly
   104→- Other use case resources
   105→- Organization-level settings
   106→- Service account keys
   107→
   108→---
   109→
   110→## What Developers Build
   111→
   112→| Component | Responsibility |
   113→|-----------|----------------|
   114→| **Agent Logic** | Business logic using CrewAI framework |
   115→| **API Endpoints** | Request handlers behind Kong routes |
   116→| **Data Schema** | Database tables and vector collections |
   117→| **Prompts** | LLM prompts and configurations |
   118→| **Workflows** | Multi-step orchestration (if needed) |
   119→
   120→### Development Flow
   121→
   122→1. Define capability schema (inputs, outputs, SLA)
   123→2. Register capability in Schema Registry
   124→3. Implement agent or service
   125→4. Configure API routes
   126→5. Deploy to development environment via ArgoCD GitOps
   127→6. Test via API and MCP
   128→7. Promote through QA to production (ArgoCD syncs from Git)
   129→
   130→### GitOps Deployment via ArgoCD
   131→
   132→All deployments follow a GitOps workflow managed by ArgoCD running on the shared platform cluster:
   133→
   134→| Step | Action | Tool |
   135→|------|--------|------|
   136→| 1 | Push code to Bitbucket | Git |
   137→| 2 | CI pipeline builds container image | Bitbucket Pipelines |
   138→| 3 | Image pushed to Artifact Registry (`kd-ix-eur-shr-artifacts`) | Docker/Buildkit |
   139→| 4 | ArgoCD Image Updater detects new image | Automatic |
   140→| 5 | ArgoCD syncs manifests to target cluster | Automatic |
   141→| 6 | Verify deployment status | ArgoCD UI or CLI |
   142→
   143→**ArgoCD UI:** `https://argocd.ix.konecta-digital.com` (Google OIDC login)
   144→
   145→**Key concepts:**
   146→- **Application**: A single deployable unit tracked by ArgoCD
   147→- **AppProject**: Scopes what an Application can access (namespaces, clusters, repos)
   148→- **ApplicationSet**: Templated generation of Applications across environments
   149→- **Sync**: ArgoCD applies Git state to the cluster (auto or manual)
   150→
   151→---
   152→
   153→## BAOE Readiness Framework
   154→
   155→A use case is **AVAILABLE** when it meets all four readiness dimensions:
   156→
   157→| Dimension | Code | Description |
   158→|-----------|------|-------------|
   159→| **Built** | B | Autopilot flow completed in ElevenLabs/CrewAI |
   160→| **API-fied** | A | Standard Agent API contracts, lifecycle APIs |
   161→| **Observable** | O | Telemetry, decision logging, audit trails |
   162→| **Platform-Enabled** | E | Configuration-driven deployment, tenant isolation |
   163→
   164→**Progression Example:**
   165→```
   166→Month 1: B . A . O      -> Flow built, APIs ready, observable
   167→Month 2: B . A . O . E  -> Fully platform-enabled
   168→Month 3: AVAILABLE      -> Production-ready
   169→```
   170→
   171→---
   172→
   173→## Autonomy Tiers
   174→
   175→Each use case operates at a specific autonomy tier that governs agent independence:
   176→
   177→| Tier | Description | Human Involvement | Example |
   178→|------|-------------|-------------------|---------|
   179→| **Supervised** | Human monitors all actions | High — approval required | FAQ, Password Reset |
   180→| **Conditional** | Autonomous within bounds, escalates on triggers | Medium — exception handling | Scheduling, Collections |
   181→| **Assistive** | AI assists human decision-making | Medium — human leads | Copilot Sales |
   182→| **Full** | Fully autonomous, rare and restricted | Low — audit only | Simple bookings |
   183→
   184→### Escalation Triggers
   185→
   186→| Trigger | Action | Target |
   187→|---------|--------|--------|
   188→| Customer says "supervisor" | Immediate transfer | Human Expert |
   189→| Sentiment drops below threshold | Flag + optional transfer | Copilot Assisted |
   190→| Compliance violation detected | Immediate transfer | Human Expert |
   191→| Agent confidence below 70% | Request human review | Copilot Assisted |
   192→| 3+ failed resolution attempts | Escalate | Human Expert |
   193→
   194→---
   195→
   196→## Technology Specifications
   197→
   198→### CrewAI
   199→
   200→**Purpose:** Multi-agent orchestration for autonomous task execution
   201→
   202→**What It Does:**
   203→- Defines agents with roles, goals, and tools
   204→- Orchestrates tasks across multiple agents
   205→- Manages agent collaboration and handoffs
   206→- Integrates with LLM gateway for model access
   207→
   208→**Constraints:**
   209→- All LLM calls must use platform gateway (no direct API calls)
   210→- Maximum execution time configurable per agent
   211→- Agent state must be externalized for fault tolerance
   212→
   213→**Example Crew Structure:**
   214→```
   215→End-User Self-Healing Crew
   216→+-- Triage Agent
   217→|   +-- Classifies issue type, urgency, complexity
   218→+-- Diagnostic Agent
   219→|   +-- Runs diagnostic checks via Nexthink MCP
   220→+-- Resolution Agent
   221→|   +-- Executes fixes via ServiceNow/AD MCP
   222→+-- Communication Agent
   223→|   +-- Updates user on progress
   224→+-- Escalation Agent
   225→    +-- Hands off to human with full context
   226→```
   227→
   228→### ElevenLabs
   229→
   230→**Purpose:** Voice synthesis and conversational AI (primary voice runtime)
   231→
   232→**What It Does:**
   233→- Text-to-speech synthesis
   234→- Real-time conversational AI
   235→- Speech-to-Text
   236→- Multi-language support
   237→
   238→**Constraints:**
   239→- Voice calls must use platform client via Kong
   240→- Latency budget: 500ms for text-to-speech
   241→- Supported languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese (MVP)
   242→
   243→**Voice Latency Budget:**
   244→
   245→| Stage | Target | Max |
   246→|-------|--------|-----|
   247→| Speech-to-Text | 150ms | 300ms |
   248→| Agent Processing | 300ms | 500ms |
   249→| Text-to-Speech | 150ms | 300ms |
   250→| **Total Round-Trip** | **600ms** | **1100ms** |
   251→
   252→### LiteLLM
   253→
   254→**Purpose:** Unified LLM access and MCP tool gateway
   255→
   256→**What It Does (LLM Gateway):**
   257→- Abstracts multiple LLM providers behind single interface
   258→- Handles model fallback and retry logic
   259→- Manages API keys centrally
   260→- Tracks token usage per use case
   261→- Provides response caching
   262→
   263→**What It Does (MCP Gateway):**
   264→- Exposes platform capabilities as MCP tools
   265→- Enables AI agents to discover available tools
   266→- Routes tool calls to appropriate services
   267→
   268→**Available Models:**
   269→
   270→| Model | Provider | Recommended Use |
   271→|-------|----------|-----------------|
   272→| Gemini 2.5 Flash | Google | Default — fast, cost-effective |
   273→| Gemini 2.5 Pro | Google | Complex reasoning tasks |
   274→| Claude 3 Sonnet | Anthropic | Fallback |
   275→| GPT-4 Turbo | OpenAI | Fallback |
   276→
   277→**Constraints:**
   278→- No direct calls to model provider APIs
   279→- Token budgets monitored per use case
   280→- Caching enabled by default
   281→- Prompt logging with PII redaction
   282→
   283→### Kong API Gateway
   284→
   285→**Purpose:** API gateway for service exposure and third-party API abstraction
   286→
   287→**Available Capabilities:**
   288→- JWT validation (external identity integration)
   289→- API key authentication
   290→- Rate limiting (per key, per route)
   291→- Request/response transformation
   292→- Third-party API proxying
   293→
   294→**Constraints:**
   295→- All external traffic must pass through Kong
   296→- No direct pod access from outside cluster
   297→- Rate limits enforced per API key
   298→
   299→### Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL)
   300→
   301→**Purpose:** Relational data storage
   302→
   303→**Specifications:**
   304→- PostgreSQL version 15
   305→- Instance: 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM (adjustable)
   306→- Storage: SSD with auto-grow
   307→- Backups: Daily, 7-day retention
   308→- HA: Regional (Prod), Zonal (Dev/QA)
   309→
   310→**Constraints:**
   311→- No DDL changes in application code (use migrations)
   312→- Connection pooling required
   313→- Private IP access only
   314→
   315→### Redis (Memorystore)
   316→
   317→**Purpose:** Caching and session state
   318→
   319→**Specifications:**
   320→- Redis version 7.0
   321→- Tier: Standard (HA)
   322→- Memory: 5GB shared (expandable)
   323→- Persistence: RDB snapshots
   324→
   325→**Constraints:**
   326→- Keys must be prefixed with use case name
   327→- TTL required on all keys (24h max default)
   328→- No KEYS command (use SCAN)
   329→- No Lua scripts without approval
   330→
   331→### Qdrant
   332→
   333→**Purpose:** Vector storage for RAG and semantic search
   334→
   335→**Specifications:**
   336→- Replicas: 3 (Prod), 1 (Dev/QA)
   337→- Storage: Persistent SSD
   338→- Max vectors: 10M per collection
   339→
   340→**Constraints:**
   341→- Collection names prefixed with use case
   342→- Must use platform embedding model for consistency
   343→- Backup responsibility with platform team
   344→
   345→### Pub/Sub
   346→
   347→**Purpose:** Asynchronous messaging and event-driven architecture
   348→
   349→**Specifications:**
   350→- Message retention: 7 days
   351→- Ack deadline: 60 seconds
   352→- Max message size: 10MB
   353→- Ordering: Optional per topic
   354→
   355→**Constraints:**
   356→- Topic/subscription names prefixed with use case
   357→- Dead letter queue required for production
   358→- Idempotent message handling required
   359→
   360→### GCS (Cloud Storage)
   361→
   362→**Purpose:** Object storage for documents and artifacts
   363→
   364→**Specifications:**
   365→- Storage class: Standard
   366→- Location: EU (multi-region)
   367→- Lifecycle: 90d -> Nearline -> 365d -> Archive
   368→- Versioning: Enabled
   369→
   370→**Constraints:**
   371→- No public access
   372→- Signed URLs for temporary external access
   373→- Max object size: 5TB
   374→
   375→### Channel Hub
   376→
   377→**Purpose:** Outbound messaging across multiple channels
   378→
   379→**Supported Channels:**
   380→
   381→| Channel | Requirements |
   382→|---------|--------------|
   383→| SMS | Approved sender ID |
   384→| Email | Verified sending domain |
   385→| WhatsApp | Pre-approved message templates |
   386→| Google Chat | Internal use only |
   387→
   388→**Constraints:**
   389→- All messages logged for audit
   390→- Rate limits per channel
   391→- PII handling rules apply
   392→- Templates required for WhatsApp
   393→
   394→---
   395→
   396→## Service Patterns
   397→
   398→### Exposing a Capability
   399→
   400→**Step 1: Define Schema**
   401→
   402→Create a JSON Schema defining inputs, outputs, and metadata including:
   403→- Input parameters with types and validation
   404→- Output structure
   405→- SLA requirements (latency, availability)
   406→- Routing rules (which engine handles requests)
   407→
   408→**Step 2: Register in Schema Registry**
   409→
   410→Register the capability with:
   411→- Name and version
   412→- Owner team
   413→- Description
   414→- Input/output schemas
   415→- SLA targets
   416→- Default routing configuration
   417→
   418→**Step 3: Implement Service**
   419→
   420→Build the service that handles requests:
   421→- Implement business logic
   422→- Use platform clients for dependencies
   423→- Follow error handling patterns
   424→- Add observability instrumentation
   425→
   426→**Step 4: Build Agents**
   427→
   428→Build any agents required in CrewAI:
   429→- Create your agents and publish them
   430→- Define agent roles, goals, and available tools
   431→- Configure agent collaboration patterns
   432→
   433→**Step 5: Configure Routing**
   434→
   435→Define Kong routes:
   436→- API path
   437→- Authentication requirements
   438→- Rate limits
   439→- Any request/response transformations
   440→
   441→**Step 6: Register MCP Tool (Optional)**
   442→
   443→If the capability should be available to AI agents:
   444→- Register tool in MCP Gateway
   445→- Define tool description for discovery
   446→- Map to underlying service
   447→
   448→### Consuming a Capability
   449→
   450→**Via REST API:**
   451→- Obtain API key or JWT token
   452→- Call Kong endpoint with authentication header
   453→- Handle standard error responses
   454→- Use trace ID for debugging
   455→
   456→**Via MCP (AI Agents):**
   457→- Query MCP Gateway for available tools
   458→- Call tool with required parameters
   459→- Receive structured response
   460→- Handle errors gracefully
   461→
   462→**Via Internal Service:**
   463→- Use platform-provided client library
   464→- Authentication handled automatically
   465→- Retry and circuit breaker included
   466→
   467→### Error Handling
   468→
   469→All services must return errors in standard format:
   470→
   471→| Field | Description |
   472→|-------|-------------|
   473→| code | Machine-readable error code |
   474→| message | Human-readable description |
   475→| details | Additional context (optional) |
   476→| trace_id | Correlation ID for debugging |
   477→
   478→**Standard Error Codes:**
   479→
   480→| Code | HTTP Status | Meaning |
   481→|------|-------------|---------|
   482→| VALIDATION_ERROR | 400 | Invalid input |
   483→| UNAUTHORIZED | 401 | Missing or invalid authentication |
   484→| FORBIDDEN | 403 | Insufficient permissions |
   485→| NOT_FOUND | 404 | Resource not found |
   486→| CONFLICT | 409 | Business rule violation |
   487→| RATE_LIMITED | 429 | Too many requests |
   488→| INTERNAL_ERROR | 500 | Unexpected failure |
   489→
   490→### Async Patterns
   491→
   492→**Callback Pattern:**
   493→- Submit request with callback URL
   494→- Receive request ID immediately
   495→- Platform calls callback when complete
   496→
   497→**Event-Driven Pattern:**
   498→- Publish event to Pub/Sub topic
   499→- Subscribers react to events
   500→- Decoupled processing
   501→

   599→## Governance Requirements
   600→
   601→### Security Requirements
   602→
   603→| Requirement | Implementation |
   604→|-------------|----------------|
   605→| Authentication | All endpoints require JWT or API key |
   606→| Authorization | Scope-based access control |
   607→| Encryption in transit | TLS 1.3 on all connections |
   608→| Encryption at rest | Google-managed keys (CMEK for sensitive) |
   609→| Network isolation | Private IPs only, no public endpoints |
   610→| Secrets | Secret Manager, no hardcoded credentials |
   611→| Audit logging | All access logged, 7-year retention |
   612→
   613→### Compliance Requirements
   614→
   615→| Regulation | Requirement | Implementation |
   616→|------------|-------------|----------------|
   617→| GDPR | Data subject rights | Deletion and export APIs |
   618→| GDPR | Consent management | Consent service integration |
   619→| GDPR | Data residency | EU regions only |
   620→| EU AI Act | Transparency | Decision logging |
   621→| EU AI Act | Human oversight | Escalation capability |
   622→
   623→### Data Classification
   624→
   625→| Level | Examples | Requirements |
   626→|-------|----------|--------------|
   627→| Public | Marketing content | None |
   628→| Internal | Business metrics | Encryption, access control |
   629→| Confidential | Customer PII | Encryption, audit logging, need-to-know |
   630→| Restricted | Payment data | CMEK, VPC-SC, approval workflow |
   631→
   632→### Audit Requirements
   633→
   634→All of the following are logged with 7-year retention:
   635→- Authentication events
   636→- API calls
   637→- Data access
   638→- Configuration changes
   639→- LLM prompts and responses (PII redacted)

   643→## Glossary
   644→
   645→| Term | Definition |
   646→|------|------------|
   647→| **Capability** | A service exposed through the platform |
   648→| **Schema** | Metadata definition of a capability's interface |
   649→| **Northbound** | Interfaces for consumers (API, MCP, UI) |
   650→| **Southbound** | Infrastructure hidden from consumers |
   651→| **Control Plane** | Routing layer deciding human/copilot/agent |
   652→| **MCP** | Model Context Protocol — standard for AI tool integration |
   653→| **Backstage** | Internal service catalogue for service discovery |
   654→| **Use Case** | A specific business application built on KIX |
   655→| **BAOE** | Built, API-fied, Observable, Platform-Enabled readiness |

     1→# KIX Platform Strategy

     8→
     9→## Executive Summary
    10→
    11→This document defines the strategic vision, architecture, and operating model for the **KIX Platform** (Konecta Intelligence eXchange) — the orchestration platform that enables Konecta to deliver **Orchestrated Outcomes, not just operations**.
    12→
    13→**Platform Mission:** Provide a production-ready, enterprise-grade platform that abstracts infrastructure complexity and enables use case teams to focus on delivering business value through AI agents.
    14→
    15→**End-State Vision:**
    16→> "The right work, done by the right resource, at the right moment."
    17→
    18→**Key Principles:**
    19→- **Core Services:** Use case developers consume standardised services
    20→- **Security-First:** Zero-trust architecture with comprehensive audit trails
    21→- **Scalable:** Multi-tenant isolation supporting multiple use cases
    22→- **Compliant:** GDPR, EU AI Act, and enterprise security standards
    23→- **Observable:** Full visibility into application and infrastructure health
    24→

    41→## Strategic Alignment
    42→
    43→### CIO Vision: Orchestrated Outcomes
    44→
    45→| Element | Vision | KIX Implementation |
    46→|---------|--------|-------------------|
    47→| **The Challenge** | Cost reduction alone is insufficient | Outcome-based pricing models |
    48→| **The Strategy** | Move beyond static execution | Dynamic orchestration engine |
    49→| **The Solution** | Konecta Control Plane | KIX Platform with three execution engines |
    50→| **The Result** | Continuous optimisation | Real-time routing, learning, and improvement |
    51→
    52→### Critical Understanding
    53→
    54→**KIX = Control Plane + Core Components**
    55→
    56→KIX is not separate from the Control Plane — KIX IS the Control Plane plus the foundational infrastructure that powers it. The Control Plane is foundational from MVP1; what evolves is its sophistication.
    57→
    58→| Part | What It Does | Always Present |
    59→|------|--------------|----------------|
    60→| **Control Plane** | Orchestrates work across Human Experts, AI Copilots, and Autonomous Agents | Foundational |
    61→| **Core Components** | 5 layers (ENGAGE, KNOW, GOVERN, CONNECT, ACT) providing platform services | Foundational |

    65→## Control Plane Architecture
    66→
    67→The heart of the Control Plane is the **Orchestration Engine** — the decision-making system that routes each interaction to the optimal resource.

   158→### Classification Factors
   159→
   160→| Factor | Source | Impact on Routing |
   161→|--------|--------|-------------------|
   162→| **Intent** | LLM classification | Determines workflow path |
   163→| **Complexity** | Rule engine + ML | Simple → Agent, Complex → Human |
   164→| **Sentiment** | Real-time analysis | Negative → Escalation trigger |
   165→| **Customer Value** | CRM integration | Premium → Priority routing |
   166→| **Regulatory Risk** | Compliance rules | High risk → Human required |
   167→| **Historical Success** | Outcome data | Informs confidence scoring |

   170→
   171→## The Three Execution Engines
   172→
   173→The Control Plane orchestrates three distinct execution engines:
   174→
   175→| Engine | Role | When Used | KIX Component |
   176→|--------|------|-----------|---------------|
   177→| **Human Experts** | Empathy, critical thinking, exception handling | Sensitive, complex, high-value interactions | HITL Coordination Layer |
   178→| **AI Copilots** | Augmentation, consistency, real-time guidance | Tech-enabled human delivery | Agent Assist Platform |
   179→| **Autonomous Agents** | Event-driven, end-to-end execution | Routine tasks, instant resolution | CrewAI + ElevenLabs Runtime |
   180→
   181→### Engine 1: Human Experts
   182→
   183→**Purpose:** Handle exceptions AI cannot resolve, manage sensitive relationships, apply critical thinking.
   184→
   185→| Capability | Description | Technology |
   186→|------------|-------------|------------|
   187→| **Intelligent Queue** | AI-prioritised work distribution | Orchestration Engine + WFM |
   188→| **Full Context** | Complete interaction history on handoff | Unified Profile + Session Memory |
   189→| **Real-time Coaching** | AI suggestions during live interactions | Copilot Whisper Mode |
   190→| **Post-call Summary** | Automated wrap-up and documentation | LLM-powered ACW |
   191→| **Quality Assurance** | Automated QA scoring with human review | AI QA + Human Override |
   192→
   193→**Shift in Role:**
   194→- **From:** Performing repetitive transactional tasks
   195→- **To:** Solving novel problems and building relationships
   196→
   197→### Engine 2: AI Copilots
   198→
   199→**Purpose:** Augment human agents with real-time intelligence, ensuring consistency and compliance.
   200→
   201→| Capability | Description | Technology |
   202→|------------|-------------|------------|

   297→## Platform Services Catalog
   298→
   299→### Service Summary
   300→
   301→| Service Category | Key Technologies | Benefit |
   302→|-----------------|------------------|---------|
   303→| Identity & Access | Workload Identity, RBAC | Single Identity Platform consumable via API |
   304→| Secrets Management | Secret Manager, CSI Driver | Secure, compliant secret and key management |
   305→| Container Registry | Artifact Registry, Scanning | Secured, scanned and centralised |
   306→| LLM Router + MCP Gateway | LiteLLM (Kubernetes) | Unified access layer for LLM providers AND MCP tools |
   307→| External API Gateway | Kong (External APIs only) | Abstraction layer for third-party services |
   308→| Databases | Cloud SQL PostgreSQL | Provisioned per use case with standardised security |
   309→| Caching | Cloud Memorystore Redis | Provisioned per use case (also used for LLM caching) |
   310→| Object Storage | GCS with lifecycle | Provisioned per use case with standardised security |
   311→| Event Bus | Cloud Pub/Sub | Self-service publish/subscribe event bus |
   312→| AI Framework | CrewAI (Kubernetes) | Agent orchestration deployed per use case namespace |
   313→| Voice Services | ElevenLabs (via Kong) | External voice services through Kong gateway |
   314→| Messaging | Channel Hub (via Kong) | Outbound messaging (SMS, Email, WhatsApp, Google Chat) |
   315→| Observability | Cloud Monitoring, Logging, Trace | Automatic + custom metrics |
   316→| Service Catalogue | Backstage | Internal portal for service discovery and documentation |
   317→| GitOps / CD | ArgoCD (Kubernetes) | Multi-cluster continuous delivery via Git, App-of-Apps pattern |
   318→| CI/CD | GitHub Actions | Standardised DevSecOps approach |
   319→
   320→### Key Highlights for Use Case Developers
   321→
   322→1. **No Infrastructure Management:** Platform handles all GCP resources, networking, security
   323→2. **Workload Identity:** Never manage service account keys — automatic authentication
   324→3. **LiteLLM for LLM + MCP Access:** Use OpenAI-compatible API to access any LLM provider AND MCP tools
   325→4. **Kong for External APIs:** Access third-party services through Kong — credentials managed by platform
   326→5. **CrewAI in Your Namespace:** AI agents deployed alongside your application for low-latency orchestration
   327→6. **Multi-Tenant Isolation:** Your namespace is isolated with resource quotas and network policies
   328→7. **Comprehensive Observability:** Metrics, logs, and traces automatically collected
   329→8. **GitOps Deployment:** ArgoCD watches Git for changes and automatically syncs to clusters
   330→9. **Backstage Service Catalogue:** Discover available services, APIs, agents, and documentation
   331→
   332→### Traffic Flow Summary
   333→
   334→| Communication | Path | Protocol |
   335→|---------------|------|----------|
   336→| App → LLM | `Use Case App → LiteLLM → Cloud NAT → LLM Provider` | HTTP (internal) → HTTPS |
   337→| App → MCP Tools | `Use Case App → LiteLLM → MCP Services` | HTTP (internal) |
   338→| App → External API | `Use Case App → Kong → Cloud NAT → External Service` | HTTP (internal) → HTTPS |
   339→| App → Database | `Use Case App → Cloud SQL (Private IP)` | PostgreSQL over TLS |
   340→| App → Cache | `Use Case App → Memorystore Redis (Private IP)` | Redis protocol |

   344→## GCP Operating Model
   345→
   346→### Organization Structure
   347→
   348→```
   349→[Organization: konecta-group.com]
   350→├── [Root Folder: Digital] ← DELEGATED TO OUR TEAM
   351→│   ├── [Folder: Shared Services]
   352→│   │   ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-shared-network]
   353→│   │   ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-shared-security]
   354→│   │   └── [Project: kd-ix-eur-shared-artifacts]
   355→│   ├── [Folder: Lab] - isolated playground for new tech/services
   356→│   │   └── [Project: kd-ix-eur-lab-*]
   357→│   ├── [Folder: NonProd] - non production environments
   358→│   │   ├── [Folder: Dev]
   359→│   │   │   ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-dev-gke]
   360→│   │   │   ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-dev-data]
   361→│   │   │   └── [Project: kd-ix-eur-dev-security]
   362→│   │   └── [Folder: QA]
   363→│   │       ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-qa-gke]
   364→│   │       ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-qa-data]
   365→│   │       └── [Project: kd-ix-eur-qa-security]
   366→│   └── [Folder: Prod] - production environments
   367→│       ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-prod-gke]
   368→│       ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-prod-data]
   369→│       └── [Project: kd-ix-eur-prod-security]
   370→```
   371→
   372→### Delegation Model
   373→
   374→**What We Have Full Access To:**
   375→- Create and delete folders within `Digital` folder
   376→- Create and delete projects within our folder hierarchy
   377→- Create and manage service accounts within our projects
   378→- Create and manage guardrails and policies within our folder/projects
   379→- Configure IAM policies within our folder/projects
   380→- Deploy any GCP service within our projects
   381→- Manage billing and budgets for our folder
   382→- Configure network policies within our VPCs
   383→
   384→**What We Must Follow (Organization Policies):**
   385→- Adhere to root level policies
   386→- No public IP addresses — enforced via `constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess`
   387→- Domain-restricted IAM — members must be from `konecta-group.com`
   388→- No service account key downloads — Workload Identity only
   389→- Audit logging mandatory — Admin Activity & Data Access logs enabled
   390→- Data residency — Resources in EU regions only
   391→
   392→**What We Cannot Do:**
   393→- Modify organization-level policies
   394→- Access folders/projects outside our delegation
   395→- Disable mandatory security controls
   396→- Create resources in unapproved regions
   397→- Share IAM permissions with external domains
   398→
   399→### Naming Conventions
   400→
   401→| Resource Type | Pattern | Example |
   402→|---------------|---------|---------|
   403→| Projects | `kd-ix-{region}-{env}-{function}` | `kd-ix-eur-prod-gke` |
   404→| Resources | `{usecase}-{resource}-{env}` | `autopilot-db-prod` |
   405→| Service Accounts | `{usecase}-{function}@{project}.iam` | `autopilot-app@kd-ix-eur-prod-gke.iam` |
   406→| K8s Namespaces | `{usecase}-{env}` | `autopilot-scheduling-prod` |

    35→
    36→## Security Posture Summary
    37→
    38→### Key Architecture Decisions
    39→
    40→| Decision | Rationale | Risk Mitigation |
    41→|----------|-----------|-----------------|
    42→| **GCP as Cloud Provider** | Enterprise agreement, EU data centres | Multi-cloud exit strategy documented |
    43→| **GKE for Containers** | Managed Kubernetes, Workload Identity | No vendor lock-in at application layer |
    44→| **Workload Identity Only** | Eliminates credential management | Enforced by organisation policy |
    45→| **Private-First Networking** | Zero public IPs on compute | Cloud NAT for controlled egress |
    46→| **EU Data Residency** | GDPR compliance | Enforced via organisation policy |
    47→
    48→### Control Summary
    49→
    50→| Category | Implementation | Compliance |
    51→|----------|----------------|------------|
    52→| Identity | Workload Identity, domain-restricted IAM | SOC 2, ISO 27001 |
    53→| Network | Private GKE, VPC Service Controls (Prod) | CIS Benchmarks |
    54→| Data | Encryption at rest (CMEK), TLS 1.3 in transit | GDPR Article 32 |
    55→| Logging | 7-year immutable audit trail | GDPR, EU AI Act |
    56→| Access | RBAC, least privilege, quarterly reviews | ISO 27001 |
    57→
    58→---
    59→
    60→## Security Architecture
    61→
    62→### Security Principles
    63→
    64→| Principle | Implementation |
    65→|-----------|----------------|
    66→| **Zero Trust** | No implicit trust; every request authenticated and authorised |
    67→| **Defence in Depth** | Multiple security layers: network, identity, application |
    68→| **Least Privilege** | Minimal permissions; regular access reviews |
    69→| **Separation of Duties** | Different teams for dev, deploy, operate |
    70→| **Security by Default** | Secure configurations out of the box |
    71→
    72→### Security Controls Matrix
    73→
    74→| Layer | Control | Implementation | Monitoring |
    75→|-------|---------|----------------|------------|
    76→| **Perimeter** | DDoS Protection | Cloud Armor | Real-time alerts |
    77→| **Perimeter** | WAF | Cloud Armor OWASP rules | Log-based alerts |
    78→| **Network** | Firewall | VPC firewall, deny-all default | Flow logs |
    79→| **Network** | Segmentation | VPC per environment, Network Policies | VPC Flow Logs |
    80→| **Identity** | Authentication | Workload Identity, OAuth 2.0 | Audit logs |
    81→| **Identity** | Authorisation | IAM, RBAC, least privilege | Access logs |
    82→| **Application** | Input Validation | Kong plugins, application-level | Error logs |
    83→| **Application** | Secrets | Secret Manager, CSI driver | Access logs |
    84→| **GitOps** | ArgoCD RBAC | Dex OIDC (Google), AppProject-scoped access | ArgoCD audit logs |
    85→| **GitOps** | ArgoCD WAF | Cloud Armor on ArgoCD Gateway, admin path restriction | Cloud Armor logs |
    86→| **GitOps** | Workload Identity | ArgoCD SA with cross-project container.developer | IAM audit logs |
    87→| **Data** | Encryption at Rest | CMEK (Prod), Google-managed (Non-prod) | KMS audit logs |
    88→| **Data** | Encryption in Transit | TLS 1.3 mandatory | Certificate monitoring |
    89→| **Container** | Image Scanning | Artifact Registry scanning | Vulnerability alerts |
    90→| **Container** | Binary Auth | Attestation required (Prod) | Deployment logs |
    91→
    92→### Security Services
    93→
    94→```
    95→SECRET MANAGER
    96→+-- /dev/use-case-1/          +-- /qa/use-case-1/          +-- /prod/use-case-1/
    97→|   +-- db-pass               |   +-- db-pass              |   +-- db-pass
    98→|   +-- api-key               |   +-- api-key              |   +-- api-key
    99→
   100→Access: Workload Identity only, per-use-case IAM bindings
   101→Rotation: Automatic 90-day rotation for service credentials
   102→
   103→CLOUD KMS
   104→+-- Key Ring: kix-{env}-keyring (europe-west1)
   105→    +-- terraform-state-key (AES-256-GCM)
   106→    +-- database-encryption-key (AES-256-GCM)
   107→    +-- storage-encryption-key (AES-256-GCM)
   108→    +-- secret-encryption-key (AES-256-GCM)
   109→
   110→Rotation: 90-day automatic rotation
   111→Access: Service accounts only, no human access to key material
   112→
   113→CLOUD LOGGING
   114→+-- Admin Activity Logs (all environments)
   115→+-- Data Access Logs (Production only)
   116→+-- VPC Flow Logs (all environments)
   117→+-- Application Logs (all environments)
   118→
   119→Retention: 30 days hot, 7 years archive (GCS)
   120→Immutability: Logs cannot be modified or deleted
   121→```

   125→## Identity & Access Management
   126→
   127→### Identity Architecture
   128→
   129→**Human Identities:**
   130→- Google Cloud Identity (konecta-group.com)
   131→- Access via SSO with corporate IdP
   132→- MFA required for all accounts
   133→
   134→| Group | Roles |
   135→|-------|-------|
   136→| Platform Team | Project Owner, GKE Admin, Network Admin |
   137→| Use Case Developers | GKE Developer, Log Viewer, Monitoring Viewer |
   138→| Security Team | Security Admin, Audit Log Viewer |
   139→
   140→**Workload Identities:**
   141→
   142→```
   143→Kubernetes Service Account          GCP Service Account
   144→(autopilot-scheduling-sa)   --->    (autopilot-app@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com)
   145→                                          |
   146→                                          v
   147→                                    IAM Roles (Least Privilege)
   148→                                    +-- roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor
   149→                                    +-- roles/cloudsql.client
   150→                                    +-- roles/storage.objectUser
   151→                                    +-- roles/pubsub.publisher
   152→                                    +-- roles/logging.logWriter
   153→                                    +-- roles/cloudtrace.agent

   155→
   156→**NO SERVICE ACCOUNT KEYS** — Enforced by Organisation Policy
   157→
   158→### IAM Principles
   159→
   160→| Principle | Implementation |
   161→|-----------|----------------|
   162→| **Least Privilege** | Predefined roles preferred; custom roles quarterly reviewed |
   163→| **Separation of Duties** | Deploy != Approve; Dev != Prod access |
   164→| **Just-in-Time Access** | Elevated access via approval workflow, time-limited |
   165→| **Domain Restriction** | IAM members must be from konecta-group.com |
   166→| **No Shared Accounts** | Individual accounts for all human access |
   167→
   168→### Kubernetes RBAC
   169→
   170→| Role | Permissions | Binding |
   171→|------|-------------|---------|
   172→| `namespace-admin` | Full namespace access | Use case lead |
   173→| `namespace-developer` | Deploy, view logs, exec into pods | Developers |
   174→| `namespace-readonly` | View resources, logs | Support, auditors |

   176→### Break-Glass Access
   177→
   178→| Aspect | Policy |
   179→|--------|--------|
   180→| Purpose | Emergency access when normal channels unavailable |
   181→| Accounts | Dedicated break-glass accounts (2 minimum) |
   182→| Storage | Credentials in secure offline storage |
   183→| Monitoring | Real-time alerts on any break-glass usage |

   188→## Network Security
   189→
   190→### Firewall Rules
   191→
   192→| Rule | Direction | Source | Destination | Ports | Action |
   193→|------|-----------|--------|-------------|-------|--------|
   194→| allow-iap-ssh | Ingress | 35.235.240.0/20 | All instances | 22 | Allow |
   195→| allow-health-checks | Ingress | 130.211.0.0/22, 35.191.0.0/16 | GKE nodes | 80, 443 | Allow |
   196→| allow-internal | Ingress | VPC CIDR | VPC CIDR | All | Allow |
   197→| deny-all-ingress | Ingress | 0.0.0.0/0 | All | All | Deny |
   198→| allow-google-apis | Egress | GKE nodes | 199.36.153.4/30 | 443 | Allow |
   199→| allow-llm-egress | Egress | AI pods | LLM provider IPs | 443 | Allow |
   200→| deny-all-egress | Egress | All | 0.0.0.0/0 | All | Deny |
   201→
   202→### Network Security Controls
   203→
   204→| Control | Implementation |
   205→|---------|----------------|
   206→| **Private GKE** | No public node IPs; control plane access via authorised networks |
   207→| **VPC Service Controls** | Data exfiltration prevention (Production only) |
   208→| **Cloud NAT** | Controlled egress; logging enabled |
   209→| **Private Google Access** | Access GCP APIs without public internet |
   210→| **Network Policies** | Default deny-all; explicit allow rules per namespace |
   211→
   212→### Kubernetes Network Policy Example
   213→
   214→```yaml
   215→# Default deny-all policy (applied to all namespaces)
   216→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   217→kind: NetworkPolicy
   218→metadata:
   219→  name: default-deny-all
   220→spec:
   221→  podSelector: {}
   222→  policyTypes:
   223→  - Ingress
   224→  - Egress
   225→
   226→# Allow ingress from Kong gateway only
   227→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   228→kind: NetworkPolicy
   229→metadata:
   230→  name: allow-kong-ingress
   231→spec:
   232→  podSelector:
   233→    matchLabels:
   234→      app: crewai-agent
   235→  policyTypes:
   236→  - Ingress
   237→  ingress:
   238→  - from:
   239→    - namespaceSelector:
   240→        matchLabels:
   241→          name: kong
   242→    ports:
   243→    - protocol: TCP
   244→      port: 8080
   245→```
