     1→# CI/CD Runbook
     2→
     3→This runbook provides operational guidance for the KIX Platform CI/CD pipelines.
     4→
     5→## Table of Contents
     6→
     7→1. [Pipeline Overview](#pipeline-overview)
     8→2. [Deploying to Environments](#deploying-to-environments)
     9→3. [Change Windows](#change-windows)
    10→4. [Emergency Procedures](#emergency-procedures)
    11→5. [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
    12→6. [Workflow Reference](#workflow-reference)
    13→
    14→---
    15→
    16→## Pipeline Overview
    17→
    18→The KIX Platform uses a **task-based CI/CD architecture** with reusable workflows and manual deployment control.
    19→
    20→### Architecture Diagram
    21→
    22→```
    23→┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    24→│                    REUSABLE WORKFLOWS (Building Blocks)              │
    25→├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    26→│                                                                       │
    27→│  terraform-validate.yml    Format, lint, init, validate, tfsec      │
    28→│  terraform-plan.yml        Generate plan + summary/comment           │
    29→│  terraform-apply.yml       Apply with approval gate                  │
    30→│  terraform-test.yml        Run Terratest (fast or full suite)        │
    31→│  terraform-drift.yml       Detect drift from state                   │
    32→│                                                                       │
    33→└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    34→                                    ▲
    35→                                    │ calls
    36→                                    │
    37→┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    38→│                    ORCHESTRATION WORKFLOWS (Callers)                 │
    39→├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    40→│                                                                       │
    41→│  pull-request.yml          Validates PRs (validate→plan→fast tests)  │
    42→│  main-validation.yml       Proves main is deployable (validate→plan) │
    43→│  deploy.yml                Manual deployment (plan→approve→apply)    │
    44→│  nightly-quality.yml       Scheduled (full tests + drift detection)  │
    45→│                                                                       │
    46→└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    47→```
    48→
    49→### Key Principles
    50→
    51→1. **Manual Deployments** - All applies require explicit workflow_dispatch trigger
    52→2. **Fresh Plans** - Plans are generated immediately before apply (no stale artifacts)
    53→3. **Independent Environments** - Dev, QA, Prod deploy separately
    54→4. **Merge Validates, Doesn't Deploy** - Merging to main proves deployability without applying
    55→5. **Controlled Change Windows** - Production deployments restricted to approved times
    56→
    57→---
    58→
    59→## Deploying to Environments
    60→
    61→### Prerequisites
    62→
    63→- Code merged to `main` branch
    64→- Main validation passed (automatic on merge)
    65→- Change window requirements met (for production)
    66→- Required approvals obtained
    67→
    68→### Deployment Process
    69→
    70→#### 1. Navigate to Deploy Workflow
    71→
    72→1. Go to **Actions** tab in GitHub
    73→2. Select **Deploy Infrastructure** workflow
    74→3. Click **Run workflow** button
    75→
    76→#### 2. Configure Deployment
    77→
    78→Fill in the workflow inputs:
    79→
    80→| Input | Description | Options |
    81→|-------|-------------|---------|
    82→| **environment** | Target environment | dev, qa, prod, shared |
    83→| **scope** | What to deploy | network, security, gke, platform, data, kong, gateway, litellm, argocd, all |
    84→| **dry_run** | Plan only (no apply) | true/false (default: false) |
    85→| **auto_approve** | Skip approval (dev only) | true/false (default: false) |
    86→
    87→**Example configurations:**
    88→
    89→```yaml
    90→# Deploy Kong to dev (auto-approved)
    91→environment: dev
    92→scope: kong
    93→dry_run: false
    94→auto_approve: true
    95→
    96→# Review prod GKE plan (no deployment)
    97→environment: prod
    98→scope: gke
    99→dry_run: true
   100→auto_approve: false
   101→
   102→# Deploy all services to QA (requires approval)
   103→environment: qa
   104→scope: all
   105→dry_run: false
   106→auto_approve: false
   107→```
   108→
   109→#### 3. Review Pre-flight Checks
   110→
   111→The workflow will:
   112→- ✅ Validate environment and scope inputs
   113→- ✅ Check change window (production only)
   114→- ✅ Map scope to Terraform directories
   115→- ✅ Verify auto-approve restrictions (dev only)
   116→
   117→#### 4. Review Plan Output
   118→
   119→The workflow generates a fresh Terraform plan:
   120→- View plan summary in workflow logs
   121→- Check resources to be added/changed/destroyed
   122→- Verify expected changes match intent
   123→
   124→#### 5. Approve Deployment (if required)
   125→
   126→For QA and Prod environments:
   127→1. GitHub will pause workflow for approval
   128→2. Review plan output
   129→3. Approve or reject deployment
   130→4. Timeout: 30 days (configurable)
   131→
   132→For Dev environment with auto_approve=true:
   133→- No approval gate (deployment proceeds automatically)
   134→
   135→#### 6. Monitor Deployment
   136→
   137→Watch the apply job progress:
   138→- Terraform apply runs with `-auto-approve`
   139→- Post-apply validation runs
   140→- Outputs captured for reference
   141→
   142→#### 7. Verify Deployment
   143→
   144→Post-deployment checks:
   145→- Smoke tests run automatically
   146→- Review outputs in workflow summary
   147→- Verify services are healthy
   148→
   149→### Scope Mapping
   150→
   151→| Scope | Directories (Dev/QA/Prod) | Order |
   152→|-------|---------------------------|-------|
   153→| `network` | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/network` | N/A |
   154→| `security` | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/security` | N/A |
   155→| `gke` | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/gke` | N/A |
   156→| `platform` | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/platform` | N/A |
   157→| `data` | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/data` | N/A |
   158→| `kong` | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/kong` | N/A |
   159→| `gateway` | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/gateway` | N/A |
   160→| `litellm` | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/litellm` | N/A |
   161→| `all` | All above in order | Sequential |
   162→
   163→**Shared environment special scopes:**
   164→
   165→| Scope | Directories (Shared) |
   166→|-------|---------------------|
   167→| `network` | `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/network` |
   168→| `security` | `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/security` |
   169→| `gke` | `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/gke` |
   170→| `platform` | `terraform/environments/shared/kubernetes/platform` |
   171→| `argocd` | `terraform/environments/shared/kubernetes/argocd`, `argocd-bootstrap` |
   172→
   173→---
   174→
   175→## Change Windows
   176→
   177→### Development (dev)
   178→
   179→- **When:** Anytime
   180→- **Approval:** Auto-approve allowed
   181→- **Restrictions:** None
   182→- **Purpose:** Rapid iteration and testing
   183→
   184→### Quality Assurance (qa)
   185→
   186→- **When:** Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC, Mon-Fri)
   187→- **Approval:** Manual approval required
   188→- **Restrictions:** Avoid during active testing cycles
   189→- **Purpose:** Controlled validation before production
   190→
   191→### Production (prod)
   192→
   193→- **When:** **Tuesday-Thursday, 20:00-23:00 UTC only**
   194→- **Approval:** Manual approval required + change ticket
   195→- **Restrictions:**
   196→  - Outside change window: Deployment blocked automatically
   197→  - Emergency exception: See [Emergency Procedures](#emergency-procedures)
   198→- **Purpose:** Minimize risk to production services
   199→
   200→### Shared Services (shared)
   201→
   202→- **When:** Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC, Mon-Fri)
   203→- **Approval:** Manual approval required
   204→- **Restrictions:** ArgoCD changes require coordination with all environments
   205→- **Purpose:** Avoid impacting GitOps across all clusters
   206→
   207→---
   208→
   209→## Emergency Procedures
   210→
   211→### Emergency Hotfix (Outside Change Window)
   212→
   213→For critical production issues requiring immediate fix:
   214→
   215→1. **Assess Impact**
   216→   - Is this a P0/P1 incident?
   217→   - Is immediate deployment necessary?
   218→   - Can it wait for next change window?
   219→
   220→2. **Get Approval**
   221→   - Notify on-call SRE/platform lead
   222→   - Document incident ticket (Jira)
   223→   - Get emergency change approval
   224→
   225→3. **Bypass Change Window**
   226→   - Change window check is automated
   227→   - Bypass requires modifying workflow (remove change window validation step)
   228→   - Alternative: Use `dry_run: true` to validate, then manually apply via `gcloud`
   229→
   230→4. **Emergency Deployment**
   231→   ```bash
   232→   # Option 1: Manual Terraform apply (fastest)
   233→   cd terraform/environments/prod/{scope}
   234→   terraform init -backend-config="bucket=kd-tfstate-prod" \
   235→     -backend-config="prefix=terraform/environments/prod/{scope}/terraform.tfstate"
   236→   terraform plan
   237→   terraform apply  # After review
   238→
   239→   # Option 2: Modify workflow (if time permits)
   240→   # Temporarily comment out change window check in deploy.yml
   241→   ```
   242→
   243→5. **Post-Incident**
   244→   - Document emergency deployment
   245→   - Restore workflow protections
   246→   - Post-mortem review
   247→
   248→### Rollback Procedure
   249→
   250→If deployment causes issues:
   251→
   252→1. **Assess Rollback Need**
   253→   - What broke?
   254→   - Can we roll forward (fix issue)?
   255→   - Is rollback safe (no state changes)?
   256→
   257→2. **Determine Rollback Strategy**
   258→
   259→   **Option A: Terraform Rollback (Safe)**
   260→   ```bash
   261→   # Revert Terraform code to previous version
   262→   git checkout <previous-commit>
   263→
   264→   # Run deploy workflow with reverted code
   265→   # This generates fresh plan with reverted config
   266→   ```
   267→
   268→   **Option B: Manual Resource Restore (Risky)**
   269→   ```bash
   270→   # Only for critical resources that can't wait
   271→   # Use Terraform state backup
   272→   gsutil cp gs://kd-tfstate-prod/terraform/environments/prod/{scope}/terraform.tfstate.backup ./
   273→   terraform state push terraform.tfstate.backup
   274→   ```
   275→
   276→3. **Validate Rollback**
   277→   - Run smoke tests
   278→   - Verify services are healthy
   279→   - Monitor metrics/logs
   280→
   281→4. **Post-Rollback**
   282→   - Root cause analysis
   283→   - Update tests to catch issue
   284→   - Plan proper fix
   285→
   286→### State Recovery
   287→
   288→If Terraform state is corrupted or lost:
   289→
   290→1. **Check State Backup**
   291→   ```bash
   292→   # List backups
   293→   gsutil ls gs://kd-tfstate-prod/terraform/environments/prod/{scope}/
   294→
   295→   # Download backup
   296→   gsutil cp gs://kd-tfstate-prod/terraform/environments/prod/{scope}/terraform.tfstate.backup ./
   297→
   298→   # Restore
   299→   terraform state push terraform.tfstate.backup
   300→   ```
   301→
   302→2. **Import Existing Resources**
   303→   ```bash
   304→   # If no backup, import resources manually
   305→   terraform import google_compute_network.vpc projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}
   306→   ```
   307→
   308→3. **Validate State**
   309→   ```bash
   310→   terraform plan  # Should show no changes if state is correct
   311→   ```
   312→
   313→---
   314→
   315→## Troubleshooting
   316→
   317→### Common Issues
   318→
   319→#### Issue: PR Validation Takes Too Long
   320→
   321→**Symptoms:** PR validation workflow runs for >15 minutes
   322→
   323→**Causes:**
   324→- Fast test suite running full tests
   325→- Too many directories changed
   326→- GCP authentication issues
   327→
   328→**Solutions:**
   329→```bash
   330→# Check test suite configuration
   331→cat .github/workflows/reusable/terraform-test.yml | grep -A 5 "test_suite"
   332→
   333→# Verify fast tests are defined
   334→cd terraform/test
   335→grep -r "TestBasic"
   336→
   337→# Reduce parallel changes (split PR)
   338→git diff origin/main --name-only | grep "\.tf$" | wc -l
   339→```
   340→
   341→#### Issue: Plan Shows Unexpected Changes
   342→
   343→**Symptoms:** Terraform plan shows drift or unexpected resource changes
   344→
   345→**Causes:**
   346→- Manual changes in GCP console
   347→- Provider version change
   348→- Resource import/recreation
   349→
   350→**Solutions:**
   351→```bash
   352→# Check for drift
   353→terraform plan -detailed-exitcode
   354→
   355→# Review state
   356→terraform state list
   357→terraform state show <resource>
   358→
   359→# Compare with GCP
   360→gcloud compute networks describe <network> --project=<project>
   361→```
   362→
   363→#### Issue: Apply Fails with "Resource Already Exists"
   364→
   365→**Symptoms:** Apply fails because resource already exists
   366→
   367→**Causes:**
   368→- Resource created manually
   369→- State out of sync
   370→- Concurrent applies
   371→
   372→**Solutions:**
   373→```bash
   374→# Import existing resource
   375→terraform import <resource_type>.<name> <resource_id>
   376→
   377→# Example: Import GKE cluster
   378→terraform import google_container_cluster.cluster projects/<project>/locations/<region>/clusters/<name>
   379→
   380→# Verify import
   381→terraform plan  # Should show no changes
   382→```
   383→
   384→#### Issue: Workflow Stuck on Approval
   385→
   386→**Symptoms:** Deploy workflow waiting for approval indefinitely
   387→
   388→**Causes:**
   389→- No GitHub environment configured
   390→- Insufficient permissions
   391→- Approvers not notified
   392→
   393→**Solutions:**
   394→1. Check GitHub environment settings (Settings → Environments)
   395→2. Verify approvers are configured
   396→3. Check if approval notification was sent
   397→4. Manually approve in Actions tab → Review deployments
   398→
   399→#### Issue: Nightly Quality Checks Failing
   400→
   401→**Symptoms:** Nightly workflow reports failures
   402→
   403→**Causes:**
   404→- Terratest resources not cleaned up
   405→- Drift in production
   406→- Lab project quota exceeded
   407→
   408→**Solutions:**
   409→```bash
   410→# Check for orphaned resources
   411→gcloud compute instances list --project=kd-ix-eur-lab-platform | grep terratest
   412→
   413→# Clean up manually
   414→gcloud compute instances delete <instance> --project=kd-ix-eur-lab-platform
   415→
   416→# Check quotas
   417→gcloud compute project-info describe --project=kd-ix-eur-lab-platform | grep -A 20 quotas
   418→```
   419→
   420→### Debugging Workflows
   421→
   422→#### View Workflow Logs
   423→
   424→1. Go to **Actions** tab
   425→2. Click on workflow run
   426→3. Expand job steps
   427→4. Review logs for errors
   428→
   429→#### Download Artifacts
   430→
   431→```bash
   432→# Using GitHub CLI
   433→gh run download <run-id> --name terraform-apply-prod-<run-id>
   434→
   435→# View plan output
   436→cat apply_output.txt
   437→
   438→# View outputs
   439→cat outputs.json | jq
   440→```
   441→
   442→#### Re-run Failed Workflow
   443→
   444→1. Click on failed workflow run
   445→2. Click **Re-run jobs** → **Re-run failed jobs**
   446→3. Or **Re-run all jobs** for clean slate

   450→## Workflow Reference
   451→
   452→### pull-request.yml
   453→
   454→**Trigger:** Pull request to main/develop
   455→
   456→**Purpose:** Fast validation (<15 minutes)
   457→
   458→**Jobs:**
   459→1. Detect changed directories
   460→2. Validate Terraform (parallel)
   461→3. Generate plans (parallel)
   462→4. Run fast tests (if modules changed)
   463→
   464→**Outputs:**
   465→- PR comments with plan summaries
   466→- Validation status
   467→- Test results
   468→
   469→**Usage:** Automatic (triggered by PR)
   470→
   471→---
   472→
   473→### main-validation.yml
   474→
   475→**Trigger:** Push to main branch
   476→
   477→**Purpose:** Prove main is deployable (doesn't deploy)
   478→
   479→**Jobs:**
   480→1. Detect changed directories
   481→2. Validate all changes
   482→3. Generate plans for all
   483→4. Tag release with semantic version
   484→
   485→**Outputs:**
   486→- GitHub release with version tag
   487→- Deployment readiness status
   488→- No actual deployment
   489→
   490→**Usage:** Automatic (triggered by merge)
   491→
   492→---
   493→
   494→### deploy.yml
   495→
   496→**Trigger:** Manual (workflow_dispatch)
   497→
   498→**Purpose:** Deploy infrastructure to environment
   499→
   500→**Inputs:**
   501→- `environment`: dev, qa, prod, shared
   502→- `scope`: network, security, gke, platform, data, kong, gateway, litellm, argocd, all
   503→- `dry_run`: true/false
   504→- `auto_approve`: true/false (dev only)
   505→
   506→**Jobs:**
   507→1. Pre-flight checks (change window, permissions)
   508→2. Validate
   509→3. Plan (fresh)
   510→4. Approval gate (if required)
   511→5. Apply
   512→6. Post-deployment verification
   513→
   514→**Outputs:**
   515→- Deployment status

   517→- Verification results
   518→
   519→**Usage:**
   520→```bash

   523→
   524→# Via GitHub CLI

   527→  -f scope=gke \
   528→  -f dry_run=false \
   529→  -f auto_approve=false
   530→```
   531→
   532→---
   533→
   534→### nightly-quality.yml
   535→
   536→**Trigger:** Schedule (daily at 02:00 UTC) + manual
   537→
   538→**Purpose:** Comprehensive testing and drift detection
   539→
   540→**Inputs (manual trigger only):**
   541→- `skip_tests`: Skip full test suite
   542→- `skip_drift`: Skip drift detection
   543→
   544→**Jobs:**
   545→1. Full Terratest suite (90 minutes)
   546→2. Drift detection (all environments, all scopes)
   547→3. Daily quality report
   548→
   549→**Outputs:**
   550→- Test results summary

   552→- GitHub issues for drift (if detected)
   553→
   554→**Usage:**
   555→```bash
   556→# Automatic: Runs daily at 02:00 UTC
   557→
   558→# Manual trigger (with options)

   561→  -f skip_drift=false

     1→# DNS Migration Guide: AWS Route 53 → Google Cloud DNS
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This document guides the migration of the `konecta-digital.com` domain from AWS Route 53 to Google Cloud DNS using a delegated subdomain architecture. The migration is designed for zero downtime with a phased deployment strategy.
     6→
     7→## Architecture
     8→
     9→### DNS Hierarchy
    10→
    11→```
    12→AWS Route 53 (Domain Registrar Level)
    13→└── konecta-digital.com
    14→    └── NS: konecta-digital.com → [GCP Shared DNS nameservers]
    15→
    16→Google Cloud DNS (kd-ix-eur-shr-dns project)
    17→├── konecta-digital.com (root zone)
    18→│   ├── NS: crewai.konecta-digital.com → [CrewAI project nameservers]
    19→│   ├── NS: iq.konecta-digital.com → [IQ project nameservers]
    20→│   ├── NS: jobportal.konecta-digital.com → [JobPortal project nameservers]
    21→│   └── NS: ix.konecta-digital.com → [GCP Shared DNS nameservers]
    22→│
    23→└── ix.konecta-digital.com (IX parent zone)
    24→    ├── NS: dev.ix.konecta-digital.com → [Dev network project nameservers]
    25→    ├── NS: qa.ix.konecta-digital.com → [QA network project nameservers]
    26→    └── NS: prod.ix.konecta-digital.com → [Prod network project nameservers]
    27→
    28→Environment Network Projects
    29→├── kd-ix-eur-dev-network
    30→│   └── dev.ix.konecta-digital.com (public zone)
    31→│       └── A: api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com → [Load Balancer IP]
    32→│
    33→├── kd-ix-eur-np-network
    34→│   └── qa.ix.konecta-digital.com (public zone)
    35→│       └── A: api.qa.ix.konecta-digital.com → [Load Balancer IP]
    36→│
    37→└── kd-ix-eur-prod-network
    38→    └── prod.ix.konecta-digital.com (public zone)
    39→        └── A: api.prod.ix.konecta-digital.com → [Load Balancer IP]
    40→```
    41→
    42→### Design Principles
    43→
    44→1. **Separation of Concerns**: Shared services manage parent zones, environments manage their own zones
    45→2. **Blast Radius Reduction**: Environment teams can modify DNS without affecting other environments
    46→3. **GDPR Compliance**: All DNS data resides in EU region (europe-west1)
    47→4. **Security**: DNSSEC enabled on all zones with NSEC3 non-existence proof
    48→5. **Observability**: Query logging enabled for audit trail and monitoring
    49→
    50→## Infrastructure Components
    51→
    52→### Terraform Module: `public-dns`
    53→
    54→**Location**: `terraform/modules/gcp/public-dns/`
    55→
    56→Wrapper module around `terraform-google-modules/cloud-dns/google` v6.x with:
    57→- Public DNS zone creation
    58→- DNSSEC support (enabled by default)
    59→- Query logging to Cloud Logging
    60→- DNS record management (A, CNAME, NS, TXT, MX, etc.)
    61→- Standardized labeling for cost tracking
    62→
    63→**Key Features**:
    64→- `force_destroy = false` prevents accidental deletion while records exist
    65→- Comprehensive variable validation
    66→- Full DNSSEC support with NSEC3
    67→
    68→### Shared DNS Deployment
    69→
    70→**Location**: `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/`
    71→
    72→Manages two zones in the `kd-ix-eur-shr-dns` project:
    73→
    74→1. **Root Domain Zone** (`konecta-digital.com`)
    75→   - Contains NS delegations to existing subdomains (crewai, iq, jobportal)
    76→   - Contains NS delegation to ix subdomain
    77→   - Protected with `force_destroy = false` to prevent accidental deletion
    78→
    79→2. **IX Parent Zone** (`ix.konecta-digital.com`)
    80→   - Contains NS delegations to environment zones (dev, qa, prod)
    81→   - Acts as parent zone for all KIX platform environments
    82→
    83→### Landing Zone Integration
    84→
    85→**Location**: `terraform/modules/gcp/landing-zone/public-dns.tf`
    86→
    87→Extends the landing-zone module with optional public DNS support:
    88→- Conditionally creates public DNS zones based on `public_dns_config.enabled`
    89→- Creates zones in the network project (`var.network_project_id`)
    90→- Integrates with environment config.json for easy configuration
    91→
    92→### Environment Configuration
    93→
    94→**Files**: `terraform/environments/{dev,qa,prod}/config.json`
    95→
    96→Each environment has a `public_dns_config` section:
    97→
    98→```json
    99→{
   100→  "public_dns_config": {
   101→    "enabled": true,
   102→    "zone_name": "dev-ix-konecta-digital-com",
   103→    "domain": "dev.ix.konecta-digital.com.",
   104→    "enable_logging": true,
   105→    "enable_dnssec": true,
   106→    "force_destroy": false,
   107→    "recordsets": []
   108→  }
   109→}
   110→```
   111→
   112→## Migration Procedure
   113→
   114→### Pre-Migration Checklist
   115→
   116→- [ ] Backup existing AWS Route 53 records
   117→- [ ] Document current DNS TTL values
   118→- [ ] Identify all hostnames using konecta-digital.com domain
   119→- [ ] Verify GKE Gateway API load balancer IPs (if applicable)
   120→- [ ] Confirm GCP DNS API enabled in all projects:
   121→  ```bash
   122→  gcloud services enable dns.googleapis.com --project=kd-ix-eur-shr-dns
   123→  gcloud services enable dns.googleapis.com --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-network
   124→  gcloud services enable dns.googleapis.com --project=kd-ix-eur-np-network
   125→  gcloud services enable dns.googleapis.com --project=kd-ix-eur-prod-network
   126→  ```
   127→- [ ] Verify IAM permissions (`roles/dns.admin` on DNS project)
   128→- [ ] **Contact DNS team** to coordinate AWS Route 53 delegation timing
   129→- [ ] Review and update NS delegation placeholders with actual nameservers from existing projects
   130→
   131→### Phase 1: Deploy Shared DNS Zones
   132→
   133→**Objective**: Create root domain and IX parent zones in shared DNS project.
   134→
   135→```bash
   136→cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns
   137→
   138→# Initialize Terraform
   139→terraform init
   140→
   141→# Review the plan
   142→terraform plan
   143→
   144→# Apply (creates both root_domain and ix_parent_zone)
   145→terraform apply
   146→
   147→# Capture nameservers for AWS delegation
   148→terraform output root_name_servers
   149→terraform output root_name_servers_formatted
   150→```
   151→
   152→**Expected Outputs**:
   153→```
   154→root_name_servers = [
   155→  "ns-cloud-a1.googledomains.com.",
   156→  "ns-cloud-a2.googledomains.com.",
   157→  "ns-cloud-a3.googledomains.com.",
   158→  "ns-cloud-a4.googledomains.com.",
   159→]
   160→
   161→ix_name_servers = [
   162→  "ns-cloud-b1.googledomains.com.",
   163→  "ns-cloud-b2.googledomains.com.",
   164→  "ns-cloud-b3.googledomains.com.",
   165→  "ns-cloud-b4.googledomains.com.",
   166→]
   167→```
   168→
   169→**Important**: The root domain includes placeholder NS records for crewai, iq, and jobportal subdomains. You must update these with actual nameservers from those projects before applying.
   170→
   171→### Phase 2: Deploy Environment DNS Zones
   172→
   173→**Objective**: Create environment-specific zones in network projects.
   174→
   175→#### Dev Environment
   176→
   177→```bash
   178→cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   179→
   180→terraform init
   181→terraform plan -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   182→terraform apply -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   183→
   184→# Capture nameservers
   185→terraform output public_dns_name_servers
   186→```
   187→
   188→#### QA Environment
   189→
   190→```bash
   191→cd terraform/environments/qa/gcp/network
   192→
   193→terraform init
   194→terraform plan -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   195→terraform apply -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   196→
   197→# Capture nameservers
   198→terraform output public_dns_name_servers
   199→```
   200→
   201→#### Prod Environment
   202→
   203→```bash
   204→cd terraform/environments/prod/gcp/network
   205→
   206→terraform init
   207→terraform plan -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   208→terraform apply -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   209→
   210→# Capture nameservers
   211→terraform output public_dns_name_servers
   212→```
   213→
   214→### Phase 3: Update Parent Zone with NS Delegation
   215→
   216→**Objective**: Add NS delegation records to IX parent zone.
   217→
   218→1. Edit `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/main.tf`
   219→2. Update the `ix_parent_zone` module's `recordsets` with actual nameservers from Phase 2
   220→3. Uncomment the NS delegation records and replace placeholder nameservers:
   221→
   222→```hcl
   223→recordsets = [
   224→  {
   225→    name    = "dev"
   226→    type    = "NS"
   227→    ttl     = 21600
   228→    records = [

   232→      "ns-cloud-d3.googledomains.com.",
   233→      "ns-cloud-d4.googledomains.com."
   234→    ]
   235→  },

   282→

   302→- Centralized DNS management within GCP

   432→## Rollback Plan
   433→
   434→If issues arise during migration:
   435→
   436→### Immediate Rollback (AWS Route 53)
   437→
   438→**Contact DNS team immediately** to revert NS records in AWS Route 53:
   439→- Remove GCP nameservers
   440→- Restore original AWS Route 53 nameservers
   441→- DNS will revert to AWS configuration
   442→- Zero downtime (existing Route 53 records still exist)
   443→
   444→### Partial Rollback (Environment Level)
   445→
   446→If a specific environment has issues:
   447→
   448→1. Remove NS delegation from parent zone:
   449→   ```bash
   450→   cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns
   451→   # Edit main.tf, comment out problematic environment NS record
   452→   terraform apply
   453→   ```
   454→
   455→2. Wait for TTL propagation (21600 seconds = 6 hours)
   456→
   457→### Terraform State Recovery
   458→
   459→If Terraform state corruption occurs:
   460→
   461→```bash
   462→# Remove problematic resource from state
   463→terraform state rm module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone[0]
   464→
   465→# Re-import if resource exists
   466→terraform import module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone[0] projects/PROJECT_ID/managedZones/ZONE_NAME
   467→```
   468→
   469→### Complete Cleanup
   470→
   471→To fully remove GCP DNS infrastructure:
   472→
   473→```bash
   474→# 1. Remove all DNS records first (due to force_destroy=false)
   475→# Edit main.tf, set recordsets = [] for all zones
   476→cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns
   477→terraform apply
   478→
   479→# 2. Destroy environment zones
   480→cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   481→terraform destroy -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   482→
   483→# Repeat for QA and Prod
   484→
   485→# 3. Destroy shared zones
   486→cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns
   487→terraform destroy
   488→```

   491→
   492→### Adding a New Environment
   493→
   494→1. Add `public_dns_config` to environment's `config.json`
   495→2. Deploy landing zone to create environment zone
   496→3. Capture nameservers from output
   497→4. Update shared DNS `ix_parent_zone` with NS delegation
   498→5. Apply shared DNS changes
   499→
   500→### Adding DNS Records
   501→
   502→**For environment-specific records** (e.g., api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com):
   503→
   504→1. Edit `terraform/environments/dev/config.json`:
   505→   ```json
   506→   "public_dns_config": {
   507→     "recordsets": [
   508→       {
   509→         "name": "api",
   510→         "type": "A",
   511→         "ttl": 300,
   512→         "records": ["34.56.78.90"]
   513→       }
   514→     ]
   515→   }
   516→   ```
   517→
   518→2. Apply:
   519→   ```bash
   520→   cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   521→   terraform apply
   522→   ```
   523→
   524→**For root domain records** (e.g., www.konecta-digital.com):
   525→
   526→1. Edit `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/main.tf`
   527→2. Add to `root_domain` module's `recordsets`
   528→3. Apply shared DNS changes

   530→### Updating Existing Records
   531→
   532→1. Locate the record in appropriate config file
   533→2. Modify TTL, type, or records array

   562→## Security Considerations
   563→
   564→### IAM Permissions
   565→
   566→**Principle of Least Privilege**: Only platform engineers should have DNS admin access.
   567→
   568→```bash
   569→# Grant DNS admin to specific users
   570→gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding kd-ix-eur-shr-dns \
   571→  --member="user:platform-engineer@konecta-group.com" \
   572→  --role="roles/dns.admin"
   573→
   574→# For automation (use Workload Identity, never service account keys)
   575→gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding kd-ix-eur-shr-dns \
   576→  --member="serviceAccount:terraform-automation@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
   577→  --role="roles/dns.admin"
   578→```
   579→
   580→### DNSSEC Key Management
   581→
   582→- **Key Rotation**: Google Cloud DNS automatically manages DNSSEC key rotation
   583→- **KSK (Key Signing Key)**: Rotated annually
   584→- **ZSK (Zone Signing Key)**: Rotated every 90 days
   585→- **DS Records**: If using external domain registrar, DS records must be updated manually
   586→
   587→### Audit Logging
   588→
   589→All DNS changes are logged:
   590→
   591→```bash
   592→# View DNS admin activity
   593→gcloud logging read '
   594→  protoPayload.serviceName="dns.googleapis.com"
   595→  AND protoPayload.methodName:("ManagedZones" OR "ResourceRecordSets")
   596→' --limit 50 --project=kd-ix-eur-shr-dns
   597→```
   598→
   599→### Network Security
   600→
   601→- **Public Zones**: Accessible from internet (required for external DNS resolution)
   602→- **Private Zones**: Remain isolated within VPC (see landing-zone dns.tf)
   603→- **No Cross-Project Access**: Each environment manages only its own zone
   604→
   605→## Cost Estimation
   606→
   607→**Google Cloud DNS Pricing** (as of 2025):
   608→
   609→| Resource | Price | Estimated Usage | Monthly Cost |
   610→|----------|-------|-----------------|--------------|
   611→| Hosted Zone | $0.20/zone/month | 5 zones | $1.00 |
   612→| DNS Queries | $0.40/million (first 1B) | 10M queries | $4.00 |
   613→| DNSSEC | No additional cost | - | $0.00 |
   614→| **Total** | | | **~$5.00/month** |
   615→
   616→**Comparison to AWS Route 53**:
   617→- AWS Hosted Zone: $0.50/zone/month
   618→- AWS Queries: $0.40/million
   619→- **GCP Savings**: ~$1.50/month (30% cheaper on zones)
   620→
   621→## Troubleshooting
   622→
   623→### DNS Resolution Failures
   624→
   625→**Symptom**: `dig` returns SERVFAIL or NXDOMAIN
   626→
   627→**Diagnosis**:
   628→```bash
   629→# Check delegation chain
   630→dig +trace api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   631→
   632→# Check specific nameserver
   633→dig @ns-cloud-d1.googledomains.com api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   634→```
   635→
   636→**Common Causes**:
   637→1. NS delegation not configured correctly
   638→2. Zone not created in correct project
   639→3. TTL propagation still in progress (wait longer)
   640→4. DNSSEC validation failure
   641→
   642→**Resolution**:
   643→- Verify NS records in parent zone match child zone nameservers
   644→- Check zone exists: `gcloud dns managed-zones list --project=PROJECT_ID`
   645→- Wait for TTL propagation (use longer TTL values initially)
   646→
   647→### DNSSEC Validation Errors
   648→
   649→**Symptom**: DNSSEC validation fails, queries return SERVFAIL when validated
   650→
   651→**Diagnosis**:
   652→```bash
   653→# Check DNSSEC chain
   654→dig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com +dnssec +multiline
   655→
   656→# Validate with dnssec-analyzer
   657→dnsviz probe api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   658→```
   659→
   660→**Common Causes**:
   661→1. DS records not configured in parent zone (if using external registrar)
   662→2. DNSSEC chain broken due to incorrect delegation
   663→3. Time sync issues (clock skew)
   664→
   665→**Resolution**:
   666→- For GCP-to-GCP delegation: DNSSEC is automatic, check NS delegation
   667→- For external registrar: Add DS records to domain registrar
   668→- Verify server time is synchronized (DNSSEC is time-sensitive)
   669→
   670→### Terraform State Issues
   671→
   672→**Symptom**: Terraform detects unwanted changes on every plan
   673→
   674→**Diagnosis**:
   675→```bash
   676→terraform plan -refresh=false  # Skip refresh to see actual config drift
   677→terraform show  # Inspect current state
   678→```
   679→
   680→**Resolution**:
   681→```bash
   682→# Refresh state from actual infrastructure
   683→terraform refresh
   684→
   685→# If state is corrupted, remove and re-import
   686→terraform state rm MODULE.RESOURCE
   687→terraform import MODULE.RESOURCE projects/PROJECT_ID/managedZones/ZONE_NAME
   688→```
   689→
   690→### Query Logging Not Appearing
   691→
   692→**Symptom**: No DNS query logs in Cloud Logging
   693→
   694→**Diagnosis**:
   695→```bash
   696→# Check if logging is enabled
   697→gcloud dns managed-zones describe ZONE_NAME --project=PROJECT_ID
   698→
   699→# Verify log query
   700→gcloud logging read 'resource.type="dns_query"' --limit 10
   701→```
   702→
   703→**Resolution**:
   704→- Verify `enable_logging = true` in Terraform
   705→- Check IAM permissions for Cloud Logging
   706→- Wait 5-10 minutes for logs to appear initially
   707→

   734→## Appendix
   735→
   736→### DNS Record Types Reference
   737→
   738→| Type | Purpose | Example |
   739→|------|---------|---------|
   740→| A | IPv4 address | `api 300 IN A 34.56.78.90` |
   741→| AAAA | IPv6 address | `api 300 IN AAAA 2001:db8::1` |
   742→| CNAME | Alias to another name | `www 3600 IN CNAME api.example.com.` |
   743→| NS | Nameserver delegation | `dev 21600 IN NS ns1.google.com.` |
   744→| MX | Mail exchange | `@ 3600 IN MX 10 mail.example.com.` |
   745→| TXT | Text records (SPF, DKIM) | `@ 3600 IN TXT "v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all"` |
   746→| CAA | Certificate authority authorization | `@ 3600 IN CAA 0 issue "letsencrypt.org"` |
   747→
   748→### TTL Guidelines
   749→
   750→| Use Case | Recommended TTL | Rationale |
   751→|----------|----------------|-----------|
   752→| Production A records | 300 seconds (5 min) | Fast failover for load balancer changes |
   753→| CNAME records | 3600 seconds (1 hour) | Stable aliases, infrequent changes |
   754→| NS delegation | 21600 seconds (6 hours) | High stability, rare changes |
   755→| Development records | 60 seconds (1 min) | Rapid iteration during development |
   756→| SOA/Authority records | 7200 seconds (2 hours) | Standard authority TTL |
   757→
   758→### Common DNS Commands
   759→
   760→```bash
   761→# Query specific record type
   762→dig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com A
   763→
   764→# Query specific nameserver
   765→dig @ns-cloud-d1.googledomains.com api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   766→
   767→# Show full delegation chain
   768→dig +trace api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   769→
   770→# DNSSEC validation
   771→dig +dnssec api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   772→
   773→# Reverse DNS lookup
   774→dig -x 34.56.78.90
   775→
   776→# List all records in zone (requires zone transfer permission)
   777→dig axfr ix.konecta-digital.com @ns-cloud-b1.googledomains.com
   778→```

   167→## Critical Findings Summary
   168→
   169→### Security (3 High-Priority Items)

   171→| Priority | Finding | Impact | Recommendation |
   172→|----------|---------|--------|----------------|
   173→| **HIGH** | CMEK not configured | Compliance gap (SOC 2, GDPR audits) | Enable CMEK for Cloud SQL, GCS in prod |
   174→| **HIGH** | Binary Authorization policies undefined | Feature enabled but no policies | Configure attestation and enforcement policies |

   179→| Priority | Finding | Impact | Recommendation |

   181→| **CRITICAL** | No multi-region HA | Single region failure = full outage | Implement multi-region GKE + Cloud SQL replication |
   182→| **CRITICAL** | No disaster recovery plan | Data loss risk, undefined RTO/RPO | Document RTO/RPO targets, test backup/restore |
   183→| **HIGH** | Limited observability | Slow incident response | Deploy Prometheus/Grafana, configure SLO-based alerts |

   191→| **MEDIUM** | No config.json schema validation | Runtime errors from typos | Create JSON schema validator |
   192→| **MEDIUM** | No CI/CD test integration | Tests not run automatically | Add GitHub Actions/Bitbucket Pipelines |
   193→
   194→### Kubernetes (4 Critical Items)
   195→
   196→| Priority | Finding | Impact | Recommendation |
   197→|----------|---------|--------|----------------|

   199→| **CRITICAL** | No PriorityClasses | Platform services can be evicted | Add PriorityClasses for critical workloads |
   200→| **CRITICAL** | No volume snapshots | No point-in-time recovery | Enable VolumeSnapshotClass |
   201→| **CRITICAL** | No PDBs for use case workloads | Apps can be fully evicted during maintenance | Add PodDisruptionBudgets for use cases |

     1→# Testing Strategy and Documentation
     2→
     3→> **NOTE:** This document provides the canonical reference for testing on the KIX Platform.
     4→> For implementation history, see [ALL_PHASES_COMPLETE.md](./ALL_PHASES_COMPLETE.md).
     5→
     6→## Overview
     7→
     8→The KIX Platform uses a comprehensive testing strategy combining:
     9→- **Terratest** (Go-based infrastructure testing framework)
    10→- **Gherkin scenarios** (human-readable test documentation)
    11→- **GitHub Actions** (automated CI/CD test execution)
    12→- **Lab environment** (isolated testing infrastructure)
    13→
    14→**Testing Philosophy:**
    15→- Every infrastructure module has automated tests
    16→- Tests validate deployment, security, configuration, and idempotency
    17→- Human-readable scenarios enable stakeholder review
    18→- CI/CD ensures every PR is validated before merge
    19→
    20→---
    21→
    22→## Test Execution
    23→
    24→See [terraform/test/TEST_STRATEGY.md](../terraform/test/TEST_STRATEGY.md) for detailed test execution strategy:
    25→- **7-stage test execution flow** (Foundation → GKE → K8s → Platform → Data → Integration → Cleanup)
    26→- **Test patterns** (sequential, parallel, idempotency)
    27→- **Module dependency graph**
    28→- **Local testing instructions**
    29→- **Troubleshooting guide**
    30→
    31→### Quick Start
    32→
    33→```bash
    34→cd terraform/test
    35→export GOOGLE_PROJECT=kd-ix-eur-lab-platform
    36→export GOOGLE_REGION=europe-west1
    37→
    38→# Run all tests (60-90 minutes)
    39→go test -v -timeout 90m ./...
    40→
    41→# Run by category
    42→go test -v -timeout 60m -run "TestBase|TestLanding|TestGKE" ./modules/  # GCP Infrastructure
    43→go test -v -timeout 45m -run "TestGkeConfig|TestKong|TestLitellm" ./modules/  # Kubernetes
    44→go test -v -timeout 30m -run "TestCloudSQL|TestRedis|TestGCS" ./modules/  # Data Services
    45→
    46→# Run specific module
    47→go test -v -timeout 30m -run TestGKEAutopilot ./modules/
    48→
    49→# Debug mode (keep resources after test)
    50→export SKIP_TERRAFORM_DESTROY=true
    51→go test -v -timeout 30m -run TestGKEAutopilotBasic ./modules/
    52→```

   111→
   112→## CI/CD Integration
   113→
   114→Automated testing runs on every PR to main via GitHub Actions.
   115→
   116→### Workflows
   117→
   118→| Workflow | Purpose | Duration |
   119→|----------|---------|----------|
   120→| [feature-branch-ci.yml](../.github/workflows/feature-branch-ci.yml) | Fast feedback (format, lint) | < 5 mins |
   121→| [develop-quality-gates.yml](../.github/workflows/develop-quality-gates.yml) | Code quality & security scan | < 10 mins |
   122→| [main-pr-validation.yml](../.github/workflows/main-pr-validation.yml) | Full Terratest suite in lab | 30-45 mins |
   123→| [production-deployment.yml](../.github/workflows/production-deployment.yml) | QA/Prod deployment automation | Varies |
   124→
   125→### Test Execution Flow
   126→
   127→**main-pr-validation.yml** (runs on every PR to main):
   128→
   129→1. **Quality Gates** (~5 min)
   130→   - Terraform format check
   131→   - tfsec security scan (SARIF to GitHub Security)
   132→
   133→2. **Deploy Lab Environment** (~15 min)
   134→   - Full environment deployment to `kd-ix-eur-lab-platform`
   135→   - GCP Workload Identity authentication (no service account keys)
   136→
   137→3. **Terratest Validation** (~30-40 min, parallel)
   138→   - **Group 1:** GCP Infrastructure (BaseEnvironment, LandingZone, GKE)
   139→   - **Group 2:** Kubernetes Platform (GKEConfig, Kong, LiteLLM, ArgoCD)
   140→   - **Group 3:** Data Services (CloudSQL, Redis, GCS, Pub/Sub)
   141→
   142→4. **Cleanup** (~5 min, always runs)
   143→   - Automatic resource destruction (cost control)
   144→   - Runs even if tests fail
   145→
   146→**Results:** Posted as PR comment with pass/fail status per test suite
   147→
   148→**Cost:** ~$0.15-0.25 per run
   149→

   173→## Test Framework Architecture
   174→
   175→**Terratest Helpers** (903 lines):
   176→- `helpers.go` (598 lines) - Core framework with 50+ utility functions
   177→- `config.go` (100 lines) - Test configuration management
   178→- `labels.go` (67 lines) - Label validation utilities
   179→- `security.go` (138 lines) - Security compliance checks
   180→
   181→**Key Helper Functions:**
   182→- **Configuration:** `LoadTestConfig`, `GetDefaultTestConfig`
   183→- **Region:** `ValidateRegion`, `AssertRegionIsEU`
   184→- **Labels:** `ValidateRequiredLabels` (6 labels enforced: environment, managed_by, project, cost_center, data_classification, compliance)
   185→- **GCP API:** `AssertProjectExists`, `AssertAPIEnabled`
   186→- **Security:** `AssertNoPublicIP`, `AssertWorkloadIdentityConfigured`
   187→- **Terraform:** `DefaultTerraformOptions`, `AssertTerraformIdempotent`
   188→- **Cleanup:** `CleanupTerraform` (with retry logic for state locks)

   191→
   192→## Test Categories
   193→
   194→### 1. Deployment Tests
   195→- Validate successful resource creation
   196→- Check all outputs are populated
   197→- Verify resource state matches expected configuration
   198→- **Coverage:** All 13 modules
   199→
   200→### 2. Security Tests
   201→- Private cluster enforcement (no public endpoints)
   202→- Workload Identity configuration
   203→- Required labels (GDPR compliance)
   204→- No public IPs on VMs
   205→- Domain-restricted IAM (@konecta-group.com)
   206→- **Coverage:** 10 modules
   207→
   208→### 3. Configuration Validation
   209→- Input variable validation
   210→- Output verification
   211→- Network configuration (private IPs, subnets)
   212→- Resource quotas and limits
   213→- **Coverage:** 8 modules
   214→
   215→### 4. Idempotency Tests
   216→- Second `terraform apply` with no changes
   217→- Validates state convergence
   218→- Ensures no drift or recreation
   219→- **Coverage:** 8 modules
   220→
   221→### 5. API Integration Tests
   222→- GCP API interactions
   223→- Kubernetes API validation
   224→- Service health checks
   225→- **Coverage:** 10 modules
   226→
   227→### 6. Integration Tests
   228→- Cross-module dependencies
   229→- End-to-end workflows
   230→- GKE + Kong + LiteLLM integration
   231→- **Coverage:** 4 modules

   272→
   273→## Troubleshooting
   274→
   275→### Common Issues
   276→
   277→**1. State Lock Timeout**
   278→```bash
   279→# Manually unlock state
   280→terraform force-unlock <lock-id>
   281→
   282→# Or wait 10 minutes for automatic unlock
   283→```
   284→
   285→**2. GKE Cluster Creation Timeout**
   286→```bash
   287→# Increase timeout in test
   288→go test -v -timeout 90m -run TestGKECluster ./modules/
   289→```
   290→
   291→**3. Resource Already Exists**
   292→```bash
   293→# Clean up orphaned resources
   294→cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/gke
   295→terraform destroy -auto-approve
   296→
   297→# Or use lab cleanup script
   298→cd scripts
   299→./cleanup-lab-environment.sh
   300→```
   301→
   302→**4. Permission Denied**
   303→```bash
   304→# Verify service account has required roles
   305→gcloud projects get-iam-policy $GOOGLE_PROJECT \
   306→  --flatten="bindings[].members" \
   307→  --filter="bindings.members:serviceAccount:github-actions@*"
   308→```
   309→
   310→**5. Network Policy Test Failures**
   311→```bash
   312→# Check GCP health check IPs are allowed (35.191.0.0/16, 130.211.0.0/22)
   313→kubectl get networkpolicy -n <namespace> -o yaml
   314→```

   120→## Use Cases
   121→
   122→### Launch Use Cases Summary
   123→
   124→| Use Case | Type | Channel | Description |
   125→|----------|------|---------|-------------|
   126→| End-User Self-Healing | Customer-Zero | Google Chat | IT support automation |
   127→| Autopilot Scheduling | Business | Voice + Digital | Appointment scheduling |
   128→| Autopilot Collections | Business | Voice (Outbound) | Collections with compliance |
   129→| Autopilot Sales | Business | Voice (Inbound) | Sales assistant |
   130→
   131→### Use Case 1: End-User Self-Healing
   132→
   133→**Value:** 70% workstation incidents resolved without human intervention
   134→
   135→**Journey:**
   136→1. User initiates chat with "IT Support" in Google Chat
   137→2. Agent identifies intent and checks context (tickets, history, device)
   138→3. Agent correlates data across ServiceNow, Nexthink
   139→4. Agent implements remediation and documents in ITSM
   140→5. If unresolvable, hands over to human with full context
   141→
   142→**Success Metrics:**
   143→- 70% automated resolution
   144→- 90% user satisfaction
   145→- <10 minute resolution time
   146→
   147→### Use Case 2: Autopilot Scheduling
   148→
   149→**Value:** Automate appointment interactions, reduce agent workload
   150→
   151→**Flows:**
   152→- **Inbound:** Customer calls -> identify intent -> retrieve availability -> propose slots -> confirm
   153→- **Outbound:** Proactive confirmations, reminders, rescheduling
   154→
   155→**Success Metrics:**
   156→- 95% appointments fully automated
   157→- <20% escalation rate
   158→- High CSAT scores
   159→
   160→### Use Case 3: Autopilot Collections
   161→
   162→**Value:** Increase recovery rates with strict compliance
   163→
   164→**Journey:**
   165→1. Trigger outbound call based on business rules
   166→2. Authenticate customer
   167→3. Communicate balance, due date, payment reminder
   168→4. Capture response (promise-to-pay, refusal, dispute)
   169→5. Hand over if distress/dispute detected
   170→
   171→**Success Metrics:**
   172→- Recovery rate uplift vs baseline
   173→- Zero compliance incidents
   174→- <15% escalation rate
   175→
   176→### Use Case 4: Autopilot Sales
   177→
   178→**Value:** Increase conversion rates through qualification automation
   179→
   180→**Journey:**
   181→1. Customer calls with sales inquiry
   182→2. Qualify needs and retrieve eligible offers
   183→3. Present offer details and conditions
   184→4. Capture intent (accept/clarify/reject)
   185→5. Hand over for negotiation/exceptions
   186→
   187→**Success Metrics:**
   188→- Conversion rate improvement
   189→- Revenue per interaction
   190→- <25% escalation rate

   366→
   367→## Risk Register
   368→
   369→| ID | Risk | Prob | Impact | Mitigation | Owner |
   370→|----|------|------|--------|------------|-------|
   371→| R-001 | GitHub not available | Med | Med | Use Bitbucket for Phase 1; GitHub migration in Phase 2 | DevSecOps |
   372→| R-002 | Claude Code not available | Med | High | Engage Anthropic early; identify alternatives | Chief Engineer |
   373→| R-003 | Security vulnerabilities | Med | Crit | Automated scanning, 48hr SLA for critical patches | DevSecOps |
   374→| R-004 | GCP permissions delayed | Low | High | Submit requests immediately; interim sandbox | Chief Engineer |
   375→| R-005 | Resource/skill gaps | High | Med | AI tools for productivity; prioritize hires | Chief Engineer |
   376→| R-006 | Budget uncertainty | Low | Low | Document estimates early; provisional approval | Exec Sponsor |
   377→| R-007 | ServiceNow/Nexthink delays | Med | High | Develop mock APIs for early testing | Customer-Zero |
   378→| R-008 | LLM API changes/outages | Low | Med | LiteLLM abstraction; provider failover | AI Lead |
   379→
   380→**Review Cadence:** Weekly during sprint planning
   381→
   382→---
   383→
   384→## Architecture Decision Records
   385→
   386→### ADR-001: GKE over Cloud Run
   387→**Decision:** Google Kubernetes Engine
   388→
   389→**Rationale:**
   390→- Full networking control
   391→- Stateful workload support
   392→- Multi-tenancy with namespace isolation
   393→- Integration with Kong, MCP Gateway
   394→
   395→### ADR-002: Kong over Apigee
   396→**Decision:** Kong API Gateway
   397→
   398→**Rationale:**
   399→- Kubernetes-native
   400→- Open-source with enterprise features
   401→- Lower cost
   402→- Declarative configuration
   403→
   404→### ADR-003: Manual Deployments (Phase 1)
   405→**Decision:** Manual deployments with runbooks
   406→
   407→**Rationale:**
   408→- Faster implementation
   409→- Lower initial complexity
   410→- Automation deferred to Phase 2 (GitOps)
   411→
   412→### ADR-004: Cloud Observability Only (Phase 1)
   413→**Decision:** GCP native observability stack
   414→
   415→**Rationale:**
   416→- Fully managed
   417→- Native GKE integration
   418→- OpenTelemetry for instrumentation
   419→
   420→### ADR-005: Kong for 3rd Party API Abstraction
   421→**Decision:** All external APIs through Kong
   422→
   423→**Rationale:**
   424→- Centralised auth and rate limiting
   425→- Audit logging
   426→- Single integration point
   427→
   428→### ADR-006: No Data Lake (Phase 1)
   429→**Decision:** Defer Databricks to Phase 2
   430→
   431→**Rationale:**
   432→- Separate project dependency
   433→- Cloud SQL and GCS sufficient for MVP
   434→- Focus on core platform first
   435→

     5→
     6→# KIX Platform Documentation
     7→
     8→Welcome to the documentation for the **KIX Platform** (Konecta Intelligence eXchange) - an enterprise-grade AI agent platform built on Google Cloud Platform using the CrewAI framework.
     9→
    10→## Quick Navigation
    11→
    12→| Document | Description |
    13→|----------|-------------|
    14→| [Architecture Overview](docs/ARCHITECTURE) | Technical architecture, security model, and compliance |
    15→| [Getting Started](docs/ONBOARDING) | Set up your environment and deploy infrastructure |
    16→| [Developer Guide](docs/DEVELOPER_GUIDE) | Building AI agents on KIX Platform |
    17→| [Platform Strategy](docs/STRATEGY) | Platform services, operating model, and roadmap |
    18→| [Security & Compliance](docs/SECURITY_REVIEW) | Security controls, GDPR, ISO 27001, NIS2 |
    19→| [CI/CD Runbook](docs/CICD_RUNBOOK) | Pipeline operations and troubleshooting |
    20→| [Testing Guide](docs/TESTING) | Writing and running Terratest tests |
    21→
    22→## Platform Overview
    23→
    24→The KIX Platform provides enterprise-grade infrastructure for deploying AI agents with:
    25→
    26→- **Multi-Tenant Isolation** - Separate Kubernetes namespaces per use case with RBAC and network policies
    27→- **API Gateway** - Kong for 3rd party API abstraction and management
    28→- **LLM Proxy** - LiteLLM for unified access to multiple LLM providers
    29→- **GitOps** - ArgoCD for declarative infrastructure and application deployment
    30→- **Security** - Cloud Armor WAF, Workload Identity, EU data residency
    31→
    32→## Architecture
    33→
    34→```
    35→External Users → Cloud Load Balancer → Kong API Gateway → GKE (Use Case Namespaces)
    36→                                                               ↓
    37→                                       Cloud SQL / Redis / GCS / Pub/Sub (Private)
    38→
    39→Shared Services → ArgoCD (GitOps) → Multi-Cluster Deployments (Dev/QA/Prod)
    40→```
    41→
    42→See [Architecture Overview](docs/ARCHITECTURE) for detailed diagrams and technical specifications.
    43→
    44→## Repositories
    45→
    46→| Repository | Purpose | Links |
    47→|------------|---------|-------|
    48→| **kix-platform-modules** | Reusable Terraform/Helm modules | [GitHub](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules) |
    49→| **kix-platform-infrastructure** | Environment deployment configurations | [GitHub](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-infrastructure) |
    50→| **kix-platform-docs** | Platform documentation (this site) | [GitHub](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs) |
    51→| **kix-services-*** | Platform service configurations | [GitHub](https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/) |
    52→
    53→## Getting Started
    54→
    55→### For Platform Engineers
    56→
    57→1. [Onboarding Guide](docs/ONBOARDING) - Set up your development environment
    58→2. [CI/CD Runbook](docs/CICD_RUNBOOK) - Understand deployment pipelines
    59→3. [Architecture Overview](docs/ARCHITECTURE) - Learn platform internals
    60→
    61→### For AI Engineers
    62→
    63→1. [Developer Guide](docs/DEVELOPER_GUIDE) - Build AI agents on KIX Platform
    64→2. [Platform Strategy](docs/STRATEGY) - Understand platform services and capabilities
    65→3. [Security Review](docs/SECURITY_REVIEW) - Security requirements and compliance
    66→
    67→### For Leadership
    68→
    69→1. [Executive Summary](docs/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY) - Platform vision and value proposition
    70→2. [Platform Strategy](docs/STRATEGY) - Roadmap and operating model
    71→3. [Project Plan](docs/PROJECT_PLAN) - Implementation timeline and milestones
    72→
    73→## Key Features
    74→
    75→### Infrastructure as Code
    76→- **Terraform** modules for all GCP resources
    77→- **Helm** charts for Kubernetes applications
    78→- **Terratest** for automated testing
    79→
    80→### Security & Compliance
    81→- **GDPR** compliant data handling
    82→- **ISO 27001** security controls
    83→- **NIS2** cybersecurity requirements
    84→- **Workload Identity** (no service account keys)
    85→- **EU data residency** (europe-west1, europe-west4)
    86→
    87→### Developer Experience
    88→- **Self-service** namespace provisioning
    89→- **GitOps** deployments via ArgoCD
    90→- **Backstage** service catalog
    91→- **Standardized** patterns and templates

    47→## Local Development
    48→
    49→This site uses Jekyll for GitHub Pages.
    50→
    51→### Prerequisites
    52→
    53→```bash
    54→# Install Ruby and Bundler
    55→brew install ruby
    56→gem install bundler
    57→
    58→# Or use rbenv for version management
    59→brew install rbenv
    60→rbenv install 3.1.2
    61→rbenv global 3.1.2
    62→```
    63→
    64→### Running Locally
    65→
    66→```bash
    67→# Install dependencies
    68→bundle install
    69→
    70→# Serve locally (with live reload)

    72→
    73→# Open in browser

    76→
    77→### Adding Dependencies

    86→## Adding Documentation

   130→## Documentation Standards
   131→
   132→### Markdown Guidelines
   133→
   134→- **Headings:** Use `#` for document title, `##` for sections, `###` for subsections
   135→- **Code Blocks:** Always specify language for syntax highlighting
   136→- **Links:** Use absolute URLs for cross-repository references
   137→- **Tables:** Use for structured data, keep concise
   138→- **Lists:** Use for sequential steps or itemized content
   139→
   140→### Writing Style
   141→
   142→**For Engineers:**
   143→- Technical accuracy first
   144→- Code examples with syntax highlighting
   145→- Command-line examples (copy-paste ready)
   146→- Architecture diagrams with clear labels
   147→
   148→**For Developers:**
   149→- How-to guides with numbered steps
   150→- Prerequisites stated upfront
   151→- Expected outcomes after each step
   152→- Common issues and solutions
   153→
   154→**For Leadership:**
   155→- Executive summary first
   156→- Business value and ROI focus
   157→- High-level architecture (minimal jargon)
   158→- Clear next steps and milestones
   159→
   160→### Example Code Block
   161→
   162→````markdown
   163→```bash
   164→# Deploy infrastructure
   165→cd environments/dev/gcp/network
   166→terraform init
   167→terraform plan
   168→terraform apply
   169→```
   170→
   171→```hcl
   172→module "landing_zone" {
   173→  source = "github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules//terraform/gcp/landing-zone?ref=v1.0.0"
   174→
   175→  project_id  = "kd-ix-eur-dev-network"
   176→  environment = "dev"
   177→}
   178→```
   179→````

     1→# KIX UI Design — KonectaIQ
     2→
     3→**Version:** 1.0
     4→**Date:** January 2026
     5→**Classification:** Confidential - Internal Use Only
     6→
     7→*The unified interface for configuration and control plane management*
     8→
     9→---
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→KonectaIQ is the administrative interface for the KIX Platform. It provides a unified experience for managing the Konecta Control Plane — orchestrating the blend of Human Experts, AI Copilots, and Autonomous Agents.
    14→
    15→**Design Inspiration:** LiteLLM Admin Dashboard — a React/Next.js single-page application with sidebar navigation, role-based access control, and centralised API client architecture.
    16→
    17→**Key Differentiator:** KonectaIQ combines LiteLLM-style configuration management with real-time Control Plane orchestration visibility.
    18→
    19→---
    20→
    21→## Design Principles
    22→
    23→| Principle | Description |
    24→|-----------|-------------|
    25→| **Configuration + Control** | Unified view of both platform configuration and real-time orchestration |
    26→| **Role-Based Experience** | Different views for Admin, Developer, Business User, Operations |
    27→| **API-First** | Every UI action calls the underlying KIX API — the UI is one of many clients |
    28→| **Progressive Disclosure** | Simple by default, powerful when needed |
    29→| **Real-Time Awareness** | Live visibility into Control Plane routing decisions |
    30→
    31→---
    32→
    33→## Navigation Architecture
    34→
    35→### Two-Tier Navigation (LiteLLM Pattern)
    36→
    37→**Top Navbar:**
    38→- KIX logo and environment indicator (Dev / QA / Prod)
    39→- Global search
    40→- Notifications bell
    41→- User dropdown (profile, role, logout)
    42→- Theme toggle (light/dark)
    43→
    44→**Left Sidebar (Collapsible):**
    45→- Organized into logical groups
    46→- Role-based filtering (Admin sees all, Developer sees relevant)
    47→- Active state indicators
    48→- Collapse to icons for more workspace
    49→
    50→---
    51→
    52→## Sidebar Menu Structure
    53→
    54→```
    55→┌─────────────────────────────────────┐

   604→
   605→## Technical Architecture
   606→
   607→### Technology Stack
   608→
   609→| Component | Technology | Rationale |
   610→|-----------|------------|-----------|
   611→| **Framework** | Next.js 14 | Server components, App Router, LiteLLM pattern |
   612→| **UI Library** | Ant Design | Comprehensive components, LiteLLM uses this |
   613→| **State Management** | TanStack Query | Server state management |
   614→| **Styling** | Tailwind CSS | Konecta design system compatibility |
   615→| **Charts** | Recharts | React-native charts for dashboards |
   616→| **Real-time** | WebSocket / SSE | Live Control Plane updates |
   617→
   618→### API Client Pattern (from LiteLLM)
   619→
   620→```
   621→networking.ts
   622→├── proxyBaseUrl configuration
   623→├── Authentication headers (globalLitellmHeaderName)
   624→├── Typed API functions for all endpoints
   625→├── Error handling with auto-logout on session expiry
   626→└── Session storage caching
   627→```
   628→
   629→### Authentication Flow
   630→
   631→1. User accesses `/ui`
   632→2. Redirect to Google SSO (via Kong)
   633→3. JWT token stored in HTTP-only cookie
   634→4. Token validated on every API call
   635→5. Session expiry triggers re-authentication
   636→

   701→
   702→## Summary
   703→
   704→KonectaIQ is designed as a **unified configuration and control plane interface** that:
   705→
   706→1. **Follows proven patterns** from LiteLLM's admin dashboard
   707→2. **Adds Control Plane visibility** unique to Konecta's orchestration model
   708→3. **Supports multiple user roles** with appropriate access levels
   709→4. **Enables self-service** for developers and business users
   710→5. **Provides operational excellence** through comprehensive observability
   711→
   712→The key innovation is combining **LiteLLM-style API/model/key management** with **real-time Control Plane routing visibility** — showing not just what's configured, but what's actually happening in the orchestration layer.
   713→

    34→
    35→## Technology Stack Summary
    36→
    37→The stack is built on three foundational constraints:
    38→
    39→| Constraint | Technology | Rationale |
    40→|------------|------------|-----------|
    41→| **Cloud Platform** | Google Cloud Platform (GCP) | Enterprise standard, Konecta relationship |
    42→| **Agent Framework** | CrewAI | Multi-agent orchestration, production-ready |
    43→| **Voice AI** | ElevenLabs | Best-in-class voice synthesis and STT |
    44→
    45→### Core Technology Choices
    46→
    47→| Layer | Capability | Primary Technology |
    48→|-------|------------|-------------------|
    49→| **ENGAGE** | Voice AI | ElevenLabs |
    50→| **ENGAGE** | Conversational AI | CrewAI + LiteLLM |
    51→| **KNOW** | Journey Analytics | Third-party solution (Q2 selection) |
    52→| **KNOW** | Customer Profile | Cloud SQL + Redis (LaaS in Phase 2) |
    53→| **GOVERN** | AI Governance | LiteLLM + Custom |
    54→| **GOVERN** | Compliance | Cloud Audit Logs |
    55→| **CONNECT** | Omnichannel | Channel Hub + Kong |
    56→| **ACT** | Agent Runtime | CrewAI on GKE |
    57→| **ACT** | LLM Proxy | LiteLLM Proxy |
    58→| **ACT** | Tool Integration | MCP Gateway |
    59→| **ACT** | API Gateway | Kong API Gateway |
    60→| **ACT** | Event Bus | Cloud Pub/Sub |
    61→| **ACT** | Vector DB | Qdrant |
    62→| **ACT** | Service Catalogue | Backstage |
    63→
    64→### Infrastructure Stack
    65→
    66→| Component | Technology | Configuration |
    67→|-----------|------------|---------------|
    68→| **Kubernetes** | GKE Autopilot | Auto-scaling, managed control plane |
    69→| **Relational DB** | Cloud SQL PostgreSQL | HA with failover replica (LaaS in Phase 2) |
    70→| **Cache** | Cloud Memorystore Redis | Standard tier |
    71→| **Object Storage** | Google Cloud Storage | Regional, lifecycle policies |
    72→| **Vector DB** | Qdrant (on GKE) | 3 replicas, persistent storage |
    73→| **Data Lake** | Databricks LaaS | Phase 2 - analytics, ML integration |
    74→| **Service Catalogue** | Backstage | Internal service discovery |
    75→| **Identity** | Workload Identity | No service account keys |
    76→| **Secrets** | Secret Manager + CSI Driver | Auto-rotation |
    77→| **Encryption** | Cloud KMS (CMEK for Prod) | AES-256 |
    78→| **Network** | VPC with Private Google Access | No public IPs |
    79→| **WAF** | Cloud Armor | DDoS protection |
    80→| **Metrics** | Cloud Monitoring | Custom dashboards |
    81→| **Logging** | Cloud Logging | 30-day hot, 7-year archive |
    82→| **Tracing** | Cloud Trace + OpenTelemetry | Distributed tracing |
    83→| **GitOps** | ArgoCD | Multi-cluster CD, App-of-Apps, Image Updater |
    84→| **CI/CD** | GitHub Actions | Continuous integration and deployment pipelines |
    85→
    86→---

   194→### Component Responsibilities
   195→
   196→| Component | Namespace | Purpose | Internal Consumers |
   197→|-----------|-----------|---------|-------------------|
   198→| **Kong Gateway** | `kong` | External 3rd party API abstraction ONLY | All use case apps |
   199→| **LiteLLM** | `litellm` | Unified LLM proxy (OpenAI-compatible) | All CrewAI agents |
   200→| **ArgoCD** | `argocd` (shared cluster) | GitOps continuous delivery, multi-cluster management | All environments |
   201→| **CrewAI Agents** | Per-use-case | AI agent orchestration | Use case applications |
   202→| **Use Case Apps** | Per-use-case | Business logic, API endpoints | External users |
   203→| **Monitoring Stack** | `monitoring` | Prometheus, Grafana, Loki | All services |

   205→---
   206→
   207→## GKE Cluster Design
   208→
   209→### Architecture Decision: Kubernetes over Cloud Run
   210→
   211→After careful analysis, **Kubernetes namespaces within the same GKE cluster** is the deployment target for all workloads.
   212→
   213→| Factor | Cloud Run | Kubernetes | Winner |
   214→|--------|-----------|------------|--------|
   215→| **Internal Latency** | Cross-service via VPC connector (~5-10ms) | Pod-to-pod via cluster network (<1ms) | **K8s** |
   216→| **LiteLLM Access** | Requires private endpoint exposure | Direct ClusterIP service | **K8s** |
   217→| **CrewAI Integration** | Separate deployment, complex orchestration | Same namespace, shared resources | **K8s** |
   218→| **Network Policies** | VPC-level only | Fine-grained pod-level | **K8s** |
   219→| **Operational Complexity** | Simpler per-service | Single cluster management | **K8s** |
   220→
   221→**Critical factors favoring Kubernetes:**
   222→
   223→1. **Low-Latency LLM Access**: CrewAI agents frequently call LiteLLM. In-cluster communication (<1ms) vs Cloud Run to GKE (5-10ms) significantly impacts response times.
   224→
   225→2. **Unified Observability**: Single cluster means unified metrics, traces, and logs.
   226→
   227→3. **Network Isolation**: Kubernetes Network Policies provide pod-level isolation.
   228→
   229→4. **Operational Consistency**: Single operational model (kubectl, ArgoCD, Helm). ArgoCD runs on a dedicated shared cluster and manages deployments across all environment clusters via GitOps.
   230→
   231→### GKE Gateway API Architecture
   232→
   233→The platform uses the **Kubernetes Gateway API** with GKE's managed implementation:
   234→
   235→| Component | Resource | Purpose |
   236→|-----------|----------|---------|
   237→| **GatewayClass** | `gke-l7-global-external-managed` | GKE-managed, creates Global External HTTPS LB |
   238→| **Gateway** | `kix-platform-gateway` | Shared entry point, defines listeners (HTTP/HTTPS) |
   239→| **HTTPRoute** | Per-application | Routes traffic based on hostname to backend services |
   240→| **GCPBackendPolicy** | Per-backend | Attaches Cloud Armor, configures health checks |
   241→
   242→**Benefits of Gateway API over Ingress:**
   243→- **Multi-tenant friendly**: Teams create HTTPRoutes in their own namespaces
   244→- **Scalable**: Add applications without modifying central infrastructure
   245→- **Future-proof**: Gateway API is the Kubernetes standard
   246→- **Flexible**: Supports advanced routing, traffic splitting, header manipulation
   247→
   248→---

   252→### Namespace Taxonomy
   253→
   254→```
   255→GKE Cluster

   283→### Environment Differentiation
   284→
   285→Settings vary by environment via `config.json`:
   286→
   287→| Setting | Dev | QA | Prod |
   288→|---------|-----|-----|------|
   289→| `cloud_sql.availability_type` | ZONAL | ZONAL | REGIONAL |
   290→| `cloud_sql.deletion_protection` | false | false | true |
   291→| `cloud_sql.point_in_time_recovery` | false | false | true |
   292→| `gcs.force_destroy` | true | true | false |
   293→| `namespace.network_isolation.allow_egress_internet` | true | true | false |
   294→| `litellm.replicas` | 1 | 2 | 3 |
   295→| `kong_gateway.enable_admin_api` | true | true | false |

   298→
   299→## Network Traffic Flows
   300→
   301→### Flow 1: External User Request (via GKE Gateway)
   302→
   303→```
   304→Internet -> GKE Gateway (Global HTTPS LB) -> Cloud Armor -> HTTPRoute
   305→                                                              |
   306→                                                              v
   307→                                              +------------------------------+
   308→                                              | Host-based routing:          |
   309→                                              | api.kix... -> Kong proxy     |
   310→                                              | app1.kix... -> Direct to App |
   311→                                              +------------------------------+
   312→```
   313→
   314→### Flow 2: Use Case App -> LLM Request
   315→
   316→```
   317→Use Case App -> CrewAI Agent -> LiteLLM Service -> Cloud NAT -> LLM Provider
   318→(namespace)    (same ns)       (litellm ns)       (egress)     (OpenAI/etc)
   319→
   320→Path: ClusterIP -> ClusterIP -> NAT Gateway -> Internet
   321→Latency: <1ms -> <1ms -> ~50-200ms
   322→```
   323→
   324→### Flow 3: Use Case App -> External API (Salesforce, ElevenLabs)
   325→
   326→```
   327→Use Case App -> Kong Gateway -> Cloud NAT -> External Service
   328→(namespace)    (kong ns)       (egress)     (Salesforce/etc)
   329→
   330→Kong handles:
   331→- Credential injection (API keys from Secret Manager)
   332→- Rate limiting per use case
   333→- Request/response transformation
   334→- Circuit breaking and retries
   335→- Logging and metrics
   336→```
   337→
   338→### Flow 4: Use Case App -> Data Services
   339→
   340→```
   341→Use Case App -> Cloud SQL (Private IP)
   342→            -> Memorystore Redis (Private IP)
   343→            -> GCS (Private Google Access)
   344→            -> Pub/Sub (Private Google Access)
   345→
   346→All data services accessed via private networking, no public internet.
   347→```
   348→
   349→### Flow 5: Internal Service Discovery
   350→
   351→Services discover each other via Kubernetes DNS:
   352→
   353→| Service | Endpoint |
   354→|---------|----------|
   355→| LiteLLM | `litellm.litellm.svc.cluster.local:80` |
   356→| Kong Proxy | `kong-proxy.kong.svc.cluster.local:80` |
   357→| Prometheus | `prometheus.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:9090` |
   358→
   359→---
   360→
   361→## Service Communication Patterns
   362→
   363→### Use Case App -> LiteLLM
   364→
   365→```python
   366→from openai import OpenAI
   367→
   368→client = OpenAI(
   369→    base_url="http://litellm.litellm.svc.cluster.local:80/v1",
   370→    api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_API_KEY"]
   371→)
   372→
   373→response = client.chat.completions.create(
   374→    model="gpt-4",  # Or "claude-3", "gemini-pro" - LiteLLM routes
   375→    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
   376→)
   377→```
   378→
   379→### Use Case App -> Kong (External APIs)
   380→
   381→```python
   382→import requests
   383→
   384→response = requests.get(
   385→    "http://kong-proxy.kong.svc.cluster.local/salesforce/services/data/v57.0",
   386→    headers={
   387→        "X-Use-Case-Key": os.environ["KONG_API_KEY"],
   388→        "X-Use-Case": "autopilot-scheduling"
   389→    }
   390→)
   391→# Kong injects Salesforce OAuth token automatically
   392→```
   393→
   394→### CrewAI Agent -> Tools
   395→
   396→| Tool Type | Path |
   397→|-----------|------|
   398→| LLM | Via LiteLLM (OpenAI-compatible API) |
   399→| Salesforce | Via Kong -> Salesforce |
   400→| ElevenLabs | Via Kong -> ElevenLabs |
   401→| MCP Tools | Via MCP Gateway (future) |
   402→| Database | Direct to Cloud SQL via SQLAlchemy |
   403→| Cache | Direct to Redis via redis-py |

   406→
   407→## Security Architecture
   408→
   409→### Security Layers
   410→
   411→```
   412→+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
   413→|                         SECURITY ARCHITECTURE                                 |
   414→+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
   415→
   416→NETWORK SECURITY
   417→- Private GKE cluster (no public node IPs)
   418→- Cloud Armor WAF + DDoS protection at ingress
   419→- Network Policies for pod-to-pod isolation
   420→- Cloud NAT for controlled egress
   421→- VPC Service Controls (Production only)
   422→
   423→IDENTITY & ACCESS
   424→- Workload Identity for all GCP access (NO service account keys)
   425→- Per-use-case GCP service accounts with least privilege
   426→- Kubernetes RBAC for namespace isolation
   427→- Kong API keys for use case identification
   428→- LiteLLM API keys for LLM access control
   429→
   430→SECRETS MANAGEMENT
   431→- Secret Manager as source of truth
   432→- External Secrets Operator for K8s sync
   433→- No secrets in Git, no secrets in environment variables at build time
   434→- Automatic rotation (90-day policy)
   435→
   436→DATA PROTECTION
   437→- Encryption at rest (Google-managed, CMEK for Prod)
   438→- TLS 1.3 in transit
   439→- Private Google Access for GCP services
   440→- Data residency: EU only (europe-west1, europe-west4)
   441→```
   442→
   443→### Workload Identity Configuration
   444→
   445→```hcl
   446→# GCP Service Account for the use case
   447→resource "google_service_account" "use_case" {
   448→  project      = var.project_id
   449→  account_id   = "${var.use_case_name}-app"
   450→  display_name = "Use Case: ${var.use_case_name}"
   451→}
   452→
   453→# Workload Identity binding
   454→resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "workload_identity" {
   455→  service_account_id = google_service_account.use_case.name
   456→  role               = "roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser"
   457→
   458→  members = [
   459→    "serviceAccount:${var.project_id}.svc.id.goog[${var.namespace}/${var.k8s_service_account}]"
   460→  ]
   461→}
   462→
   463→# IAM roles for the use case (least privilege)
   464→resource "google_project_iam_member" "secret_accessor" {
   465→  project = var.project_id
   466→  role    = "roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"
   467→  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.use_case.email}"
   468→
   469→  condition {
   470→    title       = "Use case secrets only"
   471→    expression  = "resource.name.startsWith('projects/${var.project_id}/secrets/${var.use_case_name}-')"
   472→  }
   473→}
   474→```
   475→
   476→### Network Policy Example
   477→
   478→```yaml
   479→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   480→kind: NetworkPolicy
   481→metadata:
   482→  name: use-case-default
   483→  namespace: autopilot-scheduling-dev
   484→spec:
   485→  podSelector: {}
   486→  policyTypes:
   487→    - Ingress
   488→    - Egress
   489→
   490→  ingress:
   491→    # Allow from Kong ingress controller
   492→    - from:
   493→        - namespaceSelector:
   494→            matchLabels:
   495→              app.kubernetes.io/component: api-gateway
   496→      ports:
   497→        - protocol: TCP
   498→          port: 8080
   499→
   500→  egress:
   501→    # Allow to LiteLLM
   502→    - to:
   503→        - namespaceSelector:
   504→            matchLabels:
   505→              app.kubernetes.io/component: llm-proxy
   506→      ports:
   507→        - protocol: TCP
   508→          port: 80
   509→
   510→    # Allow to Kong for external API calls
   511→    - to:
   512→        - namespaceSelector:
   513→            matchLabels:
   514→              app.kubernetes.io/component: api-gateway
   515→      ports:
   516→        - protocol: TCP
   517→          port: 80
   518→
   519→    # Allow to Cloud SQL (private IP range)
   520→    - to:
   521→        - ipBlock:
   522→            cidr: 10.1.0.0/24
   523→      ports:
   524→        - protocol: TCP
   525→          port: 5432
   526→
   527→    # Allow to GCP APIs via Private Google Access
   528→    - to:
   529→        - ipBlock:
   530→            cidr: 199.36.153.4/30
   531→      ports:
   532→        - protocol: TCP
   533→          port: 443
   534→
   535→    # Allow DNS resolution
   536→    - to:
   537→        - namespaceSelector: {}
   538→          podSelector:
   539→            matchLabels:
   540→              k8s-app: kube-dns
   541→      ports:
   542→        - protocol: UDP
   543→          port: 53
   544→```
