   591→
   592→### State Management
   593→
   594→Each environment uses **separate state files per service layer**:
   595→
   596→```
   597→gs://kd-tfstate-{env}/
   598→+-- gcp/network/          # VPC, NAT, DNS, Firewall
   599→+-- gcp/gke/              # GKE cluster and node pools
   600→+-- gcp/data/             # Cloud SQL, GCS, Pub/Sub per use case
   601→+-- kubernetes/platform/  # Kong, LiteLLM, namespaces, RBAC
   602→
   603→gs://kd-tfstate-shared/   # Shared services
   604→+-- gcp/network/          # Shared VPC
   605→+-- gcp/security/         # Cloud Armor WAF
   606→+-- gcp/gke/              # Shared platform cluster
   607→+-- gcp/iam/              # Service accounts, Workload Identity
   608→+-- kubernetes/argocd/    # ArgoCD deployment + GKE Gateway
   609→+-- kubernetes/argocd-bootstrap/  # App-of-Apps, AppProjects
   610→```
   611→
   612→**Apply Order (per env):** `network -> gke -> data -> kubernetes/platform`
   613→
   614→**Apply Order (shared):** `network -> security -> gke -> iam -> argocd -> argocd-bootstrap`
   615→
   616→### config.json Structure
   617→
   618→Each environment has a `config.json` that drives all deployments:
   619→
   620→```json
   621→{
   622→  "global": {
   623→    "environment": "dev",
   624→    "region": "europe-west1",
   625→    "gke_project_id": "kd-ix-eur-dev-gke",
   626→    "data_project_id": "kd-ix-eur-dev-data",
   627→    "network_project_id": "kd-ix-eur-np-network"
   628→  },
   629→  "landing_zone": { ... },
   630→  "gke_cluster": { ... },
   631→  "gke_config": {
   632→    "platform_namespaces": {
   633→      "kong": { "enabled": true },
   634→      "litellm": { "enabled": true },
   635→      "monitoring": { "enabled": true }
   636→    }
   637→  },
   638→  "use_cases": {
   639→    "autopilot-scheduling": {
   640→      "enabled": true,
   641→      "display_name": "Autopilot Scheduling",
   642→      "namespace": { ... },
   643→      "cloud_sql": { "enabled": true, ... },
   644→      "gcs": { "enabled": true, "buckets": { ... } },
   645→      "pubsub": { "enabled": true, "topics": { ... } }
   646→    }
   647→  },
   648→  "litellm": { ... },
   649→  "kong_gateway": { ... }
   650→}
   651→```
   652→
   653→---
   654→
   655→## Technology Decision Records
   656→
   657→### TDR-001: LiteLLM Proxy for LLM Gateway
   658→
   659→**Decision:** Use LiteLLM Proxy as the LLM gateway instead of direct Vertex AI calls.
   660→
   661→**Rationale:**
   662→- Multi-provider abstraction (future flexibility)
   663→- Built-in load balancing and fallback
   664→- Cost tracking and budget enforcement
   665→- 8ms P95 latency at 1k RPS
   666→- OpenAI-compatible API format
   667→
   668→**Trade-offs:**
   669→- Additional operational component
   670→- Slight latency overhead (~5ms)
   671→
   672→### TDR-002: MCP for Tool Integration
   673→
   674→**Decision:** Use MCP (Model Context Protocol) for all tool integrations.
   675→
   676→**Rationale:**
   677→- Industry standard (Anthropic, OpenAI adopted)
   678→- Structured tool/resource/prompt primitives
   679→- Async task support (2025 spec)
   680→- Security model with server identity
   681→- Growing ecosystem of pre-built servers
   682→
   683→**Trade-offs:**
   684→- Newer protocol (less mature than REST)
   685→- Requires MCP gateway development
   686→
   687→### TDR-003: Backstage for Service Catalogue
   688→
   689→**Decision:** Use Backstage as internal service catalogue for use case discovery.
   690→
   691→**Rationale:**
   692→- Open-source with strong community (Spotify-backed, CNCF)
   693→- Software catalogue for service discovery
   694→- Provides schema for use case teams to understand available services
   695→- Tech docs aggregation
   696→- Plugin architecture for extensibility
   697→
   698→**Trade-offs:**
   699→- Requires hosting and maintenance
   700→- Initial setup and configuration effort
   701→
   702→**Note:** Agent-to-agent communication is handled natively by CrewAI framework.
   703→
   704→### TDR-004: Kong API Gateway
   705→
   706→**Decision:** Use Kong API Gateway instead of Apigee.
   707→
   708→**Rationale:**
   709→- Kubernetes-native deployment
   710→- AI-specific features (AI Proxy, MCP bridge)
   711→- 1000+ plugins available
   712→- Lower cost than Apigee
   713→- Declarative GitOps-friendly configuration
   714→
   715→**Trade-offs:**
   716→- Self-managed (vs. Apigee fully managed)
   717→- Requires Kong expertise
   718→
   719→### TDR-005: ArgoCD for GitOps Continuous Delivery
   720→
   721→**Decision:** Use ArgoCD as the GitOps continuous delivery engine, deployed on a shared platform cluster.
   722→
   723→**Rationale:**
   724→- GitOps workflow: Git as single source of truth for deployments
   725→- Multi-cluster management from a single control plane
   726→- ApplicationSet controller for templated app generation
   727→- Image Updater watches Artifact Registry for new images
   728→- Dex integration for Google OIDC authentication
   729→- Declarative, auditable deployment history
   730→
   731→**Trade-offs:**
   732→- Requires dedicated shared GKE cluster
   733→- Additional operational component to manage
   734→- Cross-project IAM needed for multi-cluster access
   735→
   736→### TDR-006: Qdrant for Vector Database
   737→
   738→**Decision:** Use Qdrant instead of Vertex AI Matching Engine.
   739→
   740→**Rationale:**
   741→- Open-source with commercial support
   742→- High performance benchmarks
   743→- Kubernetes-native deployment
   744→- No vendor lock-in
   745→
   746→**Trade-offs:**
   747→- Self-managed (vs. managed Vertex AI)
   748→- Operational overhead
   749→
   750→---
   751→
   752→## Quick Reference
   753→
   754→### Service Endpoints (Internal)
   755→
   756→| Service | Endpoint | Port |
   757→|---------|----------|------|
   758→| LiteLLM | `litellm.litellm.svc.cluster.local` | 80 |
   759→| Kong Proxy | `kong-proxy.kong.svc.cluster.local` | 80/443 |
   760→| Kong Admin | `kong-admin.kong.svc.cluster.local` | 8001 |
   761→| ArgoCD Server | `argocd-server.argocd.svc.cluster.local` (shared cluster) | 80/443 |
   762→| Prometheus | `prometheus.monitoring.svc.cluster.local` | 9090 |
   763→| Grafana | `grafana.monitoring.svc.cluster.local` | 3000 |
   764→
   765→### GKE Gateway (External Access)
   766→
   767→| Property | Value |
   768→|----------|-------|
   769→| Gateway Name | `kix-platform-gateway` (per-env), `argocd-gateway` (shared) |
   770→| Gateway Namespace | `kong` (per-env), `argocd` (shared) |
   771→| GatewayClass | `gke-l7-global-external-managed` |
   772→| HTTPS Listener | `https` (port 443) |
   773→| Cloud Armor Policy | `kix-{env}-waf-policy` (per-env), `kd-ix-eur-shr-waf` (shared) |
   774→
   775→### Required Labels
   776→
   777→```hcl
   778→labels = {
   779→  environment = var.environment
   780→  use_case    = var.use_case_name
   781→  managed_by  = "terraform"
   782→  cost_center = var.cost_center
   783→  project     = "kix-platform"
   784→  compliance  = "gdpr"
   785→}
   786→```
   787→
   788→### Naming Conventions
   789→
   790→| Resource | Pattern | Example |
   791→|----------|---------|---------|
   792→| Namespace | `{use-case}-{env}` | `autopilot-scheduling-dev` |
   793→| Deployment | `{use-case}-{component}` | `autopilot-scheduling-agent` |
   794→| Service | `{use-case}-{component}` | `autopilot-scheduling-api` |
   795→| GCP SA | `{use-case}-app@{project}.iam` | `autopilot-app@kd-ix-eur-dev-gke.iam` |
   796→
   797→### Estimated Monthly Costs
   798→
   799→| Component | Dev | QA | Prod |
   800→|-----------|-----|----|----- |
   801→| GKE Cluster | ~$1,162 | ~$1,162 | ~$2,252 |
   802→| Cloud SQL | $200 | $200 | $400 (HA) |
   803→| Memorystore Redis | $175 | $175 | $350 (HA) |
   804→| Networking | $45 | $45 | $290 |
   805→| Storage/Logging | ~$103 | ~$103 | ~$260 |
   806→| **Subtotal Infrastructure** | **~$1,685** | **~$1,685** | **~$3,552** |
   807→| LLM API Costs (Variable) | $500 | $1,000 | $5,000+ |
   808→| **Total Estimated** | **~$2,185** | **~$2,685** | **~$8,552+** |
   809→
   810→---

{
  "command": "python3 -c \"\nimport struct, zlib\n# Create a minimal 16x16 favicon ICO\n# Generate a 16x16 PNG first\ndef create_png():\n    width, height = 16, 16\n    # Navy blue (#0f0f72) with green K placeholder - simple solid color for now\n    r, g, b = 0x0f, 0x0f, 0x72\n    raw = b''\n    for y in range(height):\n        raw += b'\\x00'  # filter byte\n        for x in range(width):\n            raw += bytes([r, g, b, 255])\n    \n    def chunk(chunk_type, data):\n        c = chunk_type + data\n        return struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + c + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(c) & 0xffffffff)\n    \n    ihdr = struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', width, height, 8, 6, 0, 0, 0)\n    png = b'\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n'\n    png += chunk(b'IHDR', ihdr)\n    png += chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(raw))\n    png += chunk(b'IEND', b'')\n    return png\n\n# Write as ICO (just use PNG data in ICO container)\npng_data = create_png()\nwith open('static/img/favicon.ico', 'wb') as f:\n    # ICO header\n    f.write(struct.pack('<HHH', 0, 1, 1))  # reserved, type=icon, count=1\n    # Directory entry\n    f.write(struct.pack('<BBBBHHII', 16, 16, 0, 0, 1, 32, len(png_data), 22))\n    f.write(png_data)\nprint('favicon.ico created')\n\"\n",
  "description": "Generate a minimal favicon.ico"
}

     6→     6→**Audience:** CISO, CIO, Enterprise Architecture, Security Review Board

    10→    10→## Executive Summary
    11→    11→
    12→    12→This document provides a comprehensive security and compliance overview of the KIX Platform for executive and security leadership review. It validates architectural decisions, security controls, and compliance posture.
    13→    13→
    14→    14→**Related Documents:**
    15→    15→- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — Technical infrastructure details

    35→    35→
    36→    36→## Security Posture Summary
    37→    37→
    38→    38→### Key Architecture Decisions
    39→    39→
    40→    40→| Decision | Rationale | Risk Mitigation |
    41→    41→|----------|-----------|-----------------|
    42→    42→| **GCP as Cloud Provider** | Enterprise agreement, EU data centres | Multi-cloud exit strategy documented |
    43→    43→| **GKE for Containers** | Managed Kubernetes, Workload Identity | No vendor lock-in at application layer |
    44→    44→| **Workload Identity Only** | Eliminates credential management | Enforced by organisation policy |
    45→    45→| **Private-First Networking** | Zero public IPs on compute | Cloud NAT for controlled egress |
    46→    46→| **EU Data Residency** | GDPR compliance | Enforced via organisation policy |
    47→    47→
    48→    48→### Control Summary
    49→    49→
    50→    50→| Category | Implementation | Compliance |
    51→    51→|----------|----------------|------------|
    52→    52→| Identity | Workload Identity, domain-restricted IAM | SOC 2, ISO 27001 |
    53→    53→| Network | Private GKE, VPC Service Controls (Prod) | CIS Benchmarks |
    54→    54→| Data | Encryption at rest (CMEK), TLS 1.3 in transit | GDPR Article 32 |
    55→    55→| Logging | 7-year immutable audit trail | GDPR, EU AI Act |
    56→    56→| Access | RBAC, least privilege, quarterly reviews | ISO 27001 |
    57→    57→
    58→    58→---
    59→    59→
    60→    60→## Security Architecture
    61→    61→
    62→    62→### Security Principles
    63→    63→
    64→    64→| Principle | Implementation |
    65→    65→|-----------|----------------|
    66→    66→| **Zero Trust** | No implicit trust; every request authenticated and authorised |
    67→    67→| **Defence in Depth** | Multiple security layers: network, identity, application |
    68→    68→| **Least Privilege** | Minimal permissions; regular access reviews |
    69→    69→| **Separation of Duties** | Different teams for dev, deploy, operate |
    70→    70→| **Security by Default** | Secure configurations out of the box |
    71→    71→
    72→    72→### Security Controls Matrix
    73→    73→
    74→    74→| Layer | Control | Implementation | Monitoring |
    75→    75→|-------|---------|----------------|------------|
    76→    76→| **Perimeter** | DDoS Protection | Cloud Armor | Real-time alerts |
    77→    77→| **Perimeter** | WAF | Cloud Armor OWASP rules | Log-based alerts |
    78→    78→| **Network** | Firewall | VPC firewall, deny-all default | Flow logs |
    79→    79→| **Network** | Segmentation | VPC per environment, Network Policies | VPC Flow Logs |
    80→    80→| **Identity** | Authentication | Workload Identity, OAuth 2.0 | Audit logs |
    81→    81→| **Identity** | Authorisation | IAM, RBAC, least privilege | Access logs |
    82→    82→| **Application** | Input Validation | Kong plugins, application-level | Error logs |
    83→    83→| **Application** | Secrets | Secret Manager, CSI driver | Access logs |
    84→    84→| **GitOps** | ArgoCD RBAC | Dex OIDC (Google), AppProject-scoped access | ArgoCD audit logs |
    85→    85→| **GitOps** | ArgoCD WAF | Cloud Armor on ArgoCD Gateway, admin path restriction | Cloud Armor logs |
    86→    86→| **GitOps** | Workload Identity | ArgoCD SA with cross-project container.developer | IAM audit logs |
    87→    87→| **Data** | Encryption at Rest | CMEK (Prod), Google-managed (Non-prod) | KMS audit logs |
    88→    88→| **Data** | Encryption in Transit | TLS 1.3 mandatory | Certificate monitoring |
    89→    89→| **Container** | Image Scanning | Artifact Registry scanning | Vulnerability alerts |
    90→    90→| **Container** | Binary Auth | Attestation required (Prod) | Deployment logs |

    92→    92→### Security Services
    93→    93→
    94→    94→```
    95→    95→SECRET MANAGER
    96→    96→+-- /dev/use-case-1/          +-- /qa/use-case-1/          +-- /prod/use-case-1/
    97→    97→|   +-- db-pass               |   +-- db-pass              |   +-- db-pass
    98→    98→|   +-- api-key               |   +-- api-key              |   +-- api-key
    99→    99→
   100→   100→Access: Workload Identity only, per-use-case IAM bindings
   101→   101→Rotation: Automatic 90-day rotation for service credentials
   102→   102→

   104→   104→+-- Key Ring: kix-{env}-keyring (europe-west1)

   106→   106→    +-- database-encryption-key (AES-256-GCM)
   107→   107→    +-- storage-encryption-key (AES-256-GCM)

   109→   109→

   125→   125→## Identity & Access Management
   126→   126→
   127→   127→### Identity Architecture
   128→   128→
   129→   129→**Human Identities:**
   130→   130→- Google Cloud Identity (konecta-group.com)
   131→   131→- Access via SSO with corporate IdP
   132→   132→- MFA required for all accounts
   133→   133→
   134→   134→| Group | Roles |
   135→   135→|-------|-------|

   138→   138→| Security Team | Security Admin, Audit Log Viewer |

   141→   141→
   142→   142→```
   143→   143→Kubernetes Service Account          GCP Service Account
   144→   144→(autopilot-scheduling-sa)   --->    (autopilot-app@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com)
   145→   145→                                          |
   146→   146→                                          v
   147→   147→                                    IAM Roles (Least Privilege)
   148→   148→                                    +-- roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor
   149→   149→                                    +-- roles/cloudsql.client
   150→   150→                                    +-- roles/storage.objectUser
   151→   151→                                    +-- roles/pubsub.publisher

   153→   153→                                    +-- roles/cloudtrace.agent

   155→   155→
   156→   156→**NO SERVICE ACCOUNT KEYS** — Enforced by Organisation Policy
   157→   157→
   158→   158→### IAM Principles
   159→   159→
   160→   160→| Principle | Implementation |
   161→   161→|-----------|----------------|
   162→   162→| **Least Privilege** | Predefined roles preferred; custom roles quarterly reviewed |
   163→   163→| **Separation of Duties** | Deploy != Approve; Dev != Prod access |
   164→   164→| **Just-in-Time Access** | Elevated access via approval workflow, time-limited |
   165→   165→| **Domain Restriction** | IAM members must be from konecta-group.com |
   166→   166→| **No Shared Accounts** | Individual accounts for all human access |
   167→   167→

   169→   169→
   170→   170→| Role | Permissions | Binding |
   171→   171→|------|-------------|---------|
   172→   172→| `namespace-admin` | Full namespace access | Use case lead |
   173→   173→| `namespace-developer` | Deploy, view logs, exec into pods | Developers |
   174→   174→| `namespace-readonly` | View resources, logs | Support, auditors |
   175→   175→
   176→   176→### Break-Glass Access
   177→   177→
   178→   178→| Aspect | Policy |
   179→   179→|--------|--------|
   180→   180→| Purpose | Emergency access when normal channels unavailable |
   181→   181→| Accounts | Dedicated break-glass accounts (2 minimum) |
   182→   182→| Storage | Credentials in secure offline storage |
   183→   183→| Monitoring | Real-time alerts on any break-glass usage |
   184→   184→| Review | Mandatory post-incident review within 24 hours |

   188→   188→## Network Security
   189→   189→
   190→   190→### Firewall Rules
   191→   191→
   192→   192→| Rule | Direction | Source | Destination | Ports | Action |
   193→   193→|------|-----------|--------|-------------|-------|--------|
   194→   194→| allow-iap-ssh | Ingress | 35.235.240.0/20 | All instances | 22 | Allow |
   195→   195→| allow-health-checks | Ingress | 130.211.0.0/22, 35.191.0.0/16 | GKE nodes | 80, 443 | Allow |
   196→   196→| allow-internal | Ingress | VPC CIDR | VPC CIDR | All | Allow |
   197→   197→| deny-all-ingress | Ingress | 0.0.0.0/0 | All | All | Deny |
   198→   198→| allow-google-apis | Egress | GKE nodes | 199.36.153.4/30 | 443 | Allow |
   199→   199→| allow-llm-egress | Egress | AI pods | LLM provider IPs | 443 | Allow |
   200→   200→| deny-all-egress | Egress | All | 0.0.0.0/0 | All | Deny |
   201→   201→
   202→   202→### Network Security Controls
   203→   203→
   204→   204→| Control | Implementation |
   205→   205→|---------|----------------|
   206→   206→| **Private GKE** | No public node IPs; control plane access via authorised networks |
   207→   207→| **VPC Service Controls** | Data exfiltration prevention (Production only) |
   208→   208→| **Cloud NAT** | Controlled egress; logging enabled |
   209→   209→| **Private Google Access** | Access GCP APIs without public internet |
   210→   210→| **Network Policies** | Default deny-all; explicit allow rules per namespace |

   212→   212→### Kubernetes Network Policy Example
   213→   213→
   214→   214→```yaml
   215→   215→# Default deny-all policy (applied to all namespaces)
   216→   216→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   217→   217→kind: NetworkPolicy
   218→   218→metadata:
   219→   219→  name: default-deny-all
   220→   220→spec:
   221→   221→  podSelector: {}
   222→   222→  policyTypes:
   223→   223→  - Ingress
   224→   224→  - Egress
   225→   225→
   226→   226→# Allow ingress from Kong gateway only
   227→   227→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   228→   228→kind: NetworkPolicy
   229→   229→metadata:
   230→   230→  name: allow-kong-ingress
   231→   231→spec:
   232→   232→  podSelector:
   233→   233→    matchLabels:
   234→   234→      app: crewai-agent
   235→   235→  policyTypes:
   236→   236→  - Ingress
   237→   237→  ingress:
   238→   238→  - from:
   239→   239→    - namespaceSelector:
   240→   240→        matchLabels:
   241→   241→          name: kong
   242→   242→    ports:
   243→   243→    - protocol: TCP
   244→   244→      port: 8080
   245→   245→```

    29→    29→## Prerequisites
    30→    30→
    31→    31→### GCP Organization Access
    32→    32→
    33→    33→Before you begin, ensure you have access to the Konecta GCP Organization:
    34→    34→
    35→    35→1. **Request GCP Organization Access** - Contact IT Service Desk with:
    36→    36→   - Your konecta-group.com email address
    37→    37→   - Team: Platform Engineering
    38→    38→   - Required access: Delegated folder admin for KIX Platform
    39→    39→
    40→    40→2. **Required IAM Roles**
    41→    41→
    42→    42→You'll need the following roles on the delegated root folder:
    43→    43→- `roles/resourcemanager.folderAdmin` - Create folders and projects
    44→    44→- `roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator` - Create GCP projects
    45→    45→- `roles/billing.user` - Link projects to billing account
    46→    46→- `roles/compute.networkAdmin` - Create VPCs and networking
    47→    47→- `roles/container.admin` - Create GKE clusters
    48→    48→
    49→    49→### Required Tools
    50→    50→
    51→    51→| Tool | Version | Installation |
    52→    52→|------|---------|--------------|
    53→    53→| Terraform | >= 1.5.0 | [terraform.io/downloads](https://www.terraform.io/downloads) |
    54→    54→| gcloud CLI | Latest | [cloud.google.com/sdk/install](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/install) |
    55→    55→| Go | >= 1.21 | [go.dev/doc/install](https://go.dev/doc/install) |

    58→    58→
    59→    59→**Verify installations:**
    60→    60→
    61→    61→```bash
    62→    62→terraform version  # Should show v1.5.0 or higher
    63→    63→gcloud version     # Should show latest SDK
    64→    64→go version         # Should show go1.21 or higher
    65→    65→kubectl version --client  # Should show v1.28 or higher
    66→    66→```
    67→    67→
    68→    68→---

    70→    70→## Repository Setup
    71→    71→
    72→    72→### 1. Clone the Repository
    73→    73→
    74→    74→```bash
    75→    75→# Currently hosted on Bitbucket (migrating to GitHub soon)
    76→    76→git clone https://bitbucket.org/konecta-group/kon-gcp-platform.git
    77→    77→cd kon-gcp-platform
    78→    78→
    79→    79→git branch
    80→    80→# Expected output: * develop
    81→    81→```
    82→    82→
    83→    83→**Note:** The repository is currently on Bitbucket but will migrate to GitHub. The CI/CD pipelines already use GitHub Actions.
    84→    84→
    85→    85→**Branching Strategy:**
    86→    86→- `main` - Production-ready code, pushed at sprint end or new environment delivery
    87→    87→- `develop` - Main development branch during sprint, integration point for features
    88→    88→- Feature branches - Work in progress, merge to `develop` via PR
    89→    89→
    90→    90→### 2. Key Files to Read First
    91→    91→
    92→    92→| File | Time | Description |
    93→    93→|------|------|-------------|
    94→    94→| `CLAUDE.md` | 10 min | Project overview, security requirements, naming conventions |
    95→    95→| `docs/ONBOARDING.md` | 15 min | This file |
    96→    96→| `docs/STRATEGY.md` | 20 min | Platform vision and architecture |
    97→    97→| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | 20 min | Technical infrastructure details |
    98→    98→
    99→    99→### 3. Directory Structure
   100→   100→
   101→   101→```
   102→   102→kon-gcp-platform/
   103→   103→+-- CLAUDE.md                       # Project standards (READ THIS FIRST)
   104→   104→+-- terraform/
   105→   105→|   +-- bootstrap/                  # Org-level state buckets (run first)
   106→   106→|   +-- modules/
   107→   107→|   |   +-- gcp/                    # GCP-specific modules
   108→   108→|   |   |   +-- base-environment/   # GCP projects and folder structure
   109→   109→|   |   |   +-- landing-zone/       # VPC, networking, security baseline
   110→   110→|   |   |   +-- gke-cluster/        # GKE cluster creation
   111→   111→|   |   |   +-- data-services/      # Cloud SQL, Redis, GCS, Pub/Sub
   112→   112→|   |   +-- kubernetes/             # Kubernetes-specific modules
   113→   113→|   |       +-- gke-config/         # Namespace, RBAC, network policies
   114→   114→|   |       +-- kong-gateway/       # Kong API Gateway
   115→   115→|   |       +-- litellm/            # LiteLLM proxy
   116→   116→|   |       +-- argocd/             # ArgoCD GitOps (shared cluster)
   117→   117→|   +-- environments/               # Environment-specific configurations
   118→   118→|   |   +-- shared/                 # Shared services (ArgoCD, DNS)
   119→   119→|   |   +-- lab/                    # Playground for new technology
   120→   120→|   |   +-- dev/                    # Development
   121→   121→|   |   +-- qa/                     # QA (mirrors prod)
   122→   122→|   |   +-- prod/                   # Production
   123→   123→|   +-- test/                       # Terratest integration tests
   124→   124→+-- docs/                           # Documentation
   125→   125→```

   172→   172→
   173→   173→## Understanding the Repository Structure
   174→   174→
   175→   175→### Module Organization
   176→   176→
   177→   177→Modules are organized by provider type:
   178→   178→
   179→   179→**GCP Modules** (`modules/gcp/`):
   180→   180→- `base-environment` - GCP folders and projects
   181→   181→- `landing-zone` - VPC, networking, security baseline
   182→   182→- `gke-cluster` - GKE cluster creation
   183→   183→- `data-services/*` - Cloud SQL, Redis, GCS, Pub/Sub
   184→   184→
   185→   185→**Kubernetes Modules** (`modules/kubernetes/`):
   186→   186→- `gke-config` - Namespaces, RBAC, network policies
   187→   187→- `kong-gateway` - Kong API Gateway
   188→   188→- `litellm` - LiteLLM proxy
   189→   189→- `argocd` - ArgoCD GitOps continuous delivery (shared cluster)
   190→   190→
   191→   191→### Service Dependency Chain
   192→   192→
   193→   193→Services must be deployed in order:
   194→   194→
   195→   195→```
   196→   196→+---------------------+
   197→   197→|     bootstrap       |  Creates state buckets (run once)
   198→   198→+---------+-----------+
   199→   199→          |
   200→   200→          v
   201→   201→+---------------------+
   202→   202→|    gcp/network      |  VPC, subnets, NAT, firewall
   203→   203→+---------+-----------+
   204→   204→          |
   205→   205→          +----------------+
   206→   206→          v                v
   207→   207→+---------------+  +---------------+
   208→   208→|   gcp/gke     |  |   gcp/data    |  (can run in parallel)
   209→   209→+-------+-------+  +---------------+
   210→   210→        |
   211→   211→        v
   212→   212→+---------------------+
   213→   213→| kubernetes/platform |  gke-config, kong, litellm
   214→   214→+---------------------+
   215→   215→```
   216→   216→
   217→   217→### State Management
   218→   218→
   219→   219→Each service has its own state file:
   220→   220→
   221→   221→```
   222→   222→gs://kd-tfstate-{env}/
   223→   223→+-- gcp/network/
   224→   224→+-- gcp/gke/
   225→   225→+-- gcp/data/
   226→   226→+-- kubernetes/platform/
   227→   227→```
   228→   228→
   229→   229→---
   230→   230→
   231→   231→## Environment Configuration
   232→   232→
   233→   233→### config.json (Per Environment)
   234→   234→
   235→   235→Each environment has a `config.json` that drives all deployments:
   236→   236→
   237→   237→```json
   238→   238→{
   239→   239→  "global": {
   240→   240→    "environment": "dev",
   241→   241→    "region": "europe-west1",
   242→   242→    "gke_project_id": "kd-ix-eur-dev-gke",
   243→   243→    "data_project_id": "kd-ix-eur-dev-data"
   244→   244→  },
   245→   245→  "landing_zone": { ... },
   246→   246→  "gke_cluster": { ... },
   247→   247→  "gke_config": { ... },
   248→   248→  "kong_gateway": { ... }
   249→   249→}
   250→   250→```
   251→   251→
   252→   252→**Usage in Terraform:**
   253→   253→
   254→   254→```hcl
   255→   255→locals {
   256→   256→  config = jsondecode(file("${path.module}/../config.json"))
   257→   257→}
   258→   258→
   259→   259→module "landing_zone" {
   260→   260→  source   = "../../../../modules/gcp/landing-zone"
   261→   261→  vpc_name = local.config.landing_zone.vpc_name
   262→   262→}
   263→   263→```
   264→   264→
   265→   265→### Environment Differences
   266→   266→
   267→   267→| Setting | Dev | QA | Prod |
   268→   268→|---------|-----|-----|------|
   269→   269→| Flow logs | 50% sampling | 50% sampling | 100% sampling |
   270→   270→| Node pool min nodes | 1 | 1 | 2 |
   271→   271→| Deletion protection | false | false | true |
   272→   272→| Kong replicas | 2 | 2 | 3 |
   273→   273→| VPC Service Controls | false | false | true |
   274→   274→
   275→   275→---
   276→   276→
   277→   277→## Your First Deployment
   278→   278→
   279→   279→### Step 0: Bootstrap (One-time)
   280→   280→
   281→   281→```bash
   282→   282→cd terraform/environments/bootstrap
   283→   283→cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars
   284→   284→# Edit terraform.tfvars with your organization values
   285→   285→
   286→   286→terraform init
   287→   287→terraform apply
   288→   288→```
   289→   289→
   290→   290→### Step 1: Deploy Network
   291→   291→
   292→   292→```bash
   293→   293→cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   294→   294→
   295→   295→terraform init
   296→   296→terraform plan
   297→   297→terraform apply
   298→   298→# Takes 3-5 minutes
   299→   299→```
   300→   300→
   301→   301→**Verify:**
   302→   302→```bash
   303→   303→gcloud compute networks describe kix-dev-vpc \
   304→   304→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-network
   305→   305→```
   306→   306→
   307→   307→### Step 2: Deploy GKE
   308→   308→
   309→   309→```bash
   310→   310→cd ../gke
   311→   311→
   312→   312→terraform init
   313→   313→terraform plan
   314→   314→terraform apply
   315→   315→# Takes 15-20 minutes
   316→   316→```
   317→   317→
   318→   318→**Verify:**
   319→   319→```bash
   320→   320→gcloud container clusters get-credentials kix-dev-cluster \
   321→   321→  --region=europe-west1 \
   322→   322→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke
   323→   323→
   324→   324→kubectl cluster-info
   325→   325→kubectl get nodes
   326→   326→```
   327→   327→
   328→   328→### Step 3: Deploy Kubernetes Platform
   329→   329→
   330→   330→```bash
   331→   331→cd ../../kubernetes/platform
   332→   332→
   333→   333→terraform init
   334→   334→terraform plan
   335→   335→terraform apply
   336→   336→```
   337→   337→
   338→   338→**Verify:**
   339→   339→```bash
   340→   340→kubectl get namespaces
   341→   341→kubectl get pods -n kong
   342→   342→```
   343→   343→
   344→   344→### Cleanup (Optional)
   345→   345→
   346→   346→Destroy in reverse order:
   347→   347→```bash
   348→   348→cd terraform/environments/dev/kubernetes/platform && terraform destroy
   349→   349→cd ../../gcp/gke && terraform destroy
   350→   350→cd ../network && terraform destroy
   351→   351→```
   352→   352→

   354→   354→
   355→   355→## Terraform Development Standards
   356→   356→
   357→   357→### Module Structure
   358→   358→
   359→   359→Every module MUST include:
   360→   360→
   361→   361→```
   362→   362→module-name/
   363→   363→+-- main.tf           # Resource definitions
   364→   364→+-- variables.tf      # Input variables with descriptions
   365→   365→+-- outputs.tf        # Output values with descriptions
   366→   366→+-- versions.tf       # Provider version constraints
   367→   367→+-- README.md         # Documentation
   368→   368→+-- examples/         # Working examples
   369→   369→```
   370→   370→
   371→   371→### Variable Naming Conventions
   372→   372→
   373→   373→| Pattern | Use Case | Example |
   374→   374→|---------|----------|---------|
   375→   375→| `enable_*` | Feature flags | `enable_versioning`, `enable_auth` |
   376→   376→| `create_*` | Resource creation | `create_service_account` |
   377→   377→| `*_config` | Configuration objects | `maintenance_config`, `logging_config` |
   378→   378→| `*_policy` | Policy definitions | `retention_policy` |
   379→   379→
   380→   380→**Correct:**
   381→   381→```hcl
   382→   382→variable "enable_versioning" {
   383→   383→  type        = bool
   384→   384→  default     = true
   385→   385→  description = "Enable object versioning for the bucket"
   386→   386→}
   387→   387→
   388→   388→variable "maintenance_config" {
   389→   389→  type = object({
   390→   390→    day  = string
   391→   391→    hour = number
   392→   392→  })
   393→   393→  description = "Maintenance window configuration"
   394→   394→}
   395→   395→```
   396→   396→
   397→   397→**Incorrect:**
   398→   398→```hcl
   399→   399→variable "auth_enabled" { ... }      # Use enable_* prefix
   400→   400→variable "maintenance_policy" { ... } # Use *_config suffix
   401→   401→```
   402→   402→
   403→   403→### Required Variables (All Modules)
   404→   404→
   405→   405→| Variable | Type | Description |
   406→   406→|----------|------|-------------|
   407→   407→| `project_id` | string | GCP project ID |
   408→   408→| `environment` | string | Environment name (dev, qa, prod, lab) |
   409→   409→| `cost_center` | string | Cost center for billing |
   410→   410→
   411→   411→### Variable Validation
   412→   412→
   413→   413→```hcl
   414→   414→variable "environment" {
   415→   415→  type        = string
   416→   416→  description = "Environment name"
   417→   417→
   418→   418→  validation {
   419→   419→    condition     = contains(["dev", "qa", "prod", "lab", "shared"], var.environment)
   420→   420→    error_message = "Environment must be one of: dev, qa, prod, lab, shared"
   421→   421→  }
   422→   422→}
   423→   423→```
   424→   424→
   425→   425→### README Standards
   426→   426→
   427→   427→All module READMEs MUST include:
   428→   428→- Overview and architecture
   429→   429→- Usage examples (basic and production)
   430→   430→- **Security Requirements section** (mandatory)
   431→   431→- Inputs/Outputs tables
   432→   432→- Document metadata footer
   433→   433→
   434→   434→### Common Patterns
   435→   435→
   436→   436→**Use for_each:**
   437→   437→```hcl
   438→   438→resource "google_storage_bucket" "buckets" {
   439→   439→  for_each = toset(["documents", "artifacts", "logs"])
   440→   440→  name     = "${var.usecase_name}-${each.value}-${var.environment}"
   441→   441→}
   442→   442→```
   443→   443→
   444→   444→**Use locals for computed values:**
   445→   445→```hcl
   446→   446→locals {
   447→   447→  project_id = "kix-${var.environment}-${var.function}"
   448→   448→  common_labels = {
   449→   449→    environment = var.environment
   450→   450→    managed_by  = "terraform"
   451→   451→  }
   452→   452→}
   453→   453→```
   454→   454→
   455→   455→### Pre-Commit Checklist
   456→   456→
   457→   457→```bash
   458→   458→terraform fmt -recursive
   459→   459→terraform validate
   460→   460→terraform plan -out=tfplan
   461→   461→terraform-docs markdown . > README.md
   462→   462→```
   463→   463→
   464→   464→---

   494→   494→
   495→   495→## Deploying Infrastructure Changes
   496→   496→
   497→   497→Changes to infrastructure follow a **controlled deployment process** with manual approvals for production.
   498→   498→
   499→   499→### Overview
   500→   500→
   501→   501→```
   502→   502→Feature Branch → PR Validation → Merge to Main → Manual Deploy
   503→   503→    (fast)         (~10 min)      (validates)     (controlled)
   504→   504→```
   505→   505→
   506→   506→### 1. Make Changes in Feature Branch
   507→   507→
   508→   508→```bash
   509→   509→# Create feature branch
   510→   510→git checkout -b feature/add-redis-instance
   511→   511→
   512→   512→# Make Terraform changes
   513→   513→cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/data
   514→   514→# Edit *.tf files
   515→   515→
   516→   516→# Validate locally
   517→   517→terraform fmt -recursive
   518→   518→terraform validate
   519→   519→terraform plan
   520→   520→```
   521→   521→
   522→   522→### 2. Open Pull Request
   523→   523→
   524→   524→Submit PR to `main` branch. PR validation runs automatically (~10 minutes):
   525→   525→
   526→   526→**What happens:**
   527→   527→- ✅ Terraform format check
   528→   528→- ✅ Security scan (tfsec)
   529→   529→- ✅ Terraform validate
   530→   530→- ✅ Generate plans for changed directories
   531→   531→- ✅ Run fast smoke tests (if modules changed)
   532→   532→- 💬 Plan summary posted as PR comment
   533→   533→
   534→   534→**Review the plan output:**
   535→   535→```
   536→   536→Plan: 2 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy
   537→   537→
   538→   538→+ google_redis_instance.cache
   539→   539→+ google_compute_firewall.redis_ingress
   540→   540→~ google_service_account.redis (labels)
   541→   541→```
   542→   542→
   543→   543→### 3. Merge to Main
   544→   544→
   545→   545→After PR approval, merge to `main`. **No automatic deployment occurs.**
   546→   546→
   547→   547→**What happens:**
   548→   548→- ✅ Main validation runs (validates all changes)
   549→   549→- ✅ Plans regenerated to prove deployability
   550→   550→- 🏷️ Release tagged with semantic version (e.g., v1.2.3)
   551→   551→- ℹ️ No infrastructure changes applied
   552→   552→
   553→   553→### 4. Deploy During Change Window
   554→   554→
   555→   555→Navigate to **Actions → Deploy Infrastructure** workflow and click **Run workflow**.
   556→   556→
   557→   557→**Configure deployment:**
   558→   558→
   559→   559→| Input | Description | Example |
   560→   560→|-------|-------------|---------|
   561→   561→| **environment** | Target environment | `dev`, `qa`, `prod`, `shared` |
   562→   562→| **scope** | What to deploy | `network`, `gke`, `data`, `kong`, `all` |
   563→   563→| **dry_run** | Plan only, no apply | `false` (deploy) or `true` (plan only) |
   564→   564→| **auto_approve** | Skip approval (dev only) | `true` (dev) or `false` (qa/prod) |
   565→   565→
   566→   566→**Example: Deploy Redis to Dev**
   567→   567→```yaml
   568→   568→environment: dev
   569→   569→scope: data
   570→   570→dry_run: false
   571→   571→auto_approve: true  # Dev allows auto-approve
   572→   572→```
   573→   573→
   574→   574→**Example: Deploy GKE to Production**
   575→   575→```yaml
   576→   576→environment: prod
   577→   577→scope: gke
   578→   578→dry_run: false
   579→   579→auto_approve: false  # Prod requires approval
   580→   580→```
   581→   581→
   582→   582→**Deployment flow:**
   583→   583→1. **Pre-flight checks** - Validates change window, permissions
   584→   584→2. **Validate** - Format, security scan
   585→   585→3. **Plan** - Generates fresh plan (catches drift)
   586→   586→4. **Approval** - Manual review and approval (QA/Prod)
   587→   587→5. **Apply** - Executes Terraform apply
   588→   588→6. **Verify** - Runs smoke tests
   589→   589→7. **Summary** - Posts deployment report
   590→   590→
   591→   591→### 5. Monitor Deployment
   592→   592→
   593→   593→Watch the workflow run:
   594→   594→- Green checkmarks indicate success
   595→   595→- Review plan output before approval
   596→   596→- Monitor apply progress
   597→   597→- Verify outputs after completion
   598→   598→
   599→   599→### Change Windows
   600→   600→
   601→   601→Infrastructure deployments are restricted by environment:
   602→   602→
   603→   603→| Environment | Change Window | Approval | Notes |
   604→   604→|-------------|---------------|----------|-------|
   605→   605→| **dev** | Anytime | Optional (auto-approve allowed) | Rapid iteration |
   606→   606→| **qa** | Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC) | Required | Avoid during testing |
   607→   607→| **prod** | **Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC only** | Required + change ticket | Restricted window |
   608→   608→| **shared** | Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC) | Required | Impacts all environments |
   609→   609→
   610→   610→**Production restrictions:**
   611→   611→- Deployments outside the window are **automatically blocked**
   612→   612→- Emergency hotfixes require manual approval bypass (see CICD_RUNBOOK.md)
   613→   613→- Change tickets must be referenced in deployment approval
   614→   614→
   615→   615→### Scope Mapping
   616→   616→
   617→   617→The `scope` input maps to Terraform directories:
   618→   618→
   619→   619→| Scope | Description | Directories |
   620→   620→|-------|-------------|-------------|
   621→   621→| `network` | VPC, subnets, firewall | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/network` |
   622→   622→| `security` | Security baseline | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/security` |
   623→   623→| `gke` | GKE cluster | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/gke` |
   624→   624→| `platform` | Namespaces, RBAC | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/platform` |
   625→   625→| `data` | Cloud SQL, Redis, GCS | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/data` |
   626→   626→| `kong` | Kong API Gateway | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/kong` |
   627→   627→| `gateway` | GKE Gateway | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/gateway` |
   628→   628→| `litellm` | LiteLLM proxy | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/litellm` |
   629→   629→| `argocd` | ArgoCD (shared only) | `terraform/environments/shared/kubernetes/argocd` |
   630→   630→| `all` | All of the above | Sequential deployment (network → security → gke → platform → data) |
   631→   631→
   632→   632→### Deployment Best Practices
   633→   633→
   634→   634→**Before deploying:**
   635→   635→- ✅ Verify plan output matches intent
   636→   636→- ✅ Check for unexpected resource destruction
   637→   637→- ✅ Ensure change window compliance (production)
   638→   638→- ✅ Notify team in #kix-platform-engineering
   639→   639→
   640→   640→**During deployment:**
   641→   641→- ✅ Monitor workflow progress
   642→   642→- ✅ Watch for errors in real-time
   643→   643→- ❌ Don't close browser until complete
   644→   644→
   645→   645→**After deployment:**
   646→   646→- ✅ Verify services are healthy
   647→   647→- ✅ Review Terraform outputs
   648→   648→- ✅ Monitor metrics for anomalies
   649→   649→- ✅ Update deployment log
   650→   650→
   651→   651→### Rollback Procedure
   652→   652→
   653→   653→If deployment causes issues:
   654→   654→
   655→   655→```bash
   656→   656→# Option 1: Revert code and redeploy
   657→   657→git revert <commit-hash>
   658→   658→git push origin main
   659→   659→# Then run deploy workflow with reverted code
   660→   660→
   661→   661→# Option 2: Manual Terraform rollback (emergency only)
   662→   662→cd terraform/environments/{env}/{scope}
   663→   663→terraform init
   664→   664→terraform state pull > backup.tfstate
   665→   665→# Manually fix state or apply reverted config
   666→   666→```
   667→   667→
   668→   668→### Advanced: Drift Detection
   669→   669→
   670→   670→Nightly workflow checks for infrastructure drift:
   671→   671→- Runs daily at 02:00 UTC
   672→   672→- Checks all environments and scopes
   673→   673→- Creates GitHub issues if drift detected
   674→   674→
   675→   675→**Manually trigger drift detection:**
   676→   676→```
   677→   677→Actions → Nightly Quality Checks → Run workflow
   678→   678→```
   679→   679→
   680→   680→### Troubleshooting Deployments
   681→   681→
   682→   682→See [CICD_RUNBOOK.md](./CICD_RUNBOOK.md) for detailed troubleshooting:
   683→   683→- Plan shows unexpected changes
   684→   684→- Apply fails with "resource already exists"
   685→   685→- Workflow stuck on approval
   686→   686→- Change window blocked production deployment
   687→   687→

   716→   716→## Troubleshooting
   717→   717→
   718→   718→### Error: "The caller does not have permission"
   719→   719→
   720→   720→```bash
   721→   721→gcloud auth list
   722→   722→gcloud config get-value account
   723→   723→# If wrong account:
   724→   724→gcloud auth login your.email@konecta-group.com
   725→   725→gcloud auth application-default login
   726→   726→```
   727→   727→
   728→   728→### Error: "Failed to save state: AccessDenied"
   729→   729→
   730→   730→```bash
   731→   731→gsutil ls gs://kd-tfstate-dev
   732→   732→terraform init -reconfigure
   733→   733→```
   734→   734→
   735→   735→### Error: "Quota exceeded"
   736→   736→
   737→   737→```bash
   738→   738→gcloud compute project-info describe \
   739→   739→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke \
   740→   740→  --format="table(quotas.metric,quotas.limit,quotas.usage)"
   741→   741→# Request quota increase in GCP Console
   742→   742→```
   743→   743→
   744→   744→### Error: "Timeout waiting for cluster"
   745→   745→
   746→   746→GKE clusters take 15-20 minutes. Check status:
   747→   747→```bash
   748→   748→gcloud container clusters describe kix-dev-cluster \
   749→   749→  --region=europe-west1 \
   750→   750→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke
   751→   751→```
   752→   752→
   753→   753→### State Lock Error
   754→   754→
   755→   755→```bash
   756→   756→# Only if certain no other process is running:
   757→   757→terraform force-unlock LOCK_ID
   758→   758→```
   759→   759→
   760→   760→### Debug Logging
   761→   761→
   762→   762→```bash
   763→   763→export TF_LOG=DEBUG
   764→   764→export TF_LOG_PATH=./terraform-debug.log
   765→   765→terraform plan
   766→   766→# Review logs
   767→   767→cat terraform-debug.log
   768→   768→unset TF_LOG TF_LOG_PATH
   769→   769→```
   770→   770→

   788→   788→### GCP Terms
   789→   789→
   790→   790→| Term | Definition |
   791→   791→|------|------------|

   793→   793→| **VPC Service Controls** | Security perimeter preventing data exfiltration |
   794→   794→| **Private Google Access** | Access Google APIs without public IPs |
   795→   795→| **Shared VPC** | VPC shared across multiple GCP projects |
   796→   796→
   797→   797→### Platform Terms
   798→   798→
   799→   799→| Term | Definition |
   800→   800→|------|------------|

   802→   802→| **Landing Zone** | Foundational networking and security infrastructure |
   803→   803→| **MCP Gateway** | Model Context Protocol gateway for AI tool integration |
   804→   804→| **Control Plane** | Routing layer deciding human/copilot/agent |

   807→   807→

    38→    38→
    39→    39→| Constraint | Technology | Rationale |
    40→    40→|------------|------------|-----------|
    41→    41→| **Cloud Platform** | Google Cloud Platform (GCP) | Enterprise standard, Konecta relationship |
    42→    42→| **Agent Framework** | CrewAI | Multi-agent orchestration, production-ready |
    43→    43→| **Voice AI** | ElevenLabs | Best-in-class voice synthesis and STT |

    50→    50→| **ENGAGE** | Conversational AI | CrewAI + LiteLLM |
    51→    51→| **KNOW** | Journey Analytics | Third-party solution (Q2 selection) |
    52→    52→| **KNOW** | Customer Profile | Cloud SQL + Redis (LaaS in Phase 2) |

    54→    54→| **GOVERN** | Compliance | Cloud Audit Logs |

    56→    56→| **ACT** | Agent Runtime | CrewAI on GKE |
    57→    57→| **ACT** | LLM Proxy | LiteLLM Proxy |
    58→    58→| **ACT** | Tool Integration | MCP Gateway |
    59→    59→| **ACT** | API Gateway | Kong API Gateway |
    60→    60→| **ACT** | Event Bus | Cloud Pub/Sub |

    64→    64→### Infrastructure Stack
    65→    65→
    66→    66→| Component | Technology | Configuration |
    67→    67→|-----------|------------|---------------|
    68→    68→| **Kubernetes** | GKE Autopilot | Auto-scaling, managed control plane |
    69→    69→| **Relational DB** | Cloud SQL PostgreSQL | HA with failover replica (LaaS in Phase 2) |
    70→    70→| **Cache** | Cloud Memorystore Redis | Standard tier |
    71→    71→| **Object Storage** | Google Cloud Storage | Regional, lifecycle policies |
    72→    72→| **Vector DB** | Qdrant (on GKE) | 3 replicas, persistent storage |
    73→    73→| **Data Lake** | Databricks LaaS | Phase 2 - analytics, ML integration |
    74→    74→| **Service Catalogue** | Backstage | Internal service discovery |
    75→    75→| **Identity** | Workload Identity | No service account keys |
    76→    76→| **Secrets** | Secret Manager + CSI Driver | Auto-rotation |
    77→    77→| **Encryption** | Cloud KMS (CMEK for Prod) | AES-256 |
    78→    78→| **Network** | VPC with Private Google Access | No public IPs |
    79→    79→| **WAF** | Cloud Armor | DDoS protection |
    80→    80→| **Metrics** | Cloud Monitoring | Custom dashboards |
    81→    81→| **Logging** | Cloud Logging | 30-day hot, 7-year archive |
    82→    82→| **Tracing** | Cloud Trace + OpenTelemetry | Distributed tracing |
    83→    83→| **GitOps** | ArgoCD | Multi-cluster CD, App-of-Apps, Image Updater |
    84→    84→| **CI/CD** | GitHub Actions | Continuous integration and deployment pipelines |

   194→   194→### Component Responsibilities
   195→   195→

   197→   197→|-----------|-----------|---------|-------------------|
   198→   198→| **Kong Gateway** | `kong` | External 3rd party API abstraction ONLY | All use case apps |

   206→   206→
   207→   207→## GKE Cluster Design
   208→   208→
   209→   209→### Architecture Decision: Kubernetes over Cloud Run
   210→   210→
   211→   211→After careful analysis, **Kubernetes namespaces within the same GKE cluster** is the deployment target for all workloads.
   212→   212→
   213→   213→| Factor | Cloud Run | Kubernetes | Winner |
   214→   214→|--------|-----------|------------|--------|
   215→   215→| **Internal Latency** | Cross-service via VPC connector (~5-10ms) | Pod-to-pod via cluster network (<1ms) | **K8s** |
   216→   216→| **LiteLLM Access** | Requires private endpoint exposure | Direct ClusterIP service | **K8s** |
   217→   217→| **CrewAI Integration** | Separate deployment, complex orchestration | Same namespace, shared resources | **K8s** |
   218→   218→| **Network Policies** | VPC-level only | Fine-grained pod-level | **K8s** |
   219→   219→| **Operational Complexity** | Simpler per-service | Single cluster management | **K8s** |
   220→   220→
   221→   221→**Critical factors favoring Kubernetes:**
   222→   222→
   223→   223→1. **Low-Latency LLM Access**: CrewAI agents frequently call LiteLLM. In-cluster communication (<1ms) vs Cloud Run to GKE (5-10ms) significantly impacts response times.
   224→   224→
   225→   225→2. **Unified Observability**: Single cluster means unified metrics, traces, and logs.
   226→   226→
   227→   227→3. **Network Isolation**: Kubernetes Network Policies provide pod-level isolation.
   228→   228→
   229→   229→4. **Operational Consistency**: Single operational model (kubectl, ArgoCD, Helm). ArgoCD runs on a dedicated shared cluster and manages deployments across all environment clusters via GitOps.
   230→   230→
   231→   231→### GKE Gateway API Architecture
   232→   232→
   233→   233→The platform uses the **Kubernetes Gateway API** with GKE's managed implementation:
   234→   234→
   235→   235→| Component | Resource | Purpose |
   236→   236→|-----------|----------|---------|
   237→   237→| **GatewayClass** | `gke-l7-global-external-managed` | GKE-managed, creates Global External HTTPS LB |
   238→   238→| **Gateway** | `kix-platform-gateway` | Shared entry point, defines listeners (HTTP/HTTPS) |
   239→   239→| **HTTPRoute** | Per-application | Routes traffic based on hostname to backend services |
   240→   240→| **GCPBackendPolicy** | Per-backend | Attaches Cloud Armor, configures health checks |
   241→   241→
   242→   242→**Benefits of Gateway API over Ingress:**
   243→   243→- **Multi-tenant friendly**: Teams create HTTPRoutes in their own namespaces
   244→   244→- **Scalable**: Add applications without modifying central infrastructure
   245→   245→- **Future-proof**: Gateway API is the Kubernetes standard
   246→   246→- **Flexible**: Supports advanced routing, traffic splitting, header manipulation
   247→   247→
   248→   248→---
   249→   249→
   250→   250→## Namespace Organization
   251→   251→
   252→   252→### Namespace Taxonomy
   253→   253→
   254→   254→```
   255→   255→GKE Cluster
   256→   256→+-- Platform Namespaces (managed by platform team)
   257→   257→|   +-- kong                      # Kong API Gateway (external APIs only)
   258→   258→|   +-- litellm                   # LiteLLM unified LLM proxy
   259→   259→|   +-- monitoring                # Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo
   260→   260→|   +-- cert-manager              # TLS certificate management
   261→   261→|   +-- external-secrets          # Secret Manager sync
   262→   262→|
   263→   263→+-- Shared Platform Cluster (kd-ix-eur-shr-platform)
   264→   264→|   +-- argocd                    # ArgoCD server, controller, repo-server
   265→   265→|   |   +-- ApplicationSet controller (auto-generate apps)
   266→   266→|   |   +-- Image Updater (watch Artifact Registry)
   267→   267→|   |   +-- Notifications (Google Chat)
   268→   268→|   +-- Manages all environment clusters via GitOps
   269→   269→|
   270→   270→+-- Use Case Namespaces (defined in config.json)
   271→   271→    +-- autopilot-scheduling-{env}
   272→   272→    |   +-- Use case application (FastAPI/Flask)
   273→   273→    |   +-- CrewAI agent deployment
   274→   274→    |   +-- Per-use-case Cloud SQL instance
   275→   275→    |   +-- Per-use-case GCS buckets
   276→   276→    |   +-- Per-use-case Pub/Sub topics
   277→   277→    |
   278→   278→    +-- autopilot-outbound-{env}
   279→   279→    +-- autopilot-inbound-{env}
   280→   280→    +-- customer-zero-{env}
   281→   281→```
   282→   282→
   283→   283→### Environment Differentiation
   284→   284→
   285→   285→Settings vary by environment via `config.json`:
   286→   286→
   287→   287→| Setting | Dev | QA | Prod |
   288→   288→|---------|-----|-----|------|
   289→   289→| `cloud_sql.availability_type` | ZONAL | ZONAL | REGIONAL |
   290→   290→| `cloud_sql.deletion_protection` | false | false | true |
   291→   291→| `cloud_sql.point_in_time_recovery` | false | false | true |
   292→   292→| `gcs.force_destroy` | true | true | false |
   293→   293→| `namespace.network_isolation.allow_egress_internet` | true | true | false |
   294→   294→| `litellm.replicas` | 1 | 2 | 3 |
   295→   295→| `kong_gateway.enable_admin_api` | true | true | false |
   296→   296→
   297→   297→---
   298→   298→
   299→   299→## Network Traffic Flows
   300→   300→
   301→   301→### Flow 1: External User Request (via GKE Gateway)
   302→   302→
   303→   303→```
   304→   304→Internet -> GKE Gateway (Global HTTPS LB) -> Cloud Armor -> HTTPRoute
   305→   305→                                                              |
   306→   306→                                                              v
   307→   307→                                              +------------------------------+
   308→   308→                                              | Host-based routing:          |
   309→   309→                                              | api.kix... -> Kong proxy     |
   310→   310→                                              | app1.kix... -> Direct to App |
   311→   311→                                              +------------------------------+
   312→   312→```
   313→   313→
   314→   314→### Flow 2: Use Case App -> LLM Request
   315→   315→
   316→   316→```
   317→   317→Use Case App -> CrewAI Agent -> LiteLLM Service -> Cloud NAT -> LLM Provider
   318→   318→(namespace)    (same ns)       (litellm ns)       (egress)     (OpenAI/etc)
   319→   319→
   320→   320→Path: ClusterIP -> ClusterIP -> NAT Gateway -> Internet
   321→   321→Latency: <1ms -> <1ms -> ~50-200ms
   322→   322→```
   323→   323→
   324→   324→### Flow 3: Use Case App -> External API (Salesforce, ElevenLabs)
   325→   325→
   326→   326→```
   327→   327→Use Case App -> Kong Gateway -> Cloud NAT -> External Service
   328→   328→(namespace)    (kong ns)       (egress)     (Salesforce/etc)
   329→   329→
   330→   330→Kong handles:
   331→   331→- Credential injection (API keys from Secret Manager)
   332→   332→- Rate limiting per use case
   333→   333→- Request/response transformation
   334→   334→- Circuit breaking and retries
   335→   335→- Logging and metrics
   336→   336→```
   337→   337→
   338→   338→### Flow 4: Use Case App -> Data Services
   339→   339→
   340→   340→```
   341→   341→Use Case App -> Cloud SQL (Private IP)
   342→   342→            -> Memorystore Redis (Private IP)
   343→   343→            -> GCS (Private Google Access)
   344→   344→            -> Pub/Sub (Private Google Access)
   345→   345→
   346→   346→All data services accessed via private networking, no public internet.
   347→   347→```
   348→   348→
   349→   349→### Flow 5: Internal Service Discovery
   350→   350→
   351→   351→Services discover each other via Kubernetes DNS:
   352→   352→
   353→   353→| Service | Endpoint |
   354→   354→|---------|----------|
   355→   355→| LiteLLM | `litellm.litellm.svc.cluster.local:80` |
   356→   356→| Kong Proxy | `kong-proxy.kong.svc.cluster.local:80` |
   357→   357→| Prometheus | `prometheus.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:9090` |
   358→   358→
   359→   359→---
   360→   360→
   361→   361→## Service Communication Patterns
   362→   362→
   363→   363→### Use Case App -> LiteLLM
   364→   364→
   365→   365→```python
   366→   366→from openai import OpenAI
   367→   367→
   368→   368→client = OpenAI(
   369→   369→    base_url="http://litellm.litellm.svc.cluster.local:80/v1",
   370→   370→    api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_API_KEY"]
   371→   371→)
   372→   372→
   373→   373→response = client.chat.completions.create(
   374→   374→    model="gpt-4",  # Or "claude-3", "gemini-pro" - LiteLLM routes
   375→   375→    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
   376→   376→)
   377→   377→```
   378→   378→
   379→   379→### Use Case App -> Kong (External APIs)
   380→   380→
   381→   381→```python
   382→   382→import requests
   383→   383→
   384→   384→response = requests.get(
   385→   385→    "http://kong-proxy.kong.svc.cluster.local/salesforce/services/data/v57.0",
   386→   386→    headers={
   387→   387→        "X-Use-Case-Key": os.environ["KONG_API_KEY"],
   388→   388→        "X-Use-Case": "autopilot-scheduling"
   389→   389→    }
   390→   390→)
   391→   391→# Kong injects Salesforce OAuth token automatically
   392→   392→```
   393→   393→
   394→   394→### CrewAI Agent -> Tools
   395→   395→
   396→   396→| Tool Type | Path |
   397→   397→|-----------|------|
   398→   398→| LLM | Via LiteLLM (OpenAI-compatible API) |
   399→   399→| Salesforce | Via Kong -> Salesforce |
   400→   400→| ElevenLabs | Via Kong -> ElevenLabs |
   401→   401→| MCP Tools | Via MCP Gateway (future) |
   402→   402→| Database | Direct to Cloud SQL via SQLAlchemy |
   403→   403→| Cache | Direct to Redis via redis-py |
   404→   404→

   406→   406→
   407→   407→## Security Architecture
   408→   408→
   409→   409→### Security Layers
   410→   410→
   411→   411→```
   412→   412→+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
   413→   413→|                         SECURITY ARCHITECTURE                                 |
   414→   414→+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
   415→   415→
   416→   416→NETWORK SECURITY
   417→   417→- Private GKE cluster (no public node IPs)
   418→   418→- Cloud Armor WAF + DDoS protection at ingress
   419→   419→- Network Policies for pod-to-pod isolation
   420→   420→- Cloud NAT for controlled egress
   421→   421→- VPC Service Controls (Production only)
   422→   422→
   423→   423→IDENTITY & ACCESS
   424→   424→- Workload Identity for all GCP access (NO service account keys)
   425→   425→- Per-use-case GCP service accounts with least privilege
   426→   426→- Kubernetes RBAC for namespace isolation
   427→   427→- Kong API keys for use case identification
   428→   428→- LiteLLM API keys for LLM access control
   429→   429→
   430→   430→SECRETS MANAGEMENT
   431→   431→- Secret Manager as source of truth
   432→   432→- External Secrets Operator for K8s sync
   433→   433→- No secrets in Git, no secrets in environment variables at build time
   434→   434→- Automatic rotation (90-day policy)
   435→   435→
   436→   436→DATA PROTECTION
   437→   437→- Encryption at rest (Google-managed, CMEK for Prod)
   438→   438→- TLS 1.3 in transit
   439→   439→- Private Google Access for GCP services
   440→   440→- Data residency: EU only (europe-west1, europe-west4)
   441→   441→```
   442→   442→
   443→   443→### Workload Identity Configuration
   444→   444→
   445→   445→```hcl
   446→   446→# GCP Service Account for the use case
   447→   447→resource "google_service_account" "use_case" {
   448→   448→  project      = var.project_id
   449→   449→  account_id   = "${var.use_case_name}-app"
   450→   450→  display_name = "Use Case: ${var.use_case_name}"
   451→   451→}
   452→   452→
   453→   453→# Workload Identity binding
   454→   454→resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "workload_identity" {
   455→   455→  service_account_id = google_service_account.use_case.name
   456→   456→  role               = "roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser"
   457→   457→
   458→   458→  members = [
   459→   459→    "serviceAccount:${var.project_id}.svc.id.goog[${var.namespace}/${var.k8s_service_account}]"
   460→   460→  ]
   461→   461→}
   462→   462→
   463→   463→# IAM roles for the use case (least privilege)
   464→   464→resource "google_project_iam_member" "secret_accessor" {
   465→   465→  project = var.project_id
   466→   466→  role    = "roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"
   467→   467→  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.use_case.email}"
   468→   468→
   469→   469→  condition {
   470→   470→    title       = "Use case secrets only"
   471→   471→    expression  = "resource.name.startsWith('projects/${var.project_id}/secrets/${var.use_case_name}-')"
   472→   472→  }
   473→   473→}
   474→   474→```
   475→   475→
   476→   476→### Network Policy Example
   477→   477→
   478→   478→```yaml
   479→   479→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   480→   480→kind: NetworkPolicy
   481→   481→metadata:
   482→   482→  name: use-case-default
   483→   483→  namespace: autopilot-scheduling-dev
   484→   484→spec:
   485→   485→  podSelector: {}
   486→   486→  policyTypes:
   487→   487→    - Ingress
   488→   488→    - Egress
   489→   489→
   490→   490→  ingress:
   491→   491→    # Allow from Kong ingress controller
   492→   492→    - from:
   493→   493→        - namespaceSelector:
   494→   494→            matchLabels:
   495→   495→              app.kubernetes.io/component: api-gateway
   496→   496→      ports:
   497→   497→        - protocol: TCP
   498→   498→          port: 8080
   499→   499→
   500→   500→  egress:
   501→   501→    # Allow to LiteLLM
   502→   502→    - to:
   503→   503→        - namespaceSelector:
   504→   504→            matchLabels:
   505→   505→              app.kubernetes.io/component: llm-proxy
   506→   506→      ports:
   507→   507→        - protocol: TCP
   508→   508→          port: 80
   509→   509→
   510→   510→    # Allow to Kong for external API calls
   511→   511→    - to:
   512→   512→        - namespaceSelector:
   513→   513→            matchLabels:
   514→   514→              app.kubernetes.io/component: api-gateway
   515→   515→      ports:
   516→   516→        - protocol: TCP
   517→   517→          port: 80
   518→   518→
   519→   519→    # Allow to Cloud SQL (private IP range)
   520→   520→    - to:
   521→   521→        - ipBlock:
   522→   522→            cidr: 10.1.0.0/24
   523→   523→      ports:
   524→   524→        - protocol: TCP
   525→   525→          port: 5432
   526→   526→
   527→   527→    # Allow to GCP APIs via Private Google Access
   528→   528→    - to:
   529→   529→        - ipBlock:
   530→   530→            cidr: 199.36.153.4/30
   531→   531→      ports:
   532→   532→        - protocol: TCP
   533→   533→          port: 443
   534→   534→
   535→   535→    # Allow DNS resolution
   536→   536→    - to:
   537→   537→        - namespaceSelector: {}
   538→   538→          podSelector:
   539→   539→            matchLabels:
   540→   540→              k8s-app: kube-dns
   541→   541→      ports:
   542→   542→        - protocol: UDP
   543→   543→          port: 53
   544→   544→```

   592→   592→### State Management
   593→   593→
   594→   594→Each environment uses **separate state files per service layer**:
   595→   595→
   596→   596→```
   597→   597→gs://kd-tfstate-{env}/
   598→   598→+-- gcp/network/          # VPC, NAT, DNS, Firewall
   599→   599→+-- gcp/gke/              # GKE cluster and node pools
   600→   600→+-- gcp/data/             # Cloud SQL, GCS, Pub/Sub per use case
   601→   601→+-- kubernetes/platform/  # Kong, LiteLLM, namespaces, RBAC
   602→   602→
   603→   603→gs://kd-tfstate-shared/   # Shared services
   604→   604→+-- gcp/network/          # Shared VPC
   605→   605→+-- gcp/security/         # Cloud Armor WAF
   606→   606→+-- gcp/gke/              # Shared platform cluster
   607→   607→+-- gcp/iam/              # Service accounts, Workload Identity
   608→   608→+-- kubernetes/argocd/    # ArgoCD deployment + GKE Gateway
   609→   609→+-- kubernetes/argocd-bootstrap/  # App-of-Apps, AppProjects
   610→   610→```
   611→   611→
   612→   612→**Apply Order (per env):** `network -> gke -> data -> kubernetes/platform`
   613→   613→
   614→   614→**Apply Order (shared):** `network -> security -> gke -> iam -> argocd -> argocd-bootstrap`
   615→   615→

   654→   654→
   655→   655→## Technology Decision Records
   656→   656→
   657→   657→### TDR-001: LiteLLM Proxy for LLM Gateway
   658→   658→
   659→   659→**Decision:** Use LiteLLM Proxy as the LLM gateway instead of direct Vertex AI calls.
   660→   660→
   661→   661→**Rationale:**
   662→   662→- Multi-provider abstraction (future flexibility)
   663→   663→- Built-in load balancing and fallback
   664→   664→- Cost tracking and budget enforcement
   665→   665→- 8ms P95 latency at 1k RPS
   666→   666→- OpenAI-compatible API format
   667→   667→
   668→   668→**Trade-offs:**
   669→   669→- Additional operational component
   670→   670→- Slight latency overhead (~5ms)
   671→   671→
   672→   672→### TDR-002: MCP for Tool Integration
   673→   673→
   674→   674→**Decision:** Use MCP (Model Context Protocol) for all tool integrations.
   675→   675→
   676→   676→**Rationale:**
   677→   677→- Industry standard (Anthropic, OpenAI adopted)
   678→   678→- Structured tool/resource/prompt primitives
   679→   679→- Async task support (2025 spec)
   680→   680→- Security model with server identity
   681→   681→- Growing ecosystem of pre-built servers
   682→   682→
   683→   683→**Trade-offs:**
   684→   684→- Newer protocol (less mature than REST)
   685→   685→- Requires MCP gateway development
   686→   686→
   687→   687→### TDR-003: Backstage for Service Catalogue
   688→   688→
   689→   689→**Decision:** Use Backstage as internal service catalogue for use case discovery.
   690→   690→
   691→   691→**Rationale:**
   692→   692→- Open-source with strong community (Spotify-backed, CNCF)
   693→   693→- Software catalogue for service discovery
   694→   694→- Provides schema for use case teams to understand available services
   695→   695→- Tech docs aggregation
   696→   696→- Plugin architecture for extensibility
   697→   697→
   698→   698→**Trade-offs:**
   699→   699→- Requires hosting and maintenance
   700→   700→- Initial setup and configuration effort
   701→   701→
   702→   702→**Note:** Agent-to-agent communication is handled natively by CrewAI framework.
   703→   703→
   704→   704→### TDR-004: Kong API Gateway
   705→   705→
   706→   706→**Decision:** Use Kong API Gateway instead of Apigee.
   707→   707→
   708→   708→**Rationale:**
   709→   709→- Kubernetes-native deployment
   710→   710→- AI-specific features (AI Proxy, MCP bridge)
   711→   711→- 1000+ plugins available
   712→   712→- Lower cost than Apigee
   713→   713→- Declarative GitOps-friendly configuration
   714→   714→
   715→   715→**Trade-offs:**
   716→   716→- Self-managed (vs. Apigee fully managed)
   717→   717→- Requires Kong expertise
   718→   718→
   719→   719→### TDR-005: ArgoCD for GitOps Continuous Delivery
   720→   720→
   721→   721→**Decision:** Use ArgoCD as the GitOps continuous delivery engine, deployed on a shared platform cluster.
   722→   722→
   723→   723→**Rationale:**
   724→   724→- GitOps workflow: Git as single source of truth for deployments
   725→   725→- Multi-cluster management from a single control plane
   726→   726→- ApplicationSet controller for templated app generation
   727→   727→- Image Updater watches Artifact Registry for new images
   728→   728→- Dex integration for Google OIDC authentication
   729→   729→- Declarative, auditable deployment history
   730→   730→
   731→   731→**Trade-offs:**
   732→   732→- Requires dedicated shared GKE cluster
   733→   733→- Additional operational component to manage
   734→   734→- Cross-project IAM needed for multi-cluster access
   735→   735→
   736→   736→### TDR-006: Qdrant for Vector Database
   737→   737→
   738→   738→**Decision:** Use Qdrant instead of Vertex AI Matching Engine.
   739→   739→
   740→   740→**Rationale:**
   741→   741→- Open-source with commercial support
   742→   742→- High performance benchmarks
   743→   743→- Kubernetes-native deployment
   744→   744→- No vendor lock-in
   745→   745→
   746→   746→**Trade-offs:**
   747→   747→- Self-managed (vs. managed Vertex AI)
   748→   748→- Operational overhead
   749→   749→

     9→     9→## Executive Summary
    10→    10→
    11→    11→This document defines the strategic vision, architecture, and operating model for the **KIX Platform** (Konecta Intelligence eXchange) — the orchestration platform that enables Konecta to deliver **Orchestrated Outcomes, not just operations**.
    12→    12→
    13→    13→**Platform Mission:** Provide a production-ready, enterprise-grade platform that abstracts infrastructure complexity and enables use case teams to focus on delivering business value through AI agents.
    14→    14→
    15→    15→**End-State Vision:**
    16→    16→> "The right work, done by the right resource, at the right moment."
    17→    17→
    18→    18→**Key Principles:**
    19→    19→- **Core Services:** Use case developers consume standardised services
    20→    20→- **Security-First:** Zero-trust architecture with comprehensive audit trails
    21→    21→- **Scalable:** Multi-tenant isolation supporting multiple use cases
    22→    22→- **Compliant:** GDPR, EU AI Act, and enterprise security standards
    23→    23→- **Observable:** Full visibility into application and infrastructure health

    41→    41→## Strategic Alignment
    42→    42→
    43→    43→### CIO Vision: Orchestrated Outcomes
    44→    44→
    45→    45→| Element | Vision | KIX Implementation |
    46→    46→|---------|--------|-------------------|
    47→    47→| **The Challenge** | Cost reduction alone is insufficient | Outcome-based pricing models |
    48→    48→| **The Strategy** | Move beyond static execution | Dynamic orchestration engine |
    49→    49→| **The Solution** | Konecta Control Plane | KIX Platform with three execution engines |
    50→    50→| **The Result** | Continuous optimisation | Real-time routing, learning, and improvement |
    51→    51→
    52→    52→### Critical Understanding
    53→    53→
    54→    54→**KIX = Control Plane + Core Components**
    55→    55→
    56→    56→KIX is not separate from the Control Plane — KIX IS the Control Plane plus the foundational infrastructure that powers it. The Control Plane is foundational from MVP1; what evolves is its sophistication.
    57→    57→
    58→    58→| Part | What It Does | Always Present |
    59→    59→|------|--------------|----------------|
    60→    60→| **Control Plane** | Orchestrates work across Human Experts, AI Copilots, and Autonomous Agents | Foundational |
    61→    61→| **Core Components** | 5 layers (ENGAGE, KNOW, GOVERN, CONNECT, ACT) providing platform services | Foundational |

   170→   170→
   171→   171→## The Three Execution Engines
   172→   172→
   173→   173→The Control Plane orchestrates three distinct execution engines:
   174→   174→
   175→   175→| Engine | Role | When Used | KIX Component |
   176→   176→|--------|------|-----------|---------------|
   177→   177→| **Human Experts** | Empathy, critical thinking, exception handling | Sensitive, complex, high-value interactions | HITL Coordination Layer |
   178→   178→| **AI Copilots** | Augmentation, consistency, real-time guidance | Tech-enabled human delivery | Agent Assist Platform |
   179→   179→| **Autonomous Agents** | Event-driven, end-to-end execution | Routine tasks, instant resolution | CrewAI + ElevenLabs Runtime |
   180→   180→
   181→   181→### Engine 1: Human Experts
   182→   182→
   183→   183→**Purpose:** Handle exceptions AI cannot resolve, manage sensitive relationships, apply critical thinking.
   184→   184→
   185→   185→| Capability | Description | Technology |
   186→   186→|------------|-------------|------------|
   187→   187→| **Intelligent Queue** | AI-prioritised work distribution | Orchestration Engine + WFM |
   188→   188→| **Full Context** | Complete interaction history on handoff | Unified Profile + Session Memory |
   189→   189→| **Real-time Coaching** | AI suggestions during live interactions | Copilot Whisper Mode |
   190→   190→| **Post-call Summary** | Automated wrap-up and documentation | LLM-powered ACW |
   191→   191→| **Quality Assurance** | Automated QA scoring with human review | AI QA + Human Override |
   192→   192→
   193→   193→**Shift in Role:**
   194→   194→- **From:** Performing repetitive transactional tasks
   195→   195→- **To:** Solving novel problems and building relationships
   196→   196→
   197→   197→### Engine 2: AI Copilots
   198→   198→
   199→   199→**Purpose:** Augment human agents with real-time intelligence, ensuring consistency and compliance.
   200→   200→
   201→   201→| Capability | Description | Technology |
   202→   202→|------------|-------------|------------|
   203→   203→| **Next Best Action** | Context-aware recommendations | LLM + RAG Pipeline |
   204→   204→| **Knowledge Retrieval** | Instant access to relevant articles | Qdrant + Semantic Search |
   205→   205→| **Compliance Whisper** | Real-time regulatory guidance | Rules Engine + LLM |
   206→   206→| **Response Suggestions** | Draft replies for agent approval | LLM with tone matching |
   207→   207→| **Sentiment Alerts** | Early warning on customer frustration | Real-time Sentiment Analysis |
   208→   208→
   209→   209→**Deployment Modes:**
   210→   210→
   211→   211→| Mode | Description | Use Case |
   212→   212→|------|-------------|----------|
   213→   213→| **Sidebar** | Suggestions displayed alongside agent desktop | Desktop Integration |
   214→   214→| **Whisper** | Audio guidance during voice calls | Voice Copilot |
   215→   215→| **Overlay** | Pop-up recommendations on trigger events | Critical Alerts |
   216→   216→| **Ambient** | Background assistance, surfaces when needed | Always-on Support |
   217→   217→
   218→   218→### Engine 3: Autonomous Agents
   219→   219→
   220→   220→**Purpose:** Handle end-to-end tasks without human involvement, triggered by events and customer intent.
   221→   221→
   222→   222→| Capability | Description | Technology |
   223→   223→|------------|-------------|------------|
   224→   224→| **Voice Autopilot** | Full voice conversations | ElevenLabs Conversational AI |
   225→   225→| **Digital Autopilot** | Chat and messaging automation | CrewAI + Channel Hub |
   226→   226→| **Proactive Outreach** | Event-triggered outbound | CrewAI + Event Bus |
   227→   227→| **Multi-step Workflows** | Complex process automation | CrewAI Crews + MCP Tools |
   228→   228→| **Seamless Escalation** | Context-preserving handoff | HITL Coordination |
   229→   229→| **Self-improvement** | Learning from outcomes | Feedback Loop + Fine-tuning |
   230→   230→
   231→   231→**Autonomy Tiers:**
   232→   232→
   233→   233→| Tier | Description | Human Involvement | Example |
   234→   234→|------|-------------|-------------------|---------|
   235→   235→| **Supervised** | Human monitors all actions | High — approval required | Initial deployment |
   236→   236→| **Conditional** | Autonomous within defined bounds | Medium — exception handling | Scheduling, FAQ |
   237→   237→| **Assistive** | AI leads, human available | Low — optional review | Copilot Mode |
   238→   238→| **Full** | Fully autonomous, audit only | Minimal — post-hoc review | Simple bookings |
   239→   239→

   286→   286→| Component | End-State Capability | Technology |
