   288→   288→| **Agent Runtime** | Multi-agent orchestration | CrewAI on GKE |
   289→   289→| **LLM Gateway** | Multi-provider with fallback | LiteLLM Proxy |
   290→   290→| **MCP Gateway** | Tool integration hub | LiteLLM + Custom |
   291→   291→| **Knowledge Base** | RAG-enabled retrieval | Qdrant + LangChain |
   292→   292→| **Event Bus** | Async event processing | Cloud Pub/Sub |
   293→   293→| **Service Catalogue** | Internal service discovery | Backstage |
   294→   294→
   295→   295→---
   296→   296→
   297→   297→## Platform Services Catalog
   298→   298→
   299→   299→### Service Summary
   300→   300→
   301→   301→| Service Category | Key Technologies | Benefit |
   302→   302→|-----------------|------------------|---------|
   303→   303→| Identity & Access | Workload Identity, RBAC | Single Identity Platform consumable via API |
   304→   304→| Secrets Management | Secret Manager, CSI Driver | Secure, compliant secret and key management |
   305→   305→| Container Registry | Artifact Registry, Scanning | Secured, scanned and centralised |
   306→   306→| LLM Router + MCP Gateway | LiteLLM (Kubernetes) | Unified access layer for LLM providers AND MCP tools |
   307→   307→| External API Gateway | Kong (External APIs only) | Abstraction layer for third-party services |
   308→   308→| Databases | Cloud SQL PostgreSQL | Provisioned per use case with standardised security |
   309→   309→| Caching | Cloud Memorystore Redis | Provisioned per use case (also used for LLM caching) |
   310→   310→| Object Storage | GCS with lifecycle | Provisioned per use case with standardised security |
   311→   311→| Event Bus | Cloud Pub/Sub | Self-service publish/subscribe event bus |
   312→   312→| AI Framework | CrewAI (Kubernetes) | Agent orchestration deployed per use case namespace |
   313→   313→| Voice Services | ElevenLabs (via Kong) | External voice services through Kong gateway |
   314→   314→| Messaging | Channel Hub (via Kong) | Outbound messaging (SMS, Email, WhatsApp, Google Chat) |
   315→   315→| Observability | Cloud Monitoring, Logging, Trace | Automatic + custom metrics |
   316→   316→| Service Catalogue | Backstage | Internal portal for service discovery and documentation |
   317→   317→| GitOps / CD | ArgoCD (Kubernetes) | Multi-cluster continuous delivery via Git, App-of-Apps pattern |
   318→   318→| CI/CD | GitHub Actions | Standardised DevSecOps approach |
   319→   319→
   320→   320→### Key Highlights for Use Case Developers
   321→   321→
   322→   322→1. **No Infrastructure Management:** Platform handles all GCP resources, networking, security
   323→   323→2. **Workload Identity:** Never manage service account keys — automatic authentication
   324→   324→3. **LiteLLM for LLM + MCP Access:** Use OpenAI-compatible API to access any LLM provider AND MCP tools
   325→   325→4. **Kong for External APIs:** Access third-party services through Kong — credentials managed by platform
   326→   326→5. **CrewAI in Your Namespace:** AI agents deployed alongside your application for low-latency orchestration
   327→   327→6. **Multi-Tenant Isolation:** Your namespace is isolated with resource quotas and network policies
   328→   328→7. **Comprehensive Observability:** Metrics, logs, and traces automatically collected
   329→   329→8. **GitOps Deployment:** ArgoCD watches Git for changes and automatically syncs to clusters
   330→   330→9. **Backstage Service Catalogue:** Discover available services, APIs, agents, and documentation
   331→   331→
   332→   332→### Traffic Flow Summary
   333→   333→
   334→   334→| Communication | Path | Protocol |
   335→   335→|---------------|------|----------|
   336→   336→| App → LLM | `Use Case App → LiteLLM → Cloud NAT → LLM Provider` | HTTP (internal) → HTTPS |
   337→   337→| App → MCP Tools | `Use Case App → LiteLLM → MCP Services` | HTTP (internal) |
   338→   338→| App → External API | `Use Case App → Kong → Cloud NAT → External Service` | HTTP (internal) → HTTPS |
   339→   339→| App → Database | `Use Case App → Cloud SQL (Private IP)` | PostgreSQL over TLS |
   340→   340→| App → Cache | `Use Case App → Memorystore Redis (Private IP)` | Redis protocol |
   341→   341→
   342→   342→---

   344→   344→## GCP Operating Model
   345→   345→
   346→   346→### Organization Structure
   347→   347→
   348→   348→```
   349→   349→[Organization: konecta-group.com]
   350→   350→├── [Root Folder: Digital] ← DELEGATED TO OUR TEAM
   351→   351→│   ├── [Folder: Shared Services]
   352→   352→│   │   ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-shared-network]
   353→   353→│   │   ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-shared-security]
   354→   354→│   │   └── [Project: kd-ix-eur-shared-artifacts]
   355→   355→│   ├── [Folder: Lab] - isolated playground for new tech/services
   356→   356→│   │   └── [Project: kd-ix-eur-lab-*]
   357→   357→│   ├── [Folder: NonProd] - non production environments
   358→   358→│   │   ├── [Folder: Dev]

   360→   360→│   │   │   ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-dev-data]
   361→   361→│   │   │   └── [Project: kd-ix-eur-dev-security]
   362→   362→│   │   └── [Folder: QA]
   363→   363→│   │       ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-qa-gke]
   364→   364→│   │       ├── [Project: kd-ix-eur-qa-data]
   365→   365→│   │       └── [Project: kd-ix-eur-qa-security]
   366→   366→│   └── [Folder: Prod] - production environments

   371→   371→
   372→   372→### Delegation Model
   373→   373→
   374→   374→**What We Have Full Access To:**
   375→   375→- Create and delete folders within `Digital` folder
   376→   376→- Create and delete projects within our folder hierarchy
   377→   377→- Create and manage service accounts within our projects
   378→   378→- Create and manage guardrails and policies within our folder/projects
   379→   379→- Configure IAM policies within our folder/projects
   380→   380→- Deploy any GCP service within our projects
   381→   381→- Manage billing and budgets for our folder
   382→   382→- Configure network policies within our VPCs
   383→   383→
   384→   384→**What We Must Follow (Organization Policies):**
   385→   385→- Adhere to root level policies
   386→   386→- No public IP addresses — enforced via `constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess`
   387→   387→- Domain-restricted IAM — members must be from `konecta-group.com`
   388→   388→- No service account key downloads — Workload Identity only
   389→   389→- Audit logging mandatory — Admin Activity & Data Access logs enabled
   390→   390→- Data residency — Resources in EU regions only
   391→   391→
   392→   392→**What We Cannot Do:**
   393→   393→- Modify organization-level policies
   394→   394→- Access folders/projects outside our delegation
   395→   395→- Disable mandatory security controls
   396→   396→- Create resources in unapproved regions
   397→   397→- Share IAM permissions with external domains
   398→   398→
   399→   399→### Naming Conventions
   400→   400→

   404→   404→| Resources | `{usecase}-{resource}-{env}` | `autopilot-db-prod` |

     1→     1→# CI/CD Runbook
     2→     2→
     3→     3→This runbook provides operational guidance for the KIX Platform CI/CD pipelines.
     4→     4→
     5→     5→## Table of Contents
     6→     6→
     7→     7→1. [Pipeline Overview](#pipeline-overview)
     8→     8→2. [Deploying to Environments](#deploying-to-environments)
     9→     9→3. [Change Windows](#change-windows)
    10→    10→4. [Emergency Procedures](#emergency-procedures)
    11→    11→5. [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
    12→    12→6. [Workflow Reference](#workflow-reference)
    13→    13→
    14→    14→---
    15→    15→
    16→    16→## Pipeline Overview
    17→    17→
    18→    18→The KIX Platform uses a **task-based CI/CD architecture** with reusable workflows and manual deployment control.
    19→    19→
    20→    20→### Architecture Diagram
    21→    21→
    22→    22→```
    23→    23→┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    24→    24→│                    REUSABLE WORKFLOWS (Building Blocks)              │
    25→    25→├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    26→    26→│                                                                       │
    27→    27→│  terraform-validate.yml    Format, lint, init, validate, tfsec      │
    28→    28→│  terraform-plan.yml        Generate plan + summary/comment           │
    29→    29→│  terraform-apply.yml       Apply with approval gate                  │
    30→    30→│  terraform-test.yml        Run Terratest (fast or full suite)        │
    31→    31→│  terraform-drift.yml       Detect drift from state                   │
    32→    32→│                                                                       │
    33→    33→└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    34→    34→                                    ▲
    35→    35→                                    │ calls
    36→    36→                                    │
    37→    37→┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    38→    38→│                    ORCHESTRATION WORKFLOWS (Callers)                 │
    39→    39→├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    40→    40→│                                                                       │
    41→    41→│  pull-request.yml          Validates PRs (validate→plan→fast tests)  │
    42→    42→│  main-validation.yml       Proves main is deployable (validate→plan) │
    43→    43→│  deploy.yml                Manual deployment (plan→approve→apply)    │
    44→    44→│  nightly-quality.yml       Scheduled (full tests + drift detection)  │
    45→    45→│                                                                       │
    46→    46→└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    47→    47→```
    48→    48→
    49→    49→### Key Principles
    50→    50→
    51→    51→1. **Manual Deployments** - All applies require explicit workflow_dispatch trigger
    52→    52→2. **Fresh Plans** - Plans are generated immediately before apply (no stale artifacts)
    53→    53→3. **Independent Environments** - Dev, QA, Prod deploy separately
    54→    54→4. **Merge Validates, Doesn't Deploy** - Merging to main proves deployability without applying
    55→    55→5. **Controlled Change Windows** - Production deployments restricted to approved times
    56→    56→
    57→    57→---
    58→    58→
    59→    59→## Deploying to Environments
    60→    60→
    61→    61→### Prerequisites
    62→    62→
    63→    63→- Code merged to `main` branch
    64→    64→- Main validation passed (automatic on merge)
    65→    65→- Change window requirements met (for production)
    66→    66→- Required approvals obtained
    67→    67→
    68→    68→### Deployment Process
    69→    69→
    70→    70→#### 1. Navigate to Deploy Workflow
    71→    71→
    72→    72→1. Go to **Actions** tab in GitHub
    73→    73→2. Select **Deploy Infrastructure** workflow
    74→    74→3. Click **Run workflow** button
    75→    75→
    76→    76→#### 2. Configure Deployment
    77→    77→
    78→    78→Fill in the workflow inputs:
    79→    79→
    80→    80→| Input | Description | Options |
    81→    81→|-------|-------------|---------|
    82→    82→| **environment** | Target environment | dev, qa, prod, shared |
    83→    83→| **scope** | What to deploy | network, security, gke, platform, data, kong, gateway, litellm, argocd, all |
    84→    84→| **dry_run** | Plan only (no apply) | true/false (default: false) |
    85→    85→| **auto_approve** | Skip approval (dev only) | true/false (default: false) |
    86→    86→
    87→    87→**Example configurations:**
    88→    88→
    89→    89→```yaml
    90→    90→# Deploy Kong to dev (auto-approved)
    91→    91→environment: dev
    92→    92→scope: kong
    93→    93→dry_run: false
    94→    94→auto_approve: true
    95→    95→
    96→    96→# Review prod GKE plan (no deployment)
    97→    97→environment: prod
    98→    98→scope: gke
    99→    99→dry_run: true
   100→   100→auto_approve: false
   101→   101→
   102→   102→# Deploy all services to QA (requires approval)
   103→   103→environment: qa
   104→   104→scope: all
   105→   105→dry_run: false
   106→   106→auto_approve: false
   107→   107→```
   108→   108→
   109→   109→#### 3. Review Pre-flight Checks
   110→   110→
   111→   111→The workflow will:
   112→   112→- ✅ Validate environment and scope inputs
   113→   113→- ✅ Check change window (production only)
   114→   114→- ✅ Map scope to Terraform directories
   115→   115→- ✅ Verify auto-approve restrictions (dev only)
   116→   116→
   117→   117→#### 4. Review Plan Output
   118→   118→
   119→   119→The workflow generates a fresh Terraform plan:
   120→   120→- View plan summary in workflow logs
   121→   121→- Check resources to be added/changed/destroyed
   122→   122→- Verify expected changes match intent
   123→   123→
   124→   124→#### 5. Approve Deployment (if required)
   125→   125→
   126→   126→For QA and Prod environments:
   127→   127→1. GitHub will pause workflow for approval
   128→   128→2. Review plan output
   129→   129→3. Approve or reject deployment
   130→   130→4. Timeout: 30 days (configurable)
   131→   131→
   132→   132→For Dev environment with auto_approve=true:
   133→   133→- No approval gate (deployment proceeds automatically)
   134→   134→
   135→   135→#### 6. Monitor Deployment
   136→   136→
   137→   137→Watch the apply job progress:
   138→   138→- Terraform apply runs with `-auto-approve`
   139→   139→- Post-apply validation runs
   140→   140→- Outputs captured for reference
   141→   141→
   142→   142→#### 7. Verify Deployment
   143→   143→
   144→   144→Post-deployment checks:
   145→   145→- Smoke tests run automatically
   146→   146→- Review outputs in workflow summary
   147→   147→- Verify services are healthy
   148→   148→
   149→   149→### Scope Mapping
   150→   150→
   151→   151→| Scope | Directories (Dev/QA/Prod) | Order |
   152→   152→|-------|---------------------------|-------|
   153→   153→| `network` | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/network` | N/A |
   154→   154→| `security` | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/security` | N/A |
   155→   155→| `gke` | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/gke` | N/A |
   156→   156→| `platform` | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/platform` | N/A |
   157→   157→| `data` | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/data` | N/A |
   158→   158→| `kong` | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/kong` | N/A |
   159→   159→| `gateway` | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/gateway` | N/A |
   160→   160→| `litellm` | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/litellm` | N/A |
   161→   161→| `all` | All above in order | Sequential |
   162→   162→
   163→   163→**Shared environment special scopes:**
   164→   164→
   165→   165→| Scope | Directories (Shared) |
   166→   166→|-------|---------------------|
   167→   167→| `network` | `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/network` |
   168→   168→| `security` | `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/security` |
   169→   169→| `gke` | `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/gke` |
   170→   170→| `platform` | `terraform/environments/shared/kubernetes/platform` |
   171→   171→| `argocd` | `terraform/environments/shared/kubernetes/argocd`, `argocd-bootstrap` |
   172→   172→
   173→   173→---
   174→   174→
   175→   175→## Change Windows
   176→   176→
   177→   177→### Development (dev)
   178→   178→
   179→   179→- **When:** Anytime
   180→   180→- **Approval:** Auto-approve allowed
   181→   181→- **Restrictions:** None
   182→   182→- **Purpose:** Rapid iteration and testing
   183→   183→
   184→   184→### Quality Assurance (qa)
   185→   185→
   186→   186→- **When:** Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC, Mon-Fri)
   187→   187→- **Approval:** Manual approval required
   188→   188→- **Restrictions:** Avoid during active testing cycles
   189→   189→- **Purpose:** Controlled validation before production
   190→   190→
   191→   191→### Production (prod)
   192→   192→
   193→   193→- **When:** **Tuesday-Thursday, 20:00-23:00 UTC only**
   194→   194→- **Approval:** Manual approval required + change ticket
   195→   195→- **Restrictions:**
   196→   196→  - Outside change window: Deployment blocked automatically
   197→   197→  - Emergency exception: See [Emergency Procedures](#emergency-procedures)
   198→   198→- **Purpose:** Minimize risk to production services
   199→   199→
   200→   200→### Shared Services (shared)
   201→   201→
   202→   202→- **When:** Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC, Mon-Fri)
   203→   203→- **Approval:** Manual approval required
   204→   204→- **Restrictions:** ArgoCD changes require coordination with all environments
   205→   205→- **Purpose:** Avoid impacting GitOps across all clusters
   206→   206→
   207→   207→---
   208→   208→
   209→   209→## Emergency Procedures
   210→   210→
   211→   211→### Emergency Hotfix (Outside Change Window)
   212→   212→
   213→   213→For critical production issues requiring immediate fix:
   214→   214→
   215→   215→1. **Assess Impact**
   216→   216→   - Is this a P0/P1 incident?
   217→   217→   - Is immediate deployment necessary?
   218→   218→   - Can it wait for next change window?
   219→   219→
   220→   220→2. **Get Approval**
   221→   221→   - Notify on-call SRE/platform lead
   222→   222→   - Document incident ticket (Jira)
   223→   223→   - Get emergency change approval
   224→   224→
   225→   225→3. **Bypass Change Window**
   226→   226→   - Change window check is automated
   227→   227→   - Bypass requires modifying workflow (remove change window validation step)
   228→   228→   - Alternative: Use `dry_run: true` to validate, then manually apply via `gcloud`
   229→   229→
   230→   230→4. **Emergency Deployment**
   231→   231→   ```bash
   232→   232→   # Option 1: Manual Terraform apply (fastest)
   233→   233→   cd terraform/environments/prod/{scope}
   234→   234→   terraform init -backend-config="bucket=kd-tfstate-prod" \
   235→   235→     -backend-config="prefix=terraform/environments/prod/{scope}/terraform.tfstate"
   236→   236→   terraform plan
   237→   237→   terraform apply  # After review
   238→   238→
   239→   239→   # Option 2: Modify workflow (if time permits)
   240→   240→   # Temporarily comment out change window check in deploy.yml
   241→   241→   ```
   242→   242→
   243→   243→5. **Post-Incident**
   244→   244→   - Document emergency deployment
   245→   245→   - Restore workflow protections
   246→   246→   - Post-mortem review
   247→   247→
   248→   248→### Rollback Procedure
   249→   249→
   250→   250→If deployment causes issues:
   251→   251→
   252→   252→1. **Assess Rollback Need**
   253→   253→   - What broke?
   254→   254→   - Can we roll forward (fix issue)?
   255→   255→   - Is rollback safe (no state changes)?
   256→   256→
   257→   257→2. **Determine Rollback Strategy**
   258→   258→
   259→   259→   **Option A: Terraform Rollback (Safe)**
   260→   260→   ```bash
   261→   261→   # Revert Terraform code to previous version
   262→   262→   git checkout <previous-commit>
   263→   263→
   264→   264→   # Run deploy workflow with reverted code
   265→   265→   # This generates fresh plan with reverted config
   266→   266→   ```
   267→   267→
   268→   268→   **Option B: Manual Resource Restore (Risky)**
   269→   269→   ```bash
   270→   270→   # Only for critical resources that can't wait
   271→   271→   # Use Terraform state backup
   272→   272→   gsutil cp gs://kd-tfstate-prod/terraform/environments/prod/{scope}/terraform.tfstate.backup ./
   273→   273→   terraform state push terraform.tfstate.backup
   274→   274→   ```
   275→   275→
   276→   276→3. **Validate Rollback**
   277→   277→   - Run smoke tests
   278→   278→   - Verify services are healthy
   279→   279→   - Monitor metrics/logs
   280→   280→
   281→   281→4. **Post-Rollback**
   282→   282→   - Root cause analysis
   283→   283→   - Update tests to catch issue
   284→   284→   - Plan proper fix
   285→   285→
   286→   286→### State Recovery
   287→   287→
   288→   288→If Terraform state is corrupted or lost:
   289→   289→
   290→   290→1. **Check State Backup**
   291→   291→   ```bash
   292→   292→   # List backups
   293→   293→   gsutil ls gs://kd-tfstate-prod/terraform/environments/prod/{scope}/
   294→   294→
   295→   295→   # Download backup
   296→   296→   gsutil cp gs://kd-tfstate-prod/terraform/environments/prod/{scope}/terraform.tfstate.backup ./
   297→   297→
   298→   298→   # Restore
   299→   299→   terraform state push terraform.tfstate.backup
   300→   300→   ```
   301→   301→
   302→   302→2. **Import Existing Resources**
   303→   303→   ```bash
   304→   304→   # If no backup, import resources manually
   305→   305→   terraform import google_compute_network.vpc projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}
   306→   306→   ```
   307→   307→
   308→   308→3. **Validate State**
   309→   309→   ```bash
   310→   310→   terraform plan  # Should show no changes if state is correct
   311→   311→   ```
   312→   312→
   313→   313→---
   314→   314→
   315→   315→## Troubleshooting
   316→   316→
   317→   317→### Common Issues
   318→   318→
   319→   319→#### Issue: PR Validation Takes Too Long
   320→   320→
   321→   321→**Symptoms:** PR validation workflow runs for >15 minutes
   322→   322→
   323→   323→**Causes:**
   324→   324→- Fast test suite running full tests
   325→   325→- Too many directories changed
   326→   326→- GCP authentication issues
   327→   327→
   328→   328→**Solutions:**
   329→   329→```bash
   330→   330→# Check test suite configuration
   331→   331→cat .github/workflows/reusable/terraform-test.yml | grep -A 5 "test_suite"
   332→   332→
   333→   333→# Verify fast tests are defined
   334→   334→cd terraform/test
   335→   335→grep -r "TestBasic"
   336→   336→
   337→   337→# Reduce parallel changes (split PR)
   338→   338→git diff origin/main --name-only | grep "\.tf$" | wc -l
   339→   339→```
   340→   340→
   341→   341→#### Issue: Plan Shows Unexpected Changes
   342→   342→
   343→   343→**Symptoms:** Terraform plan shows drift or unexpected resource changes
   344→   344→
   345→   345→**Causes:**
   346→   346→- Manual changes in GCP console
   347→   347→- Provider version change
   348→   348→- Resource import/recreation
   349→   349→
   350→   350→**Solutions:**
   351→   351→```bash
   352→   352→# Check for drift
   353→   353→terraform plan -detailed-exitcode
   354→   354→
   355→   355→# Review state
   356→   356→terraform state list
   357→   357→terraform state show <resource>
   358→   358→
   359→   359→# Compare with GCP
   360→   360→gcloud compute networks describe <network> --project=<project>
   361→   361→```
   362→   362→
   363→   363→#### Issue: Apply Fails with "Resource Already Exists"
   364→   364→
   365→   365→**Symptoms:** Apply fails because resource already exists
   366→   366→
   367→   367→**Causes:**
   368→   368→- Resource created manually
   369→   369→- State out of sync
   370→   370→- Concurrent applies
   371→   371→
   372→   372→**Solutions:**
   373→   373→```bash
   374→   374→# Import existing resource
   375→   375→terraform import <resource_type>.<name> <resource_id>
   376→   376→
   377→   377→# Example: Import GKE cluster
   378→   378→terraform import google_container_cluster.cluster projects/<project>/locations/<region>/clusters/<name>
   379→   379→
   380→   380→# Verify import
   381→   381→terraform plan  # Should show no changes
   382→   382→```
   383→   383→
   384→   384→#### Issue: Workflow Stuck on Approval
   385→   385→
   386→   386→**Symptoms:** Deploy workflow waiting for approval indefinitely
   387→   387→
   388→   388→**Causes:**
   389→   389→- No GitHub environment configured
   390→   390→- Insufficient permissions
   391→   391→- Approvers not notified
   392→   392→
   393→   393→**Solutions:**
   394→   394→1. Check GitHub environment settings (Settings → Environments)
   395→   395→2. Verify approvers are configured
   396→   396→3. Check if approval notification was sent
   397→   397→4. Manually approve in Actions tab → Review deployments
   398→   398→
   399→   399→#### Issue: Nightly Quality Checks Failing
   400→   400→
   401→   401→**Symptoms:** Nightly workflow reports failures
   402→   402→
   403→   403→**Causes:**
   404→   404→- Terratest resources not cleaned up
   405→   405→- Drift in production
   406→   406→- Lab project quota exceeded
   407→   407→
   408→   408→**Solutions:**
   409→   409→```bash
   410→   410→# Check for orphaned resources
   411→   411→gcloud compute instances list --project=kd-ix-eur-lab-platform | grep terratest
   412→   412→
   413→   413→# Clean up manually
   414→   414→gcloud compute instances delete <instance> --project=kd-ix-eur-lab-platform
   415→   415→
   416→   416→# Check quotas
   417→   417→gcloud compute project-info describe --project=kd-ix-eur-lab-platform | grep -A 20 quotas
   418→   418→```
   419→   419→
   420→   420→### Debugging Workflows
   421→   421→
   422→   422→#### View Workflow Logs
   423→   423→
   424→   424→1. Go to **Actions** tab
   425→   425→2. Click on workflow run
   426→   426→3. Expand job steps
   427→   427→4. Review logs for errors
   428→   428→
   429→   429→#### Download Artifacts
   430→   430→
   431→   431→```bash
   432→   432→# Using GitHub CLI
   433→   433→gh run download <run-id> --name terraform-apply-prod-<run-id>
   434→   434→
   435→   435→# View plan output
   436→   436→cat apply_output.txt
   437→   437→
   438→   438→# View outputs
   439→   439→cat outputs.json | jq
   440→   440→```
   441→   441→
   442→   442→#### Re-run Failed Workflow
   443→   443→
   444→   444→1. Click on failed workflow run
   445→   445→2. Click **Re-run jobs** → **Re-run failed jobs**
   446→   446→3. Or **Re-run all jobs** for clean slate
   447→   447→
   448→   448→---
   449→   449→
   450→   450→## Workflow Reference
   451→   451→
   452→   452→### pull-request.yml
   453→   453→
   454→   454→**Trigger:** Pull request to main/develop
   455→   455→
   456→   456→**Purpose:** Fast validation (<15 minutes)
   457→   457→
   458→   458→**Jobs:**
   459→   459→1. Detect changed directories
   460→   460→2. Validate Terraform (parallel)
   461→   461→3. Generate plans (parallel)
   462→   462→4. Run fast tests (if modules changed)
   463→   463→
   464→   464→**Outputs:**
   465→   465→- PR comments with plan summaries
   466→   466→- Validation status
   467→   467→- Test results
   468→   468→
   469→   469→**Usage:** Automatic (triggered by PR)
   470→   470→
   471→   471→---
   472→   472→
   473→   473→### main-validation.yml
   474→   474→
   475→   475→**Trigger:** Push to main branch
   476→   476→
   477→   477→**Purpose:** Prove main is deployable (doesn't deploy)
   478→   478→
   479→   479→**Jobs:**
   480→   480→1. Detect changed directories
   481→   481→2. Validate all changes
   482→   482→3. Generate plans for all
   483→   483→4. Tag release with semantic version
   484→   484→
   485→   485→**Outputs:**
   486→   486→- GitHub release with version tag
   487→   487→- Deployment readiness status
   488→   488→- No actual deployment
   489→   489→
   490→   490→**Usage:** Automatic (triggered by merge)
   491→   491→
   492→   492→---
   493→   493→
   494→   494→### deploy.yml
   495→   495→
   496→   496→**Trigger:** Manual (workflow_dispatch)
   497→   497→
   498→   498→**Purpose:** Deploy infrastructure to environment
   499→   499→
   500→   500→**Inputs:**
   501→   501→- `environment`: dev, qa, prod, shared
   502→   502→- `scope`: network, security, gke, platform, data, kong, gateway, litellm, argocd, all
   503→   503→- `dry_run`: true/false
   504→   504→- `auto_approve`: true/false (dev only)
   505→   505→
   506→   506→**Jobs:**
   507→   507→1. Pre-flight checks (change window, permissions)
   508→   508→2. Validate
   509→   509→3. Plan (fresh)
   510→   510→4. Approval gate (if required)
   511→   511→5. Apply
   512→   512→6. Post-deployment verification
   513→   513→
   514→   514→**Outputs:**
   515→   515→- Deployment status
   516→   516→- Terraform outputs
   517→   517→- Verification results
   518→   518→
   519→   519→**Usage:**
   520→   520→```bash
   521→   521→# Via GitHub UI
   522→   522→Actions → Deploy Infrastructure → Run workflow
   523→   523→
   524→   524→# Via GitHub CLI
   525→   525→gh workflow run deploy.yml \
   526→   526→  -f environment=prod \
   527→   527→  -f scope=gke \
   528→   528→  -f dry_run=false \
   529→   529→  -f auto_approve=false
   530→   530→```
   531→   531→
   532→   532→---
   533→   533→
   534→   534→### nightly-quality.yml
   535→   535→
   536→   536→**Trigger:** Schedule (daily at 02:00 UTC) + manual
   537→   537→
   538→   538→**Purpose:** Comprehensive testing and drift detection
   539→   539→
   540→   540→**Inputs (manual trigger only):**
   541→   541→- `skip_tests`: Skip full test suite
   542→   542→- `skip_drift`: Skip drift detection
   543→   543→
   544→   544→**Jobs:**
   545→   545→1. Full Terratest suite (90 minutes)
   546→   546→2. Drift detection (all environments, all scopes)
   547→   547→3. Daily quality report
   548→   548→
   549→   549→**Outputs:**
   550→   550→- Test results summary
   551→   551→- Drift detection report
   552→   552→- GitHub issues for drift (if detected)
   553→   553→
   554→   554→**Usage:**
   555→   555→```bash
   556→   556→# Automatic: Runs daily at 02:00 UTC
   557→   557→
   558→   558→# Manual trigger (with options)
   559→   559→gh workflow run nightly-quality.yml \
   560→   560→  -f skip_tests=false \
   561→   561→  -f skip_drift=false
   562→   562→```
   563→   563→
   564→   564→---
   565→   565→
   566→   566→## Reusable Workflows
   567→   567→
   568→   568→### terraform-validate.yml
   569→   569→
   570→   570→**Inputs:**
   571→   571→- `working_directory`: Terraform directory
   572→   572→- `terraform_version`: Terraform version (default: 1.5.0)
   573→   573→- `enable_tfsec`: Enable security scan (default: true)
   574→   574→- `tfsec_severity`: Minimum severity (default: MEDIUM)
   575→   575→
   576→   576→**Outputs:**
   577→   577→- `validation_status`: success/failure
   578→   578→- `tfsec_findings_count`: Number of findings
   579→   579→
   580→   580→**Usage:**
   581→   581→```yaml
   582→   582→uses: ./.github/workflows/reusable/terraform-validate.yml
   583→   583→with:
   584→   584→  working_directory: terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   585→   585→```
   586→   586→
   587→   587→---
   588→   588→
   589→   589→### terraform-plan.yml
   590→   590→
   591→   591→**Inputs:**
   592→   592→- `working_directory`: Terraform directory
   593→   593→- `environment`: dev, qa, prod, shared
   594→   594→- `gcp_project_id`: GCP project
   595→   595→- `backend_bucket`: State bucket
   596→   596→- `backend_prefix`: State path
   597→   597→- `comment_on_pr`: Post to PR (default: true)
   598→   598→- `upload_artifact`: Upload plan (default: false)

   600→   600→**Outputs:**

   604→   604→- `artifact_name`: Artifact name (if uploaded)

   606→   606→**Usage:**
   607→   607→```yaml

   609→   609→secrets: inherit
   610→   610→with:
   611→   611→  working_directory: terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   612→   612→  environment: dev
   613→   613→  gcp_project_id: kd-ix-eur-dev-foundation
   614→   614→  backend_bucket: kd-tfstate-dev
   615→   615→  backend_prefix: terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network/terraform.tfstate
   616→   616→```
   617→   617→
   618→   618→---
   619→   619→
   620→   620→### terraform-apply.yml
   621→   621→
   622→   622→**Inputs:**
   623→   623→- `working_directory`: Terraform directory
   624→   624→- `environment`: dev, qa, prod

   626→   626→- `backend_bucket`: State bucket

   708→   708→## Best Practices
   709→   709→
   710→   710→### Before Deployment
   711→   711→
   712→   712→- ✅ Run `terraform plan` locally first
   713→   713→- ✅ Review plan output carefully
   714→   714→- ✅ Check for unexpected resource destruction
   715→   715→- ✅ Verify GCP project and region
   716→   716→- ✅ Ensure change window compliance (prod)
   717→   717→- ✅ Notify team of deployment
   718→   718→
   719→   719→### During Deployment
   720→   720→
   721→   721→- ✅ Monitor workflow progress
   722→   722→- ✅ Watch for errors in real-time
   723→   723→- ✅ Keep communication channel open
   724→   724→- ✅ Have rollback plan ready
   725→   725→- ❌ Don't close browser until complete
   726→   726→
   727→   727→### After Deployment
   728→   728→
   729→   729→- ✅ Verify services are healthy
   730→   730→- ✅ Check application functionality
   731→   731→- ✅ Review Terraform outputs
   732→   732→- ✅ Monitor metrics for anomalies
   733→   733→- ✅ Update deployment log
   734→   734→- ✅ Notify team of completion
   735→   735→

    34→    34→
    35→    35→## Platform Overview
    36→    36→
    37→    37→### Architecture Layers
    38→    38→
    39→    39→| Layer | Purpose | Components |
    40→    40→|-------|---------|------------|
    41→    41→| **Northbound** | Service exposure to consumers | Kong API Gateway, LiteLLM MCP Gateway, Admin UI |
    42→    42→| **Capability** | Business logic and orchestration | Control Plane, Agents, Voice, Messaging, Knowledge |
    43→    43→| **Southbound** | Infrastructure (abstracted) | GCP services, databases, storage, events |
    44→    44→
    45→    45→### Service Consumption Model
    46→    46→
    47→    47→Consumers access platform capabilities through three methods:
    48→    48→
    49→    49→| Method | Consumer Type | Authentication |
    50→    50→|--------|---------------|----------------|
    51→    51→| REST API (Kong) | External systems, applications | API Key or JWT |
    52→    52→| MCP Tools (LiteLLM) | AI agents | Service account |
    53→    53→| Admin UI | Internal users | OIDC |
    54→    54→
    55→    55→All requests are authenticated, routed through the appropriate gateway, and executed by the capability layer. Infrastructure is never exposed directly to consumers.
    56→    56→
    57→    57→---
    58→    58→
    59→    59→## What the Platform Provides
    60→    60→
    61→    61→When a use case is onboarded, the platform automatically provisions:
    62→    62→
    63→    63→| Resource | Description |
    64→    64→|----------|-------------|
    65→    65→| **Kubernetes Namespace** | Isolated environment for workloads |
    66→    66→| **PostgreSQL Database** | Dedicated database with credentials |
    67→    67→| **Redis Key Prefix** | Shared cache with isolated keyspace |
    68→    68→| **GCS Bucket** | Object storage for documents and artifacts |
    69→    69→| **Pub/Sub Topic** | Event bus for async messaging |
    70→    70→| **Kong Routes** | API endpoints at `/api/v1/{use-case}/*` |
    71→    71→| **Secrets Folder** | Secret Manager path for credentials |
    72→    72→| **Service Account** | GCP identity with least-privilege permissions |
    73→    73→| **Observability** | Pre-configured dashboard, logs, and traces |
    74→    74→| **Identity** | Identity services abstracting credential handling |
    75→    75→| **Security** | Security monitoring, WAF, and firewall services |
    76→    76→| **Service Catalogue** | Backstage portal for discovering available services |
    77→    77→
    78→    78→### Service Discovery via Backstage
    79→    79→
    80→    80→Use case developers discover available platform services through **Backstage**, the internal service catalogue:
    81→    81→
    82→    82→| What You Can Discover | Examples |
    83→    83→|----------------------|----------|
    84→    84→| **Platform Services** | LiteLLM endpoints, Kong routes, MCP tools |
    85→    85→| **Data Services** | Available databases, Redis instances, GCS buckets |
    86→    86→| **CrewAI Agents** | Existing agents you can call or integrate with |
    87→    87→| **Pub/Sub Topics** | Event bus topics for async messaging |
    88→    88→| **API Schemas** | OpenAPI specs for all platform APIs |
    89→    89→| **Documentation** | Tech docs aggregated from all services |
    90→    90→
    91→    91→Access Backstage at: `https://backstage.kix.konecta.com` (internal only)
    92→    92→
    93→    93→### What Developers CAN Access
    94→    94→
    95→    95→- Kubernetes namespace (isolated)
    96→    96→- Database connection (their database only)
    97→    97→- Cache client (their key prefix only)
    98→    98→- Storage bucket (their bucket only)
    99→    99→- Pub/Sub topic (their topic only)
   100→   100→
   101→   101→### What Developers CANNOT Access
   102→   102→
   103→   103→- GCP console directly
   104→   104→- Other use case resources
   105→   105→- Organization-level settings
   106→   106→- Service account keys
   107→   107→
   108→   108→---
   109→   109→
   110→   110→## What Developers Build
   111→   111→
   112→   112→| Component | Responsibility |
   113→   113→|-----------|----------------|
   114→   114→| **Agent Logic** | Business logic using CrewAI framework |
   115→   115→| **API Endpoints** | Request handlers behind Kong routes |
   116→   116→| **Data Schema** | Database tables and vector collections |
   117→   117→| **Prompts** | LLM prompts and configurations |
   118→   118→| **Workflows** | Multi-step orchestration (if needed) |
   119→   119→
   120→   120→### Development Flow
   121→   121→
   122→   122→1. Define capability schema (inputs, outputs, SLA)
   123→   123→2. Register capability in Schema Registry
   124→   124→3. Implement agent or service
   125→   125→4. Configure API routes
   126→   126→5. Deploy to development environment via ArgoCD GitOps
   127→   127→6. Test via API and MCP
   128→   128→7. Promote through QA to production (ArgoCD syncs from Git)
   129→   129→
   130→   130→### GitOps Deployment via ArgoCD
   131→   131→
   132→   132→All deployments follow a GitOps workflow managed by ArgoCD running on the shared platform cluster:
   133→   133→
   134→   134→| Step | Action | Tool |
   135→   135→|------|--------|------|
   136→   136→| 1 | Push code to Bitbucket | Git |
   137→   137→| 2 | CI pipeline builds container image | Bitbucket Pipelines |
   138→   138→| 3 | Image pushed to Artifact Registry (`kd-ix-eur-shr-artifacts`) | Docker/Buildkit |
   139→   139→| 4 | ArgoCD Image Updater detects new image | Automatic |
   140→   140→| 5 | ArgoCD syncs manifests to target cluster | Automatic |
   141→   141→| 6 | Verify deployment status | ArgoCD UI or CLI |
   142→   142→
   143→   143→**ArgoCD UI:** `https://argocd.ix.konecta-digital.com` (Google OIDC login)
   144→   144→
   145→   145→**Key concepts:**
   146→   146→- **Application**: A single deployable unit tracked by ArgoCD
   147→   147→- **AppProject**: Scopes what an Application can access (namespaces, clusters, repos)
   148→   148→- **ApplicationSet**: Templated generation of Applications across environments
   149→   149→- **Sync**: ArgoCD applies Git state to the cluster (auto or manual)
   150→   150→
   151→   151→---
   152→   152→
   153→   153→## BAOE Readiness Framework
   154→   154→
   155→   155→A use case is **AVAILABLE** when it meets all four readiness dimensions:
   156→   156→
   157→   157→| Dimension | Code | Description |
   158→   158→|-----------|------|-------------|
   159→   159→| **Built** | B | Autopilot flow completed in ElevenLabs/CrewAI |
   160→   160→| **API-fied** | A | Standard Agent API contracts, lifecycle APIs |
   161→   161→| **Observable** | O | Telemetry, decision logging, audit trails |
   162→   162→| **Platform-Enabled** | E | Configuration-driven deployment, tenant isolation |
   163→   163→
   164→   164→**Progression Example:**
   165→   165→```
   166→   166→Month 1: B . A . O      -> Flow built, APIs ready, observable
   167→   167→Month 2: B . A . O . E  -> Fully platform-enabled
   168→   168→Month 3: AVAILABLE      -> Production-ready
   169→   169→```
   170→   170→
   171→   171→---
   172→   172→
   173→   173→## Autonomy Tiers
   174→   174→
   175→   175→Each use case operates at a specific autonomy tier that governs agent independence:
   176→   176→
   177→   177→| Tier | Description | Human Involvement | Example |
   178→   178→|------|-------------|-------------------|---------|
   179→   179→| **Supervised** | Human monitors all actions | High — approval required | FAQ, Password Reset |
   180→   180→| **Conditional** | Autonomous within bounds, escalates on triggers | Medium — exception handling | Scheduling, Collections |
   181→   181→| **Assistive** | AI assists human decision-making | Medium — human leads | Copilot Sales |
   182→   182→| **Full** | Fully autonomous, rare and restricted | Low — audit only | Simple bookings |
   183→   183→
   184→   184→### Escalation Triggers
   185→   185→
   186→   186→| Trigger | Action | Target |
   187→   187→|---------|--------|--------|
   188→   188→| Customer says "supervisor" | Immediate transfer | Human Expert |
   189→   189→| Sentiment drops below threshold | Flag + optional transfer | Copilot Assisted |
   190→   190→| Compliance violation detected | Immediate transfer | Human Expert |
   191→   191→| Agent confidence below 70% | Request human review | Copilot Assisted |
   192→   192→| 3+ failed resolution attempts | Escalate | Human Expert |
   193→   193→

   195→   195→
   196→   196→## Technology Specifications
   197→   197→
   198→   198→### CrewAI
   199→   199→
   200→   200→**Purpose:** Multi-agent orchestration for autonomous task execution
   201→   201→
   202→   202→**What It Does:**
   203→   203→- Defines agents with roles, goals, and tools
   204→   204→- Orchestrates tasks across multiple agents
   205→   205→- Manages agent collaboration and handoffs
   206→   206→- Integrates with LLM gateway for model access
   207→   207→
   208→   208→**Constraints:**
   209→   209→- All LLM calls must use platform gateway (no direct API calls)
   210→   210→- Maximum execution time configurable per agent
   211→   211→- Agent state must be externalized for fault tolerance
   212→   212→
   213→   213→**Example Crew Structure:**
   214→   214→```
   215→   215→End-User Self-Healing Crew
   216→   216→+-- Triage Agent
   217→   217→|   +-- Classifies issue type, urgency, complexity
   218→   218→+-- Diagnostic Agent
   219→   219→|   +-- Runs diagnostic checks via Nexthink MCP
   220→   220→+-- Resolution Agent
   221→   221→|   +-- Executes fixes via ServiceNow/AD MCP
   222→   222→+-- Communication Agent
   223→   223→|   +-- Updates user on progress
   224→   224→+-- Escalation Agent
   225→   225→    +-- Hands off to human with full context
   226→   226→```
   227→   227→
   228→   228→### ElevenLabs
   229→   229→
   230→   230→**Purpose:** Voice synthesis and conversational AI (primary voice runtime)
   231→   231→
   232→   232→**What It Does:**
   233→   233→- Text-to-speech synthesis
   234→   234→- Real-time conversational AI
   235→   235→- Speech-to-Text
   236→   236→- Multi-language support
   237→   237→
   238→   238→**Constraints:**
   239→   239→- Voice calls must use platform client via Kong
   240→   240→- Latency budget: 500ms for text-to-speech
   241→   241→- Supported languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese (MVP)
   242→   242→
   243→   243→**Voice Latency Budget:**
   244→   244→
   245→   245→| Stage | Target | Max |
   246→   246→|-------|--------|-----|
   247→   247→| Speech-to-Text | 150ms | 300ms |
   248→   248→| Agent Processing | 300ms | 500ms |
   249→   249→| Text-to-Speech | 150ms | 300ms |
   250→   250→| **Total Round-Trip** | **600ms** | **1100ms** |
   251→   251→
   252→   252→### LiteLLM
   253→   253→
   254→   254→**Purpose:** Unified LLM access and MCP tool gateway
   255→   255→
   256→   256→**What It Does (LLM Gateway):**
   257→   257→- Abstracts multiple LLM providers behind single interface
   258→   258→- Handles model fallback and retry logic
   259→   259→- Manages API keys centrally
   260→   260→- Tracks token usage per use case
   261→   261→- Provides response caching
   262→   262→
   263→   263→**What It Does (MCP Gateway):**
   264→   264→- Exposes platform capabilities as MCP tools
   265→   265→- Enables AI agents to discover available tools
   266→   266→- Routes tool calls to appropriate services
   267→   267→
   268→   268→**Available Models:**
   269→   269→
   270→   270→| Model | Provider | Recommended Use |
   271→   271→|-------|----------|-----------------|
   272→   272→| Gemini 2.5 Flash | Google | Default — fast, cost-effective |
   273→   273→| Gemini 2.5 Pro | Google | Complex reasoning tasks |
   274→   274→| Claude 3 Sonnet | Anthropic | Fallback |
   275→   275→| GPT-4 Turbo | OpenAI | Fallback |
   276→   276→
   277→   277→**Constraints:**
   278→   278→- No direct calls to model provider APIs
   279→   279→- Token budgets monitored per use case
   280→   280→- Caching enabled by default
   281→   281→- Prompt logging with PII redaction
   282→   282→
   283→   283→### Kong API Gateway
   284→   284→
   285→   285→**Purpose:** API gateway for service exposure and third-party API abstraction
   286→   286→
   287→   287→**Available Capabilities:**
   288→   288→- JWT validation (external identity integration)
   289→   289→- API key authentication
   290→   290→- Rate limiting (per key, per route)
   291→   291→- Request/response transformation
   292→   292→- Third-party API proxying
   293→   293→
   294→   294→**Constraints:**
   295→   295→- All external traffic must pass through Kong
   296→   296→- No direct pod access from outside cluster
   297→   297→- Rate limits enforced per API key
   298→   298→
   299→   299→### Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL)
   300→   300→
   301→   301→**Purpose:** Relational data storage
   302→   302→
   303→   303→**Specifications:**
   304→   304→- PostgreSQL version 15
   305→   305→- Instance: 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM (adjustable)
   306→   306→- Storage: SSD with auto-grow
   307→   307→- Backups: Daily, 7-day retention
   308→   308→- HA: Regional (Prod), Zonal (Dev/QA)
   309→   309→
   310→   310→**Constraints:**
   311→   311→- No DDL changes in application code (use migrations)
   312→   312→- Connection pooling required
   313→   313→- Private IP access only
   314→   314→
   315→   315→### Redis (Memorystore)
   316→   316→
   317→   317→**Purpose:** Caching and session state
   318→   318→
   319→   319→**Specifications:**
   320→   320→- Redis version 7.0
   321→   321→- Tier: Standard (HA)
   322→   322→- Memory: 5GB shared (expandable)
   323→   323→- Persistence: RDB snapshots
   324→   324→
   325→   325→**Constraints:**
   326→   326→- Keys must be prefixed with use case name
   327→   327→- TTL required on all keys (24h max default)
   328→   328→- No KEYS command (use SCAN)
   329→   329→- No Lua scripts without approval
   330→   330→
   331→   331→### Qdrant
   332→   332→
   333→   333→**Purpose:** Vector storage for RAG and semantic search
   334→   334→
   335→   335→**Specifications:**
   336→   336→- Replicas: 3 (Prod), 1 (Dev/QA)
   337→   337→- Storage: Persistent SSD
   338→   338→- Max vectors: 10M per collection
   339→   339→
   340→   340→**Constraints:**
   341→   341→- Collection names prefixed with use case
   342→   342→- Must use platform embedding model for consistency
   343→   343→- Backup responsibility with platform team
   344→   344→
   345→   345→### Pub/Sub
   346→   346→
   347→   347→**Purpose:** Asynchronous messaging and event-driven architecture
   348→   348→
   349→   349→**Specifications:**
   350→   350→- Message retention: 7 days
   351→   351→- Ack deadline: 60 seconds
   352→   352→- Max message size: 10MB
   353→   353→- Ordering: Optional per topic
   354→   354→
   355→   355→**Constraints:**
   356→   356→- Topic/subscription names prefixed with use case
   357→   357→- Dead letter queue required for production
   358→   358→- Idempotent message handling required
   359→   359→
   360→   360→### GCS (Cloud Storage)
   361→   361→
   362→   362→**Purpose:** Object storage for documents and artifacts
   363→   363→
   364→   364→**Specifications:**
   365→   365→- Storage class: Standard
   366→   366→- Location: EU (multi-region)
   367→   367→- Lifecycle: 90d -> Nearline -> 365d -> Archive
   368→   368→- Versioning: Enabled
   369→   369→
   370→   370→**Constraints:**
   371→   371→- No public access
   372→   372→- Signed URLs for temporary external access
   373→   373→- Max object size: 5TB
   374→   374→
   375→   375→### Channel Hub
   376→   376→
   377→   377→**Purpose:** Outbound messaging across multiple channels
   378→   378→
   379→   379→**Supported Channels:**
   380→   380→
   381→   381→| Channel | Requirements |
   382→   382→|---------|--------------|
   383→   383→| SMS | Approved sender ID |
   384→   384→| Email | Verified sending domain |
   385→   385→| WhatsApp | Pre-approved message templates |
   386→   386→| Google Chat | Internal use only |
   387→   387→
   388→   388→**Constraints:**
   389→   389→- All messages logged for audit
   390→   390→- Rate limits per channel
   391→   391→- PII handling rules apply
   392→   392→- Templates required for WhatsApp
   393→   393→
   394→   394→---
   395→   395→
   396→   396→## Service Patterns
   397→   397→
   398→   398→### Exposing a Capability
   399→   399→
   400→   400→**Step 1: Define Schema**
   401→   401→
   402→   402→Create a JSON Schema defining inputs, outputs, and metadata including:
   403→   403→- Input parameters with types and validation
   404→   404→- Output structure
   405→   405→- SLA requirements (latency, availability)
   406→   406→- Routing rules (which engine handles requests)
   407→   407→
   408→   408→**Step 2: Register in Schema Registry**
   409→   409→
   410→   410→Register the capability with:
   411→   411→- Name and version
   412→   412→- Owner team
   413→   413→- Description
   414→   414→- Input/output schemas
   415→   415→- SLA targets
   416→   416→- Default routing configuration
   417→   417→
   418→   418→**Step 3: Implement Service**
   419→   419→
   420→   420→Build the service that handles requests:
   421→   421→- Implement business logic
   422→   422→- Use platform clients for dependencies
   423→   423→- Follow error handling patterns
   424→   424→- Add observability instrumentation
   425→   425→
   426→   426→**Step 4: Build Agents**
   427→   427→
   428→   428→Build any agents required in CrewAI:
   429→   429→- Create your agents and publish them
   430→   430→- Define agent roles, goals, and available tools
   431→   431→- Configure agent collaboration patterns
   432→   432→
   433→   433→**Step 5: Configure Routing**
   434→   434→
   435→   435→Define Kong routes:
   436→   436→- API path
   437→   437→- Authentication requirements
   438→   438→- Rate limits
   439→   439→- Any request/response transformations
   440→   440→
   441→   441→**Step 6: Register MCP Tool (Optional)**
   442→   442→
   443→   443→If the capability should be available to AI agents:
   444→   444→- Register tool in MCP Gateway
   445→   445→- Define tool description for discovery
   446→   446→- Map to underlying service
   447→   447→
   448→   448→### Consuming a Capability
   449→   449→
   450→   450→**Via REST API:**
   451→   451→- Obtain API key or JWT token
   452→   452→- Call Kong endpoint with authentication header
   453→   453→- Handle standard error responses
   454→   454→- Use trace ID for debugging
   455→   455→
   456→   456→**Via MCP (AI Agents):**
   457→   457→- Query MCP Gateway for available tools
   458→   458→- Call tool with required parameters
   459→   459→- Receive structured response
   460→   460→- Handle errors gracefully
   461→   461→
   462→   462→**Via Internal Service:**
   463→   463→- Use platform-provided client library
   464→   464→- Authentication handled automatically
   465→   465→- Retry and circuit breaker included
   466→   466→
   467→   467→### Error Handling
   468→   468→
   469→   469→All services must return errors in standard format:
   470→   470→
   471→   471→| Field | Description |
   472→   472→|-------|-------------|
   473→   473→| code | Machine-readable error code |
   474→   474→| message | Human-readable description |
   475→   475→| details | Additional context (optional) |
   476→   476→| trace_id | Correlation ID for debugging |
   477→   477→
   478→   478→**Standard Error Codes:**
   479→   479→
   480→   480→| Code | HTTP Status | Meaning |
   481→   481→|------|-------------|---------|
   482→   482→| VALIDATION_ERROR | 400 | Invalid input |
   483→   483→| UNAUTHORIZED | 401 | Missing or invalid authentication |
   484→   484→| FORBIDDEN | 403 | Insufficient permissions |
   485→   485→| NOT_FOUND | 404 | Resource not found |
   486→   486→| CONFLICT | 409 | Business rule violation |
   487→   487→| RATE_LIMITED | 429 | Too many requests |
   488→   488→| INTERNAL_ERROR | 500 | Unexpected failure |
   489→   489→
   490→   490→### Async Patterns
   491→   491→
   492→   492→**Callback Pattern:**
   493→   493→- Submit request with callback URL
   494→   494→- Receive request ID immediately
   495→   495→- Platform calls callback when complete
   496→   496→
   497→   497→**Event-Driven Pattern:**
   498→   498→- Publish event to Pub/Sub topic
   499→   499→- Subscribers react to events
   500→   500→- Decoupled processing
   501→   501→
   502→   502→---

   504→   504→## Use Case Examples
   505→   505→
   506→   506→### Use Case 1: End-User Self-Healing
   507→   507→
   508→   508→**Description:** IT support automation for Konecta employees via Google Chat.
   509→   509→
   510→   510→**Control Plane Flow:**
   511→   511→
   512→   512→| Intent | Routing |
   513→   513→|--------|---------|
   514→   514→| Password reset | Autonomous Agent |
   515→   515→| Software install | Autonomous Agent |
   516→   516→| Hardware issue | Human Expert |
   517→   517→| Complex/unclear | Copilot-Assisted |
   518→   518→
   519→   519→**Layer Mapping:**
   520→   520→
   521→   521→| Layer | Component | Technology |
   522→   522→|-------|-----------|------------|
   523→   523→| ENGAGE | Conversational AI | CrewAI Crew |
   524→   524→| KNOW | User Context | Employee profile |
   525→   525→| GOVERN | Decision Logging | Audit trail |
   526→   526→| CONNECT | Channel | Google Chat API |
   527→   527→| ACT | Tool Integration | MCP (ServiceNow, Nexthink, AD) |
   528→   528→
   529→   529→### Use Case 2: Autopilot Scheduling
   530→   530→
   531→   531→**Description:** AI-powered appointment scheduling for inbound/outbound interactions.
   532→   532→
   533→   533→**Control Plane Distribution:**
   534→   534→- Autonomous: 95%
   535→   535→- Copilot: 3%
   536→   536→- Human: 2%
   537→   537→
   538→   538→**Layer Mapping:**
   539→   539→
   540→   540→| Layer | Component | Technology |
   541→   541→|-------|-----------|------------|
   542→   542→| ENGAGE | Voice Agent | ElevenLabs Conversational AI |
   543→   543→| KNOW | Customer Context | Unified profile |
   544→   544→| GOVERN | Compliance | Call recording, consent |
   545→   545→| CONNECT | Voice + Messaging | ElevenLabs + SIP |
   546→   546→| ACT | Calendar Integration | MCP (CRM/scheduling) |
   547→   547→
   548→   548→### Use Case 3: Autopilot Collections
   549→   549→
   550→   550→**Description:** Automated outbound collections with compliance guardrails.
   551→   551→
   552→   552→**Compliance Guardrails:**
   553→   553→
   554→   554→| Regulation | Implementation |
   555→   555→|------------|----------------|
   556→   556→| TCPA | Time-of-day restrictions, consent verification |
   557→   557→| FDCPA | No harassment, debt validation on request |
   558→   558→| State Laws | State-specific scripts, frequency limits |
   559→   559→| Mini-Miranda | Automated disclosure at call start |
   560→   560→
   561→   561→**Layer Mapping:**
   562→   562→

It covers what the platform provides, how to build use cases, service patterns, and technology specifications.\n\n**Audience:** Use case developers building on KIX\n\n## Architecture Layers\n\n| Layer | Purpose | Components |\n|-------|---------|------------|\n| **Northbound** | Service exposure to consumers | Kong API Gateway, LiteLLM MCP Gateway, Admin UI |\n| **Capability** | Business logic and orchestration | Control Plane, Agents, Voice, Messaging, Knowledge |\n| **Southbound** | Infrastructure (abstracted) | GCP services, databases, storage, events |\n\n## Service Consumption Model\n\nConsumers access platform capabilities through three methods:\n\n| Method | Consumer Type | Authentication |\n|--------|---------------|----------------|\n| REST API (Kong) | External systems, applications | API Key or JWT |\n| MCP Tools (LiteLLM) | AI agents | Service account |\n| Admin UI | Internal users | OIDC |\n\nAll requests are authenticated, routed through the appropriate gateway, and executed by the capability layer. Architecture](/docs/architecture) — Technical infrastructure details\n- [Onboarding](/docs/getting-started/onboarding) — Getting started with the repository\n- [Strategy](/docs/strategy) — Platform vision and business goals\n```\n\nFile 2: docs/developer-guide/platform-overview.md\n```\n---\ntitle: \"Platform Overview\"\nsidebar_label: \"Platform Overview\"\nsidebar_position: 2\ndescription: \"What the KIX Platform provides to use case developers and what developers are responsible for building\"\n---\n\n# Platform Overview\n\n## What the Platform Provides\n\nWhen a use case is onboarded, the platform automatically provisions:\n\n| Resource | Description |\n|----------|-------------|\n| **Kubernetes Namespace** | Isolated environment for workloads |\n| **PostgreSQL Database** | Dedicated database with credentials |\n| **Redis Key Prefix** | Shared cache with isolated keyspace |\n| **GCS Bucket** | Object storage for documents and artifacts |\n| **Pub/Sub Topic** | Event bus for async messaging |\n| **Kong Routes** | API endpoints at `/api/v1/{use-case}/*` |\n| **Secrets Folder** | Secret Manager path for credentials |\n| **Service Account** | GCP identity with least-privilege permissions |\n| **Observability** | Pre-configured dashboard, logs, and traces |\n| **Identity** | Identity services abstracting credential handling |\n| **Security** | Security monitoring, WAF, and firewall services |\n| **Service Catalogue** | Backstage portal for discovering available services |\n\n### Service Discovery via Backstage\n\nUse case developers discover available platform services through **Backstage**, the internal service catalogue:\n\n| What You Can Discover | Examples |\n|----------------------|----------|\n| **Platform Services** | LiteLLM endpoints, Kong routes, MCP tools |\n| **Data Services** | Available databases, Redis instances, GCS buckets |\n| **CrewAI Agents** | Existing agents you can call or integrate with |\n| **Pub/Sub Topics** | Event bus topics for async messaging |\n| **API Schemas** | OpenAPI specs for all platform APIs |\n| **Documentation** | Tech docs aggregated from all services |\n\nAccess Backstage at: `https://backstage.kix.konecta.com` (internal only)\n\n### What Developers CAN Access\n\n- Kubernetes namespace (isolated)\n- Database connection (their database only)\n- Cache client (their key prefix only)\n- Storage bucket (their bucket only)\n- Pub/Sub topic (their topic only)\n\n### What Developers CANNOT Access\n\n- GCP console directly\n- Other use case resources\n- Organization-level settings\n- Service account keys\n\n## What Developers Build\n\n| Component | Responsibility |\n|-----------|----------------|\n| **Agent Logic** | Business logic using CrewAI framework |\n| **API Endpoints** | Request handlers behind Kong routes |\n| **Data Schema** | Database tables and vector collections |\n| **Prompts** | LLM prompts and configurations |\n| **Workflows** | Multi-step orchestration (if needed) |\n\n## BAOE Readiness Framework\n\nA use case is **AVAILABLE** when it meets all four readiness dimensions:\n\n| Dimension | Code | Description |\n|-----------|------|-------------|\n| **Built** | B | Autopilot flow completed in ElevenLabs/CrewAI |\n| **API-fied** | A | Standard Agent API contracts, lifecycle APIs |\n| **Observable** | O | Telemetry, decision logging, audit trails |\n| **Platform-Enabled** | E | Configuration-driven deployment, tenant isolation |\n\n**Progression Example:**\n```\nMonth 1: B . A . O      -> Flow built, APIs ready, observable\nMonth 2: B . A . O . E  -> Fully platform-enabled\nMonth 3: AVAILABLE      -> Production-ready\n```\n\n## Autonomy Tiers\n\nEach use case operates at a specific autonomy tier:\n\n| Tier | Description | Human Involvement | Example |\n|------|-------------|-------------------|---------|\n| **Supervised** | Human monitors all actions | High — approval required | FAQ, Password Reset |\n| **Conditional** | Autonomous within bounds, escalates on triggers | Medium — exception handling | Scheduling, Collections |\n| **Assistive** | AI assists human decision-making | Medium — human leads | Copilot Sales |\n| **Full** | Fully autonomous, rare and restricted | Low — audit only | Simple bookings |\n\n### Escalation Triggers\n\n| Trigger | Action | Target |\n|---------|--------|--------|\n| Customer says \"supervisor\" | Immediate transfer | Human Expert |\n| Sentiment drops below threshold | Flag + optional transfer | Copilot Assisted |\n| Compliance violation detected | Immediate transfer | Human Expert |\n| Agent confidence below 70% | Request human review | Copilot Assisted |\n| 3+ failed resolution attempts | Escalate | Human Expert |\n```\n\nFile 3: docs/developer-guide/building-use-cases.md\n```\n---\ntitle: \"Building Use Cases\"\nsidebar_label: \"Building Use Cases\"\nsidebar_position: 3\ndescription: \"Development flow, service patterns, and deployment guide for building use cases on the KIX Platform\"\n---\n\n# Building Use Cases\n\n## Development Flow\n\n1. Define capability schema (inputs, outputs, SLA)\n2. Register capability in Schema Registry\n3. Implement agent or service\n4. Configure API routes\n5. Deploy to development environment via ArgoCD GitOps\n6. Test via API and MCP\n7. Promote through QA to production (ArgoCD syncs from Git)\n\n### GitOps Deployment via ArgoCD\n\nAll deployments follow a GitOps workflow managed by ArgoCD running on the shared platform cluster:\n\n| Step | Action | Tool |\n|------|--------|------|\n| 1 | Push code to repository | Git |\n| 2 | CI pipeline builds container image | GitHub Actions |\n| 3 | Image pushed to Artifact Registry (`kd-ix-eur-shr-artifacts`) | Docker/Buildkit |\n| 4 | ArgoCD Image Updater detects new image | Automatic |\n| 5 | ArgoCD syncs manifests to target cluster | Automatic |\n| 6 | Verify deployment status | ArgoCD UI or CLI |\n\n**ArgoCD UI:** `https://argocd.ix.konecta-digital.com` (Google OIDC login)\n\n**Key concepts:**\n- **Application**: A single deployable unit tracked by ArgoCD\n- **AppProject**: Scopes what an Application can access (namespaces, clusters, repos)\n- **ApplicationSet**: Templated generation of Applications across environments\n- **Sync**: ArgoCD applies Git state to the cluster (auto or manual)\n\n## Service Patterns\n\n### Exposing a Capability\n\n**Step 1: Define Schema** — Create a JSON Schema defining inputs, outputs, and metadata including input parameters with types and validation, output structure, SLA requirements, and routing rules.\n\n**Step 2: Register in Schema Registry** — Register the capability with name, version, owner team, description, input/output schemas, SLA targets, and default routing configuration.\n\n**Step 3: Implement Service** — Build the service that handles requests. Use platform clients for dependencies, follow error handling patterns, add observability instrumentation.\n\n**Step 4: Build Agents** — Build any agents required in CrewAI. Define agent roles, goals, and available tools. Configure agent collaboration patterns.\n\n**Step 5: Configure Routing** — Define Kong routes including API path, authentication requirements, rate limits, and request/response transformations.\n\n**Step 6: Register MCP Tool (Optional)** — If the capability should be available to AI agents, register tool in MCP Gateway, define tool description for discovery, map to underlying service.\n\n### Consuming a Capability\n\n**Via REST API:**\n- Obtain API key or JWT token\n- Call Kong endpoint with authentication header\n- Handle standard error responses\n- Use trace ID for debugging\n\n**Via MCP (AI Agents):**\n- Query MCP Gateway for available tools\n- Call tool with required parameters\n- Receive structured response\n- Handle errors gracefully\n\n**Via Internal Service:**\n- Use platform-provided client library\n- Authentication handled automatically\n- Retry and circuit breaker included\n\n### Error Handling\n\nAll services must return errors in standard format:\n\n| Field | Description |\n|-------|-------------|\n| code | Machine-readable error code |\n| message | Human-readable description |\n| details | Additional context (optional) |\n| trace_id | Correlation ID for debugging |\n\n**Standard Error Codes:**\n\n| Code | HTTP Status | Meaning |\n|------|-------------|---------|\n| VALIDATION_ERROR | 400 | Invalid input |\n| UNAUTHORIZED | 401 | Missing or invalid authentication |\n| FORBIDDEN | 403 | Insufficient permissions |\n| NOT_FOUND | 404 | Resource not found |\n| CONFLICT | 409 | Business rule violation |\n| RATE_LIMITED | 429 | Too many requests |\n| INTERNAL_ERROR | 500 | Unexpected failure |\n\n### Async Patterns\n\n**Callback Pattern:**\n- Submit request with callback URL\n- Receive request ID immediately\n- Platform calls callback when complete\n\n**Event-Driven Pattern:**\n- Publish event to Pub/Sub topic\n- Subscribers react to events\n- Decoupled processing\n\n## Governance Requirements\n\n### Security Requirements\n\n| Requirement | Implementation |\n|-------------|----------------|\n| Authentication | All endpoints require JWT or API key |\n| Authorization | Scope-based access control |\n| Encryption in transit | TLS 1.3 on all connections |\n| Encryption at rest | Google-managed keys (CMEK for sensitive) |\n| Network isolation | Private IPs only, no public endpoints |\n| Secrets | Secret Manager, no hardcoded credentials |\n| Audit logging | All access logged, 7-year retention |\n\n### Compliance Requirements\n\n| Regulation | Requirement | Implementation |\n|------------|-------------|----------------|\n| GDPR | Data subject rights | Deletion and export APIs |\n| GDPR | Consent management | Consent service integration |\n| GDPR | Data residency | EU regions only |\n| EU AI Act | Transparency | Decision logging |\n| EU AI Act | Human oversight | Escalation capability |\n\n### Data Classification\n\n| Level | Examples | Requirements |\n|-------|----------|--------------|\n| Public | Marketing content | None |\n| Internal | Business metrics | Encryption, access control |\n| Confidential | Customer PII | Encryption, audit logging, need-to-know |\n| Restricted | Payment data | CMEK, VPC-SC, approval workflow |\n```\n\nFile 4: docs/developer-guide/technology-specs.md\n```\n---\ntitle: \"Technology Specifications\"\nsidebar_label: \"Technology Specs\"\nsidebar_position: 4\ndescription: \"Detailed specifications for each platform component including CrewAI, LiteLLM, Kong, databases, and more\"\n---\n\n# Technology Specifications\n\n## CrewAI\n\n**Purpose:** Multi-agent orchestration for autonomous task execution\n\n**What It Does:**\n- Defines agents with roles, goals, and tools\n- Orchestrates tasks across multiple agents\n- Manages agent collaboration and handoffs\n- Integrates with LLM gateway for model access\n\n**Constraints:**\n- All LLM calls must use platform gateway (no direct API calls)\n- Maximum execution time configurable per agent\n- Agent state must be externalized for fault tolerance\n\n**Example Crew Structure:**\n```\nEnd-User Self-Healing Crew\n├── Triage Agent\n│   └── Classifies issue type, urgency, complexity\n├── Diagnostic Agent\n│   └── Runs diagnostic checks via Nexthink MCP\n├── Resolution Agent\n│   └── Executes fixes via ServiceNow/AD MCP\n├── Communication Agent\n│   └── Updates user on progress\n└── Escalation Agent\n    └── Hands off to human with full context\n```\n\n## ElevenLabs\n\n**Purpose:** Voice synthesis and conversational AI (primary voice runtime)\n\n**What It Does:**\n- Text-to-speech synthesis\n- Real-time conversational AI\n- Speech-to-Text\n- Multi-language support\n\n**Constraints:**\n- Voice calls must use platform client via Kong\n- Latency budget: 500ms for text-to-speech\n- Supported languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese (MVP)\n\n**Voice Latency Budget:**\n\n| Stage | Target | Max |\n|-------|--------|-----|\n| Speech-to-Text | 150ms | 300ms |\n| Agent Processing | 300ms | 500ms |\n| Text-to-Speech | 150ms | 300ms |\n| **Total Round-Trip** | **600ms** | **1100ms** |\n\n## LiteLLM\n\n**Purpose:** Unified LLM access and MCP tool gateway\n\n**LLM Gateway Features:**\n- Abstracts multiple LLM providers behind single interface\n- Handles model fallback and retry logic\n- Manages API keys centrally\n- Tracks token usage per use case\n- Provides response caching\n\n**MCP Gateway Features:**\n- Exposes platform capabilities as MCP tools\n- Enables AI agents to discover available tools\n- Routes tool calls to appropriate services\n\n**Available Models:**\n\n| Model | Provider | Recommended Use |\n|-------|----------|-----------------|\n| Gemini 2.5 Flash | Google | Default — fast, cost-effective |\n| Gemini 2.5 Pro | Google | Complex reasoning tasks |\n| Claude 3 Sonnet | Anthropic | Fallback |\n| GPT-4 Turbo | OpenAI | Fallback |\n\n**Constraints:**\n- No direct calls to model provider APIs\n- Token budgets monitored per use case\n- Caching enabled by default\n- Prompt logging with PII redaction\n\n## Kong API Gateway\n\n**Purpose:** API gateway for service exposure and third-party API abstraction\n\n**Available Capabilities:**\n- JWT validation (external identity integration)\n- API key authentication\n- Rate limiting (per key, per route)\n- Request/response transformation\n- Third-party API proxying\n\n**Constraints:**\n- All external traffic must pass through Kong\n- No direct pod access from outside cluster\n- Rate limits enforced per API key\n\n## Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL)\n\n**Purpose:** Relational data storage\n\n**Specifications:**\n- PostgreSQL version 15\n- Instance: 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM (adjustable)\n- Storage: SSD with auto-grow\n- Backups: Daily, 7-day retention\n- HA: Regional (Prod), Zonal (Dev/QA)\n\n**Constraints:**\n- No DDL changes in application code (use migrations)\n- Connection pooling required\n- Private IP access only\n\n## Redis (Memorystore)\n\n**Purpose:** Caching and session state\n\n**Specifications:**\n- Redis version 7.0\n- Tier: Standard (HA)\n- Memory: 5GB shared (expandable)\n- Persistence: RDB snapshots\n\n**Constraints:**\n- Keys must be prefixed with use case name\n- TTL required on all keys (24h max default)\n- No KEYS command (use SCAN)\n- No Lua scripts without approval\n\n## Qdrant\n\n**Purpose:** Vector storage for RAG and semantic search\n\n**Specifications:**\n- Replicas: 3 (Prod), 1 (Dev/QA)\n- Storage: Persistent SSD\n- Max vectors: 10M per collection\n\n**Constraints:**\n- Collection names prefixed with use case\n- Must use platform embedding model for consistency\n- Backup responsibility with platform team\n\n## Pub/Sub\n\n**Purpose:** Asynchronous messaging and event-driven architecture\n\n**Specifications:**\n- Message retention: 7 days\n- Ack deadline: 60 seconds\n- Max message size: 10MB\n- Ordering: Optional per topic\n\n**Constraints:**\n- Topic/subscription names prefixed with use case\n- Dead letter queue required for production\n- Idempotent message handling required\n\n## GCS (Cloud Storage)\n\n**Purpose:** Object storage for documents and artifacts\n\n**Specifications:**\n- Storage class: Standard\n- Location: EU (multi-region)\n- Lifecycle: 90d → Nearline → 365d → Archive\n- Versioning: Enabled\n\n**Constraints:**\n- No public access\n- Signed URLs for temporary external access\n- Max object size: 5TB\n\n## Channel Hub\n\n**Purpose:** Outbound messaging across multiple channels\n\n**Supported Channels:**\n\n| Channel | Requirements |\n|---------|--------------|\n| SMS | Approved sender ID |\n| Email | Verified sending domain |\n| WhatsApp | Pre-approved message templates |\n| Google Chat | Internal use only |\n\n**Constraints:**\n- All messages logged for audit\n- Rate limits per channel\n- PII handling rules apply\n- Templates required for WhatsApp\n```\n\nFile 5: docs/developer-guide/use-case-examples.md\n```\n---\ntitle: \"Use Case Examples\"\nsidebar_label: \"Use Case Examples\"\nsidebar_position: 5\ndescription: \"Real-world use automation for Konecta employees via Google Chat.\n\n**Control Plane Flow:**\n\n| Intent | Routing |\n|--------|---------|\n| Password reset | Autonomous Agent |\n| Software install | Autonomous Agent |\n| Hardware issue | Human Expert |\n| Complex/unclear | Copilot-Assisted |\n\n**Layer Mapping:**\n\n| Layer | Component | Technology |\n|-------|-----------|------------|\n| ENGAGE | Conversational   "content": "import { readFileSync } from \"fs\";\nimport { resolve, relative, basename } from \"path\";\nimport { glob } from \"glob\";\nimport matter from \"gray-matter\";\n\nexport interface DocPage {\n  path: string;\n  relativePath: string;\n  title: string;\n  sidebarLabel: string;\n  description: string;\n  category: string;\n  content: string;\n  rawContent: string;\n}\n\nexport interface GlossaryEntry {\n  term: string;\n  definition: string;\n}\n\nexport interface ModuleEntry {\n  name: string;\n  type: string;\n  description: string;\n  path: string;\n  repoUrl: string;\n}\n\nexport interface AdrEntry {\n  id: string;\n  title: string;\n  status: string;\n  content: string;\n  path: string;\n}\n\nexport async function loadDocs(docsRoot: string): Promise<DocPage[]> {\n  const pattern = resolve(docsRoot, \"**/*.md\");\n  const files = await glob(pattern);\n  const pages: DocPage[] = [];\n\n  for (const filePath of files) {\n    try {\n      const raw = readFileSync(filePath, \"utf-8\");\n      const { data, content } = matter(raw);\n      const rel = relative(docsRoot, filePath);\n      const parts = rel.split(\"/\");\n      const category = parts.length > 1 ? parts[0] : \"root\";\n\n      pages.push({\n        path: filePath,\n        relativePath: rel.replace(/\\.md$/, \"\"),\n        title: data.title || basename(filePath, \".md\"),\n        sidebarLabel: data.sidebar_label || data.title || basename(filePath, \".md\"),\n        description: data.description || \"\",\n        category,\n        content,\n        rawContent: raw,\n      });\n    } catch (err) {\n      console.error(`Failed to load ${filePath}: ${err}`);\n    }\n  }\n\n  return pages;\n}\n\nexport function extractGlossary(pages: DocPage[]): GlossaryEntry[] {\n  const glossaryPage = pages.find(\n    (p) => p.relativePath === \"reference/glossary\"\n  );\n  if (!glossaryPage) return [];\n\n  const entries: GlossaryEntry[] = [];\n  const lines = glossaryPage.content.split(\"\\n\");\n\n  for (const line of lines) {\n    const match = line.match(\n      /^\\|\\s*\\*\\*(.+?)\\*\\*\\s*\\|\\s*(.+?)\\s*\\|$/\n    );\n    if (match) {\n      entries.push({ term: match[1], definition: match[2] });\n    }\n  }\n\n  return entries;\n}\n\nexport function extractModules(pages: DocPage[]): ModuleEntry[] {\n  const catalogPage = pages.find(\n    (p) => p.relativePath === \"reference/module-catalog\"\n  );\n  if (!catalogPage) return [];\n\n  const entries: ModuleEntry[] = [];\n  const lines = catalogPage.content.split(\"\\n\");\n  let currentType = \"unknown\";\n\n  for (const line of lines) {\n    if (line.startsWith(\"## \") || line.startsWith(\"### \")) {\n      currentType = line.replace(/^#+\\s*/, \"\").trim();\n    }\n    const match = line.match(\n      /^\\|\\s*\\*?\\*?`?(\\S+?)`?\\*?\\*?\\s*\\|\\s*(.+?)\\s*\\|/\n    );\n    if (match && !match[1].startsWith(\"Module\") && !match[1].startsWith(\"---\")) {\n      entries.push({\n        name: match[1],\n        type: currentType,\n        description: match[2].replace(/\\|.*$/, \"\").trim(),\n        path: `reference/module-catalog`,\n        repoUrl: `https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules`,\n      });\n    }\n  }\n\n  return entries;\n}\n\nexport function extractAdrs(pages: DocPage[]): AdrEntry[] {\n  return pages\n    .filter((p) => p.category === \"adr\" && p.relativePath !== \"adr/index\")\n    .map((p) => {\n      const idMatch = p.relativePath.match(/adr-(\\d+)/);\n      const statusMatch = p.content.match(/\\*\\*Status:\\*\\*\\s*(.+)/);\n      return {\n        id: idMatch ? `ADR-${idMatch[1]}` : p.relativePath,\n        title: p.title,\n        status: statusMatch ? statusMatch[1].trim() : \"Unknown\",\n        content: p.content,\n        path: p.relativePath,\n      };\n    });\n}\n"
}

{

  "content": "import MiniSearch from \"minisearch\";\nimport type { DocPage } from \"./content-loader.js\";\n\nexport interface SearchResult {\n  path: string;\n  title: string;\n  snippet: string;\n  score: number;\n  category: string;\n}\n\nlet searchIndex: MiniSearch<DocPage> | null = null;\nlet indexedPages: DocPage[] = [];\n\nexport function buildSearchIndex(pages: DocPage[]): void {\n  indexedPages = pages;\n  searchIndex = new MiniSearch<DocPage>({\n    fields: [\"title\", \"description\", \"content\", \"category\"],\n    storeFields: [\"title\", \"relativePath\", \"description\", \"category\"],\n    idField: \"relativePath\",\n    searchOptions: {\n      boost: { title: 3, description: 2, content: 1 },\n      fuzzy: 0.2,\n      prefix: true,\n    },\n  });\n\n  searchIndex.addAll(pages);\n  console.error(`Search index built with ${pages.length} documents`);\n}\n\nexport function searchDocs(\n  query: string,\n  category?: string,\n  limit: number = 10\n): SearchResult[] {\n  if (!searchIndex) return [];\n\n  const filter = category\n    ? { filter: (result: { category: string }) => result.category === category }\n    : {};\n\n  const results = searchIndex.search(query, filter);\n\n  return results.slice(0, limit).map((result) => {\n    const page = indexedPages.find((p) => p.relativePath === result.id);\n    const snippet = extractSnippet(page?.content || \"\", query);\n\n    return {\n      path: result.id as string,\n      title: (result as unknown as { title: string }).title || String(result.id),\n      snippet,\n      score: result.score,\n      category: (result as unknown as { category: string }).category || \"unknown\",\n    };\n  });\n}\n\nfunction extractSnippet(content: string, query: string): string {\n  const terms = query.toLowerCase().split(/\\s+/);\n  const lines = content.split(\"\\n\").filter((l) => l.trim().length > 0);\n\n  for (const line of lines) {\n    const lower = line.toLowerCase();\n    if (terms.some((term) => lower.includes(term))) {\n      const cleaned = line.replace(/[#*|`]/g, \"\").trim();\n      return cleaned.length > 200 ? cleaned.substring(0, 200) + \"...\" : cleaned;\n    }\n  }\n\n  const firstContent = lines\n    .find((l) => !l.startsWith(\"#\") && !l.startsWith(\"|\") && !l.startsWith(\"---\"))\n    ?.trim();\n  return firstContent\n    ? firstContent.length > 200\n      ? firstContent.substring(0, 200) + \"...\"\n      : firstContent\n    : \"\";\n}\n"
}
