  "content": "import type { DocPage } from \"./content-loader.js\";\n\nexport function listDocResources(pages: DocPage[]) {\n  return pages.map((page) => ({\n    uri: `docs://kix-platform/${page.relativePath}`,\n    name: page.title,\n    description: page.description || `Documentation page: ${page.title}`,\n    mimeType: \"text/markdown\" as const,\n  }));\n}\n\nexport function getDocIndex(pages: DocPage[]) {\n  return JSON.stringify(\n    pages.map((p) => ({\n      path: p.relativePath,\n      title: p.title,\n      description: p.description,\n      category: p.category,\n    })),\n    null,\n    2\n  );\n}\n\nexport function readDocResource(\n  pages: DocPage[],\n  uri: string\n): string | null {\n  const path = uri.replace(\"docs://kix-platform/\", \"\");\n\n  if (path === \"index\") {\n    return getDocIndex(pages);\n  }\n\n  const page = pages.find((p) => p.relativePath === path);\n  return page ? page.rawContent : null;\n}\n"
}

{\n        type: \"text\" as const,\n        text: JSON.stringify(\n          adrs.map((a) => ({\n            id: a.id,\n            title: a.title,\n            status: a.status,\n          })),\n Completeness\n- Are there any missing sections?\n- Are prerequisites stated?\n- Are edge cases covered?\n- Is there a clear \"next steps\" or related docs section?\n\n## 3. Clarity\n- Is the language clear and concise?\n- Is jargon explained?\n- Are steps numbered and actionable?\n- Would a new team member understand this?\n\n## 4. Standards Compliance\n- Does it follow the KIX documentation standards?\n- Is the front matter complete (title, sidebar_label, sidebar_position, description)?\n- Are code blocks properly formatted with language hints?\n- Are cross-references using absolute Docusaurus paths?\n\nProvide your review as:\n- **Issues Found:** List of problems with severity (Critical/Major/Minor)\n- **Suggestions:** Improvements that would enhance the page\n- **Overall Assessment:** Brief summary of documentation quality`;\n}\n"
}

${pages.length} pages, ${glossary.length} glossary entries, ${modules.length} modules, ${adrs.length} ADRs`\n  );\n\n  // Create MCP server\n  const server = new McpServer({\n    name: \"kix-docs\",\n    version: \"1.0.0\",\n  });\n\n  // Register resources\n  server.resource(\n    \"doc-index\",\n    \"docs://kix-platform/index\",\n    {\n      description: \"Index of all KIX Platform documentation pages\",\n      mimeType: \"application/json\",\n    },\n    async () => ({\n      contents: [\n        {\n          uri: \"docs://kix-platform/index\",\n          mimeType: \"application/json\" as const,\n          text: JSON.stringify(\n            pages.map((p) => ({\n              path: p.relativePath,\n              title: p.title,\n              description: p.description,\n              category: p.category,\n            })),\n            null,\n            2\n          ),\n        },\n      ],\n    })\n  );\n\n  // Register individual doc page resources\n  for (const page of pages) {\n    const uri = `docs://kix-platform/${page.relativePath}`;\n    server.resource(\n      `doc-${page.relativePath.replace(/\\//g, \"-\")}`,\n      uri,\n      {\n        description: page.description || `Documentation: ${page.title}`,\n        mimeType: \"text/markdown\",\n      },\n      async () => ({\n        contents: [\n          {\n            uri,\n            mimeType: \"text/markdown\" as const,\n            text: page.rawContent,\n          },\n        ],\n      })\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Register tools\n  server.tool(\n    \"search_docs\",\n    \"Search KIX Platform documentation by keyword or phrase\",\n    searchDocsSchema.shape,\n    async (args) => handleSearchDocs(searchDocsSchema.parse(args))\n  );\n\n  server.tool(\n    \"lookup_glossary\",\n    \"Look up a term in the KIX Platform glossary\",\n    lookupGlossarySchema.shape,\n    async (args) => handleLookupGlossary(lookupGlossarySchema.parse(args), glossary)\n  );\n\n  server.tool(\n    \"lookup_module\",\n    \"Look up a Terraform or Helm module in the module catalog\",\n    lookupModuleSchema.shape,\n    async (args) => handleLookupModule(lookupModuleSchema.parse(args), modules)\n  );\n\n  server.tool(\n    \"lookup_adr\",\n    \"Look up an Architecture Decision Record by ID or keyword\",\n    lookupAdrSchema.shape,\n    async (args) => handleLookupAdr(lookupAdrSchema.parse(args), adrs)\n  );\n\n  // Register prompts\n  server.prompt(\n    DOC_REVIEW_PROMPT.name,\n    DOC_REVIEW_PROMPT.description,\n    DOC_REVIEW_PROMPT.arguments,\n    async (args) => {\n      const pagePath = args.page_path;\n      const content = readDocResource(pages, `docs://kix-platform/${pagePath}`);\n\n      if (!content) {\n        return {\n          messages: [\n            {\n              role: \"user\" as const,\n              content: {\n                type: \"text\" as const,\n                text: `Documentation page not found: ${pagePath}\\n\\nAvailable pages:\\n${pages.map((p) => `- ${p.relativePath}`).join(\"\\n\")}`,\n              },\n            },\n          ],\n        };\n      }\n\n      return {\n        messages: [\n          {\n            role: \"user\" as const,\n            content: {\n              type: \"text\" as const,\n              text: getDocReviewPrompt(content, pagePath),\n            },\n          },\n        ],\n      };\n    }\n  );\n\n  // Start server with stdio transport\n  const transport = new StdioServerTransport();\n  await server.connect(transport);\n\n  console.error(\"KIX Docs MCP Server running on stdio\");\n}\n\nmain().catch((error) => {\n  console.error(\"Fatal error:\", error);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n"
}

    29→## Universal Operational Standards
    30→
    31→These standards apply to **all repositories** in the KIX Platform organization.
    32→
    33→### Challenge and Validation Protocol
    34→
    35→**Core Principle:** Always validate work before claiming completion. Never declare "done" without evidence.
    36→
    37→**Before Claiming Task Complete:**
    38→
    39→1. **Prove It Works**
    40→   - [ ] Run validation commands (terraform plan, tests, builds)
    41→   - [ ] Capture output showing success
    42→   - [ ] Verify against acceptance criteria
    43→   - [ ] Check for warnings or unexpected side effects
    44→
    45→2. **Review for Quality**
    46→   - [ ] Code follows repository standards
    47→   - [ ] No security vulnerabilities introduced
    48→   - [ ] Documentation updated if needed
    49→   - [ ] No over-engineering beyond requirements
    50→
    51→3. **Verify Completeness**
    52→   - [ ] All subtasks completed
    53→   - [ ] Edge cases considered
    54→   - [ ] Rollback plan documented (for infrastructure changes)
    55→   - [ ] User can reproduce/verify independently
    56→
    57→**Volunteer Evidence:** Don't wait for user to ask "did it work?" - proactively share:
    58→- Command output showing success
    59→- Test results
    60→- Metrics (files changed, time taken)
    61→- Known limitations or follow-up items
    62→
    63→**When Blocked:** If you can't complete a task:
    64→- State the blocker clearly
    65→- Explain what you tried
    66→- Suggest alternatives or next steps
    67→- Don't claim partial completion as "done"
    68→
    69→### When to Use Plan Mode
    70→
    71→**ALWAYS use plan mode for:**
    72→
    73→1. **Environment Cloning** (dev → qa, qa → prod)
    74→   - Multiple config files to sync
    75→   - Risk of inconsistencies
    76→   - 15+ step process with dependencies
    77→
    78→2. **New Module Creation**
    79→   - Module design decisions
    80→   - Security requirements analysis
    81→   - Test strategy planning
    82→
    83→3. **Multi-Tier Infrastructure Changes**
    84→   - Changes spanning foundation → platform → kubernetes
    85→   - Complex apply order dependencies
    86→   - High risk of breaking existing workloads
    87→
    88→4. **Security-Sensitive Changes**
    89→   - IAM policy modifications
    90→   - Network policy changes
    91→   - Cloud Armor rule updates
    92→
    93→5. **First-Time Tasks** (no checklist exists)
    94→   - Need to explore patterns
    95→   - Unclear best approach
    96→   - Multiple valid options
    97→
    98→**DON'T use plan mode for:**
    99→- Single file edits with clear requirements
   100→- Well-documented operations with checklists

    35→
    36→## Quick Links
    37→
    38→| Document | Audience | Description |

    40→| [Architecture](https://konecta-ix-platform.github.io/kix-platform-docs/docs/ARCHITECTURE) | Engineers | Technical architecture, security model, compliance |

    46→
    47→## Local Development
    48→
    49→This site uses Jekyll for GitHub Pages.
    50→
    51→### Prerequisites
    52→
    53→```bash
    54→# Install Ruby and Bundler
    55→brew install ruby
    56→gem install bundler
    57→
    58→# Or use rbenv for version management
    59→brew install rbenv
    60→rbenv install 3.1.2
    61→rbenv global 3.1.2
    62→```
    63→
    64→### Running Locally
    65→
    66→```bash
    67→# Install dependencies
    68→bundle install
    69→
    70→# Serve locally (with live reload)
    71→bundle exec jekyll serve
    72→
    73→# Open in browser
    74→open http://localhost:4000
    75→```
    76→
    77→### Adding Dependencies
    78→
    79→If you need additional Jekyll plugins:
    80→
    81→1. Add to `Gemfile`
    82→2. Add to `_config.yml` plugins section
    83→3. Run `bundle install`
    84→4. Test locally before pushing
    85→
    86→## Adding Documentation
    87→
    88→### Create a New Document
    89→
    90→1. **Create markdown file:**
    91→   ```bash
    92→   touch docs/NEW_GUIDE.md
    93→   ```
    94→
    95→2. **Add Jekyll front matter:**
    96→   ```yaml
    97→   ---
    98→   layout: default
    99→   title: New Guide
   100→   ---
   101→
   102→   # New Guide
   103→
   104→   Content here...
   105→   ```
   106→
   107→3. **Add to navigation** in `_config.yml`:
   108→   ```yaml
   109→   navigation:
   110→     - title: New Guide
   111→       url: /docs/NEW_GUIDE
   112→   ```
   113→
   114→4. **Link from index.md** and related docs
   115→
   116→5. **Test locally** with `bundle exec jekyll serve`
   117→
   118→6. **Commit and push** to main
   119→
   120→### Adding Diagrams
   121→
   122→1. Create diagram (Draw.io, Lucidchart, etc.)
   123→2. Export as PNG or SVG
   124→3. Save to `docs/diagrams/` with descriptive name
   125→4. Embed in markdown:
   126→   ```markdown
   127→   ![Architecture Diagram](diagrams/kix-mvp-architecture.png)
   128→   ```
   129→
   130→## Documentation Standards
   131→
   132→### Markdown Guidelines
   133→
   134→- **Headings:** Use `#` for document title, `##` for sections, `###` for subsections
   135→- **Code Blocks:** Always specify language for syntax highlighting
   136→- **Links:** Use absolute URLs for cross-repository references
   137→- **Tables:** Use for structured data, keep concise
   138→- **Lists:** Use for sequential steps or itemized content
   139→
   140→### Writing Style
   141→
   142→**For Engineers:**
   143→- Technical accuracy first
   144→- Code examples with syntax highlighting
   145→- Command-line examples (copy-paste ready)
   146→- Architecture diagrams with clear labels
   147→
   148→**For Developers:**
   149→- How-to guides with numbered steps
   150→- Prerequisites stated upfront
   151→- Expected outcomes after each step
   152→- Common issues and solutions
   153→
   154→**For Leadership:**
   155→- Executive summary first
   156→- Business value and ROI focus
   157→- High-level architecture (minimal jargon)
   158→- Clear next steps and milestones
   159→
   160→### Example Code Block
   161→
   162→````markdown
   163→```bash
   164→# Deploy infrastructure
   165→cd environments/dev/gcp/network
   166→terraform init
   167→terraform plan
   168→terraform apply
   169→```
   170→
   171→```hcl
   172→module "landing_zone" {
   173→  source = "github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules//terraform/gcp/landing-zone?ref=v1.0.0"
   174→
   175→  project_id  = "kd-ix-eur-dev-network"
   176→  environment = "dev"
   177→}
   178→```
   179→````
   180→
   181→## Publishing
   182→
   183→Documentation is automatically published to GitHub Pages when pushed to main branch.
   184→
   185→**Process:**
   186→1. Push changes to main
   187→2. GitHub Actions builds site with Jekyll
   188→3. Site published to https://konecta-ix-platform.github.io/kix-platform-docs
   189→4. Changes visible within 1-2 minutes
   190→
   191→**Configuration:**
   192→- Repository Settings → Pages → Source: `main` branch
   193→- Build and deployment: GitHub Actions
   194→- Custom domain: Not configured (using default GitHub Pages URL)
   195→
   196→## Working with Claude Code
   197→
   198→This repository includes [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) with operational guidance for Claude Code:
   199→
   200→- **Documentation Standards** - Accuracy, clarity, completeness
   201→- **Documentation Principles** - Write for audience, structure for scanability
   202→- **Document Types** - Technical, how-to, strategic
   203→- **GitHub Pages** - Local testing, publishing
   204→- **Common Tasks** - Adding docs, diagrams, updating links
   205→
   206→See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for complete guide.
   207→
   208→## Repository Relationships
   209→
   210→This documentation references:
   211→
   212→- **[kix-platform-modules](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules)** - Terraform/Helm modules
   213→- **[kix-platform-infrastructure](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-infrastructure)** - Infrastructure deployments
   214→- **[kix-services-*](https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/)** - Platform services (Kong, LiteLLM, etc.)
   215→
   216→**Linking Guidelines:**
   217→- Use GitHub URLs (not relative paths)
   218→- Link to specific files when possible
   219→- Keep links current when repositories restructure
   220→
   221→## Contributing
   222→
   223→### Documentation Updates
   224→
   225→1. Fork or create feature branch
   226→2. Make changes
   227→3. Test locally with Jekyll
   228→4. Create pull request
   229→5. Address review comments
   230→6. Merge to main (auto-publishes)
   231→
   232→### Reporting Issues
   233→
   234→- **Broken Links:** Create GitHub Issue with link and expected destination
   235→- **Outdated Content:** Create GitHub Issue with section and update needed
   236→- **New Documentation:** Propose via GitHub Issue or PR

   # Kubernetes-specific modules\n|   |       +-- gke-config/         # Namespace, RBAC, network policies\n|   |       +-- kong-gateway/       # Kong API Gateway\n|   |       +-- litellm/            # LiteLLM proxy\n|   |       +-- argocd/             # ArgoCD GitOps (shared cluster)\n|   +-- environments/               # Environment-specific configurations\n|   |   +-- shared/                 # Shared services (ArgoCD, DNS)\n|   |   +-- lab/                    # Playground for new technology\n|   |   +-- dev/                    # Development\n|   |   +-- qa/                     # QA (mirrors prod)\n|   |   +-- prod/                   # Production\n|   +-- test/                       # Terratest integration tests\n+-- docs/                           # Documentation\n```\n\n---\n\n## Understanding the Repository Structure\n\n### Module Organization\n\nModules are organized by provider type:\n\n**GCP Modules** (`modules/gcp/`):\n- `base-environment` - GCP folders and projects\n- `landing-zone` - VPC, networking, security baseline\n- `gke-cluster` - GKE cluster creation\n- `data-services/*` - Cloud SQL, Redis, GCS, Pub/Sub\n\n**Kubernetes Modules** (`modules/kubernetes/`):\n- `gke-config` - Namespaces, RBAC, network policies\n- `kong-gateway` - Kong API Gateway\n- `litellm` - LiteLLM proxy\n- `argocd` - ArgoCD GitOps continuous delivery (shared cluster)\n\n### Service Dependency Chain\n\nServices must be deployed in order:\n\n```\n+---------------------+\n|     bootstrap       |  Creates state buckets (run once)\n+---------+-----------+\n          |\n          v\n+---------------------+\n|    gcp/network      |  VPC, subnets, NAT, firewall\n+---------+-----------+\n          |\n          +----------------+\n          v                v\n+---------------+  +---------------+\n|   gcp/gke     |  |   gcp/data    |  (can run in parallel)\n+-------+-------+  +---------------+\n        |\n        v\n+---------------------+\n| kubernetes/platform |  gke-config, kong, litellm\n+---------------------+\n```\n\n### State Management\n\nEach service has its own state file:\n\n```\ngs://kd-tfstate-{env}/\n+-- gcp/network/\n+-- gcp/gke/\n+-- gcp/data/\n+-- kubernetes/platform/\n```\n\n---\n\n## Environment Configuration\n\n### config.json (Per Environment)\n\nEach environment has a `config.json` that drives all deployments:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"global\": {\n    \"environment\": \"dev\",\n    \"region\": \"europe-west1\",\n    \"gke_project_id\": \"kd-ix-eur-dev-gke\",\n    \"data_project_id\": \"kd-ix-eur-dev-data\"\n  },\n  \"landing_zone\": { ... },\n  \"gke_cluster\": { ... },\n  \"gke_config\": { ... },\n  \"kong_gateway\": { ... }\n}\n```\n\n**Usage in Terraform:**\n\n```hcl\nlocals {\n  config = jsondecode(file(\"${path.module}/../config.json\"))\n}\n\nmodule \"landing_zone\" {\n  source   = \"../../../../modules/gcp/landing-zone\"\n  vpc_name = local.config.landing_zone.vpc_name\n}\n```\n\n### Environment Differences\n\n| Setting | Dev | QA | Prod |\n|---------|-----|-----|------|\n| Flow logs | 50% sampling | 50% sampling | 100% sampling |\n| Node pool min nodes | 1 | 1 | 2 |\n| Deletion protection | false | false | true |\n| Kong replicas | 2 | 2 | 3 |\n| VPC Service Controls | false | false | true |\n\n---\n\n## Your First Deployment\n\n### Step 0: Bootstrap (One-time)\n\n```bash\ncd terraform/environments/bootstrap\ncp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars\n# Edit terraform.tfvars with your organization values\n\nterraform init\nterraform apply\n```\n\n### Step 1: Deploy Network\n\n```bash\ncd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network\n\nterraform init\nterraform plan\nterraform apply\n# Takes 3-5 minutes\n```\n\n**Verify:**\n```bash\ngcloud compute networks describe kix-dev-vpc \\\n  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-network\n```\n\n### Step 2: Deploy GKE\n\n```bash\ncd ../gke\n\nterraform init\nterraform plan\nterraform apply\n# Takes 15-20 minutes\n```\n\n**Verify:**\n```bash\ngcloud container clusters get-credentials kix-dev-cluster \\\n  --region=europe-west1 \\\n  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke\n\nkubectl cluster-info\nkubectl get nodes\n```\n\n### Step 3: Deploy Kubernetes Platform\n\n```bash\ncd ../../kubernetes/platform\n\nterraform init\nterraform plan\nterraform apply\n```\n\n**Verify:**\n```bash\nkubectl get namespaces\nkubectl get pods -n kong\n```\n\n### Cleanup (Optional)\n\nDestroy in reverse order:\n```bash\ncd terraform/environments/dev/kubernetes/platform && terraform destroy\ncd ../../gcp/gke && terraform destroy\ncd ../network && terraform destroy\n```\n\n---\n\n## Terraform Development Standards\n\n### Module Structure\n\nEvery module MUST include:\n\n```\nmodule-name/\n+-- main.tf           # Resource definitions\n+-- variables.tf      # Input variables with descriptions\n+-- outputs.tf        # Output values with descriptions\n+-- versions.tf       # Provider version constraints\n+-- README.md         # Documentation\n+-- examples/         # Working examples\n```\n\n### Variable Naming Conventions\n\n| Pattern | Use Case | Example |\n|---------|----------|---------|\n| `enable_*` | Feature flags | `enable_versioning`, `enable_auth` |\n| `create_*` | Resource creation | `create_service_account` |\n| `*_config` | Configuration objects | `maintenance_config`, `logging_config` |\n| `*_policy` | Policy definitions | `retention_policy` |\n\n**Correct:**\n```hcl\nvariable \"enable_versioning\" {\n  type        = bool\n  default     = true\n  description = \"Enable object versioning for the bucket\"\n}\n\nvariable \"maintenance_config\" {\n  type = object({\n    day  = string\n    hour = number\n  })\n  description = \"Maintenance window configuration\"\n}\n```\n\n**Incorrect:**\n```hcl\nvariable \"auth_enabled\" { ... }      # Use enable_* prefix\nvariable \"maintenance_policy\" { ... } # Use *_config suffix\n```\n\n### Required Variables (All Modules)\n\n| Variable | Type | Description |\n|----------|------|-------------|\n| `project_id` | string | GCP project ID |\n| `environment` | string | Environment name (dev, qa, prod, lab) |\n| `cost_center` | string | Cost center for billing |\n\n### Variable Validation\n\n```hcl\nvariable \"environment\" {\n  type        = string\n  description = \"Environment name\"\n\n  validation {\n    condition     = contains([\"dev\", \"qa\", \"prod\", \"lab\", \"shared\"], var.environment)\n    error_message = \"Environment must be one of: dev, qa, prod, lab, shared\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### README Standards\n\nAll module READMEs MUST include:\n- Overview and architecture\n- Usage examples (basic and production)\n- **Security Requirements section** (mandatory)\n- Inputs/Outputs tables\n- Document metadata footer\n\n### Common Patterns\n\n**Use for_each:**\n```hcl\nresource \"google_storage_bucket\" \"buckets\" {\n  for_each = toset([\"documents\", \"artifacts\", \"logs\"])\n  name     = \"${var.usecase_name}-${each.value}-${var.environment}\"\n}\n```\n\n**Use locals for computed values:**\n```hcl\nlocals {\n  project_id = \"kix-${var.environment}-${var.function}\"\n  common_labels = {\n    environment = var.environment\n    managed_by  = \"terraform\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Pre-Commit Checklist\n\n```bash\nterraform fmt -recursive\nterraform validate\nterraform plan -out=tfplan\nterraform-docs markdown . > README.md\n```\n\n---\n\n## Running Tests\n\n### Run Individual Tests\n\n```bash\ncd terraform/test\n\ngo test -v -timeout 30m -run TestBaseEnvironment\ngo test -v -timeout 30m -run TestLandingZone\ngo test -v -timeout 60m -run TestGKECluster\ngo test -v -timeout 30m -run TestArgoCD\n```\n\n### Run All Tests\n\n```bash\ngo test -v -timeout 120m ./...\n```\n\n### Debug Mode\n\n```bash\nexport SKIP_TEARDOWN=true\ngo test -v -timeout 30m -run TestGKECluster\n# Manually inspect, then destroy\n```\n\n---\n\n## Deploying Infrastructure Changes\n\nChanges to infrastructure follow a **controlled deployment process** with manual approvals for production.\n\n### Overview\n\n```\nFeature Branch --> PR Validation --> Merge to Main --> Manual Deploy\n    (fast)           (~10 min)       (validates)       (controlled)\n```\n\n### 1. Make Changes in Feature Branch\n\n```bash\n# Create feature branch\ngit checkout -b feature/add-redis-instance\n\n# Make Terraform changes\ncd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/data\n# Edit *.tf files\n\n# Validate locally\nterraform fmt -recursive\nterraform validate\nterraform plan\n```\n\n### 2. Open Pull Request\n\nSubmit PR to `main` branch. PR validation runs automatically (~10 minutes):\n\n**What happens:**\n- Terraform format check\n- Security scan (tfsec)\n- Terraform validate\n- Generate plans for changed directories\n- Run fast smoke tests (if modules changed)\n- Plan summary posted as PR comment\n\n**Review the plan output:**\n```\nPlan: 2 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy\n\n+ google_redis_instance.cache\n+ google_compute_firewall.redis_ingress\n~ google_service_account.redis (labels)\n```\n\n### 3. Merge to Main\n\nAfter PR approval, merge to `main`. **No automatic deployment occurs.**\n\n**What happens:**\n- Main validation runs (validates all changes)\n- Plans regenerated to prove deployability\n- Release tagged with semantic version (e.g., v1.2.3)\n- No infrastructure changes applied\n\n### 4. Deploy During Change Window\n\nNavigate to **Actions > Deploy Infrastructure** workflow and click **Run workflow**.\n\n**Configure deployment:**\n\n| Input | Description | Example |\n|-------|-------------|---------|\n| **environment** | Target environment | `dev`, `qa`, `prod`, `shared` |\n| **scope** | What to deploy | `network`, `gke`, `data`, `kong`, `all` |\n| **dry_run** | Plan only, no apply | `false` (deploy) or `true` (plan only) |\n| **auto_approve** | Skip approval (dev only) | `true` (dev) or `false` (qa/prod) |\n\n**Example: Deploy Redis to Dev**\n```yaml\nenvironment: dev\nscope: data\ndry_run: false\nauto_approve: true  # Dev allows auto-approve\n```\n\n**Example: Deploy GKE to Production**\n```yaml\nenvironment: prod\nscope: gke\ndry_run: false\nauto_approve: false  # Prod requires approval\n```\n\n**Deployment flow:**\n1. **Pre-flight checks** - Validates change window, permissions\n2. **Validate** - Format, security scan\n3. **Plan** - Generates fresh plan (catches drift)\n4. **Approval** - Manual review and approval (QA/Prod)\n5. **Apply** - Executes Terraform apply\n6. **Verify** - Runs smoke tests\n7. **Summary** - Posts deployment report\n\n### 5. Monitor Deployment\n\nWatch the workflow run:\n- Green checkmarks indicate success\n- Review plan output before approval\n- Monitor apply progress\n- Verify outputs after completion\n\n### Change Windows\n\nInfrastructure deployments are restricted by environment:\n\n| Environment | Change Window | Approval | Notes |\n|-------------|---------------|----------|-------|\n| **dev** | Anytime | Optional (auto-approve allowed) | Rapid iteration |\n| **qa** | Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC) | Required | Avoid during testing |\n| **prod** | **Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC only** | Required + change ticket | Restricted window |\n| **shared** | Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC) | Required | Impacts all environments |\n\n**Production restrictions:**\n- Deployments outside the window are **automatically blocked**\n- Emergency hotfixes require manual approval bypass (see [CI/CD Runbook](/docs/infrastructure-ops/cicd-runbook))\n- Change tickets must be referenced in deployment approval\n\n### Scope Mapping\n\nThe `scope` input maps to Terraform directories:\n\n| Scope | Description | Directories |\n|-------|-------------|-------------|\n| `network` | VPC, subnets, firewall | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/network` |\n| `security` | Security baseline | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/security` |\n| `gke` | GKE cluster | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/gke` |\n| `platform` | Namespaces, RBAC | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/platform` |\n| `data` | Cloud SQL, Redis, GCS | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/data` |\n| `kong` | Kong API Gateway | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/kong` |\n| `gateway` | GKE Gateway | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/gateway` |\n| `litellm` | LiteLLM proxy | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/litellm` |\n| `argocd` | ArgoCD (shared only) | `terraform/environments/shared/kubernetes/argocd` |\n| `all` | All of the above | Sequential deployment (network > security > gke > platform > data) |\n\n### Deployment Best Practices\n\n**Before deploying:**\n- Verify plan output matches intent\n- Check for unexpected resource destruction\n- Ensure change window compliance (production)\n- Notify team in #kix-platform-engineering\n\n**During deployment:**\n- Monitor workflow progress\n- Watch for errors in real-time\n- Don't close browser until complete\n\n**After deployment:**\n- Verify services are healthy\n- Review Terraform outputs\n- Monitor metrics for anomalies\n- Update deployment log\n\n### Rollback Procedure\n\nIf deployment causes issues:\n\n```bash\n# Option 1: Revert code and redeploy\ngit revert <commit-hash>\ngit push origin main\n# Then run deploy workflow with reverted code\n\n# Option 2: Manual Terraform rollback (emergency only)\ncd terraform/environments/{env}/{scope}\nterraform init\nterraform state pull > backup.tfstate\n# Manually fix state or apply reverted config\n```\n\n### Advanced: Drift Detection\n\nNightly workflow checks for infrastructure drift:\n- Runs daily at 02:00 UTC\n- Checks all environments and scopes\n- Creates GitHub issues if drift detected\n\n**Manually trigger drift detection:**\n```\nActions > Nightly Quality Checks > Run workflow\n```\n\n### Troubleshooting Deployments\n\nSee [CI/CD Runbook](/docs/infrastructure-ops/cicd-runbook) for detailed troubleshooting:\n- Plan shows unexpected changes\n- Apply fails with \"resource already exists\"\n- Workflow stuck on approval\n- Change window blocked production deployment\n\n---\n\n## Contributing\n\n### Before Contributing\n\n1. Read `CLAUDE.md` section \"Approval Requirements\"\n2. Create feature branch: `git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name`\n3. Follow pre-commit checklist\n4. Submit PR for review\n\n### Good First Contributions\n\n- Fix documentation typos\n- Add examples to module READMEs\n- Improve variable descriptions\n- Add validation rules\n\n### Approval Requirements\n\n| Environment | Approvers |\n|-------------|-----------|\n| Dev | Infrastructure Lead |\n| QA | Infrastructure Lead + DevSecOps Lead |\n| Prod | Chief Engineer + Infrastructure Lead + CISO |\n\n---\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Error: \"The caller does not have permission\"\n\n```bash\ngcloud auth list\ngcloud config get-value account\n# If wrong account:\ngcloud auth login your.email@konecta-group.com\ngcloud auth application-default login\n```\n\n### Error: \"Failed to save state: AccessDenied\"\n\n```bash\ngsutil ls gs://kd-tfstate-dev\nterraform init -reconfigure\n```\n\n### Error: \"Quota exceeded\"\n\n```bash\ngcloud compute project-info describe \\\n  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke \\\n  --format=\"table(quotas.metric,quotas.limit,quotas.usage)\"\n# Request quota increase in GCP Console\n```\n\n### Error: \"Timeout waiting for cluster\"\n\nGKE clusters take 15-20 minutes. Check status:\n```bash\ngcloud container clusters describe kix-dev-cluster \\\n  --region=europe-west1 \\\n  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke\n```\n\n### State Lock Error\n\n```bash\n# Only if certain no other process is running:\nterraform force-unlock LOCK_ID\n```\n\n### Debug Logging\n\n```bash\nexport TF_LOG=DEBUG\nexport TF_LOG_PATH=./terraform-debug.log\nterraform plan\n# Review logs\ncat terraform-debug.log\nunset TF_LOG TF_LOG_PATH\n```\n\n### Getting Help\n\n**Include when asking for help:**\n1. Full error message\n2. Terraform version: `terraform version`\n3. Module/environment\n4. Steps to reproduce\n\n---\n\n## Contact Information\n\n| Role | Name | Email |\n|------|------|-------|\n| Chief Engineer | Adam Dolman | adam.dolman@konecta.com |\n| Infrastructure Lead | Nathan Booth | nathan.booth@konecta.com |\n| DevSecOps Lead | Meghant Sharma | meghant.sharma@konecta.com |\n| AI Lead | Mischa van Oijen | mischa.vanoijen@konecta.com |\n\n**Communication:**\n- Slack: #kix-platform-engineering\n- Urgent: #kix-platform-oncall\n- Security: security@konecta-group.com\n- Weekly sync: Fridays 10:00 UTC\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":237,"cache_read_input_tokens":28548,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":237},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"}},"requestId":"req_011CXvxAxBaUz36HWTt82qf7","type":"assistant","uuid":"c6f6fa3b-09f1-4c97-8bff-b86c9cfd0edf","timestamp":"2026-02-08T17:03:28.970Z"}

{"parentUuid":"280e02a9-7bac-4225-bccd-85173e53094d","isSidechain":true,"userType":"external","cwd":"/home/nathan_booth/code/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs","sessionId":"6fe4c50f-eba6-46a5-94a4-267042841ddc","version":"2.1.34","gitBranch":"main","agentId":"aaa6752","slug":"memoized-prancing-marshmallow","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01RbL2kbN8PSriXV1qussLwd","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012WTHATUXGtibxLjZ1HSwoQ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/nathan_booth/code/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/docs/adr/adr-006-qdrant.md","content":"---\ntitle: \"ADR-006: Qdrant for Vector Storage\"\nsidebar_label: \"ADR-006: Qdrant\"\nsidebar_position: 7\ndescription: \"Decision to deploy Qdrant on GKE for RAG and semantic search workloads\"\n---\n\n# ADR-006: Qdrant for Vector Storage\n\n**Status:** Accepted\n**Date:** January 2026\n\n## Context\n\nThe KIX Platform supports Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines and semantic search capabilities for use case agents. Agents need to:\n\n- Store and retrieve vector embeddings for knowledge base articles\n- Perform similarity searches for real-time knowledge retrieval\n- Maintain collection isolation between use cases\n- Support low-latency retrieval during live interactions (voice and chat)\n\nThe main alternative considered was **Vertex AI Matching Engine**, GCP's managed vector search service.\n\n| Criteria | Qdrant | Vertex AI Matching Engine |\n|----------|--------|--------------------------|\n| Open-source | Yes | No |\n| Kubernetes-native | Yes (runs on GKE) | No (managed service) |\n| Vendor lock-in | None | GCP-specific |\n| Cost | Lower (self-managed) | Higher (managed service) |\n| Performance | High benchmarks | High benchmarks |\n| Operational overhead | Self-managed | Fully managed |\n\n## Decision\n\nDeploy **Qdrant** on GKE with persistent SSD storage for all vector storage and semantic search workloads.\n\n**Key configuration:**\n- 3 replicas in production, 1 in dev/QA\n- Persistent SSD storage for durability\n- Max 10M vectors per collection\n- Collection names prefixed with use case for isolation\n- Platform embedding model used for consistency across collections\n- Platform team manages backups\n\n**Usage constraints:**\n- Collection names must be prefixed with the use case name (e.g., `self-healing-knowledge`, `scheduling-faqs`)\n- All embeddings must use the platform-provided embedding model to ensure consistency across collections\n- Backup and restore operations are managed by the platform team\n\n## Consequences\n\n### Positive\n\n- **Low-latency retrieval** -- In-cluster deployment provides sub-millisecond network overhead for vector queries\n- **Collection isolation** -- Per-use-case collections with naming conventions prevent cross-contamination\n- **No vendor lock-in** -- Open-source with commercial support available; portable to any Kubernetes cluster\n- **Cost-effective** -- Lower cost than managed alternatives, especially at scale\n- **Kubernetes-native** -- Scales with the cluster, managed alongside other platform services\n- **High performance** -- Competitive benchmarks for both indexing and query latency\n\n### Negative\n\n- **Self-managed** -- Platform team responsible for upgrades, monitoring, backup/restore, and incident response\n- **Operational overhead** -- Persistent storage management, replica coordination, and capacity planning\n- **No managed backups** -- Must implement custom backup procedures (scheduled snapshots to GCS)\n\n### Risks\n\n- **Data loss** -- Persistent volume failure could lose vectors (mitigated by replication and scheduled backups)\n- **Scaling limits** -- 10M vector limit per collection may be insufficient for large knowledge bases\n- **Version upgrades** -- Qdrant upgrades may require careful migration of persistent data\n- **Embedding model changes** -- Changing the platform embedding model requires re-indexing all collections\n\n## Related\n\n- [ADR-001: LiteLLM as LLM Gateway](/docs/adr/adr-001-litellm) -- LiteLLM provides embedding model access\n- [Services Catalog](/docs/strategy/services-catalog) -- Qdrant listed as platform service\n- [Developer Guide](/docs/guides/developer-guide) -- Qdrant specifications and constraints\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":9685,"cache_read_input_tokens":99429,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":9685},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"}},"requestId":"req_011CXvxcbNf8TbsaGqYB6FKx","type":"assistant","uuid":"8d0e6ee7-384f-4146-9856-6459a0c6f796","timestamp":"2026-02-08T17:02:36.847Z"}

Manual intervention only if all providers are down.\n\n### T4: Container Vulnerability\n\n**Description:** Critical vulnerability discovered in deployed container images.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- Artifact Registry scanning on every image push\n- CRITICAL vulnerabilities blocked from production deployment\n- Daily continuous rescanning of deployed images\n- 48-hour patching SLA for critical CVEs\n- Binary Authorization required for production\n\n**Recovery:** Patch and redeploy via standard CI/CD pipeline. Emergency hotfix procedure available for critical issues.\n\n### T5: Network Misconfiguration\n\n**Description:** Network firewall rules or network policies misconfigured, causing service disruption or security exposure.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- All network configuration managed via Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform)\n- PR-based review for all changes\n- tfsec security scanning on every PR\n- Default deny-all network policies\n- VPC Flow Logs for visibility\n\n**Recovery:** Revert Terraform code and redeploy. See [Rollback Procedure](/docs/infrastructure-ops/cicd-runbook#rollback-procedure).\n\n## Security Risks\n\n| ID | Risk | Prob | Impact | Mitigation | Owner |\n|----|------|------|--------|------------|-------|\n| S1 | Credential exposure | Low | Critical | Workload Identity (no keys), Secret Manager | DevSecOps Lead |\n| S2 | Data exfiltration | Low | Critical | VPC Service Controls, egress controls | DevSecOps Lead |\n| S3 | Insider threat | Low | High | Least privilege, audit logging, access reviews | DevSecOps Lead |\n| S4 | DDoS attack | Medium | Medium | Cloud Armor, rate limiting | Infrastructure Lead |\n| S5 | Supply chain attack | Low | High | Binary Authorization, image scanning | DevSecOps Lead |\n\n### S1: Credential Exposure\n\n**Description:** Service credentials or API keys exposed through code, logs, or misconfiguration.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- Workload Identity eliminates service account keys entirely (enforced by org policy)\n- Secret Manager with automatic 90-day rotation\n- External Secrets Operator syncs secrets to Kubernetes\n- No secrets in Git (pre-commit hooks, secret scanning)\n- No secrets in environment variables at build time\n\n**Recovery:** Rotate affected credentials immediately. Review audit logs for unauthorized access.\n\n### S2: Data Exfiltration\n\n**Description:** Unauthorized transfer of data outside the organization's control.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- VPC Service Controls in production create a security perimeter\n- Egress controls via Cloud NAT with logging\n- Default deny-all egress network policies\n- Data residency enforcement (EU only)\n- Audit logging on all data access (production)\n\n**Recovery:** VPC Service Controls block exfiltration attempts. Investigate via audit logs and VPC Flow Logs.\n\n### S3: Insider Threat\n\n**Description:** Authorized user misuses access to compromise data or systems.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- Least privilege IAM with quarterly access reviews\n- Separation of duties (deploy != approve)\n- Comprehensive audit logging (7-year retention)\n- Just-in-time access for elevated permissions\n- Domain-restricted IAM (konecta-group.com only)\n- No shared accounts\n\n**Recovery:** Revoke access immediately. Forensic analysis via immutable audit logs.\n\n### S4: DDoS Attack\n\n**Description:** Distributed denial-of-service attack targeting platform endpoints.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- Cloud Armor WAF with DDoS protection at the edge\n- OWASP rule set enabled\n- Rate limiting via Cloud Armor and Kong\n- Global external HTTPS load balancer with Google's infrastructure\n\n**Recovery:** Cloud Armor provides automatic mitigation. Adjust rules if needed. Kong rate limiting provides application-layer protection.\n\n### S5: Supply Chain Attack\n\n**Description:** Compromised dependency or container image introduced into the build pipeline.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- Binary Authorization requires attestation for production deployments\n- Artifact Registry scanning on every image push\n- Dependency scanning in CI pipeline\n- Private Artifact Registry (no public pulls in production)\n\n**Recovery:** Identify compromised component via scanning results. Roll back to last known good image. Investigate scope of impact.\n\n## Compliance Risks\n\n| ID | Risk | Prob | Impact | Mitigation | Owner |\n|----|------|------|--------|------------|-------|\n| C1 | GDPR breach | Low | Critical | Encryption, access controls, incident response | Chief Engineer |\n| C2 | EU AI Act non-compliance | Medium | High | Risk classification, documentation, human oversight | AI Lead |\n| C3 | Audit failure | Low | Medium | Comprehensive logging, quarterly reviews | DevSecOps Lead |\n| C4 | Data residency violation | Low | High | Organisation policy enforcement, monitoring | Infrastructure Lead |\n\n### C1: GDPR Breach\n\n**Description:** Personal data breach resulting in regulatory notification requirements.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- Encryption at rest (CMEK in production) and in transit (TLS 1.3)\n- Strict access controls with audit logging\n- 72-hour incident response procedure documented\n- Data classification framework applied to all data\n- Privacy by design architecture (private-first networking)\n\n**Recovery:** Follow [incident response process](/docs/security/governance#incident-response). GDPR breach notification within 72 hours if personal data involved.\n\n### C2: EU AI Act Non-Compliance\n\n**Description:** AI use cases deployed without meeting EU AI Act requirements for their risk level.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- Per-use-case risk classification before deployment\n- High-risk use cases require human oversight and conformity assessment\n- All AI decisions logged with input, output, model, and confidence\n- Transparency disclosures for limited-risk use cases\n- Bias monitoring for high-risk use cases\n\n**Recovery:** Suspend non-compliant use case. Implement required controls. Re-assess and redeploy. See [AI Governance](/docs/security/compliance#ai-governance).\n\n### C3: Audit Failure\n\n**Description:** Internal or external audit identifies compliance gaps.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- Comprehensive logging with 7-year immutable retention\n- Quarterly security reviews and access audits\n- Infrastructure-as-Code provides auditable configuration history\n- ArgoCD provides deployment audit trail\n\n**Recovery:** Address audit findings within SLA. Document remediation actions. Update controls to prevent recurrence.\n\n### C4: Data Residency Violation\n\n**Description:** Data stored or processed outside approved EU regions.\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- GCP organisation policy constrains resource creation to EU regions only\n- Terraform variable validation rejects non-European regions\n- Quarterly data residency audit\n- Allowed regions: `europe-west1` (Belgium), `europe-west4` (Netherlands)\n\n**Recovery:** Identify and migrate non-compliant resources.      1→import MiniSearch from "minisearch";
     2→import type { DocPage } from "./content-loader.js";
     3→
     4→export interface SearchResult {
     5→  path: string;
     6→  title: string;
     7→  snippet: string;
     8→  score: number;
     9→  category: string;
    10→}
    11→
    12→let searchIndex: MiniSearch<DocPage> | null = null;
    13→let indexedPages: DocPage[] = [];
    14→
    15→export function buildSearchIndex(pages: DocPage[]): void {
    16→  indexedPages = pages;
    17→  searchIndex = new MiniSearch<DocPage>({
    18→    fields: ["title", "description", "content", "category"],
    19→    storeFields: ["title", "relativePath", "description", "category"],
    20→    idField: "relativePath",
    21→    searchOptions: {
    22→      boost: { title: 3, description: 2, content: 1 },
    23→      fuzzy: 0.2,
    24→      prefix: true,
    25→    },
    26→  });
    27→
    28→  searchIndex.addAll(pages);
    29→  console.error(`Search index built with ${pages.length} documents`);
    30→}
    31→
    32→export function searchDocs(
    33→  query: string,
    34→  category?: string,
    35→  limit: number = 10
    36→): SearchResult[] {
    37→  if (!searchIndex) return [];
    38→
    39→  const filter = category
    40→    ? { filter: (result: { category: string }) => result.category === category }
    41→    : {};
    42→
    43→  const results = searchIndex.search(query, filter);
    44→
    45→  return results.slice(0, limit).map((result) => {
    46→    const page = indexedPages.find((p) => p.relativePath === result.id);
    47→    const snippet = extractSnippet(page?.content || "", query);
    48→
    49→    return {
    50→      path: result.id as string,
    51→      title: (result as unknown as { title: string }).title || String(result.id),
    52→      snippet,
    53→      score: result.score,
    54→      category: (result as unknown as { category: string }).category || "unknown",
    55→    };
    56→  });
    57→}
    58→
    59→function extractSnippet(content: string, query: string): string {
    60→  const terms = query.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/);
    61→  const lines = content.split("\n").filter((l) => l.trim().length > 0);
    62→
    63→  for (const line of lines) {
    64→    const lower = line.toLowerCase();
    65→    if (terms.some((term) => lower.includes(term))) {
    66→      const cleaned = line.replace(/[#*|`]/g, "").trim();
    67→      return cleaned.length > 200 ? cleaned.substring(0, 200) + "..." : cleaned;
    68→    }
    69→  }
    70→
    71→  const firstContent = lines
    72→    .find((l) => !l.startsWith("#") && !l.startsWith("|") && !l.startsWith("---"))
    73→    ?.trim();
    74→  return firstContent
    75→    ? firstContent.length > 200
    76→      ? firstContent.substring(0, 200) + "..."
    77→      : firstContent
    78→    : "";
    79→}
    80→

     1→import { McpServer } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js";
     2→import { StdioServerTransport } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js";
     3→import { resolve } from "path";
     4→import {
     5→  loadDocs,
     6→  extractGlossary,
     7→  extractModules,
     8→  extractAdrs,
     9→  type DocPage,
    10→  type GlossaryEntry,
    11→  type ModuleEntry,
    12→  type AdrEntry,
    13→} from "./content-loader.js";
    14→import { buildSearchIndex } from "./search-index.js";
    15→import { listDocResources, readDocResource } from "./resources.js";
    16→import {
    17→  searchDocsSchema,
    18→  lookupGlossarySchema,
    19→  lookupModuleSchema,
    20→  lookupAdrSchema,
    21→  handleSearchDocs,
    22→  handleLookupGlossary,
    23→  handleLookupModule,
    24→  handleLookupAdr,
    25→} from "./tools.js";
    26→import { DOC_REVIEW_PROMPT, getDocReviewPrompt } from "./prompts.js";
    27→
    28→const DOCS_ROOT = resolve(process.env.DOCS_ROOT || "docs");
    29→
    30→async function main() {
    31→  console.error("KIX Docs MCP Server starting...");
    32→  console.error(`Loading docs from: ${DOCS_ROOT}`);
    33→
    34→  // Load and index all documentation
    35→  const pages: DocPage[] = await loadDocs(DOCS_ROOT);
    36→  const glossary: GlossaryEntry[] = extractGlossary(pages);
    37→  const modules: ModuleEntry[] = extractModules(pages);
    38→  const adrs: AdrEntry[] = extractAdrs(pages);
    39→
    40→  buildSearchIndex(pages);
    41→
    42→  console.error(
    43→    `Loaded: ${pages.length} pages, ${glossary.length} glossary entries, ${modules.length} modules, ${adrs.length} ADRs`
    44→  );
    45→
    46→  // Create MCP server
    47→  const server = new McpServer({
    48→    name: "kix-docs",
    49→    version: "1.0.0",
    50→  });
    51→
    52→  // Register resources
    53→  server.resource(
    54→    "doc-index",
    55→    "docs://kix-platform/index",
    56→    {
    57→      description: "Index of all KIX Platform documentation pages",
    58→      mimeType: "application/json",
    59→    },
    60→    async () => ({
    61→      contents: [
    62→        {
    63→          uri: "docs://kix-platform/index",
    64→          mimeType: "application/json" as const,
    65→          text: JSON.stringify(
    66→            pages.map((p) => ({
    67→              path: p.relativePath,
    68→              title: p.title,
    69→              description: p.description,
    70→              category: p.category,
    71→            })),
    72→            null,
    73→            2
    74→          ),
    75→        },
    76→      ],
    77→    })
    78→  );
    79→
    80→  // Register individual doc page resources
    81→  for (const page of pages) {
    82→    const uri = `docs://kix-platform/${page.relativePath}`;
    83→    server.resource(
    84→      `doc-${page.relativePath.replace(/\//g, "-")}`,
    85→      uri,
    86→      {
    87→        description: page.description || `Documentation: ${page.title}`,
    88→        mimeType: "text/markdown",
    89→      },
    90→      async () => ({
    91→        contents: [
    92→          {
    93→            uri,
    94→            mimeType: "text/markdown" as const,
    95→            text: page.rawContent,
    96→          },
    97→        ],
    98→      })
    99→    );
   100→  }
   101→
   102→  // Register tools
   103→  server.tool(
   104→    "search_docs",
   105→    "Search KIX Platform documentation by keyword or phrase",
   106→    searchDocsSchema.shape,
   107→    async (args) => handleSearchDocs(searchDocsSchema.parse(args))
   108→  );
   109→
   110→  server.tool(
   111→    "lookup_glossary",
   112→    "Look up a term in the KIX Platform glossary",
   113→    lookupGlossarySchema.shape,
   114→    async (args) => handleLookupGlossary(lookupGlossarySchema.parse(args), glossary)
   115→  );
   116→
   117→  server.tool(
   118→    "lookup_module",
   119→    "Look up a Terraform or Helm module in the module catalog",
   120→    lookupModuleSchema.shape,
   121→    async (args) => handleLookupModule(lookupModuleSchema.parse(args), modules)
   122→  );
   123→
   124→  server.tool(
   125→    "lookup_adr",
   126→    "Look up an Architecture Decision Record by ID or keyword",
   127→    lookupAdrSchema.shape,
   128→    async (args) => handleLookupAdr(lookupAdrSchema.parse(args), adrs)
   129→  );
   130→
   131→  // Register prompts
   132→  server.prompt(
   133→    DOC_REVIEW_PROMPT.name,
   134→    DOC_REVIEW_PROMPT.description,
   135→    DOC_REVIEW_PROMPT.arguments as Record<string, never>[],
   136→    async (args) => {
   137→      const pagePath = args.page_path;
   138→      const content = readDocResource(pages, `docs://kix-platform/${pagePath}`);
   139→
   140→      if (!content) {
   141→        return {
   142→          messages: [
   143→            {
   144→              role: "user" as const,
   145→              content: {
   146→                type: "text" as const,
   147→                text: `Documentation page not found: ${pagePath}\n\nAvailable pages:\n${pages.map((p) => `- ${p.relativePath}`).join("\n")}`,
   148→              },
   149→            },
   150→          ],
   151→        };
   152→      }
   153→
   154→      return {
   155→        messages: [

   157→            role: "user" as const,
   158→            content: {
   159→              type: "text" as const,
   160→              text: getDocReviewPrompt(content, pagePath),
   161→            },
   162→          },
   163→        ],
   164→      };
   165→    }
   166→  );
   167→
   168→  // Start server with stdio transport
   169→  const transport = new StdioServerTransport();
   170→  await server.connect(transport);
   171→
   172→  console.error("KIX Docs MCP Server running on stdio");
   173→}

     6→# KIX Platform Documentation
     7→
     8→Welcome to the documentation for the **KIX Platform** (Konecta Intelligence eXchange) - an enterprise-grade AI agent platform built on Google Cloud Platform using the CrewAI framework.
     9→
    10→## Quick Navigation
    11→
    12→| Document | Description |
    13→|----------|-------------|
    14→| [Architecture Overview](docs/ARCHITECTURE) | Technical architecture, security model, and compliance |
    15→| [Getting Started](docs/ONBOARDING) | Set up your environment and deploy infrastructure |

    17→| [Platform Strategy](docs/STRATEGY) | Platform services, operating model, and roadmap |
    18→| [Security & Compliance](docs/SECURITY_REVIEW) | Security controls, GDPR, ISO 27001, NIS2 |
    19→| [CI/CD Runbook](docs/CICD_RUNBOOK) | Pipeline operations and troubleshooting |
    20→| [Testing Guide](docs/TESTING) | Writing and running Terratest tests |
    21→
    22→## Platform Overview
    23→
    24→The KIX Platform provides enterprise-grade infrastructure for deploying AI agents with:
    25→
    26→- **Multi-Tenant Isolation** - Separate Kubernetes namespaces per use case with RBAC and network policies
    27→- **API Gateway** - Kong for 3rd party API abstraction and management
    28→- **LLM Proxy** - LiteLLM for unified access to multiple LLM providers
    29→- **GitOps** - ArgoCD for declarative infrastructure and application deployment
    30→- **Security** - Cloud Armor WAF, Workload Identity, EU data residency
    31→
    32→## Architecture
    33→
    34→```
    35→External Users → Cloud Load Balancer → Kong API Gateway → GKE (Use Case Namespaces)
    36→                                                               ↓
    37→                                       Cloud SQL / Redis / GCS / Pub/Sub (Private)
    38→
    39→Shared Services → ArgoCD (GitOps) → Multi-Cluster Deployments (Dev/QA/Prod)
    40→```
    41→
    42→See [Architecture Overview](docs/ARCHITECTURE) for detailed diagrams and technical specifications.
    43→
    44→## Repositories
    45→
    46→| Repository | Purpose | Links |
    47→|------------|---------|-------|
    48→| **kix-platform-modules** | Reusable Terraform/Helm modules | [GitHub](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules) |
    49→| **kix-platform-infrastructure** | Environment deployment configurations | [GitHub](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-infrastructure) |
    50→| **kix-platform-docs** | Platform documentation (this site) | [GitHub](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs) |
    51→| **kix-services-*** | Platform service configurations | [GitHub](https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/) |
    52→

    55→### For Platform Engineers

    57→1. [Onboarding Guide](docs/ONBOARDING) - Set up your development environment
    58→2. [CI/CD Runbook](docs/CICD_RUNBOOK) - Understand deployment pipelines

    63→1. [Developer Guide](docs/DEVELOPER_GUIDE) - Build AI agents on KIX Platform

    69→1. [Executive Summary](docs/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY) - Platform vision and value proposition

    73→## Key Features
    74→
    75→### Infrastructure as Code
    76→- **Terraform** modules for all GCP resources
    77→- **Helm** charts for Kubernetes applications
    78→- **Terratest** for automated testing
    79→
    80→### Security & Compliance
    81→- **GDPR** compliant data handling

     1→---

     4→description: "Step-by-step guide for creating new KIX Platform repositories with appropriate CLAUDE.md documentation"
     5→---
     6→
     7→# Creating New Repositories - CLAUDE.md Guide
     8→
     9→**Purpose:** Step-by-step guide for creating new KIX Platform repositories with appropriate CLAUDE.md documentation
    10→
    11→**Last Updated:** 2026-02-03
    12→
    13→---
    14→
    15→## Overview
    16→
    17→Every KIX Platform repository MUST have a CLAUDE.md file. This guide helps you select the right template and configure it correctly.
    18→
    19→---
    20→
    21→## Step 1: Repository Classification
    22→
    23→Use this decision tree to determine which CLAUDE.md pattern to use:
    24→
    25→```
    26→What's the repository complexity?
    27→
    28→├─ HIGH (Multi-tier, complex workflows, 15+ config files, strict dependencies)
    29→│  └─ Pattern A: Extended CLAUDE.md (~2,500-3,000 tokens)
    30→│     Use template: CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_EXTENDED.md
    31→│
    32→├─ MEDIUM (Standard app/service, single tech stack, clear structure)
    33→│  └─ Pattern B: Standard CLAUDE.md (~1,500-2,000 tokens)
    34→│     Use template: CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_STANDARD.md
    35→│
    36→└─ LOW (Demo, utility, doc-only, experimental, <100 lines code)
    37→   └─ Pattern C: Minimal CLAUDE.md (~500-800 tokens)
    38→      Use template: CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_MINIMAL.md
    39→```
    40→
    41→### Pattern A - Extended (Complex)
    42→
    43→**Use when:**
    44→- Multi-environment operations (dev/qa/prod)
    45→- Complex apply order dependencies (3+ tiers)
    46→- Comprehensive testing requirements
    47→- Multiple technology layers
    48→- Critical production impact
    49→- 15+ configuration files
    50→- Complex state management
    51→
    52→**Examples:**
    53→- kix-platform-infrastructure (multi-tier Terraform)
    54→- kix-platform-modules (module development + Terratest)
    55→- kix-services-kong (complex service with network policies)
    56→
    57→**Token Budget:** ~2,500-3,000 tokens
    58→
    59→### Pattern B - Standard (Medium)
    60→
    61→**Use when:**
    62→- Single service or application
    63→- Clear technology stack
    64→- Standard development workflow
    65→- Moderate complexity
    66→- 3-15 configuration files
    67→- Single or dual environment
    68→
    69→**Examples:**
    70→- kix-services-litellm (service deployment)
    71→- kix-services-backstage (platform service)
    72→- kix-crews-library (crew development)
    73→- kix-usecase-* (use case applications)
    74→- kix-mcp-* (MCP servers)
    75→
    76→**Token Budget:** ~1,500-2,000 tokens
    77→
    78→### Pattern C - Minimal (Simple)
    79→
    80→**Use when:**
    81→- Demos and POCs
    82→- Single-purpose utilities
    83→- Documentation-only repos
    84→- Experimental/short-lived
    85→- Less than 100 lines of code
    86→- 1-2 configuration files
    87→
    88→**Examples:**
    89→- kix-demo-* (demonstrations)
    90→- Small utilities
    91→- Proof of concepts
    92→- Experimental projects
    93→
    94→**Token Budget:** ~500-800 tokens
    95→
    96→---
    97→
    98→## Step 2: Check for Organization-Level Guidance
    99→
   100→Determine if your organization has a CLAUDE_ORG.md file:
   101→
   102→### Organizations WITH Organization-Level Files
   103→
   104→**konecta-ix-platform:**
   105→- 📍 [.github/CLAUDE_ORG.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/.github/blob/main/CLAUDE_ORG.md)
   106→- Contains: Terraform workflow, module development, GCS state management
   107→
   108→**konecta-ix-services:**
   109→- 📍 [.github/CLAUDE_ORG.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/.github/blob/main/CLAUDE_ORG.md)
   110→- Contains: Terraform → Helm migration, service deployment standards
   111→
   112→### Organizations WITHOUT Organization-Level Files
   113→
   114→- konecta-ix-crews
   115→- konecta-ix-workloads
   116→- konecta-ix-mcp-servers
   117→- konecta-ix-demos
   118→
   119→If your organization doesn't have a CLAUDE_ORG.md file, reference only Master CLAUDE.md.
   120→
   121→---
   122→
   123→## Step 3: Copy and Customize Template
   124→
   125→### 3.1 Copy Template File
   126→
   127→**Location:** `kix-platform-docs/templates/`
   128→
   129→**Copy command:**
   130→```bash
   131→# For Extended Pattern (A)
   132→cp templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_EXTENDED.md ../[your-repo]/CLAUDE.md
   133→
   134→# For Standard Pattern (B)
   135→cp templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_STANDARD.md ../[your-repo]/CLAUDE.md
   136→
   137→# For Minimal Pattern (C)
   138→cp templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_MINIMAL.md ../[your-repo]/CLAUDE.md
   139→```
   140→
   141→### 3.2 Replace Placeholders
   142→
   143→Search and replace these placeholders in your CLAUDE.md:
   144→
   145→| Placeholder | Replace With | Example |
   146→|------------|--------------|---------|
   147→| `[REPOSITORY_NAME]` | Your repository name | kix-services-monitoring |
   148→| `[ORGANIZATION_NAME]` | Your organization | konecta-ix-services |
   149→| `[ORGANIZATION]` | Organization short name | konecta-ix-services |
   150→| `[DATE]` | Today's date | 2026-02-03 |
   151→| `[Team Name]` | Your team name | Platform Services Team |
   152→
   153→**Quick replace command:**
   154→```bash
   155→cd [your-repo]
   156→
   157→# macOS
   158→sed -i '' 's/\[REPOSITORY_NAME\]/kix-services-monitoring/g' CLAUDE.md
   159→sed -i '' 's/\[ORGANIZATION_NAME\]/konecta-ix-services/g' CLAUDE.md
   160→sed -i '' 's/\[ORGANIZATION\]/konecta-ix-services/g' CLAUDE.md
   161→sed -i '' 's/\[DATE\]/2026-02-03/g' CLAUDE.md
   162→sed -i '' 's/\[Team Name\]/Platform Services Team/g' CLAUDE.md
   163→
   164→# Linux
   165→sed -i 's/\[REPOSITORY_NAME\]/kix-services-monitoring/g' CLAUDE.md
   166→sed -i 's/\[ORGANIZATION_NAME\]/konecta-ix-services/g' CLAUDE.md
   167→sed -i 's/\[ORGANIZATION\]/konecta-ix-services/g' CLAUDE.md
   168→sed -i 's/\[DATE\]/2026-02-03/g' CLAUDE.md
   169→sed -i 's/\[Team Name\]/Platform Services Team/g' CLAUDE.md
   170→```
   171→
   172→### 3.3 Fill in Content
   173→
   174→Go through the template section by section and replace bracketed placeholders:
   175→
   176→**Pattern A (Extended):**
   177→- Repository Overview (purpose, tech stack, environments, dependencies)
   178→- Quick Start (prerequisites, setup commands)
   179→- Repository Structure (directory tree with descriptions)
   180→- Key Workflows (3+ major workflows with commands)
   181→- Environment Management (if multi-environment)
   182→- Apply Order & Dependencies (if applicable)
   183→- Testing Strategy (unit, integration, post-deployment)
   184→- Common Operations (frequent commands)
   185→- Troubleshooting (3+ common issues)
   186→
   187→**Pattern B (Standard):**
   188→- Repository Overview (purpose, tech stack)
   189→- Quick Start (prerequisites, setup, quick commands)
   190→- Repository Structure (directory tree)
   191→- Key Workflows (development, deployment)
   192→- Testing (unit, integration)
   193→- Deployment (steps and rollback)
   194→- Common Operations (frequent commands)
   195→- Troubleshooting (common issues)
   196→
   197→**Pattern C (Minimal):**
   198→- Overview (purpose, type, tech, status)
   199→- Quick Start (prerequisites, setup & run)
   200→- Structure (simple tree)
   201→- Key Commands (2-3 commands)
   202→- Notes (important context)
   203→- Experimental Status (if applicable)
   204→
   205→### 3.4 Update Reference Links
   206→
   207→**Ensure these links are correct:**
   208→
   209→1. **Master CLAUDE.md link:**
   210→   ```markdown
   211→   [Master CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)
   212→   ```
   213→
   214→2. **Organization CLAUDE_ORG.md link** (if applicable):
   215→   ```markdown
   216→   [Organization CLAUDE_ORG.md](https://github.com/[YOUR-ORG]/.github/blob/main/CLAUDE_ORG.md)
   217→   ```
   218→
   219→3. **Navigation guide link:**
   220→   ```markdown
   221→   [CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/blob/main/CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md)
   222→   ```
   223→
   224→---
   225→
   226→## Step 4: Validation Checklist
   227→
   228→Before committing your CLAUDE.md, verify:
   229→
   230→### Content Completeness
   231→- [ ] All `[PLACEHOLDER]` text replaced
   232→- [ ] Repository overview filled in
   233→- [ ] Technology stack specified with versions
   234→- [ ] Quick start commands tested and work
   235→- [ ] Repository structure reflects actual structure
   236→- [ ] Key workflows documented with real commands
   237→- [ ] Common operations include copy-paste ready commands
   238→- [ ] Troubleshooting includes real issues (can add more over time)
   239→
   240→### References
   241→- [ ] Master CLAUDE.md link works
   242→- [ ] Organization CLAUDE_ORG.md link works (if applicable)
   243→- [ ] Navigation guide link works
   244→- [ ] All internal links (anchors) work
   245→- [ ] Cross-repository links use absolute GitHub URLs
   246→
   247→### Standards Compliance
   248→- [ ] Follows Master CLAUDE.md security requirements
   249→- [ ] Follows Master CLAUDE.md git workflow standards
   250→- [ ] References universal operational standards
   251→- [ ] No duplicate content from Master or Org files
   252→- [ ] Token budget target met (check with Claude Code)
   253→
   254→### Testing
   255→- [ ] Commands in Quick Start have been tested
   256→- [ ] Validation commands produce expected output
   257→- [ ] Troubleshooting solutions actually fix problems
   258→- [ ] All code blocks have syntax highlighting (language specified)
   259→
   260→---
   261→
   262→## Step 5: Token Budget Verification
   263→
   264→Ask Claude Code to estimate token count:
   265→
   266→**Pattern A (Extended):** Target ~2,500-3,000 tokens
   267→**Pattern B (Standard):** Target ~1,500-2,000 tokens
   268→**Pattern C (Minimal):** Target ~500-800 tokens
   269→
   270→**If over budget:**
   271→- Remove unnecessary details
   272→- Move repo-specific patterns to code comments instead
   273→- Link to external documentation for deep dives
   274→- Condense repetitive sections
   275→
   276→**If significantly under budget:**
   277→- Add missing workflows or operations
   278→- Expand troubleshooting section
   279→- Add validation commands and expected outputs
   280→- Include more examples
   281→
   282→---
   283→
   284→## Step 6: Commit and Register
   285→
   286→### 6.1 Commit CLAUDE.md
   287→
   288→```bash
   289→git add CLAUDE.md
   290→git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   291→docs: add CLAUDE.md with [Pattern A/B/C] guidance
   292→
   293→Initialize repository-specific guidance for Claude Code using [Extended/Standard/Minimal] pattern.
   294→
   295→References Master CLAUDE.md for universal standards.
   296→
   297→Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
   298→EOF
   299→)"
   300→git push origin main
   301→```
   302→
   303→### 6.2 Register in Navigation Guide
   304→
   305→Update `kix-platform-docs/CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md`:
   306→
   307→1. Add your repository to the appropriate organization table
   308→2. Specify pattern (A/B/C)
   309→3. Include token budget
   310→4. Describe primary content
   311→
   312→**Example:**
   313→```markdown
   314→| [kix-services-monitoring/CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/kix-services-monitoring/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) | Standard (B) | ~1,500 | Prometheus, Grafana, alerting |
   315→```
   316→
   317→### 6.3 Create PR for Navigation Update
   318→
   319→```bash
   320→cd kix-platform-docs
   321→git checkout -b docs/register-[repo-name]
   322→git add CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md
   323→git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   324→docs: register [repo-name] in CLAUDE navigation
   325→
   326→Add [repo-name] to navigation guide with Pattern [A/B/C] classification.
   327→
   328→Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
   329→EOF
   330→)"
   331→git push -u origin docs/register-[repo-name]
   332→gh pr create --title "docs: register [repo-name] in CLAUDE navigation"
   333→```
   334→
   335→---
   336→
   337→## Step 7: Ongoing Maintenance
   338→
   339→### When to Update CLAUDE.md
   340→
   341→**Immediate updates needed when:**
   342→- Adding new major workflow or operation
   343→- Changing technology stack (versions, tools)
   344→- Discovering new common mistakes
   345→- Restructuring repository
   346→- Changing deployment process
   347→
   348→**Monthly reviews:**
   349→- Update token budget if significantly changed
   350→- Review and prune outdated sections
   351→- Add new troubleshooting entries
   352→- Update "Last Updated" date
   353→
   354→**Quarterly reviews:**
   355→- Evaluate if pattern classification still appropriate
   356→- Consider promoting repo-specific mistakes to org/master
   357→- Review and optimize token usage
   358→- Validate all links still work
   359→
   360→### Promoting Mistakes
   361→
   362→**When a mistake occurs 3+ times in your repo:**
   363→1. Document in your CLAUDE.md "Repository-Specific Mistakes"
   364→2. If pattern emerges, suggest promotion to Org file
   365→
   366→**When mistake affects 3+ repos in org:**
   367→1. Coordinate with team to promote to Org CLAUDE_ORG.md
   368→2. Remove from individual repo CLAUDE.md files
   369→3. Add reference to Org file
   370→
   371→**When mistake affects 3+ orgs:**
   372→1. Propose addition to Master CLAUDE.md
   373→2. Create PR to kix-platform-docs
   374→3. Remove from Org files after Master updated
   375→
   376→---
   377→
   378→## Examples
   379→
   380→### Example 1: Creating Extended Pattern Repository
   381→
   382→**Scenario:** New infrastructure repository for database tier
   383→
   384→```bash
   385→# 1. Create repository
   386→gh repo create konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-databases --public
   387→
   388→# 2. Clone and setup
   389→git clone https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-databases.git
   390→cd kix-platform-databases
   391→
   392→# 3. Copy Extended template
   393→cp ../kix-platform-docs/templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_EXTENDED.md CLAUDE.md
   394→
   395→# 4. Customize
   396→# Open CLAUDE.md and fill in:
   397→# - Repository overview
   398→# - Technology stack (Terraform, Cloud SQL, Redis)
   399→# - Environment management (dev/qa/prod)
   400→# - Apply order (foundation → databases)
   401→# - Testing strategy (Terratest)
   402→# - Common operations
   403→
   404→# 5. Commit
   405→git add CLAUDE.md
   406→git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   407→docs: add CLAUDE.md with Extended pattern guidance
   408→
   409→Initialize repository-specific guidance for Claude Code using Extended pattern.
   410→Covers multi-tier database infrastructure deployment.
   411→
   412→References Master CLAUDE.md and Platform Org CLAUDE_ORG.md.
   413→
   414→Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
   415→EOF
   416→)"
   417→git push origin main
   418→
   419→# 6. Register in navigation (separate PR to kix-platform-docs)
   420→```
   421→

   496→---
   497→
   498→## Troubleshooting
   499→
   500→### Issue: Not sure which pattern to use
   501→
   502→**Solution:** Ask yourself:
   503→- How many configuration files? (15+ = Extended, 3-15 = Standard, 1-2 = Minimal)
   504→- Multi-environment? (Yes = Extended, No = Standard/Minimal)
   505→- Complex dependencies? (Yes = Extended, No = Standard)
   506→- Demo/experimental? (Yes = Minimal)
   507→
   508→When in doubt, start with Standard (B) and upgrade to Extended (A) if needed.
   509→
   510→### Issue: Token count too high
   511→
   512→**Solution:**
   513→- Remove duplicate content from Master/Org files
   514→- Link to external docs instead of embedding
   515→- Condense similar operations into patterns
   516→- Move detailed examples to separate docs
   517→
   518→### Issue: Don't know what workflows to document
   519→
   520→**Solution:**
   521→- Document the 3 most common operations
   522→- What does a new developer need to know?
   523→- What mistakes have you made?
   524→- What do you repeatedly look up?
   525→
   526→### Issue: Organization doesn't have CLAUDE_ORG.md but should
   527→
   528→**Solution:**
   529→If 5+ repositories in your org share common patterns:
   530→1. Create issue in your organization's .github repository
   531→2. Propose creating CLAUDE_ORG.md
   532→3. Use CLAUDE_ORG_TEMPLATE.md as starting point
   533→4. Coordinate with team to extract shared patterns
   534→
   535→---
   536→
   537→## Quick Reference
   538→
   539→### Decision Tree (Text)
   540→
   541→1. **Is this a demo, POC, or utility?** → Minimal (C)
   542→2. **Is this multi-environment with complex dependencies?** → Extended (A)
   543→3. **Otherwise** → Standard (B)
   544→
   545→### Template Locations
   546→
   547→- Extended: `kix-platform-docs/templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_EXTENDED.md`
   548→- Standard: `kix-platform-docs/templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_STANDARD.md`
   549→- Minimal: `kix-platform-docs/templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_MINIMAL.md`
   550→- Org: `kix-platform-docs/templates/CLAUDE_ORG_TEMPLATE.md`
   551→
   552→### Token Budgets
   553→
   554→- Extended (A): ~2,500-3,000 tokens
   555→- Standard (B): ~1,500-2,000 tokens
   556→- Minimal (C): ~500-800 tokens
   557→- Org: ~1,500-2,000 tokens
   558→- Master: ~4,000-4,500 tokens
   559→
   560→### Support
   561→
   562→**Questions?**
   563→- Slack: #platform-engineering
   564→- Documentation: https://konecta-ix-platform.github.io/kix-platform-docs
   565→- Navigation Guide: [CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/blob/main/CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md)
   566→

## 6. ANIMATIONS

### Keyframe Animations
- `fadeIn`: 0% opacity 0 → 100% opacity 1
- `slideUp`: 0% opacity 0, translateY(10px) → 100% opacity 1, translateY(0)
- `gradientShift`: Background position 0% → 100% → 0% (8s loop)
- `orbFloat`: Position and scale variation over 20s
- `glowPulse`: Opacity and scale variation over 8s
- `skeleton-shimmer`: Background position 200% → -200% (1.5s)
- `dropdownFadeIn`: 0% opacity 0, translateY(-8px) → 100% opacity 1, translateY(0)
- `megaDropdownOpen`: Scale and translation animation over 0.25s
- `megaDropdownItemSlide`: Staggered item entrance (30ms each, offset 0.03s)
- `modalFadeIn`: Simple fade in 0.2s
- `modalSlideIn`: Scale 0.95 + translateY -10px → scale 1 + translateY 0 (0.3s)
- `spin`: 0deg → 360deg (1s linear infinite)

## 9. RESPONSIVE DESIGN

### Breakpoints (Defined in CSS)
- **Mobile**: `max-width: 768px`
- **Tablet/Medium**: `max-width: 1200px`
- **Tablet**: `max-width: 1024px`
- **Large Desktop**: `max-width: 900px`

### Container Breakpoints
| Breakpoint | Max Width |
|------------|-----------|
| < 640px | 630px |
| ≥ 640px | 630px |
| ≥ 768px | 758px |
| ≥ 1024px | 1014px |
| ≥ 1280px | 1270px |
| ≥ 1536px | 1530px |

---

## 10. FRAMEWORK INTEGRATION

- **Framework**: Nuxt 3 with `@nuxt/ui` (v4.4.0)
- **CSS Framework**: Tailwind CSS (v4.1.18)
- **Font**: Poppins (via system font)
- **CSS Loading**: 3 CSS files injected
  - `~/assets/css/konecta-theme.css` (color variables)
  - `~/assets/css/main.css` (base & theme)
  - `~/assets/css/index.css` (critical FOUC prevention)

---

## 11. SPECIAL EFFECTS & DETAILS

### Authentication Page Orbs
Three animated radial gradients with different colors and timing:
- Orb 1 (Blue): `rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.4)`, blur(80px), top: -100px, left: -100px
- Orb 2 (Purple): `rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.35)`, blur(80px), bottom: -150px, right: -150px
- Orb 3 (Cyan): `rgba(6, 182, 212, 0.3)`, blur(80px), center position

### Page Loading & FOUC Prevention
- Critical CSS in `index.css` prevents white flash
- Background color set to `#0a1120` at HTML level
- Font family: Poppins, sans-serif applied system-wide

---

## Summary

This is a **modern dark-mode design system** with:
- **6 extended color palettes** (Lagon, Aqua, Vegetal, Solar, Infrapink + primary brand colors)
- **Poppins typography** throughout (no serifs)
- **Glass morphism effects** with backdrop blur
- **Smooth animations** and transitions across all components
- **Flexible spacing scale** for consistent layouts
- **Nuxt UI + Tailwind CSS** integration
- **Accessibility-first component styling** with proper focus states
- **Responsive design** with mobile-first approach

## EXHAUSTIVE VISUAL STYLING ANALYSIS: KonectaIQ Portal

I have conducted a comprehensive analysis of ALL CSS files in the KonectaIQ portal. Here is the complete picture of how pages look:

### COLOR SYSTEM

**Dark Theme Foundation:**
- Primary background: `#0a1120` (very dark navy)
- Secondary bg: `#0f172a` (slightly lighter navy)
- Tertiary bg: `#1e293b` (slate)
- Elevated bg: `#1a2235` (elevated panels)
- Card backgrounds: `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03)` to `0.07` (semi-transparent white)

**Konecta Brand Colors:**
- Lagon (Cyan): #2dc5ff (400) to #006faa (700) - primary accent
- Aqua: #00b4d8 (500) - secondary accent
- Vegetal (Green): #0dca61 (500) - success/growth
- Solar (Orange): #fd6221 (500) - warmth
- InfraPink (Pink): #f24168 (500) - vibrancy
- Blue: #2800c8 (deep brand blue)

**Text Colors:**
- Primary text: `#ffffff` (white)
- Secondary text: `#a1a1aa` (light gray)
- Muted text: `#71717a` (darker gray)

**Status Colors:**
- Success: `#22c55e` (bright green)
- Warning: `#f59e0b` (amber)
- Danger: `#ef4444` (red)
- Primary: `#3b82f6` (blue)

### 1. PAGE-LEVEL VISUAL EFFECTS

**Background Patterns & Decorative Elements:**
- **Animated Orbs** (Landing & Auth pages): Multiple large blurred circles with radial gradients animating across the page
  - Auth page: 3 floating orbs (blue, purple, cyan) with `blur(80px)` filter
  - Landing page: 5 circles with continuous pulsing `glowPulse` animation
  - Movement animations: `circleMove1-5` (35-55s cycles) + `circlePulse1-5` (7-12s cycles)
  - Opacity range: 0.3-0.6 with semi-transparent colors

- **Glass/Frosted Effect**:
  ```
  backdrop-filter: blur(12px) to blur(20px)
  border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1)
  background: rgba(20, 20, 22, 0.8) to rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03)
  ```

- **Subtle Top Border Gradient** (cards on hover):
  - `linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2), transparent)`
  - Appears via `::after` pseudo-element on hover

**No full-page noise textures or patterns** - design relies on color separation and animated elements instead.

### 2. CONTENT AREA STYLING

**Container System:**
- Base container: `width: 100%`, `padding: 0 30px`
- Responsive max-widths: 630px (640px+), 758px (768px+), 1014px (1024px+), 1270px (1280px+), 1530px (1536px+)

**Main Layout:**
- `.main-layout`: Full viewport height flex column
- `.main-content`: `flex: 1`, `padding-top: 80px` (navbar height), `overflow-y: auto`
- `.navbar`: Fixed position, 80px tall, stays at top
- On scroll, navbar shrinks to `0.75rem` padding with enhanced blur

**Card Grid Pattern:**
- Cards use `border-radius: var(--radius-lg)` (1rem)
- Consistent `padding: var(--spacing-lg)` (1.5rem)
- Border: `1px solid var(--border-color)` (rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1))
- Cards hover up 4px and increase shadow

### 3. TYPOGRAPHY IN PRACTICE

**Type Scale (actual pixel values):**
```
Page Title (.page-title):        20px, weight 700, line-height 1.3
Page Subtitle (.page-subtitle):  14px, weight 400, line-height 1.5
Section Title (.section-title):  15px, weight 600
Card Title (.card-title):        15px, weight 600
Card Description:                13px, weight 400, color secondary
Label (.label):                  12px, weight 500, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.03em
Caption (.caption):              12px, color muted
```

**Gradient Text Effects:**
- `.text-gradient` class applies `var(--gradient-text)`: 
  - `linear-gradient(135deg, var(--konecta-aqua-600) 0%, var(--konecta-aqua-100) 100%)`
  - Uses `-webkit-background-clip: text`, `-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent`
  - Applied to auth titles, hero text

**Heading Decorations:**
- `.roadmap-title::after`: Gradient underline (60px wide, 3px height) centered below text
  - Gradient: `linear-gradient(90deg, var(--konecta-vegetal-500), var(--konecta-lagon-500), var(--konecta-blue))`

### 4. DIVIDERS & SEPARATORS

**Border Lines:**
- Standard: `1px solid var(--border-color)` (rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1))
- Dividers between sections: `.dropdown-divider`, `.modal-divider`
  - `margin: 0.5rem 0`, `height: 1px`

**Gradient Dividers:**
- Top border on cards hover: Gradient line from transparent > white > transparent
- Roadmap item dividers: `.roadmap-item::before` creates gradient line across top

**Spacing Separators:**
- Section gaps: `margin: 0.75rem 0` to `2rem 0`
- Large sections: `border-top: 1px solid var(--border-color)`, `padding-top: 1.5rem`

### 5. LINK STYLING

**Link Colors:**
- Default: `var(--primary)` (#3b82f6)
- Hover: `#a855f7` (purple) in markdown contexts
- Underline: Always present on links in content

**Link Behaviors:**
