color: var(--primary);

### 8. IMAGE & MEDIA STYLING

### 23. AGENT & SHOWCASE CARDS

**Agent Card Grid View:**
- 180px thumbnail height with square image support (`object-fit: contain`)
- Title: 17px font, weight 600
- Description: 13px, 2-line clamp with ellipsis
- Footer: flex between, meta items with icons
- Hover: Image scales 1.05x

**Agent Card List View:**
- Horizontal layout with 48px thumbnail
- Content right-aligned, full width
- Description: 1-line clamp
- Meta items: flex gap 1.5rem

### 24. ANIMATION KEYFRAMES SUMMARY

**Entrance Animations:**
- `fadeInUp`: 0% {opacity: 0, translateY(16px)} → 100% {opacity: 1, translateY(0)}
- `fadeInScale`: Combines fade + scale(0.95) → scale(1)
- `slideUp`: Slide from 20px down + opacity fade

**Loading/Status Animations:**
- `skeleton-shimmer`: Background gradient shifts left-right (1.5s)
- `spin`: Full rotation (1s linear)
- `typingBounce`: Dots bounce up-down (1.4s)
- `pulse`: Opacity & scale pulse (1.5-2s)

**Glow/Light Effects:**
- `glowPulse`: Box-shadow expands and contracts
- `pulseGlow`: Box-shadow 0 0 20px → 0 0 40px
- `circlePulse1-5`: 5 different radial gradient pulsing animations

**Motion Animations:**
- `circleMove1-5`: 5 different circular motion paths (35-55s duration)
- `orbFloat`: Float up-down with scale (6s)
- `gradientShift`: Background position shifts for animated CTA button (8s)

**Dropdown/Menu:**
- `dropdownFadeIn`: Fade in + slide down slightly
- `megaDropdownOpen`: Scale from 0.95, slide up, staggered item reveals
- `slideDown`: Opacity 0 → 1, translateY(-10px) → 0

### 25. RESPONSIVE DESIGN

**Breakpoints:**
- 640px: Mobile adjustments
- 768px: Tablet layout changes
- 900px: Hide desktop-only nav
- 1024px: Reduce logo text
- 1200px: Navbar adjustments
- 1400px-1600px: Kanban board column sizing

**Mobile-Specific:**
- Navbar text hidden, logo shrinks
- Mobile menu appears (absolute positioned, full-width under navbar)
- Form grid: single column
- Cards: stack vertically
- Modals: full viewport with padding
- Agent list cards: stack content vertically

### 26. SCROLLBAR STYLING

```css
::-webkit-scrollbar {
  width: 8px;
}

::-webkit-scrollbar-track {
  background: var(--bg-dark);
}

::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb {
  background: var(--border-color);
  border-radius: var(--radius-full);
}

::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover {
  background: var(--text-muted);
}
```

Custom scrollbar: thin, rounded, subtle gray color that lightens on hover

  "content": "---\ntitle: \"Using Claude Code\"\nsidebar_label: \"Claude Code\"\nsidebar_position: 6\ndescription: \"How Claude Code is configured across KIX Platform repositories using CLAUDE.md files, templates, and MCP server integration\"\n---\n\n# Using Claude Code\n\nThe KIX Platform uses [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) as an AI-assisted development tool across all repositories. Every repository includes a `CLAUDE.md` file that provides Claude Code with project-specific context, standards, and operational guidance.\n\n---\n\n## How It Works\n\nWhen you open a repository with Claude Code, it automatically reads the `CLAUDE.md` file in the project root. This file tells Claude Code about the repository's purpose, technology stack, workflows, security requirements, and common pitfalls — so it can assist effectively without needing repeated context.\n\nThe KIX Platform extends this with a **three-tier hierarchy** that keeps instructions consistent across the entire platform while allowing repository-specific customisation.\n\n---\n\n## Three-Tier CLAUDE.md Hierarchy\n\n```\nTier 1: Master CLAUDE.md (universal standards)\n  └── Located in: kix-platform-docs/CLAUDE.md\n  └── Always applies to all repositories\n\nTier 2: Organization CLAUDE_ORG.md (shared patterns)\n  └── Located in: {org}/.github-private/CLAUDE_ORG.md\n  └── Applies to all repos in that GitHub organization\n\nTier 3: Repository CLAUDE.md (repo-specific)\n  └── Located in: {repo}/CLAUDE.md\n  └── Applies only to that repository\n```\n\n### Tier 1 — Master Standards\n\nThe master `CLAUDE.md` lives in this repository (`kix-platform-docs`) and defines universal standards that apply everywhere:\n\n- **Challenge and Validation Protocol** — never claim a task is done without evidence\n- **Plan Mode guidance** — when to plan before implementing\n- **Security requirements** — Workload Identity, private networking, EU data residency, network policies\n- **Git workflow** — commit message format, PR guidelines, co-authorship attribution\n- **Self-documentation rule** — update docs immediately after any correction\n\nAll repository-level `CLAUDE.md` files reference the master as their first dependency.\n\n### Tier 2 — Organization-Level\n\nEach GitHub organization can have a `CLAUDE_ORG.md` in its `.github-private` repository. These capture patterns shared across repositories within that organization:\n\n| Organization | Focus |\n|---|---|\n| `konecta-ix-platform` | Terraform module development, GCS state management, Terratest, multi-environment operations |\n| `konecta-ix-services` | Terraform-to-Helm migration, Helm 3.x conventions, service deployment standards |\n\nOrganizations with fewer shared patterns (crews, workloads, MCP servers, demos) rely on repository-level files directly.\n\n### Tier 3 — Repository-Level\n\nEvery repository has its own `CLAUDE.md` tailored to the complexity of the project. Three patterns are available:\n\n| Pattern | Token Budget | Use When |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Extended (A)** | ~2,500-3,000 | Multi-tier, complex workflows, 15+ config files, strict dependencies |\n| **Standard (B)** | ~1,500-2,000 | Single service or application, clear tech stack, standard workflow |\n| **Minimal (C)** | ~500-800 | Demos, POCs, utilities, experimental or short-lived repos |\n\n### Token Budget\n\nThe hierarchy is designed to fit within Claude Code's context window without consuming excessive tokens:\n\n| Scenario | Total Tokens | % of 200K Context |\n|---|---|---|\n| Simple repo (Master + Repo) | ~6,000 | ~3% |\n| Complex repo (Master + Org + Repo) | ~9,500 | ~5% |\n\n---\n\n## Navigation Guide\n\nThe [CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/blob/main/CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md) file in this repository serves as a directory of all `CLAUDE.md` files across the platform. It provides:\n\n- Quick reference for which file to check for specific questions\n- Links to every organization and repository CLAUDE.md\n- Decision tree for creating new repositories\n- Token budget summary\n\n**Common lookups:**\n\n| Question | Where to Look |\n|---|---|\n| Security requirements? | Master CLAUDE.md — Security Requirements |\n| Commit message format? | Master CLAUDE.md — Git Workflow Standards |\n| How to develop a Terraform module? | Platform Org CLAUDE_ORG.md |\n| How to clone dev to qa? | kix-platform-infrastructure CLAUDE.md |\n| How to write documentation? | Master CLAUDE.md — Documentation Standards |\n\n---\n\n## Templates\n\nTemplates for each pattern live in the `templates/` directory of this repository:\n\n| Template | Pattern | File |\n|---|---|---|\n| Extended | A | [`CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_EXTENDED.md`](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/blob/main/templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_EXTENDED.md) |\n| Standard | B | [`CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_STANDARD.md`](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/blob/main/templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_STANDARD.md) |\n| Minimal | C | [`CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_MINIMAL.md`](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/blob/main/templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_MINIMAL.md) |\n| Organization | — | [`CLAUDE_ORG_TEMPLATE.md`](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/blob/main/templates/CLAUDE_ORG_TEMPLATE.md) |\n\nEach template includes placeholder sections with comments explaining what to fill in. See the [Creating New Repositories](/docs/reference/creating-new-repository) guide for step-by-step instructions.\n\n---\n\n## What the Master CLAUDE.md Covers\n\nThe master file in this repository defines the following sections:\n\n### Repository Classification Guide\n\nA decision tree to determine which CLAUDE.md pattern (A, B, or C) a new repository should use based on its complexity.\n\n### Challenge and Validation Protocol\n\nRules for proving that work is complete:\n\n1. Run validation commands and capture output\n2. Review for quality and security\n3. Verify completeness against acceptance criteria\n4. Proactively share evidence — don't wait to be asked\n\n### Plan Mode Rules\n\nClaude Code should enter plan mode for:\n\n- Environment cloning (dev to qa, qa to prod)\n- New module creation\n- Multi-tier infrastructure changes\n- Security-sensitive changes (IAM, network policies, Cloud Armor)\n- First-time tasks with no existing checklist\n\n### Security Requirements\n\nMandatory rules enforced across all repositories:\n\n- **Workload Identity** — no service account keys, ever\n- **Private networking** — no public IPs on any resource\n- **Network policies** — GCP health check IPs (`35.191.0.0/16`, `130.211.0.0/22`) must be allowed for load-balanced services\n- **IAM least privilege** — no `roles/owner` or `roles/editor`\n- **EU data residency** — `europe-west1` and `europe-west4` only\n- **Organization policy constraints** — domain-restricted IAM, audit logging mandatory\n\n### Git Workflow Standards\n\n- Conventional commit messages (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `chore:`)\n- Co-authorship attribution: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`\n- HEREDOC format for multi-line commit messages\n- Feature branch workflow with PR reviews\n\n### Self-Documentation Rule\n\nAfter every correction, documentation must be updated immediately. Mistakes are tracked at three levels:\n\n- **Repository** — specific to one repo\n- **Organization** — promoted after 3+ occurrences across repos\n- **Master** — promoted when 3+ organizations are affected\n- **Archive** — moved to `MISTAKES_ARCHIVE.md` after 1 year or when superseded\n\n---\n\n## MCP Server Integration\n\nThis documentation repository includes an MCP server that makes all documentation available as structured resources and tools for Claude Code sessions. This means Claude Code can search and reference KIX Platform documentation without you needing to copy-paste content.\n\n### Configuration\n\nThe `.mcp.json` file in the project root configures the MCP server:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"kix-docs\": {\n      \"command\": \"node\",\n      \"args\": [\"mcp-server/build/index.js\"],\n      \"env\": {\n        \"DOCS_ROOT\": \"docs\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Available Tools\n\n| Tool | Purpose | Example Query |\n|---|---|---|\n| `search_docs` | Full-text search across all documentation | `\"workload identity\"`, `\"GKE cluster\"` |\n| `lookup_glossary` | Look up platform terminology | `\"MCP\"`, `\"ENGAGE layer\"` |\n| `lookup_module` | Find Terraform/Helm module details | `\"landing-zone\"`, `\"kong\"` |\n| `lookup_adr` | Query Architecture Decision Records | `\"ADR-001\"`, `\"litellm\"` |\n\n### Building the MCP Server\n\n```bash\ncd mcp-server\nnpm install\nnpm run build\n```\n\nThe server uses stdio transport and works with both Claude Code and Claude Desktop.\n\n### Testing with MCP Inspector\n\n```bash\nnpx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node mcp-server/build/index.js\n```\n\nThis opens a web UI where you can browse resources, invoke tools, and test prompts.\n\n---\n\n## Setting Up Claude Code on a KIX Repository\n\n### 1. Install Claude Code\n\nFollow the [official installation guide](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/overview) for your platform.\n\n### 2. Open the Repository\n\n```bash\ncd /path/to/kix-repository\nclaude\n```\n\nClaude Code will automatically read the `CLAUDE.md` file in the project root.\n\n### 3. Verify Context Loading\n\nYou can verify that Claude Code has loaded the project context by asking:\n\n```\nWhat are the security requirements for this project?\n```\n\nClaude Code should reference Workload Identity, private networking, EU data residency, and network policies from the master CLAUDE.md.\n\n### 4. Enable the MCP Server (Documentation Repo Only)\n\nIf working in `kix-platform-docs`, the MCP server is configured via `.mcp.json`. Build it first:\n\n```bash\ncd mcp-server && npm install && npm run build && cd ..\n```\n\nClaude Code will then have access to `search_docs`, `lookup_glossary`, `lookup_module`, and `lookup_adr` tools.\n\n---\n\n## Creating a CLAUDE.md for a New Repository\n\n1. **Classify** the repository using the [decision tree](#repository-classification-guide)\n2. **Copy** the appropriate template from `templates/`\n3. **Fill in** the placeholder sections\n4. **Reference** the master CLAUDE.md as the first dependency\n5. **Add** to the navigation guide (`CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md`)\n\nSee the full [Creating New Repositories](/docs/reference/creating-new-repository) guide for detailed instructions including checklists and examples.\n\n---\n\n## Key Files Reference\n\n| File | Location | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| `CLAUDE.md` | Repo root | Master standards (this repo) or repo-specific guidance (other repos) |\n| `CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md` | Repo root | Directory of all CLAUDE.md files across the platform |\n| `MISTAKES_ARCHIVE.md` | Repo root | Historical mistakes superseded by automation or policy |\n| `templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_EXTENDED.md` | `templates/` | Pattern A template for complex repos |\n| `templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_STANDARD.md` | `templates/` | Pattern B template for standard repos |\n| `templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_MINIMAL.md` | `templates/` | Pattern C template for demos/POCs |\n| `templates/CLAUDE_ORG_TEMPLATE.md` | `templates/` | Organization-level template |\n| `.mcp.json` | Repo root | MCP server configuration for Claude Code |\n| `mcp-server/` | `mcp-server/` | MCP server source (TypeScript) |\n"
}

     5→description: DNS migration procedures for the KIX Platform
     6→---
     7→
     8→# DNS Migration: AWS Route 53 to Google Cloud DNS
     9→
    10→## Overview
    11→
    12→This document guides the migration of the `konecta-digital.com` domain from AWS Route 53 to Google Cloud DNS using a delegated subdomain architecture. The migration is designed for zero downtime with a phased deployment strategy.
    13→
    14→## Architecture
    15→
    16→### DNS Hierarchy
    17→
    18→```
    19→AWS Route 53 (Domain Registrar Level)
    20→+-- konecta-digital.com
    21→    +-- NS: konecta-digital.com -> [GCP Shared DNS nameservers]
    22→
    23→Google Cloud DNS (kd-ix-eur-shr-dns project)
    24→+-- konecta-digital.com (root zone)
    25→|   +-- NS: crewai.konecta-digital.com -> [CrewAI project nameservers]
    26→|   +-- NS: iq.konecta-digital.com -> [IQ project nameservers]
    27→|   +-- NS: jobportal.konecta-digital.com -> [JobPortal project nameservers]
    28→|   +-- NS: ix.konecta-digital.com -> [GCP Shared DNS nameservers]
    29→|
    30→+-- ix.konecta-digital.com (IX parent zone)
    31→    +-- NS: dev.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Dev network project nameservers]
    32→    +-- NS: qa.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [QA network project nameservers]
    33→    +-- NS: prod.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Prod network project nameservers]
    34→
    35→Environment Network Projects
    36→+-- kd-ix-eur-dev-network
    37→|   +-- dev.ix.konecta-digital.com (public zone)
    38→|       +-- A: api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Load Balancer IP]
    39→|
    40→+-- kd-ix-eur-np-network
    41→|   +-- qa.ix.konecta-digital.com (public zone)
    42→|       +-- A: api.qa.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Load Balancer IP]
    43→|
    44→+-- kd-ix-eur-prod-network
    45→    +-- prod.ix.konecta-digital.com (public zone)
    46→        +-- A: api.prod.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Load Balancer IP]
    47→```
    48→
    49→### Design Principles
    50→
    51→1. **Separation of Concerns**: Shared services manage parent zones, environments manage their own zones
    52→2. **Blast Radius Reduction**: Environment teams can modify DNS without affecting other environments
    53→3. **GDPR Compliance**: All DNS data resides in EU region (europe-west1)
    54→4. **Security**: DNSSEC enabled on all zones with NSEC3 non-existence proof
    55→5. **Observability**: Query logging enabled for audit trail and monitoring
    56→
    57→## Infrastructure Components
    58→
    59→### Terraform Module: `public-dns`
    60→
    61→**Location**: `terraform/modules/gcp/public-dns/`
    62→
    63→Wrapper module around `terraform-google-modules/cloud-dns/google` v6.x with:
    64→- Public DNS zone creation
    65→- DNSSEC support (enabled by default)
    66→- Query logging to Cloud Logging
    67→- DNS record management (A, CNAME, NS, TXT, MX, etc.)
    68→- Standardized labeling for cost tracking
    69→
    70→**Key Features**:
    71→- `force_destroy = false` prevents accidental deletion while records exist
    72→- Comprehensive variable validation
    73→- Full DNSSEC support with NSEC3
    74→
    75→### Shared DNS Deployment
    76→
    77→**Location**: `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/`
    78→
    79→Manages two zones in the `kd-ix-eur-shr-dns` project:
    80→
    81→1. **Root Domain Zone** (`konecta-digital.com`)
    82→   - Contains NS delegations to existing subdomains (crewai, iq, jobportal)
    83→   - Contains NS delegation to ix subdomain
    84→   - Protected with `force_destroy = false` to prevent accidental deletion
    85→
    86→2. **IX Parent Zone** (`ix.konecta-digital.com`)
    87→   - Contains NS delegations to environment zones (dev, qa, prod)
    88→   - Acts as parent zone for all KIX platform environments
    89→
    90→### Landing Zone Integration
    91→
    92→**Location**: `terraform/modules/gcp/landing-zone/public-dns.tf`
    93→
    94→Extends the landing-zone module with optional public DNS support:
    95→- Conditionally creates public DNS zones based on `public_dns_config.enabled`
    96→- Creates zones in the network project (`var.network_project_id`)
    97→- Integrates with environment config.json for easy configuration
    98→
    99→### Environment Configuration
   100→
   101→**Files**: `terraform/environments/{dev,qa,prod}/config.json`
   102→
   103→Each environment has a `public_dns_config` section:
   104→
   105→```json
   106→{
   107→  "public_dns_config": {
   108→    "enabled": true,
   109→    "zone_name": "dev-ix-konecta-digital-com",
   110→    "domain": "dev.ix.konecta-digital.com.",
   111→    "enable_logging": true,
   112→    "enable_dnssec": true,
   113→    "force_destroy": false,
   114→    "recordsets": []
   115→  }
   116→}
   117→```
   118→
   119→## Migration Procedure
   120→
   121→### Pre-Migration Checklist
   122→
   123→- [ ] Backup existing AWS Route 53 records
   124→- [ ] Document current DNS TTL values
   125→- [ ] Identify all hostnames using konecta-digital.com domain
   126→- [ ] Verify GKE Gateway API load balancer IPs (if applicable)
   127→- [ ] Confirm GCP DNS API enabled in all projects:
   128→  ```bash
   129→  gcloud services enable dns.googleapis.com --project=kd-ix-eur-shr-dns
   130→  gcloud services enable dns.googleapis.com --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-network
   131→  gcloud services enable dns.googleapis.com --project=kd-ix-eur-np-network
   132→  gcloud services enable dns.googleapis.com --project=kd-ix-eur-prod-network
   133→  ```
   134→- [ ] Verify IAM permissions (`roles/dns.admin` on DNS project)
   135→- [ ] **Contact DNS team** to coordinate AWS Route 53 delegation timing
   136→- [ ] Review and update NS delegation placeholders with actual nameservers from existing projects
   137→
   138→### Phase 1: Deploy Shared DNS Zones
   139→
   140→**Objective**: Create root domain and IX parent zones in shared DNS project.
   141→
   142→```bash
   143→cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns
   144→
   145→# Initialize Terraform
   146→terraform init
   147→
   148→# Review the plan
   149→terraform plan
   150→
   151→# Apply (creates both root_domain and ix_parent_zone)
   152→terraform apply
   153→
   154→# Capture nameservers for AWS delegation
   155→terraform output root_name_servers
   156→terraform output root_name_servers_formatted
   157→```
   158→
   159→**Expected Outputs**:
   160→```
   161→root_name_servers = [
   162→  "ns-cloud-a1.googledomains.com.",
   163→  "ns-cloud-a2.googledomains.com.",
   164→  "ns-cloud-a3.googledomains.com.",
   165→  "ns-cloud-a4.googledomains.com.",
   166→]
   167→
   168→ix_name_servers = [
   169→  "ns-cloud-b1.googledomains.com.",
   170→  "ns-cloud-b2.googledomains.com.",
   171→  "ns-cloud-b3.googledomains.com.",
   172→  "ns-cloud-b4.googledomains.com.",
   173→]
   174→```
   175→
   176→:::important
   177→The root domain includes placeholder NS records for crewai, iq, and jobportal subdomains. You must update these with actual nameservers from those projects before applying.
   178→:::
   179→
   180→### Phase 2: Deploy Environment DNS Zones
   181→
   182→**Objective**: Create environment-specific zones in network projects.
   183→
   184→#### Dev Environment
   185→
   186→```bash
   187→cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   188→
   189→terraform init
   190→terraform plan -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   191→terraform apply -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   192→
   193→# Capture nameservers
   194→terraform output public_dns_name_servers
   195→```
   196→
   197→#### QA Environment
   198→
   199→```bash
   200→cd terraform/environments/qa/gcp/network
   201→
   202→terraform init
   203→terraform plan -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   204→terraform apply -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   205→
   206→# Capture nameservers
   207→terraform output public_dns_name_servers
   208→```
   209→
   210→#### Prod Environment
   211→
   212→```bash
   213→cd terraform/environments/prod/gcp/network
   214→
   215→terraform init
   216→terraform plan -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   217→terraform apply -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   218→
   219→# Capture nameservers
   220→terraform output public_dns_name_servers
   221→```
   222→
   223→### Phase 3: Update Parent Zone with NS Delegation
   224→
   225→**Objective**: Add NS delegation records to IX parent zone.
   226→
   227→1. Edit `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/main.tf`
   228→2. Update the `ix_parent_zone` module's `recordsets` with actual nameservers from Phase 2
   229→3. Uncomment the NS delegation records and replace placeholder nameservers:
   230→
   231→```hcl
   232→recordsets = [
   233→  {
   234→    name    = "dev"
   235→    type    = "NS"
   236→    ttl     = 21600
   237→    records = [
   238→      # Replace with actual nameservers from dev environment output
   239→      "ns-cloud-d1.googledomains.com.",
   240→      "ns-cloud-d2.googledomains.com.",
   241→      "ns-cloud-d3.googledomains.com.",
   242→      "ns-cloud-d4.googledomains.com."
   243→    ]
   244→  },
   245→  # ... qa and prod NS records
   246→]
   247→```
   248→
   249→4. Apply the changes:
   250→
   251→```bash
   252→cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns
   253→terraform plan
   254→terraform apply
   255→```
   256→
   257→### Phase 4: Update Root Zone with IX NS Delegation
   258→
   259→**Objective**: Add NS delegation from root domain to IX parent zone.
   260→
   261→1. Edit `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/main.tf`
   262→2. Add NS record for ix subdomain in `root_domain` module's `recordsets`:
   263→
   264→```hcl
   265→recordsets = [
   266→  # ... existing crewai, iq, jobportal NS records ...
   267→  {
   268→    name    = "ix"
   269→    type    = "NS"
   270→    ttl     = 21600
   271→    records = [
   272→      # Use ix_name_servers output from Phase 1
   273→      "ns-cloud-b1.googledomains.com.",
   274→      "ns-cloud-b2.googledomains.com.",
   275→      "ns-cloud-b3.googledomains.com.",
   276→      "ns-cloud-b4.googledomains.com."
   277→    ]
   278→  }
   279→]
   280→```
   281→
   282→3. Apply:
   283→
   284→```bash
   285→cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns
   286→terraform plan
   287→terraform apply
   288→```
   289→
   290→### Phase 5: Request AWS Route 53 Delegation
   291→
   292→**Objective**: Delegate domain authority from AWS Route 53 to GCP Cloud DNS.
   293→
   294→**Contact**: DNS/Domain Management Team
   295→
   296→**Information to Provide**:
   297→
   298→```
   299→Domain: konecta-digital.com
   300→Action: Update NS records for domain delegation
   301→Record Type: NS
   302→TTL: 172800 (48 hours)
   303→Nameservers: [from Phase 1 root_name_servers output]
   304→  - ns-cloud-a1.googledomains.com.
   305→  - ns-cloud-a2.googledomains.com.
   306→  - ns-cloud-a3.googledomains.com.
   307→  - ns-cloud-a4.googledomains.com.
   308→
   309→Business Justification:
   310→Migrate KIX Platform DNS management to Google Cloud DNS for:
   311→- Centralized DNS management within GCP
   312→- Environment-level DNS delegation
   313→- Enhanced DNSSEC support
   314→- Improved observability with Cloud Logging integration
   315→```
   316→
   317→**Timeline**: DNS team should implement this change during a maintenance window. The high TTL (48 hours) ensures smooth propagation.
   318→
   319→### Phase 6: Add Application DNS Records
   320→
   321→**Objective**: Add A records for API endpoints (or other application hostnames).
   322→
   323→After GKE Gateway API creates load balancers, update environment configs with A records:
   324→
   325→1. Get load balancer IPs:
   326→   ```bash
   327→   # For dev environment
   328→   kubectl get gateway -n kong
   329→   ```
   330→
   331→2. Update `terraform/environments/dev/config.json`:
   332→   ```json
   333→   "public_dns_config": {
   334→     "recordsets": [
   335→       {
   336→         "name": "api",
   337→         "type": "A",
   338→         "ttl": 300,
   339→         "records": ["34.56.78.90"]
   340→       }
   341→     ]
   342→   }
   343→   ```
   344→
   345→3. Apply landing zone changes:
   346→   ```bash
   347→   cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   348→   terraform plan
   349→   terraform apply
   350→   ```
   351→
   352→4. Repeat for QA and Prod environments.
   353→
   354→## Verification and Testing
   355→
   356→### DNS Resolution Testing
   357→
   358→Test from multiple locations (different ISPs, geographic regions):
   359→
   360→```bash
   361→# Test root domain nameservers
   362→dig konecta-digital.com NS @8.8.8.8
   363→
   364→# Test IX parent zone nameservers
   365→dig ix.konecta-digital.com NS @8.8.8.8
   366→
   367→# Test environment zone delegation
   368→dig dev.ix.konecta-digital.com NS @8.8.8.8
   369→dig qa.ix.konecta-digital.com NS @8.8.8.8
   370→dig prod.ix.konecta-digital.com NS @8.8.8.8
   371→
   372→# Test API endpoint resolution
   373→dig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com A @8.8.8.8
   374→dig api.qa.ix.konecta-digital.com A @8.8.8.8
   375→dig api.prod.ix.konecta-digital.com A @8.8.8.8
   376→
   377→# Verify DNSSEC validation
   378→dig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com +dnssec @8.8.8.8
   379→
   380→# Test from your local resolver (uses system DNS)
   381→dig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   382→
   383→# Test delegation chain
   384→dig +trace api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   385→```
   386→
   387→**Expected Results**:
   388→- NS queries return GCP nameservers (ns-cloud-*.googledomains.com)
   389→- A queries return correct load balancer IPs
   390→- DNSSEC signatures present (RRSIG records)
   391→- No SERVFAIL or NXDOMAIN errors
   392→- Delegation chain shows proper authority delegation
   393→
   394→### Functional Testing
   395→
   396→```bash
   397→# Test API endpoints (adjust URLs based on your services)
   398→curl -I https://api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com/health
   399→curl -I https://api.qa.ix.konecta-digital.com/health
   400→curl -I https://api.prod.ix.konecta-digital.com/health

   409→2. Verify all zones are created:
   410→   - `konecta-digital-com` in kd-ix-eur-shr-dns
   411→   - `ix-konecta-digital-com` in kd-ix-eur-shr-dns
   412→   - `dev-ix-konecta-digital-com` in kd-ix-eur-dev-network
   413→   - `qa-ix-konecta-digital-com` in kd-ix-eur-np-network
   414→   - `prod-ix-konecta-digital-com` in kd-ix-eur-prod-network

   416→3. Check DNSSEC status: Should show "On" with NSEC3 algorithm

   427→# Example alert policy
   428→displayName: DNS Query Failure Rate
   429→conditions:
   430→  - displayName: High error rate
   431→    conditionThreshold:
   432→      filter: resource.type="dns_query" AND severity="ERROR"
   433→      aggregations:

   441→## Rollback Plan
   442→
   443→If issues arise during migration:
   444→
   445→### Immediate Rollback (AWS Route 53)
   446→
   447→**Contact DNS team immediately** to revert NS records in AWS Route 53:
   448→- Remove GCP nameservers
   449→- Restore original AWS Route 53 nameservers
   450→- DNS will revert to AWS configuration
   451→- Zero downtime (existing Route 53 records still exist)
   452→
   453→### Partial Rollback (Environment Level)
   454→
   455→If a specific environment has issues:
   456→
   457→1. Remove NS delegation from parent zone:
   458→   ```bash
   459→   cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns
   460→   # Edit main.tf, comment out problematic environment NS record
   461→   terraform apply
   462→   ```
   463→
   464→2. Wait for TTL propagation (21600 seconds = 6 hours)
   465→
   466→### Terraform State Recovery
   467→
   468→If Terraform state corruption occurs:
   469→
   470→```bash
   471→# Remove problematic resource from state
   472→terraform state rm module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone[0]
   473→
   474→# Re-import if resource exists
   475→terraform import module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone[0] projects/PROJECT_ID/managedZones/ZONE_NAME
   476→```
   477→
   478→### Complete Cleanup
   479→
   480→To fully remove GCP DNS infrastructure:
   481→
   482→```bash
   483→# 1. Remove all DNS records first (due to force_destroy=false)
   484→# Edit main.tf, set recordsets = [] for all zones
   485→cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns
   486→terraform apply
   487→
   488→# 2. Destroy environment zones
   489→cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   490→terraform destroy -target=module.landing_zone.module.public_dns_zone
   491→
   492→# Repeat for QA and Prod
   493→
   494→# 3. Destroy shared zones
   495→cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns
   496→terraform destroy
   497→```
   498→
   499→## Operational Procedures
   500→
   501→### Adding a New Environment
   502→
   503→1. Add `public_dns_config` to environment's `config.json`
   504→2. Deploy landing zone to create environment zone
   505→3. Capture nameservers from output
   506→4. Update shared DNS `ix_parent_zone` with NS delegation
   507→5. Apply shared DNS changes
   508→
   509→### Adding DNS Records
   510→
   511→**For environment-specific records** (e.g., api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com):
   512→
   513→1. Edit `terraform/environments/dev/config.json`:
   514→   ```json
   515→   "public_dns_config": {
   516→     "recordsets": [
   517→       {
   518→         "name": "api",
   519→         "type": "A",
   520→         "ttl": 300,
   521→         "records": ["34.56.78.90"]
   522→       }
   523→     ]
   524→   }
   525→   ```
   526→
   527→2. Apply:
   528→   ```bash
   529→   cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network
   530→   terraform apply
   531→   ```
   532→
   533→**For root domain records** (e.g., www.konecta-digital.com):
   534→
   535→1. Edit `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/main.tf`
   536→2. Add to `root_domain` module's `recordsets`
   537→3. Apply shared DNS changes
   538→
   539→### Updating Existing Records
   540→
   541→1. Locate the record in appropriate config file
   542→2. Modify TTL, type, or records array
   543→3. Apply Terraform changes
   544→4. Wait for TTL propagation before verifying
   545→
   546→### Monitoring DNS Health
   547→
   548→**Query Logging Dashboard**:
   549→
   550→1. Navigate to **Logging -> Logs Explorer**
   551→2. Use query:
   552→   ```
   553→   resource.type="dns_query"
   554→   resource.labels.project_id="kd-ix-eur-shr-dns"
   555→   ```
   556→3. Create dashboard widgets for:
   557→   - Query rate by zone
   558→   - Response codes (NOERROR, NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL)
   559→   - Query latency
   560→
   561→**DNSSEC Validation**:
   562→
   563→```bash
   564→# Check DNSSEC chain
   565→dig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com +dnssec +multiline
   566→
   567→# Verify with DNSSEC validators
   568→dnsviz graph api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   569→```
   570→
   571→## Security Considerations
   572→
   573→### IAM Permissions
   574→
   575→**Principle of Least Privilege**: Only platform engineers should have DNS admin access.
   576→
   577→```bash
   578→# Grant DNS admin to specific users
   579→gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding kd-ix-eur-shr-dns \
   580→  --member="user:platform-engineer@konecta-group.com" \
   581→  --role="roles/dns.admin"
   582→
   583→# For automation (use Workload Identity, never service account keys)
   584→gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding kd-ix-eur-shr-dns \
   585→  --member="serviceAccount:terraform-automation@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
   586→  --role="roles/dns.admin"
   587→```
   588→
   589→### DNSSEC Key Management
   590→
   591→- **Key Rotation**: Google Cloud DNS automatically manages DNSSEC key rotation
   592→- **KSK (Key Signing Key)**: Rotated annually
   593→- **ZSK (Zone Signing Key)**: Rotated every 90 days
   594→- **DS Records**: If using external domain registrar, DS records must be updated manually
   595→
   596→### Audit Logging
   597→
   598→All DNS changes are logged:
   599→
   600→```bash
   601→# View DNS admin activity
   602→gcloud logging read '
   603→  protoPayload.serviceName="dns.googleapis.com"
   604→  AND protoPayload.methodName:("ManagedZones" OR "ResourceRecordSets")
   605→' --limit 50 --project=kd-ix-eur-shr-dns
   606→```
   607→
   608→### Network Security
   609→
   610→- **Public Zones**: Accessible from internet (required for external DNS resolution)
   611→- **Private Zones**: Remain isolated within VPC (see landing-zone dns.tf)
   612→- **No Cross-Project Access**: Each environment manages only its own zone
   613→

   617→
   618→| Resource | Price | Estimated Usage | Monthly Cost |
   619→|----------|-------|-----------------|--------------|
   620→| Hosted Zone | $0.20/zone/month | 5 zones | $1.00 |
   621→| DNS Queries | $0.40/million (first 1B) | 10M queries | $4.00 |
   622→| DNSSEC | No additional cost | - | $0.00 |
   623→| **Total** | | | **~$5.00/month** |

   625→**Comparison to AWS Route 53**:

   630→## Troubleshooting
   631→
   632→### DNS Resolution Failures
   633→
   634→**Symptom**: `dig` returns SERVFAIL or NXDOMAIN
   635→
   636→**Diagnosis**:
   637→```bash
   638→# Check delegation chain
   639→dig +trace api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   640→
   641→# Check specific nameserver
   642→dig @ns-cloud-d1.googledomains.com api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   643→```
   644→
   645→**Common Causes**:
   646→1. NS delegation not configured correctly
   647→2. Zone not created in correct project
   648→3. TTL propagation still in progress (wait longer)
   649→4. DNSSEC validation failure
   650→
   651→**Resolution**:
   652→- Verify NS records in parent zone match child zone nameservers
   653→- Check zone exists: `gcloud dns managed-zones list --project=PROJECT_ID`
   654→- Wait for TTL propagation (use longer TTL values initially)
   655→
   656→### DNSSEC Validation Errors
   657→
   658→**Symptom**: DNSSEC validation fails, queries return SERVFAIL when validated
   659→
   660→**Diagnosis**:
   661→```bash
   662→# Check DNSSEC chain
   663→dig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com +dnssec +multiline
   664→
   665→# Validate with dnssec-analyzer
   666→dnsviz probe api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   667→```
   668→
   669→**Common Causes**:
   670→1. DS records not configured in parent zone (if using external registrar)
   671→2. DNSSEC chain broken due to incorrect delegation
   672→3. Time sync issues (clock skew)
   673→
   674→**Resolution**:
   675→- For GCP-to-GCP delegation: DNSSEC is automatic, check NS delegation
   676→- For external registrar: Add DS records to domain registrar
   677→- Verify server time is synchronized (DNSSEC is time-sensitive)
   678→
   679→### Terraform State Issues
   680→
   681→**Symptom**: Terraform detects unwanted changes on every plan
   682→
   683→**Diagnosis**:
   684→```bash
   685→terraform plan -refresh=false  # Skip refresh to see actual config drift
   686→terraform show  # Inspect current state
   687→```
   688→
   689→**Resolution**:
   690→```bash
   691→# Refresh state from actual infrastructure
   692→terraform refresh
   693→
   694→# If state is corrupted, remove and re-import
   695→terraform state rm MODULE.RESOURCE
   696→terraform import MODULE.RESOURCE projects/PROJECT_ID/managedZones/ZONE_NAME
   697→```
   698→
   699→### Query Logging Not Appearing
   700→
   701→**Symptom**: No DNS query logs in Cloud Logging
   702→
   703→**Diagnosis**:
   704→```bash
   705→# Check if logging is enabled
   706→gcloud dns managed-zones describe ZONE_NAME --project=PROJECT_ID
   707→
   708→# Verify log query
   709→gcloud logging read 'resource.type="dns_query"' --limit 10
   710→```
   711→
   712→**Resolution**:
   713→- Verify `enable_logging = true` in Terraform
   714→- Check IAM permissions for Cloud Logging
   715→- Wait 5-10 minutes for logs to appear initially
   716→
   717→## Appendix
   718→
   719→### DNS Record Types Reference
   720→
   721→| Type | Purpose | Example |
   722→|------|---------|---------|
   723→| A | IPv4 address | `api 300 IN A 34.56.78.90` |
   724→| AAAA | IPv6 address | `api 300 IN AAAA 2001:db8::1` |
   725→| CNAME | Alias to another name | `www 3600 IN CNAME api.example.com.` |
   726→| NS | Nameserver delegation | `dev 21600 IN NS ns1.google.com.` |
   727→| MX | Mail exchange | `@ 3600 IN MX 10 mail.example.com.` |
   728→| TXT | Text records (SPF, DKIM) | `@ 3600 IN TXT "v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all"` |
   729→| CAA | Certificate authority authorization | `@ 3600 IN CAA 0 issue "letsencrypt.org"` |
   730→
   731→### TTL Guidelines
   732→
   733→| Use Case | Recommended TTL | Rationale |
   734→|----------|----------------|-----------|
   735→| Production A records | 300 seconds (5 min) | Fast failover for load balancer changes |
   736→| CNAME records | 3600 seconds (1 hour) | Stable aliases, infrequent changes |
   737→| NS delegation | 21600 seconds (6 hours) | High stability, rare changes |
   738→| Development records | 60 seconds (1 min) | Rapid iteration during development |
   739→| SOA/Authority records | 7200 seconds (2 hours) | Standard authority TTL |
   740→
   741→### Common DNS Commands
   742→
   743→```bash
   744→# Query specific record type
   745→dig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com A
   746→
   747→# Query specific nameserver
   748→dig @ns-cloud-d1.googledomains.com api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   749→
   750→# Show full delegation chain
   751→dig +trace api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   752→
   753→# DNSSEC validation
   754→dig +dnssec api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   755→
   756→# Reverse DNS lookup
   757→dig -x 34.56.78.90
   758→
   759→# List all records in zone (requires zone transfer permission)
   760→dig axfr ix.konecta-digital.com @ns-cloud-b1.googledomains.com
   761→```
   762→
   763→## References
   764→

   768→- [Terraform Google Cloud DNS Module](https://github.com/terraform-google-modules/terraform-google-cloud-dns)
   769→- [DNSSEC on GCP](https://cloud.google.com/dns/docs/dnssec)
   770→- [DNS Best Practices](https://cloud.google.com/dns/docs/best-practices)

  "content": "---\ntitle: \"DNS Architecture\"\nsidebar_label: \"DNS Architecture\"\nsidebar_position: 5\ndescription: \"DNS zone architecture for the KIX Platform on Google Cloud DNS, managed entirely in Terraform\"\n---\n\n# DNS Architecture\n\n## Overview\n\nThe KIX Platform DNS is hosted entirely on **Google Cloud DNS** and managed as **infrastructure-as-code** through Terraform. The architecture uses a delegated subdomain model where a shared DNS project owns the root zone, and each environment manages its own zone within its network project.\n\n**Domain:** `konecta-digital.com`\n\n**Key Characteristics:**\n- All zones defined and managed in Terraform (no manual DNS changes)\n- DNSSEC enabled on every zone with NSEC3 non-existence proof\n- Query logging enabled for audit trail and observability\n- EU-only deployment (`europe-west1`) for GDPR compliance\n\n---\n\n## Zone Hierarchy\n\n```\nGoogle Cloud DNS (kd-ix-eur-shr-dns project)\n+-- konecta-digital.com (root zone)\n|   +-- NS: crewai.konecta-digital.com -> [CrewAI project nameservers]\n|   +-- NS: iq.konecta-digital.com -> [IQ project nameservers]\n|   +-- NS: jobportal.konecta-digital.com -> [JobPortal project nameservers]\n|   +-- NS: ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Shared DNS nameservers]\n|\n+-- ix.konecta-digital.com (IX parent zone)\n    +-- NS: dev.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Dev network project nameservers]\n    +-- NS: qa.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [QA network project nameservers]\n    +-- NS: prod.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Prod network project nameservers]\n\nEnvironment Network Projects\n+-- kd-ix-eur-dev-network\n|   +-- dev.ix.konecta-digital.com (public zone)\n|       +-- A: api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Load Balancer IP]\n|\n+-- kd-ix-eur-np-network\n|   +-- qa.ix.konecta-digital.com (public zone)\n|       +-- A: api.qa.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Load Balancer IP]\n|\n+-- kd-ix-eur-prod-network\n    +-- prod.ix.konecta-digital.com (public zone)\n        +-- A: api.prod.ix.konecta-digital.com -> [Load Balancer IP]\n```\n\n### Design Principles\n\n1. **Separation of Concerns** — the shared DNS project manages the root zone and IX parent zone; each environment manages only its own zone within its network project\n2. **Blast Radius Reduction** — environment teams can add or modify DNS records without affecting other environments or the root zone\n3. **GDPR Compliance** — all DNS data resides in the EU region (`europe-west1`)\n4. **Security** — DNSSEC enabled on all zones; query logging enabled for audit\n5. **Terraform-Only Changes** — no records are created manually; all state is tracked in Terraform\n\n---\n\n## Terraform Structure\n\n### DNS Module: `public-dns`\n\n**Location:** `terraform/modules/gcp/public-dns/`\n\nA wrapper module around `terraform-google-modules/cloud-dns/google` v6.x that standardises DNS zone creation across the platform:\n\n- Public DNS zone creation with configurable record sets\n- DNSSEC enabled by default (NSEC3 algorithm)\n- Query logging to Cloud Logging\n- Support for A, AAAA, CNAME, NS, TXT, MX, and CAA record types\n- Standardised labelling for cost tracking\n- `force_destroy = false` to prevent accidental zone deletion while records exist\n\n### Shared DNS Deployment\n\n**Location:** `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/`\n\n**Project:** `kd-ix-eur-shr-dns`\n\nManages two zones:\n\n| Zone | Domain | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| `root_domain` | `konecta-digital.com` | Root zone with NS delegations to platform subdomains (crewai, iq, jobportal, ix) |\n| `ix_parent_zone` | `ix.konecta-digital.com` | Parent zone for KIX Platform environments with NS delegations to dev, qa, prod |\n\nBoth zones are protected with `force_destroy = false`.\n\n### Landing Zone Integration\n\n**Location:** `terraform/modules/gcp/landing-zone/public-dns.tf`\n\nThe landing-zone module includes optional public DNS support. When `public_dns_config.enabled` is set in an environment's `config.json`, the module creates a public DNS zone in the environment's network project.\n\n### Environment Configuration\n\n**Location:** `terraform/environments/{dev,qa,prod}/config.json`\n\nEach environment includes a `public_dns_config` block:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"public_dns_config\": {\n    \"enabled\": true,\n    \"zone_name\": \"dev-ix-konecta-digital-com\",\n    \"domain\": \"dev.ix.konecta-digital.com.\",\n    \"enable_logging\": true,\n    \"enable_dnssec\": true,\n    \"force_destroy\": false,\n    \"recordsets\": [\n      {\n        \"name\": \"api\",\n        \"type\": \"A\",\n        \"ttl\": 300,\n        \"records\": [\"34.56.78.90\"]\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## GCP Project Layout\n\n| Project | Zone | Role |\n|---|---|---|\n| `kd-ix-eur-shr-dns` | `konecta-digital.com` | Root zone — NS delegations only |\n| `kd-ix-eur-shr-dns` | `ix.konecta-digital.com` | IX parent zone — NS delegations to environments |\n| `kd-ix-eur-dev-network` | `dev.ix.konecta-digital.com` | Dev environment records |\n| `kd-ix-eur-np-network` | `qa.ix.konecta-digital.com` | QA environment records |\n| `kd-ix-eur-prod-network` | `prod.ix.konecta-digital.com` | Prod environment records |\n\n---\n\n## Security\n\n### DNSSEC\n\nAll zones have DNSSEC enabled with the following configuration:\n\n- **Algorithm:** NSEC3\n- **Key Signing Key (KSK):** Rotated annually by Google Cloud DNS\n- **Zone Signing Key (ZSK):** Rotated every 90 days by Google Cloud DNS\n- **DS Records:** Managed automatically for GCP-to-GCP delegations\n\nDNSSEC key rotation is fully managed by Google Cloud DNS and requires no manual intervention.\n\n### IAM\n\nDNS administration follows the principle of least privilege:\n\n- `roles/dns.admin` granted only to platform engineers and Terraform automation service accounts\n- Terraform automation uses Workload Identity (no service account keys)\n- Each environment's network project has its own IAM bindings for DNS management\n- No cross-project DNS access between environments\n\n### Audit Logging\n\nAll DNS changes are logged via Cloud Audit Logs:\n\n```bash\ngcloud logging read '\n  protoPayload.serviceName=\"dns.googleapis.com\"\n  AND protoPayload.methodName:(\"ManagedZones\" OR \"ResourceRecordSets\")\n' --limit 50 --project=kd-ix-eur-shr-dns\n```\n\nQuery logging is enabled on all zones for traffic observability:\n\n```\nLogging > Logs Explorer\nFilter: resource.type=\"dns_query\"\n         resource.labels.target_name=\"ix.konecta-digital.com\"\n```\n\n### Network Security\n\n- **Public zones** are accessible from the internet (required for external DNS resolution)\n- **Private zones** remain isolated within the VPC (see landing-zone `dns.tf`)\n- Each environment manages only its own zone — no cross-project zone access\n\n---\n\n## Operational Procedures\n\n### Adding DNS Records to an Environment\n\n1. Edit the environment's `config.json` to add entries to the `recordsets` array:\n\n   ```json\n   \"public_dns_config\": {\n     \"recordsets\": [\n       {\n         \"name\": \"api\",\n         \"type\": \"A\",\n         \"ttl\": 300,\n         \"records\": [\"34.56.78.90\"]\n       },\n       {\n         \"name\": \"portal\",\n         \"type\": \"CNAME\",\n         \"ttl\": 3600,\n         \"records\": [\"api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com.\"]\n       }\n     ]\n   }\n   ```\n\n2. Apply through the landing zone:\n\n   ```bash\n   cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/network\n   terraform plan\n   terraform apply\n   ```\n\n### Adding Records to the Root Domain\n\nFor records directly under `konecta-digital.com` (e.g., `www.konecta-digital.com`):\n\n1. Edit `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/main.tf`\n2. Add to the `root_domain` module's `recordsets`\n3. Apply:\n\n   ```bash\n   cd terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns\n   terraform plan\n   terraform apply\n   ```\n\n### Adding a New Environment\n\n1. Add `public_dns_config` to the new environment's `config.json`\n2. Deploy the landing zone to create the environment zone\n3. Capture nameservers from the Terraform output\n4. Add NS delegation to the IX parent zone in `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/main.tf`\n5. Apply the shared DNS changes\n\n### Delegating a New Subdomain\n\nTo delegate a new subdomain (e.g., `newservice.konecta-digital.com`) to another GCP project:\n\n1. Create a DNS zone in the target project (manually or via Terraform)\n2. Note the nameservers assigned by Google Cloud DNS\n3. Add an NS record to the root zone in `terraform/environments/shared/gcp/dns/main.tf`:\n\n   ```hcl\n   {\n     name    = \"newservice\"\n     type    = \"NS\"\n     ttl     = 21600\n     records = [\n       \"ns-cloud-e1.googledomains.com.\",\n       \"ns-cloud-e2.googledomains.com.\",\n       \"ns-cloud-e3.googledomains.com.\",\n       \"ns-cloud-e4.googledomains.com.\"\n     ]\n   }\n   ```\n\n4. Apply the shared DNS changes\n\n---\n\n## Verification\n\n### DNS Resolution\n\n```bash\n# Root domain nameservers\ndig konecta-digital.com NS @8.8.8.8\n\n# IX parent zone nameservers\ndig ix.konecta-digital.com NS @8.8.8.8\n\n# Environment zone delegation\ndig dev.ix.konecta-digital.com NS @8.8.8.8\ndig qa.ix.konecta-digital.com NS @8.8.8.8\ndig prod.ix.konecta-digital.com NS @8.8.8.8\n\n# Application endpoint resolution\ndig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com A @8.8.8.8\n\n# Full delegation chain trace\ndig +trace api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com\n\n# DNSSEC validation\ndig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com +dnssec @8.8.8.8\n```\n\n**Expected results:**\n- NS queries return `ns-cloud-*.googledomains.com` nameservers\n- A queries return the correct load balancer IPs\n- DNSSEC responses include RRSIG records\n- No SERVFAIL or unexpected NXDOMAIN errors\n\n### Functional Testing\n\n```bash\ncurl -I https://api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com/health\ncurl -I https://api.qa.ix.konecta-digital.com/health\ncurl -I https://api.prod.ix.konecta-digital.com/health\n```\n\n---\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### SERVFAIL or NXDOMAIN Responses\n\n**Diagnosis:**\n\n```bash\ndig +trace api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com\ndig @ns-cloud-d1.googledomains.com api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com\n```\n\n**Common causes:**\n1. NS delegation records in parent zone don't match child zone nameservers\n2. Zone not created in the correct project\n3. TTL propagation still in progress\n\n**Resolution:**\n- Verify NS records in parent zone: `gcloud dns record-sets list --zone=ZONE_NAME --project=PROJECT_ID`\n- Confirm zone exists: `gcloud dns managed-zones list --project=PROJECT_ID`\n\n### DNSSEC Validation Errors\n\n**Diagnosis:**\n\n```bash\ndig api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com +dnssec +multiline\n```\n\n**Common causes:**\n1. DS records missing in parent zone (external registrar delegations)\n2. Broken DNSSEC chain due to incorrect NS delegation\n\n**Resolution:**\n- For GCP-to-GCP delegation, DNSSEC is automatic — check NS records\n- For external registrar, ensure DS records are published\n\n### Terraform State Drift\n\n**Diagnosis:**\n\n```bash\nterraform plan -refresh=false\nterraform show\n```\n\n**Resolution:**\n\n```bash\n# Refresh state from actual infrastructure\nterraform refresh\n\n# If state is corrupted, remove and re-import\nterraform state rm MODULE.RESOURCE\nterraform import MODULE.RESOURCE projects/PROJECT_ID/managedZones/ZONE_NAME\n```\n\n### Missing Query Logs\n\n**Diagnosis:**\n\n```bash\ngcloud dns managed-zones describe ZONE_NAME --project=PROJECT_ID\n```\n\n**Resolution:**\n- Verify `enable_logging = true` in Terraform config\n- Check Cloud Logging IAM permissions\n- Allow up to 10 minutes for initial log ingestion\n\n---\n\n## Cost\n\n| Resource | Price | Estimated Usage | Monthly Cost |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Hosted Zones | $0.20/zone/month | 5 zones | $1.00 |\n| DNS Queries | $0.40/million (first 1B) | ~10M queries | $4.00 |\n| DNSSEC | No additional cost | — | $0.00 |\n| **Total** | | | **~$5.00/month** |\n\n---\n\n## TTL Guidelines\n\n| Use Case | Recommended TTL | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| Production A records | 300s (5 min) | Fast failover for load balancer changes |\n| CNAME records | 3600s (1 hour) | Stable aliases, infrequent changes |\n| NS delegation | 21600s (6 hours) | High stability, rare changes |\n| Development records | 60s (1 min) | Rapid iteration |\n\n---\n\n## References\n\n- [Google Cloud DNS Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/dns/docs)\n- [Terraform Google Cloud DNS Module](https://github.com/terraform-google-modules/terraform-google-cloud-dns)\n- [DNSSEC on Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/dns/docs/dnssec)\n- [Cloud DNS Best Practices](https://cloud.google.com/dns/docs/best-practices)\n- [Security Architecture](/docs/security/security-architecture) — platform security controls\n- [Terraform Structure](/docs/infrastructure-ops/terraform-structure) — Terraform layout and conventions\n"
}

     7→
     8→# Infrastructure Operations
     9→
    10→This section provides operational guidance for deploying, managing, and maintaining the KIX Platform infrastructure. It covers the Terraform repository structure, deployment procedures, CI/CD pipeline operations, and DNS migration.
    11→
    12→## What You'll Find Here
    13→
    14→| Guide | Description |
    15→|-------|-------------|
    16→| [Terraform Structure](/docs/infrastructure-ops/terraform-structure) | Repository layout, module organization, state management, and config.json patterns |
    17→| [Deployment Guide](/docs/infrastructure-ops/deployment-guide) | Step-by-step deployment procedures, apply order, change windows, and rollback |
    18→| [CI/CD Runbook](/docs/infrastructure-ops/cicd-runbook) | Pipeline operations, workflow reference, and troubleshooting |
    19→| [DNS Migration](/docs/infrastructure-ops/dns-migration) | DNS migration from AWS Route 53 to Google Cloud DNS |
    20→
    21→## Service Dependency Chain
    22→
    23→Infrastructure services must be deployed in a specific order. The following diagram shows the dependency chain for each environment:
    24→
    25→```
    26→+---------------------+
    27→|     bootstrap       |  Creates state buckets (run once)
    28→+---------+-----------+
    29→          |
    30→          v
    31→+---------------------+
    32→|    gcp/network      |  VPC, subnets, NAT, firewall
    33→+---------+-----------+
    34→          |
    35→          +----------------+
    36→          v                v
    37→+---------------+  +---------------+
    38→|   gcp/gke     |  |   gcp/data    |  (can run in parallel)
    39→+-------+-------+  +---------------+
    40→        |
    41→        v
    42→+---------------------+
    43→| kubernetes/platform |  gke-config, kong, litellm
    44→+---------------------+
    45→```
    46→
    47→**Per-environment apply order:** `network` -> `gke` -> `data` -> `kubernetes/platform`
    48→
    49→**Shared services apply order:** `network` -> `security` -> `gke` -> `iam` -> `argocd` -> `argocd-bootstrap`
    50→
    51→## Environment Overview
    52→
    53→The KIX Platform operates across four environments, each with distinct operational characteristics:
    54→
    55→| Environment | Purpose | Change Window | Approval |
    56→|-------------|---------|---------------|----------|
    57→| **dev** | Rapid iteration and testing | Anytime | Optional (auto-approve allowed) |
    58→| **qa** | Controlled validation before production | Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC, Mon-Fri) | Manual approval required |
    59→| **prod** | Production workloads | Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC only | Manual approval + change ticket |
    60→| **shared** | Shared services (ArgoCD, DNS) | Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC, Mon-Fri) | Manual approval required |
    61→
    62→## Key Resources
    63→
    64→- **State Buckets:** `gs://kd-tfstate-{env}/` per environment
    65→- **CI/CD:** GitHub Actions with reusable workflows
    66→- **GitOps:** ArgoCD on shared platform cluster
    67→- **Modules Repository:** [kix-platform-modules](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules)
    68→- **Infrastructure Repository:** [kix-platform-infrastructure](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-infrastructure)
    69→
    70→## Getting Started
    71→
    72→If you are new to the platform, start with the [Terraform Structure](/docs/infrastructure-ops/terraform-structure) page to understand how the codebase is organized, then proceed to the [Deployment Guide](/docs/infrastructure-ops/deployment-guide) for step-by-step procedures. The [CI/CD Runbook](/docs/infrastructure-ops/cicd-runbook) covers pipeline operations and troubleshooting for day-to-day work.

    37→
    38→export async function loadDocs(docsRoot: string): Promise<DocPage[]> {
    39→  const pattern = resolve(docsRoot, "**/*.md");
    40→  const files = await glob(pattern);
    41→  const pages: DocPage[] = [];
    42→
    43→  for (const filePath of files) {
    44→    try {
    45→      const raw = readFileSync(filePath, "utf-8");
    46→      const { data, content } = matter(raw);
    47→      const rel = relative(docsRoot, filePath);
    48→      const parts = rel.split("/");
    49→      const category = parts.length > 1 ? parts[0] : "root";
    50→
    51→      pages.push({
    52→        path: filePath,
    53→        relativePath: rel.replace(/\.md$/, ""),
    54→        title: data.title || basename(filePath, ".md"),
    55→        sidebarLabel: data.sidebar_label || data.title || basename(filePath, ".md"),
    56→        description: data.description || "",
    57→        category,
    58→        content,
    59→        rawContent: raw,
    60→      });
    61→    } catch (err) {
    62→      console.error(`Failed to load ${filePath}: ${err}`);
    63→    }
    64→  }
    65→
    66→  return pages;
    67→}
    68→
    69→export function extractGlossary(pages: DocPage[]): GlossaryEntry[] {
    70→  const glossaryPage = pages.find(
    71→    (p) => p.relativePath === "reference/glossary"
    72→  );
    73→  if (!glossaryPage) return [];
    74→
    75→  const entries: GlossaryEntry[] = [];
    76→  const lines = glossaryPage.content.split("\n");
    77→
    78→  for (const line of lines) {
    79→    const match = line.match(
    80→      /^\|\s*\*\*(.+?)\*\*\s*\|\s*(.+?)\s*\|$/
    81→    );
    82→    if (match) {
    83→      entries.push({ term: match[1], definition: match[2] });
    84→    }
    85→  }
    86→
    87→  return entries;
    88→}
    89→
    90→export function extractModules(pages: DocPage[]): ModuleEntry[] {
    91→  const catalogPage = pages.find(
    92→    (p) => p.relativePath === "reference/module-catalog"
    93→  );
    94→  if (!catalogPage) return [];
    95→
    96→  const entries: ModuleEntry[] = [];
    97→  const lines = catalogPage.content.split("\n");
    98→  let currentType = "unknown";
    99→
   100→  for (const line of lines) {
   101→    if (line.startsWith("## ") || line.startsWith("### ")) {
   102→      currentType = line.replace(/^#+\s*/, "").trim();
   103→    }
   104→    const match = line.match(
   105→      /^\|\s*\*?\*?`?(\S+?)`?\*?\*?\s*\|\s*(.+?)\s*\|/
   106→    );
   107→    if (match && !match[1].startsWith("Module") && !match[1].startsWith("---")) {
   108→      entries.push({
   109→        name: match[1],
   110→        type: currentType,
   111→        description: match[2].replace(/\|.*$/, "").trim(),
   112→        path: `reference/module-catalog`,
   113→        repoUrl: `https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules`,
   114→      });
   115→    }
   116→  }
   117→
   118→  return entries;
   119→}
   120→
   121→export function extractAdrs(pages: DocPage[]): AdrEntry[] {
   122→  return pages
   123→    .filter((p) => p.category === "adr" && p.relativePath !== "adr/index")
   124→    .map((p) => {
   125→      const idMatch = p.relativePath.match(/adr-(\d+)/);
   126→      const statusMatch = p.content.match(/\*\*Status:\*\*\s*(.+)/);
   127→      return {
   128→        id: idMatch ? `ADR-${idMatch[1]}` : p.relativePath,
   129→        title: p.title,
   130→        status: statusMatch ? statusMatch[1].trim() : "Unknown",
   131→        content: p.content,
   132→        path: p.relativePath,
   133→      };
   134→    });
   135→}

> DEVELOPER

how do i test the mcp server?

> AGENT

Build it first, then use the MCP Inspector:

```bash
cd mcp-server
npm install
npm run build
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node build/index.js
```

The Inspector opens a web UI where you can browse resources, invoke tools (`search_docs`, `lookup_glossary`, `lookup_module`, `lookup_adr`), and test prompts.

Note the server expects `DOCS_ROOT` to point to the docs directory. By default it will look relative to the working directory. If you run from the `mcp-server/` directory you may need to set it explicitly:

```bash
DOCS_ROOT=../docs npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node build/index.js
```

To test it with Claude Code directly, the `.mcp.json` in the project root is already configured — just make sure the server is built and open Claude Code from the project root.

> AGENT

The `.mcp.json` file in the project root already configures it. Claude Code automatically picks up MCP servers from `.mcp.json` when you open a session in that directory. There's nothing extra to configure — just make sure the server is built:

```bash
cd mcp-server && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
```

Then start a new Claude Code session from the project root. The `kix-docs` MCP server will be available with its four tools (`search_docs`, `lookup_glossary`, `lookup_module`, `lookup_adr`).

You can verify it's loaded by running `/mcp` in Claude Code to list connected MCP servers, or by asking Claude Code to search the docs (e.g., "search the docs for workload identity") and it should use the `search_docs` tool.

If you want to add it globally (across all projects), you can add the same config to `~/.claude/settings.json` under the `mcpServers` key, but you'd need to use absolute paths for the command and `DOCS_ROOT`.

> DEVELOPER

can i access it via the Github pages site

> AGENT

No. The MCP server is a Node.js process that runs locally via stdio — it reads the markdown files from disk and exposes them over the MCP protocol. It's not a web service and isn't deployed to GitHub Pages.

GitHub Pages only serves the static Docusaurus site (HTML/CSS/JS). The MCP server is a separate tool for AI agents to query the documentation programmatically.

If you wanted remote access to the docs via MCP, you'd need to either:

1. **Deploy the MCP server as an HTTP service** (e.g., on Cloud Run) using SSE or Streamable HTTP transport instead of stdio
2. **Use the built-in `kix-docs` MCP server locally** by cloning the repo and building it, which is the current setup

For now, anyone who clones this repo and builds the MCP server gets access automatically via the `.mcp.json` config.
